appCatalogue.surface: The audience voting page (public/vote.html, served at /:slug/vote)
appCatalogue.summary: This is the single page the room holds in its hands: one 1,164-line HTML file with no build step, no framework and no login, served at /:slug/vote (netlify.toml redirect), talking to six public endpoints. A fan opens it, is silently given a random device id in localStorage (vote.html:287-290), and can see what is playing, see the running vote board, spend a small allowance of free votes on what plays next, buy more, tip, ask for a song that isn't listed, ask for a birthday shout-out, and read the lyrics of whatever is playing right now. Everything the room experiences is free of plan gates — the artist's plan changes the numbers behind it (how many free votes, what a pack costs, how big the room can get) but never removes a fan-facing feature. The only true feature flag on this page is `voteFinal`, which defaults ON and makes a cast vote permanent for the round.
appCatalogue.structure: One scrolling column, max 560px wide, in four tiers plus a fixed dock. (1) Sticky header: artist name (tappable, goes to their page), "Live · venue · setlist name" or "That's a wrap", and a credits pill showing remaining/total or ∞. (2) A gradient hero card — "Playing now", the song title, animated equaliser bars, and a "Lyrics" button; when nothing is playing it becomes a plain "Starting soon…" card, and when the show has ended it becomes "That's all — see you next time" with a link to the community page. (3) A "Voting open / Voting paused" strip with the fan's remaining vote count. (4) "Up next" — the top three songs by votes, #1 marked "Winning — plays next", each with a + button. (5) The ask-for-something card (only when the artist enabled requests or birthdays). (6) Search box, a three-way sort bar (Top voted / Song A–Z / Artist A–Z), and a horizontally scrolling genre chip row. (7) "Vote for these" — the rest of the pool as rows with counts and a Vote button. (8) "Already played" — replay-cost rows. (9) Back links to the artist page and to /signup. A fixed bottom dock carries "More votes" and "Tip {FirstName}", and disappears entirely once the show ends. Everything modal is a bottom sheet that can be dragged down, closed with an ✕, tapped away on the backdrop, or dismissed with Escape (vote.html:811-870). Pull-to-refresh works anywhere on the page (pull.js).
appCatalogue.design: Apple-flavoured, warm, and deliberately calm. One accent — a red-to-orange gradient (#FF375F → #FF6B45, app.css:21-26) — used only for the things that matter: the now-playing hero, the winning position pill, a cast vote, the tip button. Everything else is white cards on #F5F5F7 with two soft shadow tiers. Full automatic dark mode (app.css:40-51, pure black ground). System SF-family type, tight letter-spacing, tabular numerals for every vote count. Motion is spring-based (cubic-bezier(.34,1.4,.64,1)): buttons scale to .9 on press, the credits pill "bumps" when your balance changes (vote.html:697-699), a voted button pops, confetti falls after a successful payment (vote.html:966-977), and `prefers-reduced-motion` kills all of it (app.css:190). Haptics on nearly every action via navigator.vibrate — 6ms on a stepper tap, 18ms on a cast vote, a 10-40-10 pattern on a sent request or a gift. A skeleton loader shows before the first payload lands and the content rises in once (vote.html:307-312, 685). Copy is conversational and never technical: "Winning — plays next", "No lyrics for this one yet — you'll have to wing it. 🎤", "Couldn't reach the room — try again". Touch targets are honestly sized — the sheet grab zone is 44px tall even though the visible bar is 5px (vote.html:236-238) — and the vote sheet's Confirm/Not-yet buttons are sticky at the bottom because on a 320×568 phone the rules list used to push them off screen.

features.name: No app, no account, no email
features.whatItDoes: A fan opens a web page and can vote immediately. Identity is a random string minted in localStorage on first visit ('myset.fan'), never an account. No endpoint on this page requires auth.
features.whereInCode: public/vote.html:287-290 (fanId); netlify/functions/feedback.mjs:4-5 comment 'the audience never signs in (INVARIANT 9g)'; netlify/functions/_lib.mjs:1038 cleanFanId
features.whyRelevant: The single strongest claim the product has, and it is literally true — there is no sign-in code path on this surface at all.

features.name: Your votes live in this browser, on this phone
features.whatItDoes: The fan id is stored only in localStorage. Clearing site data, using private browsing, or switching phone mid-gig produces a new identity with a fresh free allowance and no memory of paid votes.
features.whereInCode: public/vote.html:287-290; netlify/functions/_lib.mjs:747-761 roomCounts comment ('the worst it does is count someone twice if they clear their storage mid-gig')
features.whyRelevant: The flip side of 'no account': there is no recovery. A copywriter should not imply votes follow a person.

features.name: Every artist gets their own voting address
features.whatItDoes: /:slug/vote serves this file; the page reads the artist slug from the first path segment and appends ?a=<slug> to every API call. A path segment containing a dot is treated as a real file, so the legacy /vote.html falls through to the founding artist.
features.whyRelevant: Multi-artist is real on this surface — one HTML file, resolved per request.

features.name: A deleted account's voting page 404s the same day
features.whatItDoes: publicArtist() returns null for an artist marked for deletion, so /api/show, /api/vote, /api/pay, /api/request and /api/lyrics all answer 'unknown artist' 404 immediately, thirty days before the data is actually erased.
features.whyRelevant: Part of the 2026-09-05 account work. Not marketing copy, but it explains why a link can die instantly.

features.name: The printed QR code goes to the artist's PAGE, not the voting page
features.whatItDoes: The two QR codes the Studio offers are 'profile' (myset.vip/<slug>) and 'home' (myset.vip). The /vote QR kind still resolves for codes printed earlier but is no longer offered anywhere.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/qr.mjs:12-26 (KINDS + the comment 'neither Studio offers them any more'); public/studio.html:2991-2995 QRS array
features.whyRelevant: 'They scan a code and vote' is one tap short of true. The scan lands on the profile page; voting is the next tap.

features.name: The 'Live now — vote the setlist' button only exists while a show is live
features.whatItDoes: The artist's public page renders the link into the voting page only when show.status === 'live'. When the artist has not tapped Start, there is no route into voting from the profile page at all.
features.whyRelevant: A scan before the gig starts shows a page with no way to vote. Copy that says 'scan and vote' needs the show to be live.

features.name: Silent head count of phones in the room
features.whatItDoes: The voting page alone sends in=1, which stamps the device once per show (seenShow + a salted hash of the network). It is a count of phones, not networks, and it is skipped when the stamp is already correct to save a blob read.
features.whyRelevant: This is where 'eight people were in the room' comes from. The raw IP is never stored — only a hash salted with the artist id.

features.name: Installable, and it survives bad wifi
features.whatItDoes: The page registers a service worker and ships a web manifest. Navigations are network-first (newest page always wins), static assets are stale-while-revalidate, and nothing under /api is ever cached.
features.whyRelevant: Supports the 'works on the venue's terrible wifi' claim honestly — pages cache, votes never do.

features.name: Automatic dark mode
features.whatItDoes: The whole page follows the phone's light/dark setting, including the browser chrome colour via two theme-color meta tags.
features.whyRelevant: Matters in a dark bar and it is genuinely done, not a token swap.

features.name: The tab and app switcher carry the artist's name
features.whatItDoes: Once the first payload lands the document title becomes 'Vote the setlist — <artist>'. Link previews (iMessage, WhatsApp, Slack) do NOT get this — they read the served HTML and see the neutral static title.
features.whereInCode: public/vote.html:566-573 and the comment above it
features.whyRelevant: Explicitly documented as a half-fix in the code. Never claim shared links preview with the artist's name.

features.name: What's playing right now, in one gradient card
features.whatItDoes: Title, original artist, animated four-bar equaliser, and a Lyrics button. When nothing is playing it degrades to a plain card reading 'Starting soon…'.
features.whyRelevant: It is the visual anchor of the page and the thing screenshots sell.

features.name: An ended show never claims a song is playing
features.whatItDoes: nowPlaying deliberately survives the end of a show (the history needs it), so the hero is suppressed at the point of display: the header says 'That's a wrap — thanks for coming' and the hero says 'That's all — see you next time'.
features.whyRelevant: A deliberate consistency fix, and it changes what a fan can do — see the dock feature.

features.name: 'Say something about tonight →' after the last song
features.whatItDoes: When the show has ended the hero card carries a link to the artist's community page, stamped with the show id so the post is attached to that specific night.
features.whyRelevant: Added 2026-09-04 (67f1d36). It is the only handoff from the room to anything that outlives the gig.

features.name: 'Voting open' / 'Voting paused' status strip
features.whatItDoes: A pill under the hero showing whether the artist has the voting window open, plus the fan's remaining vote count (or 'Unlimited votes'). Hidden entirely once the show has ended.
features.whyRelevant: The artist can pause voting mid-set; the room is told why buttons went dead.

features.name: A live credits pill in the header
features.whatItDoes: Shows remaining/total (or ∞ when unlimited), turns accent-red with a ring when you are out, and animates a scale bump every time the number changes.
features.whyRelevant: The one always-visible piece of state. The bump is a small, real delight moment.

features.name: 'Up next' — the top three songs by votes
features.whatItDoes: Only songs with at least one vote appear. Position 1 is gradient-filled and labelled 'Winning — plays next'. Server ordering is votes desc, then whoever was voted for first, then title.
features.whyRelevant: This is the product in one screenshot. Ties are broken by who voted first, which is a fair and quotable rule.

features.name: You can add votes to a song that is already in the top three
features.whatItDoes: Each Up-next row carries a + button. It is hidden when voting is closed, and disabled when the fan cannot afford the song's cost and does not already hold votes on it.
features.whereInCode: public/vote.html:634-641 and the comment at 82-84 ('the top three used to be display-only')
features.whyRelevant: Fixed a real dead end: a fan who voted a song into the top three had no button left.

features.name: 'Your 3 votes — tap to add more' on songs you backed
features.whatItDoes: A per-row line in Up next showing how many of your votes are on it. The suffix changes with the finality flag: '— tap to add more' when votes are final, '— tap to change' when they are not, and nothing at all while voting is closed.
features.whyRelevant: Three different strings from one line of code. Screenshot copy will differ depending on the flag.

features.name: Two different empty states for 'Up next'
features.whatItDoes: With songs in the library but no votes: 'No votes yet — Pick a song below and you'll set the queue.' With no library at all: 'Nothing on the list yet — <FirstName> is still putting tonight's songs in.'
features.whyRelevant: Shows the care level. A brand-new artist's room does not get told to pick from a list that doesn't exist.

features.name: The full pool: every song, with its live vote count and a Vote button
features.whatItDoes: Rows show title, original artist, count, and a Vote button that reads 'Vote', 'Voted', or 'Voted ×3'. The count is dimmed until a song has votes.
features.whyRelevant: The main interaction surface.

features.name: A vote button you cannot afford is disabled, never a failed tap
features.whatItDoes: Rows disable when voting is closed, or when the fan's remaining credits are below the song's cost and they do not already hold a removable vote on it. Unlimited devices are explicitly excluded from the check (null < 1 is true in JS, which once disabled every button in the room).
features.whereInCode: public/vote.html:713-720 and the comment above it; also public/vote.html:634-641 for the Up-next twin
features.whyRelevant: An explicit product rule in the code: never show the room a button that leads to a shrug (INVARIANT 0ad).

features.name: Search by song or artist
features.whatItDoes: A live filter over the pool and the already-played list, with a clear button. Focus and cursor position survive the polling re-render.
features.whyRelevant: Necessary for a 60-song setlist, and the focus-preservation across a 3-second re-render is a genuinely hard detail done right.

features.name: Search does NOT filter the top three
features.whatItDoes: The Up-next queue is built before the filter is applied, so searching narrows only the pool below — the top three stay on screen regardless of the search term.
features.whereInCode: public/vote.html:587-592 (queue built from unfiltered `voted`; `rest` filtered by match and genre)
features.whyRelevant: A copywriter describing search as 'find your song' should know the board above never hides.

features.name: Sort the list: Top voted / Song A–Z / Artist A–Z
features.whatItDoes: Three-way segmented control. 'Top voted' keeps the server's exact ranking so the pool always agrees with Up next. The choice is remembered between visits in localStorage.
features.whyRelevant: Sorting is remembered; the genre filter deliberately is not — a documented, opposite decision.

features.name: Genre / mood chips, and only the ones actually in play
features.whatItDoes: A scrolling chip row built from the genres actually used by a song the room can see. Hidden entirely when fewer than two genres are in play. Includes tempo chips (Slow / Mid-tempo / Upbeat) and 'Sing-along' alongside real genres. Never remembered between visits, on purpose.
features.whyRelevant: 'Something upbeat' is how a real room asks — that is written in the code as the reason tempo chips exist. Artists can add up to 15 of their own tags.

features.name: 'Already played' — hear it again, at a higher price
features.whatItDoes: A separate section listing songs the room has already heard, each with a cost pill. Default replay price is 5 votes. A played song stays votable even if it is not in tonight's narrowed setlist.
features.whereInCode: public/vote.html:678-679, 470; netlify/functions/show.mjs:93-105; netlify/functions/_lib.mjs:712-713 costOf; netlify/functions/_lib.mjs:699-704 votable
features.whyRelevant: An encore mechanic priced in votes rather than money — distinctive and easy to explain.

features.name: A vote sheet with a quantity stepper, not one-tap-one-vote
features.whatItDoes: Tapping a song opens a bottom sheet with a −/+ stepper, a big number, the cost line, and a Confirm button labelled with the total. Capped at 20 per song per confirm on the page; the server caps any single request at 50.
features.whyRelevant: Added 2026-09-02 (190e2b4). Replaced tap-five-times with 'say how strongly you want it'. This is the newest big change to the core interaction and the landing page may not describe it.

features.name: The rules, written on the sheet, in plain words
features.whatItDoes: Up to six lines above Confirm: how many votes you have; that free votes come back when a new song starts; how many you bought and that those are yours to keep; whether the vote is final or reversible; what happens if the artist drops the song; and that the list refreshes itself.
features.flagGate: voteFinal changes two of the lines — netlify/functions/_flags.mjs:28-37
features.whyRelevant: Born from a real gig where a fan was 'saving their votes' that had already refreshed twice. The rules being visible IS the feature.

features.name: Votes are final once confirmed
features.whatItDoes: With voteFinal on (the default since 2026-09-02), a confirmed vote cannot be taken back. The sheet says 'Are you sure? Votes can't be changed!' and the server refuses a clear with 409 'Those votes are cast — they stay with the song'. You can still ADD more to the same song.
features.whyRelevant: The single biggest behavioural change on this page since 2026-09-02, and it is on by default. Any copy promising 'change your mind' is currently wrong.

features.name: The 'take your votes back' sheet
features.whatItDoes: When finality is OFF, tapping a song you already hold votes on opens a sheet offering 'Take them back — N votes returned' / 'Leave them there'.
features.flagGate: voteFinal — unreachable while the flag is ON, which is the default
features.whyRelevant: openVote returns early to openUnvote only when finality is off, so with the shipped default this sheet never opens — and the voteFinal branch INSIDE it ('These are cast — they stay with the song') can never render at all.

features.name: A dropped response on bar wifi cannot cost you a second vote
features.whatItDoes: Each press of Confirm mints one cast id. The page retries once after 900ms with the SAME id; the server remembers the outcome against that id on the fan record (last 20 kept) and replays the first answer instead of charging again. A malformed id is refused outright rather than treated as absent.
features.whyRelevant: Added 2026-09-02 (ad69933) precisely because finality removed the toggle that used to self-correct a lost vote. Supports the 'terrible wifi' story with a real mechanism.

features.name: The number moves before the server answers
features.whatItDoes: The tally, the credits pill and the button state update instantly on tap, with a pop animation and a haptic buzz, then reconcile with the next poll. A per-song busy set stops a double submit.
features.whyRelevant: This is why it feels instant in a room. Worth showing, not saying.

features.name: Free votes come back every time a new song starts
features.whatItDoes: Default 5 free credits. Starting any song wipes every fan's votes and non-song spend across all 12 shards, so the allowance refreshes for the whole room and each gap is a fresh contest.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/_lib.mjs:176 (freeCredits: 5); netlify/functions/_lib.mjs:507-531 clearAllFanVotes; netlify/functions/admin.mjs:1771-1786 (play sets resetVotes)
features.planGate: Artists can change the number only on Plus/Pro — netlify/functions/admin.mjs:1706-1708, netlify/functions/_plan.mjs:66
features.whyRelevant: The economic engine of the whole room. Note it is per ROUND, not per night — a 20-song set gives a fan up to 100 free votes.

features.name: Unlimited voting — for the whole room, or one device
features.whatItDoes: The artist can switch the whole room to unlimited (credits pill shows ∞, no affordability checks) or grant it to specific devices, up to 20, typically their own phone for testing.
features.whyRelevant: Turns MySet into a pure popularity poll with no scarcity — a genuinely different product mode, one toggle away.

features.name: If the artist drops a song, the votes on it come back automatically
features.whatItDoes: When the playable set shrinks (a song hidden, a setlist narrowed or deleted), every credit held on the now-unvotable songs is released across all shards, and the artist is told which songs it affected. Deleting a song outright drops every vote on it, not just the first.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/_lib.mjs:589-616 releaseUnvotable; netlify/functions/_lib.mjs:618-643 dropSongVotes; netlify/functions/_lifecycle.mjs:63-78 releaseNote; INVARIANTS.md:725
features.whyRelevant: This exists because finality removed the un-vote escape hatch. It is a stronger promise than the old one — the fan need not even notice.

features.name: Honest refusals when a vote cannot land
features.whatItDoes: The server refuses with human sentences: 'The show has ended' (409), 'Voting is closed right now' (409), 'That one is playing right now' (409), "That one isn't on tonight's list" (404), 'no-credits' (402), 'busy' (503).
features.whyRelevant: The prose itself is registered as an anti-clone fingerprint (netlify/functions/_canary.mjs:20-24).

features.name: Running out of votes opens the buy sheet, not an error
features.whatItDoes: A 402 'no-credits' response toasts 'Out of votes — grab more below' and immediately opens the pack sheet. The same happens from a request that costs more than you have.
features.whyRelevant: The revenue moment. It is one tap from empty to checkout.

features.name: Buy more votes — two packs, priced by the artist
features.whatItDoes: A sheet with two tiles (default $5 / 5 votes and $10 / 15 votes) and a Stripe checkout button. Prices come from the artist's show record and are re-read server-side; the client's claimed price is never trusted. Pack cents are clamped to $1–$500 and votes to 1–100.
features.whereInCode: public/vote.html:917-932; netlify/functions/_lib.mjs:280-285 DEFAULT_PACKS; netlify/functions/_lib.mjs:290-302 normPacks; netlify/functions/pay.mjs:84-100
features.planGate: Changing the prices is Plus/Pro — netlify/functions/admin.mjs:1706-1708, _plan.mjs:66
features.whyRelevant: The $3 tier was deliberately removed because Stripe's fixed fee ate ~13% of it; $5 keeps it under 6%.

features.name: Tip the artist, with a note they see on stage
features.whatItDoes: $5 / $10 / $20 tiles plus a free-entry amount ($1–$500) and an optional 120-character note. The sheet says '100% goes to <FirstName>'.
features.planGate: none for the fan; the platform's cut of it is 10% free / 2% Plus / 0% Pro — netlify/functions/_plan.mjs:70, 85, 97
features.whyRelevant: The sheet says 100% goes to the artist, but a free-plan artist actually pays a 10% application fee on it. That contradiction matters.

features.name: When card payments are off, the buttons say so kindly
features.whatItDoes: If payments are not available, 'More votes' and 'Tip' still exist but open a sheet reading 'Card payments aren't on tonight — grab <FirstName> between songs.' The dock's subtitle changes from 'From $5' to 'Ask <FirstName>'.
features.whyRelevant: canTakeMoney requires a Stripe key AND (the founding artist OR a completed Connect onboarding). Today that means essentially only Perry's own gigs can take money.

features.name: Come back from Stripe to confetti and your votes already added
features.whatItDoes: Checkout returns to /:slug/vote?paid=<session>. The page confirms server-side, drops confetti, buzzes, and toasts either 'N extra votes added — vote away!' or 'Thank you! Your $X tip reached <FirstName>'. A cancelled checkout toasts 'Payment cancelled'.
features.whyRelevant: The delight beat of the paid path, and it is real.

features.name: A payment that got lost on the way back is redeemed on the next page load
features.whatItDoes: The session id is stored in localStorage BEFORE leaving for Stripe. If the return trip fails — tab closed, wallet app hijacked the redirect, dead wifi — the next load quietly retries for up to 26 hours. Three independent paths grant a payment: this return trip, the Stripe webhook, and the artist's reconcile sweep, all replay-safe.
features.whyRelevant: 'A payment must never be charged without the buyer getting what they bought' is written as a rule in the file and backed by three mechanisms.

features.name: Bought votes you never spent: keep them, or let the artist have them
features.whatItDoes: When a show ends holding unspent paid votes, a sheet appears after 700ms offering 'Keep them (for the next show)' or 'Let <FirstName> keep it (call it a tip)'. Doing nothing keeps them. The gift is a pledge, not a debit — if the artist ended the show by mistake and restarts, the fan is silently made whole.
features.whyRelevant: A genuinely unusual piece of fairness, and the endpoint refuses unless the show is really ended (an End tapped by mistake used to ask the whole room to give away paid votes).

features.name: Votes you paid for carry to the artist's next show
features.whatItDoes: Free credits, picks and timestamps reset at the end of a night; unspent paid votes carry over unless gifted. In-flight votes are charged against free credits first, so holding a vote when the artist ends the show costs the fan nothing.

features.whyRelevant: Quietly generous, and the code comments say a bug once made a pack a permanent boost and another once destroyed packs entirely.

features.name: The tip and buy dock disappears the moment the show ends
features.whatItDoes: The fixed bottom dock is hidden when status is 'ended', so after the last song there is no way to tip or buy votes from this page.
features.whyRelevant: A real product gap: the moment a fan most wants to tip — right after the encore — the button is gone.

features.name: Request a song that isn't on the list — paid in votes, not money
features.whatItDoes: A sheet takes a title and optional artist. Costs votes (default 3), refunded if the artist declines. The card only renders when the artist has switched it on, and the button is disabled and labelled 'Needs 3 votes' or 'Voting is paused' when it cannot be used.
features.whereInCode: public/vote.html:729-756, 757-767, 778-803; netlify/functions/request.mjs; netlify/functions/_requests.mjs:64-137; netlify/functions/_lib.mjs:182 (off by default, cost 3)
features.planGate: Turning it on is free; changing the cost is Plus/Pro — netlify/functions/admin.mjs:1931-1945
features.whyRelevant: Off by default, which is the whole design: 'a request the artist can't play is worse than no request at all'.

features.name: Birthday shout-out
features.whatItDoes: A sheet takes a name; nothing is added to the setlist, the artist just sees it on stage. Same votes-not-money mechanic, default 3 votes, refunded on decline, off until switched on.
features.planGate: Same as requests — free to switch on, Plus/Pro to reprice
features.whyRelevant: The most human feature on the page and the easiest to picture — 'a happy birthday for Maya at table four'.

features.name: Live status on what you asked for
features.whatItDoes: Under the ask card, each of your requests for tonight shows a state: 'Waiting on <FirstName>', 'On the list — go vote for it', 'Played 🎉', or 'Not tonight — votes refunded'.
features.whyRelevant: Closes the loop — a request that vanishes into silence is the failure mode this avoids.

features.name: Request throttles: one open per kind, thirty pending per show
features.whatItDoes: A fan may have one open song request and one open birthday at a time ('You've already got a request in — wait for that one first'). A show tops out at 30 pending across everyone ('There are a lot of requests in already — try again in a bit'). Votes are taken first and put back if the row cannot be stored.
features.whyRelevant: Stops one table monopolising the stage. Not marketing copy, but it bounds the claim.

features.name: A request pushes a notification to the artist's phone
features.whatItDoes: After the request is stored AND read back, a Web Push notification goes to the artist's installed Studio, if they have alerts on. Never awaited, never allowed to be the reason a paid request fails.
features.whyRelevant: Added 2026-09-02 (d459efc). The audience is never pushed to — only the artist, and only if they installed the Studio.

features.name: Lyrics for whatever is playing, so the room can sing along
features.whatItDoes: A button on the now-playing hero opens a scrolling sheet (max 62vh) with the words. Fetched from LRCLIB server-side and cached forever in Blobs, so a whole bar tapping at once is one API call, not forty. Text is not selectable.
features.planGate: none — deliberately free on every plan (netlify/functions/_plan.mjs:11-15)
features.whyRelevant: Was briefly a paid feature and was put back, with the reason written down: 'Anything the ROOM experiences stays free.'

features.name: 'Unofficial lyrics' — the footer that tells the truth about them
features.whatItDoes: Every lyric sheet ends with a credit line reading 'Unofficial lyrics' plus either 'provided by the artist' or 'community-contributed, may not be exact. For singing along in the room only.'
features.whyRelevant: The licensing posture, said out loud on the fan's screen. Never describe this as a licensed lyric feed.

features.name: Lyrics are one song at a time, never a library
features.whatItDoes: The endpoint takes one song id and refuses anything not in tonight's setlist. No browsing, no search — 'both the licensing posture and, in a bar, the better product.'
features.whyRelevant: Bounds the claim: MySet is not a lyrics app.

features.name: 'No lyrics for this one yet — you'll have to wing it. 🎤'
features.whatItDoes: When LRCLIB has nothing, or the artist has blocked lyrics for that song by saving an empty sheet, the fan gets that line. A miss is re-checked after 30 days.
features.whyRelevant: An artist can take lyrics down for a song, and a copywriter should not promise words for every song.

features.name: An artist can paste their own words for their own songs
features.whatItDoes: When the artist types lyrics in the Studio and marks them as their own, the fan's footer says 'provided by the artist' instead of 'community-contributed'.
features.whyRelevant: Directly answers 'I play originals' — an original's lyrics can only come from the artist.

features.name: 'Enjoying MySet?' — a star rating asked of the audience
features.whatItDoes: An iOS-style sheet with five stars and an optional 400-character note. Only after an hour of accumulated VISIBLE use, at most weekly, never twice once answered, never over another sheet, never mid-vote. The weekly limit is enforced on the server too, because a localStorage rule is a suggestion.
features.whereInCode: public/vote.html:335-408 (FB_AFTER, fbDue, drawFeedback, fbSend); netlify/functions/feedback.mjs; netlify/functions/_feedback.mjs:34-63
features.whyRelevant: Added 2026-09-02 (255e4cd). It is the only place MySet talks about itself to a fan, and its restraint is the point — nothing may get in the way of the gig.

features.name: The board refreshes itself, and slows down when the room goes quiet
features.whatItDoes: Adaptive polling: 3s while anything is moving, then 10s, then 25s, then a terminal 60s rung for a phone left face-up on a table. Every interval carries ±20% jitter so a whole room does not fire on the same tick. Any tap or screen-on wakes it.
features.whyRelevant: The mechanism behind 'it backs off politely when the room goes quiet'. Note the rungs are 3/10/25/60 seconds, not 'every few seconds' always.

features.name: The server tells every phone how fast to poll, live, mid-gig
features.whatItDoes: /api/show returns nextPollMs computed from the real head count: 3s up to 200 people, 5s to 1,000, 10s to 3,000, 20s beyond. The page clamps it to 1–60s and rebuilds the whole ladder off it, so a packed night slows itself down instead of melting.
features.planGate: none — the cap that drives it is per plan: free 200 / Plus 1,000 / Pro 2,000 (netlify/functions/_plan.mjs:63, 88, 106)
features.whyRelevant: Shipped 2026-09-05 21:24 (421d5ac) — 35 minutes before the landing page's last edit. In a 3,000+ person room an idle phone can sit 400 seconds between refreshes.

features.name: In a big room, a stranger's vote no longer wakes everybody's phone
features.whatItDoes: Two signatures decide whether the ladder resets. Below the point where the server widens the interval, any vote by anyone accelerates the room (which in a pub IS the product). Above it, only the artist's actions and your own credits wake you; the board still redraws, it just stops accelerating everyone.
features.whyRelevant: The newest change to this file — commit bcaf9a1, 2026-09-05 22:39, AFTER the landing page's last edit (9e9fde4). The landing page has never heard of it.

features.name: 'Big room tonight — showing the top 40' — and your own songs always stay
features.whatItDoes: Past 200 phones the server sends the top of the chart instead of all of it (40 / 25 / 15 by size). Anything this fan voted for is appended regardless of rank, and the page prints a notice saying so.
features.whyRelevant: Shipped 2026-09-05 (421d5ac). 'In a voting app, silence about that reads as my vote didn't count' — the label is a trust feature, not decoration.

features.name: Nobody is ever turned away for being over the plan's room size
features.whatItDoes: The audience number on each plan is a billing line, not a turnstile. Going over does not close the door or refuse a vote: the room slows, the board shortens, and the artist is told afterwards. There is deliberately no head-count check in the vote handler.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/show.mjs:32-46, 168; netlify/functions/vote.mjs:81-92 (the explicit non-check); netlify/functions/_lifecycle.mjs:45-57 roomCapFor
features.planGate: free 200 / Plus 1,000 / Pro 2,000, stamped on the show when it starts — netlify/functions/_plan.mjs:63, 88, 106
features.whyRelevant: Shipped 2026-09-05. The cap is stamped at show start, so an artist who upgrades mid-set does not get a bigger room until the next show.

features.name: Pull down to refresh, even when installed to the home screen
features.whatItDoes: A shared gesture library draws a spinner and refetches, then puts the poll back on its fast rung. It stands down while a sheet is open so dragging a sheet closed does not also reload the page behind it. The browser's own gesture is deliberately not suppressed.
features.whereInCode: public/vote.html:1139-1144, 34 (blocking script load, on purpose); public/pull.js:1-30, 72-80
features.whyRelevant: Added 2026-09-03 (117661d) after Perry said 'drag down to refresh doesn't work on a web app'. It cannot rescue a page whose JavaScript is broken — that limitation is written in the file.

features.name: Every sheet can be dragged down, tapped away, ✕'d or escaped
features.whatItDoes: A 44px grab zone, a corner ✕, a backdrop tap, and the Escape key. The drag ends in a close if you move 70px or flick fast; dragging from the body only counts while the sheet is scrolled to the top. Listeners are bound once for the life of the page.
features.whyRelevant: Added 2026-09-02 (fb95e31) because 'a fan who opened it by mistake was stuck reading'. The kind of care that shows in a demo.

features.name: 'Play live yourself? Get your own page →'
features.whatItDoes: A small link at the bottom of the voting page pointing at /signup, which serves the Studio.
features.whyRelevant: The only acquisition loop on this page — every fan in the room is a possible artist, and this is the one line that says so.

features.name: 'Requests are closed now, but here's what you asked for'
features.whatItDoes: Intended to show your past requests after the artist switches requests off mid-show.
features.whereInCode: public/vote.html:742-744; blocked by netlify/functions/show.mjs:111-113 and public/vote.html:733
features.whyRelevant: show.mjs only reads the requests document when at least one ask type is ON, so when both are off myAsks is [] and askCard returns an empty string — this copy can never render.

features.name: Room size, city and show time are sent to the phone but never displayed
features.whatItDoes: /api/show returns room {cap, in, over}, city and showTime. The voting page renders none of them — the header shows only venue and setlist name.
features.whyRelevant: A fan never sees how many people are in the room. Do not write copy implying they do.

trapsForCopy: Votes are FINAL by default. `voteFinal` defaults to true in code (netlify/functions/_flags.mjs:34, since 2026-09-02). Any copy saying 'changed your mind? tap again' describes the OFF state. The page's own reversible-vote sheet (public/vote.html:484-496) is unreachable with the shipped default.

'They scan a code and they're voting' is one tap short. The only QR codes the Studio prints go to the artist's PROFILE page or to myset.vip (netlify/functions/qr.mjs:12-26, public/studio.html:2991-2995). From the profile page the vote link appears ONLY while the show is live (public/artist.html:389).

Free votes are per ROUND, not per night. Starting any song wipes every fan's votes across all shards, so five free votes times a twenty-song set is up to a hundred free votes a night (netlify/functions/_lib.mjs:507-531; admin.mjs:1782).

'100% goes to the artist' appears on the tip sheet (public/vote.html:936) but a free-plan artist pays a 10% application fee on it (netlify/functions/_plan.mjs:70; _connect.mjs:59-65). Plus is 2%, Pro is 0%.

Card payments are effectively founder-only right now. canTakeMoney requires a Stripe key AND (the founding artist OR a completed Connect onboarding mirrored onto the show record) — netlify/functions/_pay.mjs:52-54, _connect.mjs:57, 284-289. For everyone else the buy and tip buttons open a 'not on tonight' sheet.

Requests and birthday shout-outs are OFF until the artist switches them on, and the fan sees nothing at all when they are off — no greyed button, no card (netlify/functions/_lib.mjs:182-183; public/vote.html:733).

'Declining a request refunds it automatically' is true only for a request made during the CURRENT show. A request carried from an earlier show is deliberately not refunded, because its credits already refreshed (netlify/functions/_requests.mjs:167-176).

'The list updates itself every few seconds' is printed on the vote sheet for every fan (public/vote.html:455) but the server can widen the floor to 20 seconds in a 3,000-person room, and the terminal idle rung is 20× the floor — 400 seconds for a pocketed phone (netlify/functions/_lib.mjs:852-858; public/vote.html:1098-1105).

'Up next' can disagree with what the artist's 'Play the winner' button will actually start. The board is built only from songs not yet played (netlify/functions/show.mjs:76), but playTop's pool includes an already-played song that is holding replay votes (netlify/functions/admin.mjs:1791-1797). A replay can win without ever showing as #1 on the fan's board.
The dock's 'From $X' figure is the minimum of the artist's pack prices AND a hard-coded 500 cents (public/vote.html:708). An artist whose cheapest pack is $8 has the page advertising 'From $5'.
Search never filters the top three — the Up-next queue is built before the filter is applied (public/vote.html:587-592). A fan searching for a song still sees the leaderboard above it.
Once the show ends the entire bottom dock is hidden (public/vote.html:704-705), so there is no way to tip or buy votes right after the last song — the exact moment a fan most wants to.

In 'pre' status (account exists, show not started) the header still renders 'Live · <venue>' with a pulsing dot while the strip below says 'Voting paused' and every button is dead (public/vote.html:598-599, 575, 620-622). Do not screenshot a pre-show page as proof of a live room.

The genre filter row is hidden entirely when fewer than two genres are in use (public/vote.html:550), and the filter is deliberately NOT remembered between visits while the sort order IS (public/vote.html:541-547).

Lyrics are unofficial and community-sourced from LRCLIB, labelled as such on the fan's screen, and an artist can take them down for any song by saving an empty sheet (netlify/functions/_lyrics.mjs:1-14; admin.mjs:966-972; public/vote.html:887-892). Never call it a licensed lyric feed.

A fan's identity is a random string in that browser's localStorage. Clearing site data, private browsing, or a second phone means a new identity, a fresh free allowance, and no memory of paid votes (public/vote.html:287-290).

Being over a plan's audience number never blocks anybody. There is no head-count check in the vote handler at all, by explicit decision (netlify/functions/vote.mjs:81-92). The room slows down and the board shortens instead. And the cap is stamped when the show STARTS, so upgrading mid-set changes nothing until the next show (netlify/functions/_lifecycle.mjs:45-57).

Nothing on this page is gated by the artist's plan for the fan — lyrics, requests, birthdays, tipping, buying, the board are identical on Free. What the plan changes is the artist's ability to set the NUMBERS (free-vote count, pack prices, replay cost, ask cost), which is Plus/Pro (netlify/functions/admin.mjs:1706-1708).
The stepper caps a single confirm at 20 votes on the page and 50 on the server (public/vote.html:427-428; netlify/functions/vote.mjs:16) — 'as many as you want' is wrong.

Unspent PAID votes carry to the artist's next show unless the fan gifts them; free votes never carry (netlify/functions/_lib.mjs:532-566). And gift.mjs computes the leftover without the fan id (gift.mjs:29 vs show.mjs:148), so an unlimited-granted device can be shown a different number than the one the ledger will honour.

appCatalogue.surface: Artist Studio — songs, setlists, library, profile
appCatalogue.summary: The Artist Studio is a single dark, phone-first page (public/studio.html, 4,263 lines, 274 KB, one file, no build step) with seven tabs: Live, Setlist, Gigs, Money, Profile, Merch, Settings. This audit covers the two that hold the artist's material — Setlist (the song library, named setlists, genres, keys, private chord charts, room-facing lyrics, the songs-to-learn list) and Profile (name, tagline, bio, five photos, five streaming links, up to 24 video/music embeds, and the community-page moderation panel). Every write goes to one endpoint, /api/admin (netlify/functions/admin.mjs, 105 KB), which authenticates by studio code + page name and answers most writes with the whole refreshed Studio state so the UI does not need a second round trip (admin.mjs:2017-2020). The library is the single source of truth for what a song IS; a named setlist only ever holds song ids, like a playlist (_lists.mjs:3-7).
appCatalogue.structure: Seven pill tabs stick under a blurred sticky header (studio.html:2539-2547); the tab choice is remembered in localStorage (studio.html:1615). SETLIST TAB, top to bottom: "See what fans see ↗" link → a two-button row, "+ Starter pack" and "Clear setlist" (1953-1957) → the setlist picker strip saying what the room currently sees, tap to open the setlists sheet (setPick, 582-597) → "Add a song" and "Import songs" (1961-1963) → the featured-count line (1965-1966) → search box → three-way sort bar (1975-1978) → "Genres" header with the "✨ Auto-tag songs" button → a chip row of only the genres actually in use, plus a "Hidden" pseudo-chip (genreBar, 837-851) → the song rows, each with Edit / Hide-Show / ✕ (1983-1995) → the "Want to learn" section (learnSection, 728-742). Tapping Edit or Add opens a bottom sheet (drag-down to dismiss, openSheet/attachDrag, 2653-2728) holding title, artist, a 12-root key chip grid with a Major/Minor toggle and a free-text key field, genre chips, the private chart textarea, and the room-facing lyrics box (drawSongSheet, 2758-2811). Setlists live in their own stacked sheets: list of sets → one set → the add-songs picker (openLists 598, openList 637, drawPicker 667). PROFILE TAB: "View your page ↗" → Who you are (name, tagline, bio with live character counters) → the photo slots (cover, portrait, three squares) → Listen & follow (five link fields) → Save profile → Videos & music (paste a link, then reorder or remove) → the community-page panel → two greyed "coming soon" cards, Press kit and Branding (2172-2224). Every photo goes through a crop sheet with drag, pinch and a zoom slider before it uploads (openCrop, 4057-4133).
appCatalogue.design: Dark only — there is no light mode. Near-black ground (#000) with #1C1C1E cards, off-white ink, and a pink-to-orange accent pair (#FF456E / #FF7A45) used as a gradient on the logo tile and primary buttons (studio.html:26-38). System font stack (SF Pro on iPhone), tabular-numerals for every count, 600px max width — this is a phone app that happens to run in a browser. It is an installable PWA with its own manifest and icon (manifest-studio.webmanifest, studio.html:22), marked noindex,nofollow (line 18). Interaction is iOS-native in feel: sticky header whose height is measured rather than guessed (fitTabs, 2577-2586), bottom sheets you can fling away, a spring easing curve, buttons that scale on press, a busy spinner that only appears after 140ms so fast taps never flicker (busy, 860-869), pull-to-refresh (public/pull.js). Locked features are shown greyed with a labelled veil rather than hidden — "Plus feature" when paying turns it on, "Coming soon" when it is designed and not built (lock, 1304-1316).

features.name: Add a song
features.whatItDoes: Title (required, 80 chars) and artist (optional, 60). Opens as a bottom sheet that also holds key, genres, chart and lyrics, so one sheet covers everything about a song.
features.planGate: none — only the featured cap and the 2,000-song ceiling apply (admin.mjs:1866-1870)
features.whyRelevant: The first thing every artist does. The whole product is empty until this happens.

features.name: Starter pack — 62 covers in one tap
features.whatItDoes: Appends a fixed list of 62 well-known covers to the library. Never replaces anything: songs already present are skipped by id. Anything over the plan's featured cap arrives switched off.
features.planGate: none — but on free only the first 50 arrive switched on (_plan.mjs:20, admin.mjs:1693-1696)
features.whyRelevant: It is the answer to "how long does setup take". EXACTLY 62 SONGS. Both the button and the landing page say "around sixty", which is honest; a specific number should be 62.

features.name: Clear setlist
features.whatItDoes: Deletes every song in the library — not the active named setlist, the whole library, hidden songs included. Behind a confirm that says "This cannot be undone."
features.whyRelevant: Named "Clear setlist" but it empties the library. Never describe it as clearing tonight's set.

features.name: Import songs — CSV, pasted text, or a Spotify playlist
features.whatItDoes: Parses in the browser first so the artist sees the count and a sample before anything is written. Splits on the first comma, tab, em/en dash or spaced hyphen; skips a header row; caps at 300 rows. The server re-validates, skips duplicates by normalised title+artist, and refuses the remainder loudly at the 2,000-song ceiling.
features.whyRelevant: The realistic path for a working act with an existing setlist. Free on every plan.

features.name: Spotify playlist import
features.whatItDoes: Reads a public Spotify playlist (up to 300 tracks over 3 pages) via the client-credentials flow and hands the titles back for the artist to confirm before importing.
features.flagGate: none — gated on env vars SPOTIFY_CLIENT_ID / SPOTIFY_CLIENT_SECRET; without them the endpoint answers 503 "Spotify import isn't switched on yet" (admin.mjs:1608)
features.whyRelevant: The button is in the Studio and MYSET.md:1120-1122 records the keys as unset in production as of 2026-09-04, so today it leads to a message rather than a result. Do not claim Spotify import on the landing page without checking Netlify env first.

features.name: The key you play it in
features.whatItDoes: A 12-root chip grid (C through B) plus a Major/Minor toggle that writes "G" or "Gm" into the field, and a free-text field for anything else the artist actually writes on their charts — "Capo 2", "Drop D". 14 characters.
features.whyRelevant: The key shows on the Now-playing card during a show (studio.html:1888) and in the setlist rows. It is free, which the landing page correctly says.

features.name: 18 built-in genres
features.whatItDoes: originals, rock, pop, acoustic, country, folk, indie, R&B/Soul, blues, reggae, funk/disco, hip-hop, jazz, latin, sing-along — plus three that are tempo rather than genre: slow, mid-tempo, upbeat.
features.whyRelevant: EIGHTEEN, not fifteen. The comment directly above the list at _lib.mjs:206 still says "Fifteen" — it predates the three tempo tags. Count the array, not the comment.

features.name: Invent your own genres
features.whatItDoes: Up to 15 custom tags, 20 characters each. Ids are prefixed 'c-' so they can never collide with a built-in, and a label that matches a built-in however it is spelled is silently refused so the filter row cannot show two identical chips.
features.whyRelevant: Deleting a custom genre strips it off every song in one write (admin.mjs:683-688), so nothing is left pointing at a tag that no longer exists.

features.name: Six genres per song
features.whatItDoes: A song can carry at most 6 tags; the chip UI refuses the seventh with a toast and shows a live "n of 6" counter.
features.whyRelevant: A hard cap enforced in three places (client, addSong, normShow).

features.name: Auto-tag my songs
features.whatItDoes: Fills in genres for every song that has NONE, from a hand-curated map. Never overwrites a choice made by hand, so it is safe to run repeatedly. Shows a preview sheet with the count first, then a results sheet listing up to 40 titles it did not recognise.
features.whyRelevant: Its reach is narrower than the name suggests — see trapsForCopy. It resets its counters inside the CAS callback so a write conflict cannot double-count (admin.mjs:643-644).

features.name: What auto-tag actually knows
features.whatItDoes: A 62-entry title+artist map (which is exactly the starter pack, verified: 62 of 62 resolve) plus a 76-entry artist-level fallback for common acts. Anything in neither comes back blank and stays blank.
features.whyRelevant: An artist who typed in their own 40 covers will get tags only for the ones by those 76 artists. Never say auto-tag tags "your whole setlist".

features.name: Your own songs are tagged Originals
features.whatItDoes: 'originals' is never in the map. It is applied at tag time when the credited artist matches the artist's own registered name (exact, or one being a prefix of the other).
features.whyRelevant: Only works if the artist typed their own name in the song's Artist field the same way it is registered. Leave the field blank and the song gets nothing.

features.name: Genre chip filter
features.whatItDoes: A row of chips showing only the genres actually present on songs, each with a count, alphabetically. Tap to filter the list; tap again to clear.
features.whyRelevant: Deliberately hides chips that match nothing.

features.name: "Hidden" filter chip
features.whatItDoes: A pseudo-genre chip that appears only when at least one song is switched off, and shows just the hidden ones. Studio-only — the room never sees hidden songs.
features.whyRelevant: The only way to find a song you hid three months ago.

features.name: Search and three sort orders
features.whatItDoes: Search matches title or artist. Sort by Top voted (the server's live ranking), Song A-Z or Artist A-Z, using locale collation so accents sort properly. The choice is remembered in localStorage. Deliberately the same search and the same three orders the audience gets on the voting page.
features.whyRelevant: Matters at 400 songs; invisible at 40.

features.name: Hide a song from fans
features.whatItDoes: Switches a song off. It stays off across every future show until switched back on, and it never appears to the room. Switching one back ON is refused if it would breach the featured cap.
features.planGate: free for hiding; turning one back on is capped at 50 live on free (admin.mjs:1851-1857)
features.whyRelevant: The landing page's answer to "can people see my whole setlist" leans on this. Hiding is free and permanent-until-undone.

features.name: Remove a song for good
features.whatItDoes: Deletes it from the library and refunds the votes fans were holding on it, so nobody's credit is stranded.
features.whyRelevant: The vote refund is the non-obvious half. Votes are final for fans (flag voteFinal, default ON), so if the artist removes a song the credit has to come back here or it is lost.

features.name: 50 songs live to the room at once (free)
features.whatItDoes: Free artists can KEEP 2,000 songs but only 50 are visible to the room at any moment. Anything added over the cap — by hand, by import, by the starter pack, by accepting a request, by "Learned it" — arrives switched off with a note saying so. Plus and Pro are unlimited.
features.whyRelevant: The free tier's real ceiling, and the one that bites soonest — the 62-song starter pack alone puts a free artist 12 songs over it on day one.

features.name: Keep 2,000 songs on any plan
features.whatItDoes: A hard ceiling on how many songs a library can hold, identical on every plan. Refusals say "more than any setlist needs".
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/_plan.mjs:133 (MAX_LIBRARY), netlify/functions/admin.mjs:393-406 (shipped to the Studio as limits.library)
features.planGate: none — same on free, plus and pro
features.whyRelevant: Upgrading does NOT buy you more storage. It buys how many are live at once.

features.name: Your chart — private, per song
features.whatItDoes: A 20,000-character monospace textarea for chords, capo notes, the bit you always forget. Never in any public payload, never fetched from anywhere, stored in its own document so the hot show record stays small. Readable full-screen mid-song from the Live tab's Now-playing card.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/_chart.mjs:1-27, netlify/functions/admin.mjs:617-622 (chartSet), public/studio.html:2789-2795 (editor), :2902-2914 (openChart), :1889 (the "☰ My chart" button)
features.whyRelevant: The landing page already lists "chord charts" as free. The strong point is that it is PRIVATE — the room never sees it — and that it is one tap away while a song is playing.

features.name: chartFlags endpoint
features.whatItDoes: A server action that reports which songs have a chart, so the Studio could show a marker without loading any of them.
features.whyRelevant: Nothing calls it. A repo-wide grep finds only its definition, its import and its registration — the Studio declares a CHARTS variable (studio.html:549) and only ever sets it to null (:2888). There is no chart marker in the song rows.

features.name: Words for the room
features.whatItDoes: Lyrics the audience can tap to see during a song. The artist can paste their own (which override anything found online and are labelled as theirs) or pull them from LRCLIB. Up to 20,000 characters.
features.planGate: none — deliberately free forever (_plan.mjs:11-15: "Anything the ROOM experiences stays free")
features.whyRelevant: It was briefly a paid feature and was put back on purpose, with a stated reason: an audience that gets a sing-along at one gig and not the next learns MySet is unreliable.

features.name: Find lyrics online
features.whatItDoes: Fetches one song's words from LRCLIB (free, keyless, no AI, ~0.4s), falling back from exact match to search. Found words are shown to the room as "Unofficial lyrics". Cached in Blobs forever so a bar full of people tapping Lyrics never becomes forty calls to a community API. A miss is re-checked after a month.
features.whyRelevant: It fails quietly and honestly — a network wobble or a miss surfaces as "Nothing found — paste them yourself", never as an error.

features.name: Remove words for a song
features.whatItDoes: Clears the lyrics and marks the song 'blocked', so it is never re-fetched and the Lyrics button simply does not appear for that song.
features.whyRelevant: Blocked is a sticky state, not a blank — pasting nothing is how you turn lyrics off for that song permanently.

features.name: Fetch lyrics for the whole setlist
features.whatItDoes: Walks every switched-on song and caches its words in one go, before a gig. Sits on the Settings tab, not the Setlist tab.
features.whyRelevant: The Studio copy says "Takes about half a minute" (studio.html:2317), but the loop sleeps 350ms per song on top of each ~0.4s fetch, so 62 songs is ~45 seconds of wall clock inside one synchronous Netlify function. There is no extended timeout configured in netlify.toml. Treat this as unreliable on a full setlist and do not put it on the landing page.

features.name: Named setlists
features.whatItDoes: Up to 20 named subsets of the one library — "Beach set", "Late set", "Irish pub". 40-character names, up to 500 song ids each. Setlists hold ids only, so renaming a song or changing its key changes it everywhere at once.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/_lists.mjs:1-127 (MAX_LISTS=20 at :29, MAX_NAME=40 at :30), netlify/functions/admin.mjs:711-803, public/studio.html:598-727
features.planGate: CREATING a new one is Plus (admin.mjs:730-737). Using, renaming, editing membership, deleting and per-gig attachment are free on every plan.
features.whyRelevant: This is the single most likely thing for marketing copy to get wrong — see trapsForCopy. The gate is on creation only, and there is a founder bypass (isPlatformOwner, _plan.mjs:154).

features.name: New setlist is a Plus feature
features.whatItDoes: listNew refuses on free with a 402 and the message "Separate setlists are a Plus feature — everything you already have keeps working." The Studio greys the "+ New setlist" button with a Plus veil and the caption "Sets you already have keep working" BEFORE the tap.
features.planGate: free false / plus true / pro true
features.whyRelevant: Added 2026-09-03 (commits 9036f98, then 533b109 "say the setlist limit before the tap"). A downgraded artist keeps every set they already made — a cap never deletes anything.

features.name: The "what the room sees" strip
features.whatItDoes: A permanent row at the top of the Setlist tab reading either "All songs — the whole library, 40 songs" or "Beach set — 12 of your 40 songs are in play". Tap it to open the setlists sheet. Says "Make a set" when there are none.
features.whyRelevant: The one place that states what the audience can currently vote for.

features.name: Empty-setlist fallback warning
features.whatItDoes: If the chosen setlist resolves to nothing votable — emptied, or every song in it hidden — the room silently gets the whole library instead so the night still works, and the Studio shows an orange strip saying so.
features.whyRelevant: An empty voting page is a broken gig. The fallback is deliberate and the artist is told rather than left to find out on stage.

features.name: Add songs to a set
features.whatItDoes: A tick-box picker with its own search, showing only switched-on songs with their genres, alphabetical. Saves the whole membership in one write.
features.planGate: none — free artists can edit sets they already have
features.whyRelevant: The picker filters to active songs only, so a hidden song cannot be added to a set from here.

features.name: Attach a setlist to a gig
features.whatItDoes: A dropdown in the gig editor with three kinds of answer: "Leave whatever I've picked", "All songs", or one of your sets. Tapping Start the show on the night switches to it automatically and says which one, with the song count.
features.planGate: none — but you need a set to attach, and creating one is Plus
features.whyRelevant: Only fires for a gig starting within the next 6 hours (_lifecycle.mjs:90). If the gig points at a setlist that has since been deleted, nothing changes and the artist is told — never silently blanked (:91-94).

features.name: Votes come back when you narrow the set
features.whatItDoes: Whenever the artist hides a song, removes one, edits a set's membership, switches sets or deletes a set, any votes fans were holding on songs the room can no longer choose are released back to them, and the artist is told which songs freed them.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/admin.mjs:717-727 (the snapshot and release in handleLists), :2005-2013, netlify/functions/_lib.mjs:587-600 (releaseUnvotable)
features.whyRelevant: Load-bearing because votes are final (flag voteFinal, default true) — there is no un-vote for the fan to fall back on, so credit would otherwise be stranded for the rest of the round.

features.name: Accepting a request adds the song to tonight's set
features.whatItDoes: When a fan pays votes to request a song and the artist accepts, the song joins the library AND is pushed into the active named setlist, so the room can actually vote for it.
features.whyRelevant: Without it the fan who paid three credits would be told "On the list — go vote for it" and then be refused.

features.name: Want to learn
features.whatItDoes: A separate list of songs the artist does not play yet — title, artist, and a note to themselves. Up to 120. Deliberately NOT in the library, so the room can never vote for something unplayable. "Learned it" moves the row into the library in one action, with genres already filled in.
features.whyRelevant: A genuinely nice touch for a working musician, and free. The toast is careful: a learned song lands in your SONGS, and with a named set active it still is not in play until you add it to that set.

features.name: Name, tagline and bio
features.whatItDoes: Name (60), one line under your name (120), and a bio (700 characters, newlines preserved) with live "n left" counters that turn amber under 30.
features.whyRelevant: If the artist leaves the name blank, the public page falls back to their registered account name (profile.mjs:21).

features.name: Five photos — cover, portrait, three small
features.whatItDoes: A wide cover, a square portrait laid over it Instagram-style, and three small squares clustered around it. Leave the portrait blank and the cover is used. A brand-new page shows a stock band photo until one is uploaded.
features.whyRelevant: The three-photo cap lives in two places on purpose after a real bug: normProfile trims the array, and admin.mjs checks the slot number. The shared SLOTS set allows p0..p11 only because a venue on Pro gets twelve (_img.mjs:10-22).

features.name: Crop and position before upload
features.whatItDoes: Drag to move, pinch or slider to zoom, with a square guide. The final crop is drawn to a canvas at 1200px wide for a cover or 640 for a square, then stepped down through four JPEG qualities until it fits comfortably under the server's limit.
features.whyRelevant: Added because silently centre-cropping a phone photo cuts people's heads off. It is a real, hand-built crop tool, not a file input.

features.name: Photos are checked by their bytes
features.whatItDoes: The phone shrinks the file before it leaves; the server then refuses anything over 900KB, anything that is not JPEG/PNG/WebP, and anything whose actual file signature does not match its claimed type.
features.whyRelevant: "Trust the bytes, not the label."

features.name: Photos are cached for a year and still update instantly
features.whatItDoes: Every uploaded photo gets a ?v= stamp that changes on upload, so the URL can be cached immutably in the browser and at Netlify's durable edge — a photo is read out of storage by a function once per version, not once per viewer.
features.whyRelevant: A cost and speed property, not a user-facing feature.

features.name: Remove a photo
features.whatItDoes: Deletes the stored bytes and clears the slot. Clearing a middle photo leaves the slot empty rather than sliding the next one into it.
features.whyRelevant: The positional behaviour was a deliberate fix — .filter used to compact the array so clearing photo 1 slid photo 2 into its place.

features.name: Listen & follow — five links
features.whatItDoes: Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube Music, Instagram and a website. Each is parsed as a URL, forced to https, checked against an exact host allowlist (website accepts any https host), and rebuilt with si/utm_*/app/uo tracking params stripped and the fragment removed.
features.whyRelevant: Anything that is not a real link for that service is dropped rather than shown broken — and the Studio names which ones were dropped in the save toast (studio.html:1800-1804).

features.name: Videos & music — up to 24 embeds
features.whatItDoes: Paste a YouTube, Spotify or Apple Music link and it becomes a playable embed on the public page. Reorder with up/down, remove with ✕. Duplicates are refused.
features.whyRelevant: Handles YouTube watch/youtu.be/embed/shorts/live links, playlists and timestamps; Spotify track/album/artist/playlist/show/episode; Apple album/song/artist/playlist/music-video. The artist's string is never stored as an iframe src — only an id is kept and the URL is rebuilt from a literal template on every read.

features.name: Links are checked before they go on your page
features.whatItDoes: YouTube and Spotify links are verified through their public oEmbed endpoints at paste time, which also pulls the real title and thumbnail. Apple Music has no oEmbed, so an Apple id is accepted unvalidated and the artist eyeballs the live preview.
features.whyRelevant: The Studio says "I check it exists before it goes on your page" (studio.html:2206) — true for YouTube and Spotify, NOT true for Apple Music.

features.name: Real numbers on your public page
features.whatItDoes: The public profile endpoint returns nights played, total votes cast, total people in the room, live song count and the date you joined — computed from archived show history, with no follower count because there is no follow.
features.whyRelevant: Where the head-count predates the room counter, it falls back to how many people VOTED — a floor, never a ceiling, so it under-states rather than inflates (profile.mjs:17-20).

features.name: The verified tick on the public page
features.whatItDoes: Shown only when the registry flag is set AND the artist's plan is not free. A lapsed or expired plan drops the tick on the next read, with nothing needing to fire.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/profile.mjs:22-27, netlify/functions/_names.mjs (legal-name + DOB matching that grants it)
features.planGate: requires a paid or comped plan in force
features.whyRelevant: Verification matches the artist's LEGAL name and date of birth against what Stripe verified, not their stage name — because most artists trade under a stage name (_names.mjs:101-112). The DOB is compared and thrown away: never stored, never logged, never shown.

features.name: Community page panel on the Profile tab
features.whatItDoes: Lists up to 30 fan posts with stars, photos, clips and report counts. Reply once per post, pin one, hide any (instant and undoable — hiding also deletes the post's photos and clip), or delete for good.
features.planGate: hiding and replying are free on every plan; permanent DELETE is Plus (moderateAllowed, _plan.mjs:159-161)
features.whyRelevant: The split is deliberate and worth saying plainly: every artist must be able to take something offensive off their page instantly, so hiding is free forever. Paying buys erasing it for good.

features.name: Your press kit
features.whatItDoes: A greyed card on the Profile tab showing what a press kit would contain.
features.planGate: listed as Pro, but in NOT_BUILT so it renders as "Coming soon" on every plan including Pro
features.whyRelevant: There is no code behind it anywhere in the repo. Must not appear on the landing page as a Pro feature you get today.

features.name: Your colours on their phones
features.whatItDoes: A greyed card on the Profile tab previewing custom branding on the audience pages.
features.planGate: listed as Pro, in NOT_BUILT, shown as "Coming soon" to everyone
features.whyRelevant: Same as press kit — designed, not built.

features.name: Profile tab reads the founding artist's profile
features.whatItDoes: The Studio's Profile tab fetches /api/profile with no artist parameter. The endpoint treats a missing slug as the founding artist, so a second artist opening the Profile tab is shown Perry Idyll's name, tagline, bio, photos, links and embeds. The "View your page ↗" button at the top of the same tab is hard-coded to /artist.html, which resolves to the founder's page for the same reason.
features.whereInCode: public/studio.html:1786-1790 (loadProf, no ?a=), :2179 (the hard-coded /artist.html link), netlify/functions/profile.mjs:9, netlify/functions/_lib.mjs:1016-1023 (no slug => DEFAULT_ARTIST)
features.whyRelevant: Saving still writes to the correct account (profileSet uses the authenticated artist id), so the effect is that a non-founder sees the wrong data in the editor and pressing Save would copy it onto their own page. public/artist.html:261-264 builds the same call correctly with the slug, and test/community.mjs:115 calls it with ?a=. Verified by reading the code, not inferred.

features.name: Crew sign-ins are not blocked from most library and profile writes
features.whatItDoes: The capability table is meant to stop a 'crew' sign-in (a sound engineer running the screen tonight) from rewriting the library or the profile. Several entries name actions that do not exist, and the real action names are absent, so the check never fires for them.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/admin.mjs:417-423 (CAPABILITY), :1594-1600 (enforcement), netlify/functions/_session.mjs:250-262 (CAN, crew gets only show+requests)
features.whyRelevant: The table lists setChart, setLyrics, listSave, listApply, songSet, bulkSongs, profileSave, imgSave, imgDelete and merchDelete — none of which are real action names. The real ones (chartSet, lyricsSet, listNew, listRename, listSongs, listToggle, listUse, learnDone, tagAdd, tagRemove, tagAuto, profileSet, photoUpload, photoClear, mediaAdd, mediaMove, mediaRemove, merchRemove) are unlisted, so crew passes. addSong, editSong, removeSong, importSongs, listDelete, learnAdd and learnRemove ARE correctly gated.

trapsForCopy: THE STARTER PACK IS 62 SONGS, exactly (netlify/functions/_lib.mjs:47-112, verified by running the module). The Studio's own confirm dialog and the current landing page both say "around sixty", which is fine; if you ever want a number, it is 62. It appends and never replaces, and skips anything already in the library by song id.

STARTER-PACK SONGS ARRIVE WITH NO GENRES AND NO KEY. The starterSetlist handler pushes {id, title, artist, active} only (admin.mjs:1972-1984) — unlike addSong and learnDone, it does not call the genre map. So "add the starter pack" and "tagged and ready" are two different steps: the artist still has to tap Auto-tag.

ON FREE, THE STARTER PACK IS 12 SONGS OVER THE CAP ON DAY ONE. Free features 50 songs at a time (_plan.mjs:20); the pack is 62. The last 12 arrive switched off, silently — starterSetlist sets active:false for them but attaches no note, unlike addSong and importSongs which both say so. Never write copy implying a free artist gets all sixty-odd live.

CREATING A NEW NAMED SETLIST IS PLUS-GATED. admin.mjs:730-737 refuses listNew on free with a 402. USING, renaming, editing membership, deleting and attaching one to a gig all stay free. public/about.html:606 lists "Setlists, chord charts, keys and genres" under Free, and the FAQ at about.html:693-699 tells the reader to "build a setlist instead — name it, put the songs you want in it" with no mention of a plan. A free artist cannot do that. This gate landed 2026-09-03 (commits 9036f98 then 533b109); the FAQ has not caught up. The safe free framing is HIDING songs, which is free and permanent-until-undone.

THE FOUNDER BYPASSES THE SETLIST GATE. isPlatformOwner (_plan.mjs:154) lets perry-idyll create setlists regardless of plan, and planForArtist returns 'free' for him because he predates the registry. So testing the free experience in Perry's own Studio will show setlists working. Same bypass exists for merch and post-deletion.

"CLEAR SETLIST" EMPTIES THE WHOLE LIBRARY, not the active set. admin.mjs:1985 is `show.songs = []`. The button sits next to "+ Starter pack" (studio.html:1955-1957) and its confirm says "Remove every song from your setlist? This cannot be undone." Any copy that says "clear tonight's set" is describing something that does not exist.

AUTO-TAG ONLY KNOWS 62 SONGS AND 76 ARTISTS. The by-song map in _genremap.mjs:25-88 IS the starter pack, one to one (all 62 resolve; verified). The fallback at :92-169 is 76 artists. A song by neither comes back with nothing and stays blank — the results sheet lists them by name so the artist can tag them by hand. Do not write "auto-tags your whole setlist"; write something like "fills in the blanks it recognises".

AUTO-TAG NEVER OVERWRITES A CHOICE. It only ever fills songs that have no genres at all (admin.mjs:648), so running it twice is safe and running it after hand-tagging leaves the hand-tagging alone. That is a genuine reassurance and worth saying.

THERE ARE 18 BUILT-IN GENRES, NOT 15. _lib.mjs:209-230 lists 18; the comment three lines above still says "Fifteen" because the three tempo tags (slow, mid-tempo, upbeat) were added later. Sing-along is one of the built-ins on purpose. Artists can add 15 more of their own, 6 per song.

UPGRADING DOES NOT BUY MORE STORAGE. MAX_LIBRARY is 2,000 on free, Plus and Pro alike (_plan.mjs:133, shipped to every plan row at admin.mjs:399). What a paid plan buys is how many are LIVE at once: 50 on free, unlimited on Plus and Pro. The Studio's own line gets this right ("Keep as many as you like (up to 2,000) — your plan shows 50 to fans at a time"); copy that says "unlimited songs" without that distinction is wrong in both directions.

THE FEATURED-COUNT LINE IS INVISIBLE ON PLUS AND PRO. shapeLimits maps Infinity to null (admin.mjs:395) and the Studio only renders that line when limits.featured is truthy (studio.html:1965). So a paying artist never sees a featured number at all.

CHORD CHARTS ARE PRIVATE; LYRICS ARE PUBLIC. Two different things in the same sheet. The chart ("only you ever see this", 20,000 chars, own document, never in any public payload — _chart.mjs:3-12) is for the artist mid-song. The lyrics box below it is what the ROOM sees when it taps Lyrics. Never conflate them.

LYRICS ARE FREE FOREVER AND THAT IS A DECISION, NOT AN OVERSIGHT. They were briefly a paid feature and were put back, with the reason written into the code: an audience that gets a sing-along at one artist's gig and not the next learns MySet is unreliable, which costs more than the subscription is worth (_plan.mjs:11-15). Anything the room experiences stays free.

FOUND LYRICS ARE LABELLED "UNOFFICIAL". They come from LRCLIB and the room is told so; only lyrics the artist types themselves are marked as theirs and override anything found online (admin.mjs:965-981, _lyrics.mjs:3-9).

"FETCH LYRICS FOR THE WHOLE SETLIST" IS SLOWER THAN THE STUDIO CLAIMS. The Settings copy says "about half a minute" (studio.html:2317); the loop sleeps 350ms per active song plus each fetch (admin.mjs:989-999), so a 62-song setlist is roughly 45 seconds inside one synchronous Netlify function, with no extended timeout configured in netlify.toml. Keep this off the landing page.

SPOTIFY PLAYLIST IMPORT NEEDS KEYS THAT MYSET.md RECORDS AS UNSET. Without SPOTIFY_CLIENT_ID / SPOTIFY_CLIENT_SECRET the endpoint answers 503 with "Spotify import isn't switched on yet — paste your songs as text instead" (admin.mjs:1608). MYSET.md:1120-1122 says they were unset in production as of 2026-09-04. CSV and pasted-text import are unaffected and work. Verify the live env before claiming Spotify import.

IMPORT DEDUPES, SO A RE-IMPORT IS A NO-OP. Duplicates are matched on normalised title+artist and skipped rather than suffixed (admin.mjs:1898-1900), and the note tells the artist how many were skipped. 300 rows per import.

"WANT TO LEARN" IS DELIBERATELY NOT THE SETLIST. Songs on that list cannot be voted for — that is the whole point (_lists.mjs:11-12). "Learned it" moves the row into the library with genres pre-filled; but with a named setlist active it still is not in play until it is added to that set, and the toast says exactly that (studio.html:773-776).

A NEW SONG IS NOT AUTOMATICALLY IN TONIGHT'S SET. This bug was fixed three separate times in three places (addSong, learnDone, askAccept) and the comments say so. When a named setlist is active, adding a song puts it in the LIBRARY only; the room cannot vote for it until it joins the set. Accepting a paid request is the one exception — that one pushes the song into the active set on purpose (admin.mjs:930-946).

HIDING A SONG IS PERMANENT UNTIL UNDONE, NOT PER-NIGHT. The Studio's helper line says "hide it from fans tonight" (studio.html:1982), but active:false persists across every future show. The landing-page FAQ gets this right ("it stays hidden across every future show"); the in-app line is the loose one.
SWITCHING A HIDDEN SONG BACK ON CAN BE REFUSED. On free, toggling a song on when 50 are already live returns a 402 (admin.mjs:1851-1857). Hiding is never refused; unhiding can be.

THE PROFILE TAB SHOWS THE FOUNDER'S PROFILE TO EVERY OTHER ARTIST. studio.html:1788 calls /api/profile with no artist parameter, and _lib.mjs:1016-1023 treats a missing slug as the founding artist. The "View your page ↗" button on the same tab is hard-coded to /artist.html (studio.html:2179), which resolves the same way. Saving writes to the right account, so the risk is a second artist copying Perry's bio onto their own page. Do not describe the Profile tab from a screenshot taken in Perry's Studio.

APPLE MUSIC LINKS ARE NOT VERIFIED. The Studio says "I check it exists before it goes on your page" (studio.html:2206). True for YouTube and Spotify via oEmbed; Apple has no oEmbed endpoint, so an Apple id is accepted unchecked and the artist eyeballs the preview (_embeds.mjs:140-143).

THE ARTIST'S PASTED URL IS NEVER THE IFRAME SRC. Only a provider, type and id are stored; the embed URL is rebuilt from a literal template on every read, and a stored record that can no longer produce a valid src is dropped on read (_profile.mjs:109-114, _embeds.mjs:95-116). Worth a line if the copy ever talks about safety.

THREE SMALL PHOTOS, NOT TWELVE. The shared slot list allows p0..p11 only because a venue on Pro gets twelve (_img.mjs:10-22); an artist's cap is 3, enforced separately at admin.mjs:1052-1053 and again on read at _profile.mjs:15. Plus five means cover + portrait + three = five images total, and up to 24 embeds on top.

PRESS KIT, BRANDING, CITY PROMOTION AND ANALYTICS ARE DESIGNED AND NOT BUILT. NOT_BUILT in _plan.mjs:130 lists all four; there is no code behind any of them. The Studio shows them greyed as "Coming soon" on every plan including Pro, on purpose, so that Perry (comped to Pro) does not walk into four dead ends. Press kit and branding both live on the Profile tab. None of them may appear on the landing page as something a Pro subscription turns on.

THE SETLIST-FALLBACK IS SILENT TO THE ROOM AND LOUD TO THE ARTIST. If the chosen set has nothing votable left, the whole library stands in for it so the night still works (_lib.mjs:672-682) and the Studio shows a warning strip. Copy that promises "the room sees only what you chose" is true right up until the set empties.

CHARTFLAGS IS DEAD CODE. netlify/functions/_chart.mjs:29-37 and admin.mjs:624-625 implement an endpoint that reports which songs have a chart; nothing calls it. The Studio declares a CHARTS variable and only ever sets it to null. There is no chart marker on the song rows, so do not claim one.

THE STUDIO IS DARK-ONLY AND noindex,nofollow. There is no light mode and no theme toggle (studio.html:26-38, :18). It is a phone app at 600px max width. Any marketing screenshot showing a light Studio is fabricated.

appCatalogue.surface: Artist Studio — the live tab, shows, calendar, requests (running a night)
