appCatalogue.summary: The Artist Studio is a single 4,263-line dark-only page at myset.vip/studio that a working musician holds on stage. It is one client-rendered app with seven tabs (Live, Setlist, Gigs, Money, Profile, Merch, Settings) driven by one `render()` function, fed by one read endpoint `/api/stage` and one write endpoint `/api/admin`. The night-running surface is the Live tab (voting open/pause, three stat tiles, now-playing, the requests panel, start/end the show, "Start top voted", the queue, the played list), the Gigs tab (a month calendar of bookings that also drives shows that start and end themselves), and the parts of Settings that price and configure a show. It is an installable PWA — that install is the only way an iPhone can receive the request alerts — and it is `noindex,nofollow`, so it is not a page marketing can link to as a demo.
appCatalogue.structure: Sign-in gate first (`gate()`, public/studio.html:959) — email code, passkey/Face ID, studio code, or a recovery code; there is no password anywhere. Past the gate the whole app is one `render()` (public/studio.html:1854) writing into `#app`: a sticky header (home mark, "● On stage" when live, artist name linking to the public page, and either an "Upgrade" button or a plan chip), then a 7-tab row that never changes with plan (public/studio.html:2539-2547), then the tab body, then a single big footer button whose destination changes by tab — "See what fans see ↗" on Live (the voting page) and "See your page ↗" everywhere else (public/studio.html:2548-2560). The chosen tab is remembered in localStorage (`myset.tab`, public/studio.html:1615). Only the Live tab auto-refreshes: a 4-second interval that fires only when the document is visible AND `TAB==='live'` (public/studio.html:4246); every other tab is static until you pull down to refresh (`MySetPull`, public/studio.html:4248). Detail work happens in bottom sheets with a drag-to-dismiss grab bar (`openSheet`, public/studio.html:2653) — add/edit a gig, the plans sheet, the setlist picker, the QR lightbox. Deep flows leave the page entirely to Stripe Checkout and come back on `?sub=`, `?connect=`, `?promoted=`, `?promocancel=` query params (public/studio.html:1013-1029, 3624-3640).
appCatalogue.design: Dark only, and deliberately — `--bg:#000`, `--surface:#1C1C1E`, `--ink:#F5F5F7`, accents `--accent:#FF456E` (pink) and `--accent-2:#FF7A45` (orange) (public/studio.html:26-32). There is no light theme and no toggle; it is built for a dim stage. iOS-flavoured: rounded surfaces, hairline dividers, big thumb-sized primary buttons (`.bigplay`, 20px padding, public/studio.html:113). A black boot screen with three animated bars and a line of copy that cycles every 1.4s through "Warming up the room / Tuning the setlist / Counting tonight's votes…" (public/studio.html:4192-4206), and a hard 6-second failsafe that tears it down whatever happens (public/studio.html:4242). Every internal link paints a full-screen "Opening…" splash and waits two animation frames before navigating, so there is never a white flash (`goTo`, public/studio.html:4213-4232). Background polls are silent — the busy overlay only appears after 140ms and never on a `quiet` call (public/studio.html:860-868). Locked features are shown, never hidden: a `.lock` wrapper dims the real control and lays a padlock pill over it reading either "Plus feature" / "Pro feature" (tappable, scrolls you to the plans) or "Coming soon" (not tappable), with the reason in plain text underneath rather than inside the veil (public/studio.html:1304-1316). The tab row's top offset is measured from the header rather than guessed, because the header grows with the phone's text-size setting (`fitTabs`, public/studio.html:2577). The QR codes render as a printable white "paper" card in a full-screen lightbox with the caption a stranger needs to understand it (public/studio.html:2998-3013).

features.name: The Live tab keeps itself up to date
features.whatItDoes: While the Live tab is open and the phone is awake, the Studio re-reads the whole show every 4 seconds, so votes, head count and requests move without touching anything.
features.whyRelevant: This is the 'it just updates' feeling, but it is Live-tab-only.

features.name: Every other tab is frozen until you pull down
features.whatItDoes: The 4-second refresh is gated on `TAB==='live'`. On Gigs, Money, Profile, Merch and Settings nothing refreshes on its own; pull-to-refresh is the only way to get new data.
features.whyRelevant: Never claim the Studio is live everywhere.

features.name: Open / Paused — the voting switch
features.whatItDoes: A two-button toggle at the very top of the Live tab. Open means the room can vote; Paused means nobody can, and the subtitle says so in words ('Fans can vote right now' / 'Paused — nobody can vote until you re-open').
features.whyRelevant: The single most-used control on stage — between songs, and to stop voting during a ballad.

features.name: Starting a song re-opens voting and clears the round
features.whatItDoes: Any `play` or `playTop` sets `windowOpen = true` and resets every vote, so each song is a fresh contest. The artist never has to remember to un-pause.
features.whyRelevant: Explains why free votes 'refresh every time you start a new song'.

features.name: Votes now
features.whatItDoes: First stat tile: the total votes currently sitting on all songs in this round.

features.name: Voting / in room / nets
features.whatItDoes: Second tile reads like '31/48' — people who have actually voted over phones present in the room tonight — plus a count of distinct networks ('· 3 nets') when known. Presence is a stamp a phone writes once when it opens the voting page, not a stored counter.
features.whyRelevant: 'How many people are in the room' is the number venues rebook on, and the artist sees it live.

features.name: Tips (all-time, labelled just 'Tips')
features.whatItDoes: Third tile shows the sum of every tip the artist has ever received, not tonight's. `meta.tips` is appended to on every tip and is never reset or trimmed.
features.whyRelevant: A copywriter would call this 'tonight's tips'. It is not.

features.name: Now playing card, with the key and your chart
features.whatItDoes: When a song is running, a raised card shows the title, the original artist, 'Key of G' if a key is saved, and a '☰ My chart' button that opens the artist's own chord chart.
features.whyRelevant: The Studio doubles as the music stand.

features.name: The requests panel
features.whatItDoes: A panel on the Live tab listing what the room has asked for tonight — song requests and birthday shout-outs — pending first, then the last six resolved. Header counts how many are waiting and states '✕ refunds their votes'.
features.whyRelevant: This is the 'requests stopped being shouted at us' story.

features.name: The requests panel disappears entirely when there is nothing
features.whatItDoes: `asksPanel()` returns an empty string if `D.asks` is empty, and `shapeRequests` filters to the CURRENT `showId` — so starting a new show empties the panel even if requests are still unresolved from the last one.

features.name: + Add — accept a request onto the setlist
features.whatItDoes: Accepting a song request adds it to the library AND, when a setlist is active tonight, into that setlist too, so the whole room can then vote for it. The server refuses rather than adding it switched-off if the plan's featured cap is full, so the fan's votes stay attached to something the artist can still honour.
features.planGate: free = 50 featured songs at once (_plan.mjs:20); accepting past that is refused with a 402
features.whyRelevant: The mechanism behind 'a request the room can then vote on'.

features.name: ✕ — decline and the votes go back automatically
features.whatItDoes: Declining refunds the votes the fan spent. If the request came from an earlier show it refunds nothing on purpose (their credits already refreshed) and says so in the toast.
features.whyRelevant: 'Turning one down refunds them automatically' is a true, checkable claim.

features.name: Did it / Played
features.whatItDoes: Marks a birthday shout-out done, or an accepted song as played. Accepted-but-not-yet-played rows keep a 'Played' button.

features.name: Requests and birthdays are switched on in Settings, not on Live
features.whatItDoes: Both request types are OFF until switched on, and the switches live in the Settings tab under 'Requests from fans' — not next to the panel that shows the results.
features.planGate: switching them ON is free; setting the vote COST is Plus (`canPrice`)
features.whyRelevant: Never say 'requests are on' by default. They are off.

features.name: Requests cost votes, never money
features.whatItDoes: A song request or birthday shout-out is paid for in the fan's vote credits at a cost the artist sets (default chips 1/2/3/5/10). No money changes hands for a request, ever.
features.planGate: the cost is Plus-gated; the standard cost keeps working on free

features.name: One request in at a time, thirty pending per show
features.whatItDoes: A fan may only have one open song request and one open birthday at a time, and the show caps out at 30 pending requests with a 'there are a lot of requests in already' message.

features.name: Start the show
features.whatItDoes: The big primary button when nothing is live. Flips the show to live, stamps `startedBy:'artist'`, applies tonight's setlist from the calendar, and counts one gig against the monthly allowance.
features.planGate: free = 4 shows per calendar month (_plan.mjs:33); founder uncapped (_lifecycle.mjs:42)

features.name: Start a new show (a fresh night)
features.whatItDoes: When the last show ended with songs played, the button becomes 'Start a new show' behind a confirm — it files last night in history, wipes the played list, the log and the votes, mints a new show id, and clears the room.

features.name: Bought votes survive a new show
features.whatItDoes: A fresh night wipes everyone's free credits and the tally, but carries every unspent PAID vote across, so somebody who bought a pack at 9pm still has it after the reset.
features.whyRelevant: A trust claim that is actually enforced in code.

features.name: Resume it instead — the undo for ending a show by mistake
features.whatItDoes: Under the start button, when a show has ended with songs on it, a line says how many songs were played and offers 'Resume it instead' — which flips the status back to live without resetting anything.
features.planGate: a resume still counts a gig unless the show is already live (_lifecycle.mjs:132-135)

features.name: End the show
features.whatItDoes: While live, the primary button becomes '■ End the show' behind a browser confirm ('End the show for fans?'). Ending archives the night first, always, then sweeps stranded votes back to the room.

features.name: The monthly gig warning arrives before the cap, never on stage
features.whatItDoes: On free, once two or fewer shows are left this month, a line appears under the start button: '2 free shows left this month. Resets on the 1st.' At zero it turns accent-coloured: "That's your 4 free shows this month… or upgrade in Settings." It only ever renders when a show is NOT live.
features.planGate: free only — Plus/Pro send `gigs: null` so the block returns empty (admin.mjs:396)
features.whyRelevant: The single most important free-tier fact in the whole app, and it is phrased carefully as a warning, not a wall.

features.name: The cap refusal wording
features.whatItDoes: If a fifth show is started on free, the server refuses with HTTP 402 and the exact sentence "That's your 4 free shows this month. Upgrade to keep playing — your allowance resets on the 1st." The count is taken inside the compare-and-swap so a retry cannot double-count.
features.planGate: free = 4/month; the month is a UTC calendar month (_lib.mjs:131)

features.name: Start top voted — one tap plays what the room chose
features.whatItDoes: A big button naming the winner and its vote count ('Start top voted — Wonderwall (12)'), disabled when there is nothing left. The winner is picked server-side from the same rule the audience board uses, so the Studio can never name a song the server would refuse.
features.whyRelevant: This IS the product in one button.

features.name: A double tap can never burn two songs
features.whatItDoes: `play` on the same song within the guard window is a silent no-op; `playTop` refuses outright with 'That one just started — give it a moment' (409), because a retry would start the NEXT song down instead.
features.whyRelevant: Written for bad bar wifi, which is a good story but not a headline.

features.name: The queue — ranked, tap ▶ to start any of them
features.whatItDoes: The top 12 unplayed songs in vote order, each with rank, title, original artist, vote count and its own '▶ Start' button. The #1 row is highlighted only when it actually has votes. A footer says '+ 14 more in the Setlist tab'.

features.name: The queue obeys tonight's setlist and hidden songs
features.whatItDoes: The pool is filtered by the server's own `votable` flag rather than recomputed in the browser, so a setlist that narrows the room's choices narrows the Studio's queue identically.

features.name: Played, with Undo on every row
features.whatItDoes: Everything played tonight, with an 'Undo' button per song that takes it back out of the played list and returns it to the pool at normal cost.

features.name: Reset votes
features.whatItDoes: A small link in the Played header that clears every vote in the room without starting a song.

features.name: Recent tips on the Live tab
features.whatItDoes: The last 15 tips with amount, the fan's note and how long ago — but, like the tips total, these are the last 15 EVER, not tonight's.

features.name: See what fans see ↗
features.whatItDoes: A full-width button under the Live tab that opens the artist's own voting page, so they can check the room's view. On every other tab the same slot becomes 'See your page ↗' and opens the public profile instead.

features.name: The header says '● On stage' while live
features.whatItDoes: The kicker above the artist name flips from 'Artist Studio' to '● On stage' whenever the show status is live.

features.name: Shows that start themselves from your calendar
features.whatItDoes: A cron rings every two minutes; a gig on the calendar whose start time has arrived starts its show by itself, taking the identical path a tap takes — the gig cap, the archive, tonight's setlist and the paid-vote carry all apply.
features.planGate: none in code — but the plans sheet lists 'Shows that start and end themselves' under Plus and Pro only (studio.html:3532, 3548)
features.whyRelevant: 'You do not have to remember to press start' is a real, shipped promise.

features.name: A self-starting show can be up to two minutes late
features.whatItDoes: The cron interval is two minutes, so the show goes live somewhere inside that window rather than on the second.

features.name: Shows that end themselves, three hours after the gig's end time
features.whatItDoes: If the artist never taps End, the schedule files the night three hours after the gig's scheduled finish — which is what makes the history and the money figures correct without anyone remembering.

features.name: It will not end a show mid-song
features.whatItDoes: If a song started within the last 45 minutes, the automatic end is deferred to the next tick and the gig stays due. A six-hour backstop finally ends it anyway, on the reasoning that the artist walked away from the tablet.

features.name: The schedule never overrules the artist
features.whatItDoes: A gig is started once and once only (the occurrence key is stamped on the show); a night the artist started and then ended by hand is left ended; a show already live for tonight is left alone; and a start refused by the free cap is remembered so it is not retried every two minutes all night.

features.name: It refuses to start a show with no songs switched on
features.whatItDoes: If nothing in the library is active, the schedule declines to start the show — an empty voting page is treated as a broken gig — and retries the moment a song is switched on.

features.name: Last night's show cannot swallow tonight
features.whatItDoes: A show still running from a previous gig is ended and filed before tonight's starts, with two hours of slack so an artist who starts early is never interrupted.
features.whyRelevant: This is the fix for the 'missing shows' story; the nights were never separate in the first place.

features.name: The 'Start shows from my calendar' switch
features.whatItDoes: A Settings toggle. Off means only the artist ever starts a show — but ending by itself STILL applies, and the copy says so.

features.name: The Live tab tells you a show started or ended by itself
features.whatItDoes: When `startedBy` is 'schedule' a line under the End button says 'Started by itself for the gig on your calendar. It ends by itself three hours after that gig's end time, unless you end it first.' When `endedBy` is 'schedule' the resume line says the show was ended by itself.

features.name: Tonight's scheduled start time is computed and never shown
features.whatItDoes: `stagePayload` reads the calendar on every 4-second Studio poll and ships `sched` (start, end, venue, local times) so the Live tab 'can say when the show will start by itself'. Nothing in studio.html ever reads it — the string 'sched' does not appear in the page except in `startedBy==='schedule'` checks.
features.whyRelevant: The Studio does NOT show a countdown to auto-start. Do not imply one.

features.name: A daily self-heal of the gig schedule
features.whatItDoes: Once a day the cron walks the artist registry in batches of 300 with a cursor and re-points every artist's schedule entry from their own calendar, so a gig saved before the index existed, or an entry a lost write dropped, is picked back up.

features.name: The gig calendar — a month grid with dots
features.whatItDoes: A full month view with weekday headers, today highlighted, out-of-month days dimmed, and up to three dots on any day that has bookings. ‹ › moves month by month and refetches.
features.planGate: none — 'gig calendar' is on the free row (_plan.mjs:6-7)

features.name: Tap any day to book it
features.whatItDoes: Tapping a calendar cell opens the Add-a-gig sheet pre-filled with that date.

features.name: Add a gig — the booking sheet
features.whatItDoes: Venue, city, country, optional address, an optional pasted Google/Apple Maps link, date, start time, end time, a repeat chip row, an optional stop-repeating date, and a setlist picker for that night. The timezone is captured from the phone.
features.planGate: none; a gig's setlist pick only does anything if you have setlists (Plus)

features.name: A residency is entered once
features.whatItDoes: Repeat options are Just once, Weekly, Every 2 weeks, Monthly and Yearly, with an optional end date. Occurrences are expanded on the server, never in the browser.
features.whyRelevant: 'A weekly residency only needs entering once' is the empty-state copy and it is true.

features.name: Cancel one night without touching the run
features.whatItDoes: ✕ on a gig row cancels that single date; the row stays visible, marked 'cancelled', with a 'Restore' button. 'Hide' then drops it from the artist's list for good while keeping the cancellation on the rule. Edit changes the whole run.

features.name: A Directions button for fans, from an address or a pasted maps link
features.whatItDoes: Either field gives the public page a Directions button that opens in whichever map app the fan's phone uses. A link that is not a real Google or Apple Maps URL is dropped, and the save toast says so rather than showing it broken.

features.name: Gigs publish themselves to your page and the city feed
features.whatItDoes: Every calendar write reindexes the artist's cities, which is what keeps the public country/city feed correct with no job to run. The tab says so in one line under the list.

features.name: Coming up — the next five, then See more
features.whatItDoes: A list of upcoming nights showing day/month badge, venue, address or city, weekday, times, whether it repeats, and which setlist it uses. Five at a time with a 'See 12 more ▾' expander, capped at 30.

features.name: A calendar holds 200 gigs
features.whatItDoes: Beyond 200 events the save is refused with 'That is as many gigs as one calendar can hold'.

features.name: Promote a gig — $10 for a featured spot
features.whatItDoes: Buys one of three spots at the top of a city's listing for one night, first come first served, paid through Stripe Checkout. Only gigs in the future that have a city can be promoted; a gig with no city is refused with an explanation.
features.planGate: none — any plan can buy it
features.flagGate: `featuredShows`, default TRUE (_flags.mjs:38-49). Off = no button, endpoint returns 503, section not rendered — but spots already paid for stay listed and reappear when it is switched back on.
features.whyRelevant: It is live today by default, but it is explicitly an experiment Perry may delete after a month.

features.name: A 'refund owed' row when a double-booked spot could not be refunded
features.whatItDoes: If a night filled up after payment and the automatic refund failed, the Featured list shows the gig with 'refund owed' and tells the artist Perry can see it too.

features.name: Venues you've asked
features.whatItDoes: On the Gigs tab: the venues this artist has pitched and what they said ('Waiting to hear back' / "They're keen — get in touch" / 'Not this time'). With none, it becomes an explainer that venues on MySet see real numbers — nights played, people in the room, votes cast — not just a bio.

features.name: Two printable QR codes
features.whatItDoes: In Settings, 'Codes to print' shows two cards — the artist's own page ('On the tables during your show') and myset.vip ('Find gigs anywhere'). Tapping one opens it full-screen as a white printable card with the caption a stranger needs ('Choose the next song') and the plain URL underneath, plus a 'Full size ↗' link to a much larger SVG.
features.whyRelevant: 'Stick these on tables, on the tip jar, or on your case' — the physical on-ramp to a gig.

features.name: The artist's QR goes to their PAGE, not straight to voting
features.whatItDoes: The code encodes myset.vip/<slug>, from which the room taps through to voting and also gets the music links and the next gigs. A `/vote` code and an invite code still RESOLVE for anything already printed, but neither Studio offers them any more.

features.name: The QR endpoint will only ever encode a MySet URL
features.whatItDoes: The caller picks a kind and the URL is built server-side; the slug must resolve in the artist or venue registry. It is deliberately not a general 'encode this text' service, which would be a free phishing-code generator on MySet's domain.

features.name: The QR encoder is hand-written, no dependency
features.whatItDoes: Byte mode, error-correction level M, versions 1–10, verified module-for-module against segno. Served as SVG with a day of cache.

features.name: Alerts on your phone
features.whatItDoes: Web Push to the artist's phone with the screen off and the Studio closed. Settings renders one of five honest states: keys not set on the server, browser can't do it, couldn't start (with a Retry), iPhone needs installing first (with a How button), blocked in phone settings, or the real on/off row with a device count.
features.flagGate: requires VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY and VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY env vars; without them the panel says 'Not switched on yet' and pushOn returns 503
features.whyRelevant: Real, spec-correct, no App Store — but conditional on server keys being set.

features.name: The only thing that pushes is a request
features.whatItDoes: The sole production notification is a song request or birthday shout-out. Turning alerts on sends one test push ('Alerts are on'). Nothing else — no tip, no payment, no show event — ever notifies, despite the service worker's comment mentioning payments.
features.whyRelevant: Do not write 'get told when money comes in'.

features.name: On iPhone, alerts only work once the Studio is on the home screen
features.whatItDoes: Detected client-side; instead of a button that would fail, the panel offers a 'How' sheet with four Safari steps and the warning that it has to be Safari, not Chrome.

features.name: Up to eight phones per artist
features.whatItDoes: Newest wins past eight subscriptions; a dead endpoint (404/410) is dropped automatically.

features.name: The Studio installs to the home screen
features.whatItDoes: Its own manifest, its own icon and title ('Studio'), black translucent status bar, and a service worker that never caches /api and always prefers the network for pages. Installing is also what unlocks alerts on iPhone.

features.name: The Studio is noindex and cannot be linked as a demo
features.whatItDoes: `<meta name="robots" content="noindex,nofollow">`, and everything past the sign-in gate needs a session.

features.name: There is no stage / big-screen view
features.whatItDoes: public/stage.html is a nine-line meta-refresh that redirects to /studio.html. `netlify/functions/stage.mjs` is not a display — it is the Studio's own private data endpoint (`/api/stage`), named historically.
features.whyRelevant: A copywriter told 'stage view' exists will invent a projector feature MySet does not have.

features.name: The room has a size, and nobody is ever turned away
features.whatItDoes: Each plan carries a room number (free 200, Plus 1,000, Pro 2,000) stamped onto the show when it starts. Going over does not close the door, refuse a vote, or interrupt anybody — the room slows down and the board shortens.
features.whyRelevant: It is on the plan cards already and it is the newest, most easily mis-stated fact in the app.

features.name: Upgrading mid-set does not resize the room underneath you
features.whatItDoes: The room ceiling is read once, when the show starts, and stamped on the show. A show started before caps existed has none and is uncapped. A change of plan applies from the next show.

features.name: The artist is NOT told when the room went over
features.whatItDoes: `/api/show` sends `room.over` to fan phones, but nothing renders it; `stagePayload` does not carry the room cap at all, and neither the Live tab nor the show history ever mentions going over. The _plan.mjs comment saying 'the artist is told afterwards' is not implemented.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/show.mjs:168 vs netlify/functions/stage.mjs:38-64; `over` unused in public/vote.html and public/studio.html
features.whyRelevant: Never write 'we let you know afterwards'.

features.name: The server sets the polling pace from the real head count
features.whatItDoes: Every response tells the phone when to come back: 3s up to 200 people, 5s to 1,000, 10s to 3,000, 20s beyond. One integer, changeable without a deploy, which is the difference between watching a room melt and turning it down mid-song.

features.name: A big room gets the top of the chart, and your own vote always survives
features.whatItDoes: Past 200 people the board carries 40 songs, 25 past 1,000, 15 past 3,000 — but anything this particular fan voted for is appended regardless of position, and the voting page labels it 'Big room tonight — showing the top 40'.

features.name: Locked features are shown greyed, never hidden
features.whatItDoes: One function decides availability and one draws the veil, so a feature can never be greyed in one place and live in another. A plan-locked control gets a tappable 'Plus feature' / 'Pro feature' pill that scrolls you to the plans; an unbuilt one gets a non-tappable 'Coming soon'. The reason sits underneath in plain text.
features.whyRelevant: Perry's own rule, and the Studio genuinely obeys it.

features.name: Four Pro features are shown as 'Coming soon' even to Pro
features.whatItDoes: `promote`, `analytics`, `presskit` and `branding` have no code behind them anywhere in the repo. They appear as preview cards with sample rows — earnings by venue, a press-kit page, your colours on their phones, promotion in other cities — greyed as 'Coming soon' for everyone including the founder, who is comped to Pro and would otherwise walk into four dead ends.
features.planGate: listed under Pro on the plan card as 'Coming soon, included' (studio.html:3549)
features.whyRelevant: Four things the landing page must NOT sell as available. Pro's own card already words it correctly.

features.name: The plans sheet — all three tiers in full
features.whatItDoes: A bottom sheet listing Free ($0), Plus ($10/month) and Pro ($20/month) with every line item, and a CTA per tier that knows what you already have: 'Your plan' disabled, 'Upgrade to Plus' (Checkout) or 'Move to Plus' (subscription change), 'Comped until <date>' for a comped account, or a disabled name for a downgrade you cannot make.
features.whyRelevant: The tier copy here is the canonical, carefully-worded feature list — a better source than any doc.

features.name: The plan card copy is hard-coded in the page, not read from the server
features.whatItDoes: TIER_COPY is a literal in studio.html. The numbers in it (4 shows, 200/1,000/2,000 in the room, 2,000 songs, 50 live, 10%/2%/0%) duplicate _plan.mjs and can drift from it silently.

features.name: The testimonials in the plans sheet are placeholders
features.whatItDoes: Three quotes attributed to 'Sample artist', 'Sample duo' and 'Sample band', each ending '(placeholder)'. The code comment says nothing here is a real quote and they come down until real ones are submitted.
features.whyRelevant: Do not lift these onto a landing page.

features.name: The founder's note under 'Your plan'
features.whatItDoes: A collapsible explanation in Perry's own voice of why there is a limit at all — every phone in the room asking the server 'has the song changed yet?' for the whole show, tens of thousands of questions, credits that add up fast, so a hobbyist plays free forever and the musicians earning from it cover the cost.
features.whyRelevant: This is the honest, already-approved framing for the free tier. Reuse it, do not reinvent it.

features.name: The plan button in the header
features.whatItDoes: Top right: a pink 'Upgrade ↗' button on free, or a soft green chip with the plan name on Plus/Pro. Both open the plans sheet.

features.name: The line under the plan button is never blank
features.whatItDoes: Says 'Free, forever', or 'Pro, on the house until 12 Sep 2027' for a comped account, or 'Renews 27 Sep 2026 · Card, invoices and receipts ↗' — using Stripe's real period end rather than the internal date, which carries three days of grace for a late card.

features.name: Got a code?
features.whatItDoes: A promo box on every account. A 100% code comps the plan outright for N months; anything less is stored as a discount for a future subscription checkout, because there is no billing to halve yet. Redeeming a full comp also gives whoever referred you one free month.

features.name: The 'your card didn't go through' banner
features.whatItDoes: Three escalating states — days of grace left, last day, and 'You're on Free for now' — each insisting nothing has been deleted. It is deliberately hidden during a live show unless you are on Settings, because a card message at 11pm on stage is the wrong pixel at the wrong moment.

features.name: The last-day banner prints 'undefined shows a month'
features.whatItDoes: It reads `PLAN.plans.free.gigsPerMonth` and `PLAN.plans.free.cutPct`, neither of which exists — `shapeLimits` sends `gigs` and `cut`. The guard `PLAN.plans.free ? … : 4` passes, so the fallback never fires and the sentence renders 'What changes is undefined shows a month … MySet's cut goes back to undefined%'.
features.whyRelevant: A real, user-visible defect in the downgrade-warning copy.

features.name: The 'your account is being deleted' bar with one-tap undo
features.whatItDoes: Sits above every tab once deletion is scheduled, names the purge date, insists everything is still here, and offers 'Undo, keep my page' plus an optional 'Free up my page address now'.

features.name: Tonight's gig — venue, city, start time
features.whatItDoes: Three free-text fields saved with one button, separate from the calendar. This is what the voting page shows the room as tonight's header.
features.whyRelevant: It is NOT wired to the calendar — two separate ideas of 'tonight'.

features.name: Free votes per person
features.whatItDoes: Chips for 1/2/3/5/10 plus any custom number 0–999, refreshed every time a new song starts. Changing it resets the current round, because votes already cast were priced against the old number.
features.planGate: Plus (`pricing`) — greyed on free with 'Everyone gets 3 free votes a song until then.'

features.name: ∞ Unlimited votes for everyone — free on every plan
features.whatItDoes: A deliberately ungated chip that lets the whole room vote as much as they like (nobody can buy votes while it is on). The copy says 'Free on every plan — it is your show, not a price.'
features.planGate: NONE, deliberately — it sits outside the pricing lock
features.whyRelevant: A genuinely generous free-tier fact that is easy to miss.

features.name: Cost to replay a played song
features.whatItDoes: Songs already played stay votable but cost more to bring back — chips 2/3/5/8/10 or any number 1–99, default 5.
features.planGate: Plus (`pricing`); on free the standard 5 still applies

features.name: Price your own vote packs
features.whatItDoes: Two editable packs (votes for $), applying to the next purchase.
features.planGate: Plus (`pricing`) — greyed with 'The standard prices stay on, and the money is still yours.'

features.name: Unlimited votes for this device
features.whatItDoes: Lets the artist's own phone vote without limit for testing, without eating the audience's credits, keyed off the same fan id the voting page uses on that phone.

features.name: New show (reset everything) in Settings
features.whatItDoes: A second, more explicit route to the same `newShow` action, confirmed with 'Clears all votes, purchased votes and the played list' — wording that contradicts the Live tab's own carry-paid-votes behaviour.
features.whyRelevant: The confirm text says purchased votes are cleared; the server carries them.

features.name: Fetch lyrics for the whole setlist before a gig
features.whatItDoes: One button pulls the words for every song once and stores them, so a room full of people tapping 'Lyrics' never hits the internet. Reports how many were found and lists the ones that were not.
features.planGate: none — lyrics were briefly paid and were deliberately put back to free (_plan.mjs:12-15)
features.whyRelevant: 'Anything the ROOM experiences stays free' is a stated principle with a code comment behind it.

features.name: Show venues my numbers
features.whatItDoes: On by default. A venue you play at can see how many people were in THEIR room and how many votes got cast, by night and by act. Your money is never included, not even as a total.
features.whyRelevant: 'We got rebooked because the bar could see how many people voted' is the venue-side story, and this switch is it.

features.name: Trying things out — the feature-flag switches
features.whatItDoes: Founder-only card listing every declared flag with what it does and what off means, one tap to flip it globally. Copy: 'Both answers work. Run a gig each way, keep the better one, then delete the loser.'

features.name: The ID review queue
features.whatItDoes: Founder-only card in Settings listing artists waiting on manual verification, with the Stripe name/DOB match result and Approve / No buttons. The ID itself is never shown here and is deleted the moment a decision is made.

features.name: Codes you hand out, and the venue verification list
features.whatItDoes: Founder-only: mint promo codes (100%/50%, Plus/Pro, months, max uses) and revoke them; and verify or un-verify any venue that has claimed a page.

features.name: The first sign-in is free on every plan; the second is Pro
features.whatItDoes: 'Who can sign in' lists the emails that can get into this Studio. The Add box only greys once the plan's seat count is reached — free and Plus have 1, Pro has 5 — so free artists keep the control they actually have.
features.whyRelevant: Plus does NOT add a seat. Only Pro does.

features.name: Roles: owner, member, crew
features.whatItDoes: A `crew` sign-in — the sound engineer running the screen tonight — can run the show and handle requests but not rewrite the library, the calendar, the profile or the shop. An unknown role falls back to crew.
features.whyRelevant: The capability table names 11 actions that do not exist, so several writes are ungated in practice.

features.name: There is no password anywhere
features.whatItDoes: Sign-in is an emailed six-digit code, a passkey (Face ID / fingerprint), a studio code for the day email is slow, or one of eight one-time recovery codes. Settings says this out loud rather than leaving somebody hunting for a 'forgot password' link.

features.name: If something looks wrong — the two hammers
features.whatItDoes: Reload the Studio, and 'Clear what's stored on this phone' (throws away the offline copy, keeps you signed in). Both exist because an installed PWA has no address bar and no reload button, and pull-to-refresh is JavaScript that cannot rescue broken JavaScript.

features.name: Bar wifi cannot throw you out mid-gig
features.whatItDoes: A network failure is distinguished from a server refusal: a transport error keeps the last good screen and lets the 4-second interval retry, instead of clearing the token and dumping the artist back at the sign-in gate mid-show.
features.whyRelevant: A real, specific reliability claim for the exact venue MySet is built for.

features.name: Every write hands back the new screen
features.whatItDoes: Actions that change the show return the full fresh Studio payload with the response, so a tap repaints without a second round trip, and a second tap is never a second action (`WRITING` guard).

trapsForCopy: THERE IS NO STAGE VIEW. public/stage.html is a nine-line meta-refresh to /studio.html (public/stage.html:1-9) and stage.mjs is the Studio's own private data endpoint, not a big screen. Never write about projecting the queue, a stage display, or a screen the room watches.

The Live tab's third stat tile says 'Tips' and shows the artist's ALL-TIME tip total, not tonight's. `meta.tips` is appended to forever and never reset or trimmed (netlify/functions/stage.mjs:36, 80; netlify/functions/_pay.mjs:91). 'Recent tips' is likewise the last 15 ever. Do not write 'see tonight's tips as they land'.
The Studio only refreshes itself on the Live tab (public/studio.html:4246). Gigs, Money, Profile, Merch and Settings do not update until you pull down. 'Your whole Studio, live' is false.

The free tier's limit is 4 SHOWS PER UTC CALENDAR MONTH, not per week and not a feature limit (netlify/functions/_plan.mjs:33; _lib.mjs:131). It was briefly two a week on 2026-09-03 and was changed straight back. Free artists get the whole Studio — the lyrics sheet, the calendar, the community page, hiding posts, show history, 2,000 stored songs. What free costs is a 10% cut and 50 songs live to the room at once.

The plan numbers are 200 / 1,000 / 2,000 people in the room (free / Plus / Pro), and they are SOFT (netlify/functions/_plan.mjs:63, 88, 106; show.mjs:32-44). Nobody is locked out, no vote is refused; the room polls more slowly and the board shortens. Pro was deliberately brought DOWN from 3,000 to 2,000 on 2026-09-05 because the arithmetic behind 3,000 was wrong — do not quote 3,000 from any older doc.

The code comment claims the artist is told after a night went over the room size. That is NOT implemented — `room.over` is sent to fan phones and rendered nowhere, and the Studio payload does not carry the cap at all. Never promise an over-capacity notice.

Four Pro features have no code behind them anywhere: promote, analytics, presskit, branding (netlify/functions/_plan.mjs:130). They are shown in the Studio as 'Coming soon' even to Pro and even to the founder. Pro's own plan card words it correctly as 'Coming soon, included'. Do not sell earnings-by-venue, a press kit, custom branding or cross-city promotion as things Pro gets today.

'Promote a gig' ($10 for one of three featured spots in a city, per night) IS live today, but it is behind the `featuredShows` feature flag with a default of ON and an explicit removal plan: after a month, if nobody buys, the flag AND the feature get deleted (netlify/functions/_flags.mjs:38-49). Treat it as an experiment, not a pillar.

Requests and birthday shout-outs are OFF until the artist switches each one on (netlify/functions/_requests.mjs:12-15), and the switches are in Settings while the results appear on the Live tab. Switching them ON is free on every plan; only setting what they COST is a Plus feature. Do not say 'requests are built in and on'.
Requests cost VOTES, never money (netlify/functions/_requests.mjs:15). A fan can have only one open song request and one open birthday at a time, and a show caps at 30 pending.

Shows that start and end themselves have no plan gate in the code — the schedule runs for everybody (netlify/functions/_auto.mjs) — but the plan cards list 'Shows that start and end themselves' only under Plus and Pro (public/studio.html:3532, 3548). The cards and the code disagree; a free artist gets it today. Ask before writing either version.

A self-starting show can be up to two minutes late (the cron interval, netlify/functions/autocron.mjs:95), and the Studio never shows a countdown — `stagePayload` computes tonight's scheduled start and the page never reads it (netlify/functions/stage.mjs:21-30). Do not write 'the Studio tells you when it will start'.

Auto-start can be switched off, but auto-END still applies to any live show. The Settings copy says exactly that (public/studio.html:2468) and the code enforces it (netlify/functions/_auto.mjs:133 gates only the start).

The only push notification that ever fires in production is a song request or birthday shout-out, plus one test push when you turn alerts on (netlify/functions/_requests.mjs:128; admin.mjs:1646). No tip, payment, or show event notifies — despite the service worker comment mentioning payments. Push also needs VAPID keys set on the server, and on iPhone needs the Studio installed to the home screen first.

Two QR codes are offered, not three: the artist's own page and myset.vip. The artist's code goes to their PAGE, not straight to voting — the room taps through from there (public/studio.html:2989-2993). Old /vote and invite codes still resolve for anything already printed but are no longer offered.
The QR panel is under Settings, and the printable card is a screenshot-or-print flow, not a download — there is no poster generator, no PDF, no template. 'Posters' would be an invention.
'Unlimited votes for everyone' is deliberately NOT gated to a paid plan (public/studio.html:2252-2255) — 'it is your show, not a price'. It is a real free-tier feature and easy to miss.
Plus does not add a second sign-in. Seats are 1 on free AND Plus, 5 only on Pro (netlify/functions/_plan.mjs:65, 89, 107).

The tips/vote-pack transaction fee ladder is 10% free / 2% Plus / 0% Pro (netlify/functions/_plan.mjs:33-97). Stripe's own fee is separate and the Studio says so on the payments card — do not present 2% as the total cost of taking money.

'Merch' is a visible tab on every plan but the whole list is under a Plus lock (public/studio.html:3273). The tab row never changes with plan (public/studio.html:2539-2547), so a screenshot of the Studio shows seven tabs regardless of what the artist is paying.
Named setlists are a Plus feature to CREATE; setlists an artist already has keep working on free, and the lock copy says so (public/studio.html:616-618).

A show started before room caps existed is uncapped, and the ceiling is stamped once at start — upgrading mid-set does not resize the room underneath the people standing in it (netlify/functions/_lifecycle.mjs:45-57).

The last-day downgrade banner has a live bug: it prints 'undefined shows a month' and 'MySet's cut goes back to undefined%' because it reads fields the plan payload does not send (public/studio.html:3705 vs admin.mjs:393-406). Do not screenshot that state.
The three testimonials inside the plans sheet are placeholders that literally say '(placeholder)' (public/studio.html:3553-3560). Nothing there is a real quote.

The Studio is dark-only by design and is `noindex,nofollow` behind a sign-in gate (public/studio.html:16, 26-32). It cannot be linked as a public demo, and there are no light-mode screenshots to be had.

Roles are only partly enforced: 11 of the action names in the capability table do not exist as actions, so a `crew` sign-in can still change chord charts, lyrics, the profile, photos and setlists (netlify/functions/admin.mjs:414-424 vs the real dispatch). Do not claim granular band-member permissions.

The founder's plan is a special case: `planForArtist` reports him as free, so the Live tab's own gig-cap warning renders for him (public/studio.html:1896-1909 reads `PLAN.limits.gigs` and never checks `PLAN.owner`) even though the server never caps him (netlify/functions/_lifecycle.mjs:42). Any screenshot from Perry's Studio may show a limit that does not apply to him.

The Settings 'New show (reset everything)' confirm says it clears purchased votes; the server deliberately carries unspent paid votes across (public/studio.html:2474 vs _lifecycle.mjs:168-169). Believe the server.

appCatalogue.surface: The public artist page (/:slug) and the city what's-on home (/)
appCatalogue.summary: This is MySet's entire public, logged-out shopfront: the artist's own page at myset.vip/:slug and the city what's-on feed at myset.vip/. The artist page is a single client-rendered file that makes exactly two API calls (/api/profile and /api/events?a=…&days=90) and draws a cover photo, a portrait cluster, name + optional verified tick, one big pink CTA that either says "Join live" or a countdown to the next gig, a row of up to five stat tiles plus a Community button, a next-gig card with Directions, a bio, an upcoming-shows list, five kinds of listen/follow link, and click-to-load YouTube/Spotify/Apple Music embeds. The home page is a country→city picker over one global `cityindex` document, which returns the next seven days of gigs in that city grouped by night — artist gigs and venue-run events side by side, with up to three $10 paid "Featured shows" at the top of each night. Everything on both pages is free to view, needs no account, and works installed to a phone's home screen as a PWA. The only plan gate anywhere on this surface is the verified tick.
appCatalogue.structure:
TWO ENTRY POINTS, connected one way. myset.vip/ (public/index.html) opens on a hero, then a two-field finder: "Choose your country" → "Choose your city" → Search. Both fields are custom comboboxes that show a live gig count beside every option (index.html:256-271, 315-325). Picking a pair fetches /api/events?country=&city= and renders the next seven days grouped by night: a day heading (Tonight / Tomorrow / weekday + date + count), an optional orange "Featured shows" block, then the ordinary list (index.html:480-490). Each row is fully tappable and navigates to /:slug for an artist gig or /v/:slug for a venue-run event (index.html:465-467). Above the results sits a client-side search box that filters the already-fetched week by act, venue, address, note, weekday or time (index.html:426-457). Below sit a dismissible "add to home screen" card and a footer with "How MySet works" → /about. Choices are remembered in localStorage and re-searched automatically on the next visit (index.html:328-337). There is NO way to search for an artist by name globally — the only path to an artist page from the home page is through a city that has one of their gigs in the next seven days.

The artist page (netlify.toml catch-all /:slug → public/artist.html) reads its slug from location.pathname client-side (artist.html:261-262) and resolves it server-side via publicArtist (_lib.mjs:1016). Order down the page: black splash → brandbar (MySet logo → "/", hamburger with two doors) → cover photo with optional "Live now — vote the setlist" pill → portrait cluster + name + tick + tagline → the big CTA → stat grid (3 across, wrapping to 3+2, with the Community button as the sixth cell) → next-gig card with Directions → About → Upcoming shows (3 rows + "See N more") → Listen & follow chips → Watch & listen embeds → footer. Sections vanish entirely when empty; a stat tile whose value is zero is dropped from the grid (artist.html:413). From here a visitor can go to /:slug/vote, /:slug/community, /studio, /venues, or out to Spotify/Apple/YouTube/Instagram/website/ticket links/map apps.
appCatalogue.design:
Dark-first iOS-app aesthetic on a shared /app.css token set. The signature colour is a pink-red gradient (#FF375F → #FF6B45) used for the logo mark, the Live pill, the primary CTA and the next-gig date chip. Orange (--accent-2) is deliberately reserved for the audience and for paid Featured listings — the code says explicitly that a paid listing must not wear the pink, which is for warnings and destructive things (index.html:114-116). Green appears exactly once in the whole product: the verified tick chip, with a separate dark-mode colour because #1B8E3C failed contrast on black (artist.html:88-94).

Both pages open on a splash: a black ground with three animated bars and the wordmark. The artist page paints #0D0B0C from an inline <style> before app.css even loads, because a phone opening a new tab was flashing white (artist.html:29-37); its splash is dismissed by the fetch completing, not a timer. The home page's splash is once per session and removed entirely under prefers-reduced-motion.

The artist page's hero is Instagram-shaped: a 16:10 cover, a 112px rounded portrait pulled up over it by -46px, and up to three 40px thumbnails stacked in a column to its LEFT, with the top one nudged 20px right so the column reads as an arc rather than a stack (artist.html:59-82). The name sits below the cover, big and tight-tracked. Photos go through Netlify's Image CDN as WebP/AVIF with an onerror fallback to the original (artist.html:284).

Motion is restrained and everywhere reduced-motion-aware: a pulsing dot on the Live button, spring-eased :active scale on every tappable pill, a bottom sheet that springs up for the install instructions. The whole thing is mobile-first — max-width constrained, safe-area insets, 44px minimum touch targets in the footer nav, tabular-nums on the countdown so it does not jitter.

features.name: Your own address — myset.vip/yourname
features.whatItDoes: Any path that is not a real file renders the artist page; the slug is read from the URL in the browser and resolved on the server against the artist registry.
features.whyRelevant: The single most concrete thing an artist gets. It is a real vanity URL, not a query string.

features.name: Rename your page and the old link still works
features.whatItDoes: When an artist renames their page the old slug is kept pointing at them and cannot be claimed by anyone else, so QR codes on bar tables and Instagram bios keep resolving.
features.whyRelevant: A genuine 'we thought about your printed QR codes' detail, and the code comment says a rename used to break a room mid-gig.

features.name: Delete your account and the page goes dark that day
features.whatItDoes: An account marked for deletion makes publicArtist return null, so the artist page, the vote page, the community page and every public endpoint 404 immediately — thirty days before the data is actually erased.
features.whyRelevant: Privacy/trust proof point: leaving is instant in public even though it is undoable for 30 days.

features.name: "No page here" for an unknown address
features.whatItDoes: Because every unknown path renders artist.html, an unresolvable slug shows a dedicated empty state naming the address tried, with a "Find gigs near you" button back to the home feed. Title becomes "Not found — MySet".
features.whyRelevant: Polish, not a claim.

features.name: The page loads on two requests, not three
features.whatItDoes: /api/profile now carries live/venue/city, so the artist page no longer runs a full 15-read audience poll just to draw the Live pill.
features.whyRelevant: Cost engineering, invisible to users — but it is the change that broke the countdown and the on-stage card (see traps).

features.name: Cover photo
features.whatItDoes: A 16:10 cover image with a gradient veil, served through Netlify's Image CDN as WebP/AVIF at 1200w with an onerror fallback to the original file.
features.whyRelevant: Part of "your page looks like a real artist page".

features.name: Portrait plus up to three more photos
features.whatItDoes: An XL rounded portrait overlapping the cover, with up to three small photos arranged in an arc to its left. Falls back to a solo, slightly larger portrait when there are no extras.
features.whyRelevant: Four photos total, not a gallery. Do not say "photo gallery".

features.name: Clearing photo 1 does not slide photo 2 into its place
features.whatItDoes: The photos array is positional and only trailing blanks are trimmed, so an artist editing slot 2 does not reshuffle the arc.
features.whyRelevant: Bug-fix detail.

features.name: "Live now — vote the setlist" pill on the cover
features.whatItDoes: A pink pill appears on the cover photo, linking straight to the vote page, whenever the artist's SHOW record has status 'live'.
features.whyRelevant: This is the moment the whole product exists for — a stranger lands on the page mid-gig and can join in one tap.

features.name: The big button: "Join live" or a countdown
features.whatItDoes: One full-width primary button. Filled pink with a pulsing dot and the words "Join live" when the show is live; otherwise an outlined button showing a countdown to the next gig.
features.whyRelevant: The page's single call to action.

features.name: Countdown to the next gig
features.whatItDoes: Computes the time to the next calendar occurrence and renders "Live in 3d 4h 12m", "Live in 4h 12m 07s", "Live in 12m 07s", or "Starting now". With no upcoming gig at all it falls back to the words "See the setlist".
features.whyRelevant: Accurate at page load, but it does NOT count down live — see the traps. about.html's own image alt text currently claims "a live countdown".

features.name: The per-second countdown timer (dead code)
features.whatItDoes: startTick() sets a 1-second interval to re-render the button label, but it returns immediately because its guard tests `S`, the show-poll object that was removed on 2026-09-04 and is now hardcoded to null.
features.whereInCode: public/artist.html:331-341 (guard at 334), 352 and 361 where S is set to null; guard written in 5cac6bd 2026-08-31, S nulled in 67f1d36 2026-09-04
features.whyRelevant: A copywriter reading the code would think there is a ticking clock. There is not.

features.name: Stat tile — Joined
features.whatItDoes: Shows the month and year the artist account was created, e.g. "Sep 2026".
features.whereInCode: public/artist.html:307-308, 410; number from netlify/functions/profile.mjs:33 (who.createdAt) via netlify/functions/_auth.mjs:134
features.whyRelevant: One of exactly five stat tiles. Disappears if the registry has no createdAt for them (e.g. the founding account, which predates the registry).

features.name: Stat tile — Shows
features.whatItDoes: The number of archived shows in the artist's history index. Nights where nothing happened are refused by the archiver, so an empty night never counts as a show.
features.whyRelevant: This is the number the whole "arrive with real numbers attached" pitch rests on. It counts nights MySet was actually used, not gigs on the calendar.

features.name: Stat tile — Fans
features.whatItDoes: The sum, across every archived show, of how many phones were in the room that night. A phone counts if it stamped itself on the voting page or clearly took part (voted, bought votes, or spent).
features.whereInCode: public/artist.html:411; netlify/functions/profile.mjs:20 (sum of x.room ?? x.peakVoters ?? 0); netlify/functions/_lib.mjs:747-761 roomCounts
features.whyRelevant: The most quotable number and the easiest to describe wrongly — it is a running total of attendances, not unique people. See traps.

features.name: Stat tile — Votes cast
features.whatItDoes: The sum of totalVotes across every archived show — every vote in every round, not just the winning song's.
features.whyRelevant: The proof-of-engagement number.

features.name: Stat tile — Songs
features.whatItDoes: How many songs in the artist's library are switched on right now (active !== false) — the live count, not everything they have ever stored.
features.whyRelevant: On the free plan a maximum of 50 songs can be live at once (_plan.mjs:20), so this tile is capped at 50 for free artists even if they store 2,000.

features.name: Empty stat tiles disappear rather than showing zero
features.whatItDoes: The stat row filters out any tile whose formatted value is falsy, and compact() returns an empty string for 0 — so a brand-new artist sees only Joined, maybe Songs, and the Community button.
features.whyRelevant: A page never says "0 Shows". Marketing screenshots of a new page will look sparse, not embarrassing.

features.name: Big numbers shorten to 1.4k / 2m
features.whatItDoes: Under 1,000 shows the integer; 1,000–9,999 shows one decimal k; up to a million shows rounded k; above that shows m.
features.whyRelevant: Cosmetic.

features.name: Community button in the stat grid
features.whatItDoes: A sixth cell in the stats grid, outlined in pink with a speech-bubble icon, linking to /:slug/community. Always shown, on every plan, whether or not the community page has anything on it.
features.whyRelevant: The only outbound link from the artist page to another MySet surface besides voting.

features.name: The verified tick
features.whatItDoes: A green "✓ Verified" chip under the artist's name, titled "MySet checked this is really them". Shown only when the registry flag is set AND the account is on a paid plan right now — a lapsed or comped-then-expired plan drops the tick on the next page load.
features.whereInCode: public/artist.html:88-94, 399; the belt-and-braces check at netlify/functions/profile.mjs:22-27 (`verified && planOf(who) !== 'free'`)
features.planGate: plus / pro — planOf(who) !== 'free' (netlify/functions/profile.mjs:27); the verification checklist itself also requires paidPlan (netlify/functions/_verify.mjs:352)
features.whyRelevant: The one and only plan-gated thing on this entire public surface.

features.name: How an artist actually gets the tick
features.whatItDoes: Four things must be true: a paid plan, Stripe Connect card payments working, a photo of an ID on file with the LEGAL name and date of birth typed in, and either Stripe's own identity check matching both strongly (automatic) or Perry looking at it by hand. The legal name is used rather than the stage name because most working artists trade under one.
features.whyRelevant: "Paying opens the door to being checked; it does not buy the tick" is the exact framing in the code (_verify.mjs:185-188).

features.name: The ID photo is never public and is deleted the moment a decision is made
features.whatItDoes: The ID is written to an image slot that img.mjs deliberately refuses to serve, and is deleted on approval or rejection. Only the decision survives. The date of birth is compared and discarded — only a boolean is kept.
features.whyRelevant: A real privacy commitment, enforced in code, that most products would only claim in a policy.

features.name: The next-gig card
features.whatItDoes: A raised card showing the gig's start time in a pink gradient chip, the word Tonight / Tomorrow / the weekday, the venue name, and the address (or city, country), with a full-width Directions button underneath when there is somewhere to point at.
features.whyRelevant: Explicitly driven by the calendar rather than the old show.showTime placeholder, which said 8:00 PM while the gig was at 8:30 (comment at artist.html:417-418).

features.name: The "Now / On stage" variant of the gig card (unreachable)
features.whatItDoes: A branch that would show a card reading "Now — On stage" with the venue and city while a show is live. It requires `S`, the show-poll object that was removed, so it can never render.
features.whyRelevant: A live artist gets the ordinary calendar card, not a special on-stage one.

features.name: Directions that open the right map app
features.whatItDoes: The server builds both an Apple Maps and a Google Maps link for every gig; the page picks Apple for iPhone/iPad/Mac and Google for everything else. Coordinates are used when they can be parsed out of a pasted map link, otherwise it searches on venue name + address + city + country.
features.whyRelevant: The code's own reasoning is quotable: there is no single link that opens in whichever map app a phone uses, so it builds both.

features.name: No Directions button when there is nowhere to send you
features.whatItDoes: mapLinks returns null unless there are coordinates, or an address, or a venue name WITH a city — because 'The Ugly Duckling' alone could send somebody to Amsterdam.
features.whyRelevant: Restraint, not a feature.

features.name: About / bio
features.whatItDoes: A free-text bio card, up to 700 characters, with line breaks preserved. The section header and card only exist if there is a bio.
features.whereInCode: public/artist.html:156, 437; cap and newline handling netlify/functions/_profile.mjs:91
features.whyRelevant: 700 characters is short — roughly a paragraph. Do not promise a long biography.

features.name: Upcoming shows list
features.whatItDoes: Up to 24 upcoming gigs; the first three are shown and the rest sit behind a "See N more ▾" button that toggles to "Show fewer ▴". The server looks 90 days ahead and returns at most 60.
features.whyRelevant: "Every gig you've got coming" is the claim; the real numbers are 90 days / 60 from the server / 24 on the page / 3 visible.

features.name: What one gig row shows
features.whatItDoes: Day number and month in a left column, an optional "On now" pill, the venue name, then weekday · start time–end time · city, then the street address, then a round Directions button and a "Tickets ↗" link when the artist added one.
features.whyRelevant: Six distinct facts per row, each of which only appears if it exists.

features.name: "On now" badge and highlight on a gig happening right now
features.whatItDoes: A gig whose window contains the current instant gets a pink "On now" pill and a tinted row background. This is derived purely from the calendar times, independent of whether the artist actually started a show.
features.whereInCode: public/artist.html:189, 444; the live flag at netlify/functions/events.mjs:160
features.whyRelevant: This is a DIFFERENT 'live' from the Live now pill. See traps.

features.name: A residency is one entry, not fifty-two
features.whatItDoes: Gigs are stored as rules and expanded on read: weekly, every two weeks, monthly or yearly, with an optional end date, individual skipped dates, and cancelled-and-dismissed dates. Monthly recurrence is always measured from the original date so 'the 31st' cannot clamp to the 28th and walk backwards through the year.
features.whyRelevant: A genuinely good feature for working musicians and the code's own framing is excellent: "a residency with no end date needs no maintenance, and there is no job to run."

features.name: Set end times, and sets that run past midnight
features.whatItDoes: The artist types the time they finish, which the server turns into a length. An end time earlier than the start means the set runs past midnight — treated as the normal case, not an error. A 10pm set running to 2am is still shown as on at 1am.
features.whyRelevant: Very specific to live music and a real differentiator against a generic events tool.

features.name: Gig times are wall-clock in the gig's own timezone
features.whatItDoes: A gig stores a date, a time and an IANA timezone, and the server converts to UTC iteratively so DST boundaries settle correctly.
features.whyRelevant: Correctness plumbing.

features.name: Listen & follow chips
features.whatItDoes: Up to five link chips in a fixed order with brand-coloured icons: Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube Music, Instagram, Website. Each only appears if filled in.
features.whyRelevant: Five, fixed, no custom links. Do not describe it as a link-in-bio tool with arbitrary links.

features.name: Music links are checked against an exact host allowlist
features.whatItDoes: A Spotify link must be on open.spotify.com, Apple Music on music.apple.com or geo.music.apple.com, YouTube Music on music.youtube.com, Instagram on instagram.com. Website accepts any https host. Anything else is stored as empty.
features.whyRelevant: Security, and a source of "I pasted my link and it vanished" support questions.

features.name: Tracking junk is stripped off pasted links
features.whatItDoes: si, utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign, app and uo are removed from every link, and the fragment is dropped.
features.whyRelevant: A small, honest privacy detail nobody would expect.

features.name: Watch & listen — embedded players
features.whatItDoes: Up to 24 embedded YouTube videos, Spotify tracks/albums/playlists/podcasts, or Apple Music albums/songs/playlists, each shown as a poster image with a play button until tapped.
features.whereInCode: public/artist.html:165-184, 466-490; parsers at netlify/functions/_embeds.mjs:11-93; 24 cap at netlify/functions/_profile.mjs:114
features.whyRelevant: This is what makes the page feel like a real artist site rather than a listing.

features.name: Nothing from YouTube, Spotify or Apple loads until you tap it
features.whatItDoes: Each embed is a static facade; the iframe is created with createElement (never innerHTML) only on tap, and its src is built from a literal template on the server rather than from anything the artist typed.
features.whyRelevant: Speed AND privacy: no third-party request happens on page load at all.

features.name: YouTube Shorts render vertical, and playlists and start times work
features.whatItDoes: A Shorts URL gets a 9:16 box capped at 70vh; ordinary videos get 16:9; playlists and ?t= start offsets are parsed and rebuilt.
features.whyRelevant: Shorts are how most musicians actually post clips.

features.name: Apple Music plays full tracks for subscribers
features.whatItDoes: The iframe carries allow-storage-access-by-user-activation, without which a signed-in Apple Music subscriber is silently stuck on 30-second previews.
features.whyRelevant: Invisible when it works.

features.name: Honest note about 30-second previews
features.whatItDoes: When any Spotify or Apple Music embed is on the page, a line of fine print says these play a short preview unless you are already signed in on this device, and points at the "Open ↗" link.
features.whyRelevant: A small piece of proactive honesty that suits Perry's voice.

features.name: Top-right menu — two doors
features.whatItDoes: A native <details> menu with exactly two items: Artist Studio and Venue Studio. The wording changes to "Open your Studio" if a token for that kind of account exists in this browser, otherwise "Set one up — it's free". Whether somebody has a Studio is never asked of the server from a public page.
features.whyRelevant: The privacy rule behind it (INVARIANT 9h) is quotable but the menu itself is not a selling point.

features.name: Pull down to refresh, even installed
features.whatItDoes: One shared pull-to-refresh implementation used by every page, because an installed home-screen app has no address bar, no reload button and no swipe-down gesture.
features.whyRelevant: The problem statement in pull.js is in Perry's own words and is a good story.

features.name: Installs to a phone's home screen
features.whatItDoes: Manifest, apple-touch-icon, theme colours for light and dark, standalone display, and a service worker registered late and non-blocking that is network-first for pages and never caches /api.
features.whyRelevant: Real, and the home page actively sells it (see the A2HS card).

features.name: Provenance stamp on public API payloads
features.whatItDoes: /api/events responses carry src: 'ms-k3f9qz', an arbitrary constant with no function, so a competitor proxying MySet's API can be proved to have done so.
features.whyRelevant: Never put this on a marketing page. Note /api/profile does NOT carry it.

features.name: The home page hero
features.whatItDoes: "Live music near you. You pick what plays." with the sub-line "Find a gig, open the link at the venue, and vote on the next song from your phone."
features.whyRelevant: This is the existing public positioning line, already live.

features.name: Country → city finder with live gig counts
features.whatItDoes: Two comboboxes. Type to narrow or tap to browse the whole list; every option carries how many gigs are on there in the next seven days. Arrow keys, Enter, Escape and a clear button all work. City is disabled until a country is chosen.
features.whyRelevant: This IS the home page. But see the trap about the 40-owner cap on the counts.

features.name: It remembers where you were last time
features.whatItDoes: The last country and city are kept in localStorage and, on the next visit, refilled and searched automatically so the feed is already on screen.
features.whyRelevant: Makes the installed app feel like a local listings app.

features.name: The week ahead in one city
features.whatItDoes: Gigs for the next seven days, grouped by night, each group headed Tonight / Tomorrow / the weekday plus the date and a count.
features.whyRelevant: Seven days, hard-coded. Not "this month" and not "all upcoming".

features.name: What one feed row shows
features.whatItDoes: Start time and short date on the left; then an "On now" pill or an "At the venue" tag, the act's name or the event title, the venue, the street address, and the artist's note; then a round Directions button and a chevron. The whole row is a link.
features.whyRelevant: The address and note lines only appear when present.

features.name: Venue-run events sit beside artist gigs
features.whatItDoes: A venue's own listings — a quiz night, a DJ, the football — come out of the same recurrence engine and into the same feed, tagged "At the venue", headlined by their title instead of an act name, and linking to /v/:slug.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/events.mjs:63-85; public/index.html:136-138, 464-472; venue owners keyed v_<venueId> at netlify/functions/_events.mjs:163-164 and netlify/functions/venueadmin.mjs:17
features.whyRelevant: This turns the page from an artist directory into a genuine what's-on feed for a town.

features.name: Featured shows — three paid spots per night per city
features.whatItDoes: Up to three gigs per city per night can sit above the ordinary list, inside an orange border, under a "Featured shows" heading. A featured gig is MOVED out of the ordinary list rather than copied, so nobody appears twice, and the heading never draws an empty slot.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/events.mjs:99-136; public/index.html:114-127, 482-486; the machinery at netlify/functions/_featured.mjs:1-361
features.planGate: none — any artist on any plan can buy one; handleFeature checks only the flag and Stripe (netlify/functions/admin.mjs:1404-1470)
features.flagGate: featuredShows, default TRUE (netlify/functions/_flags.mjs:38-49); read globally with no per-artist override (netlify/functions/events.mjs:106-114, admin.mjs:1406-1410)
features.whyRelevant: MySet's second revenue line after subscriptions, live since 2026-09-05 and completely absent from the landing page.

features.name: $10 a night, first come first served
features.whatItDoes: One spot costs $10. Three spots per city per date. The slot is held for twenty minutes before checkout opens and frees itself if the payment never lands, so nobody is ever charged for a spot they did not get.
features.whyRelevant: Perry's own number, quoted verbatim in the file header.

features.name: If the spot is gone, the money goes back automatically
features.whatItDoes: If the hold expired and the night filled while the payment was in flight, or an artist paid twice for the same night from separate tabs, the payment is refunded automatically with an idempotency key. If the refund itself fails it is written into the artist's own Featured list as an owed refund so it is visible to them and findable.
features.whyRelevant: "Telling somebody to email for a refund would be worse than the bug" is exactly Perry's voice and it is real code.

features.name: Cancel the gig and the spot is spent
features.whatItDoes: A featured row renders only when the occurrence still exists in the calendar, so deleting the gig makes the paid spot silently stop appearing. The Promote sheet warns about this before anybody pays.
features.whyRelevant: Do not promise a refund on cancellation.

features.name: A featured spot can't be stolen with a copied gig id
features.whatItDoes: The feed matches a paid spot to a gig on the OWNER as well as the event id, because event ids are chosen by the client and every gig's id is public in the feed — matching on the id alone let any artist in the city render themselves in a spot somebody else had paid $10 for.
features.whyRelevant: Found by an adversarial review, not a user. Security proof point, not marketing.

features.name: Search inside the week
features.whatItDoes: A search box above the results filters the already-fetched week on the phone — matching act or event title, venue, address, note, day label, weekday name ("tuesday"), date, or a time in either form ("8pm" or "20:30"). No extra request is made.
features.whyRelevant: It searches the seven days already on screen, not a database. It cannot find an artist who has no gig in this city this week.

features.name: Two honest empty states
features.whatItDoes: With nothing anywhere: "No gigs listed yet — MySet is brand new. If you play live, or you run a bar that does, yours can be the first ones here." With a chosen city but no gigs: "Nothing on in <city> this week" plus, when applicable, "N artists play here — nothing in the next seven days." Both offer three doors: add my gigs, add my bar, or see how MySet works.
features.whyRelevant: The empty states admit the product is new rather than faking a busy feed. Given INVARIANT 0j (never invent gig data), this is load-bearing honesty.

features.name: A city with nothing on stays in the list, with its zero
features.whatItDoes: The picker never sends someone to an empty city blind — the city is still listed, with the count, so the emptiness is visible before they commit.
features.whyRelevant: Small honesty detail.

features.name: The city index — how an artist gets into a town's feed
features.whatItDoes: One global document maps country → city → the artists and venues with gigs there, rewritten every time anybody's calendar changes. A gig must have BOTH a country and a city to count. A one-off keeps the artist in that city until seven days after it happened; a repeating gig keeps them there indefinitely.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/_events.mjs:155-203 (the 7-day rule at 182-185); rewritten from netlify/functions/admin.mjs:489, 496, 517 and netlify/functions/venueadmin.mjs:136, 146, 233
features.whyRelevant: "Add a gig and you're in your town's feed" is true — but only if the gig has a city on it.

features.name: "Saved MySet to your home screen yet?"
features.whatItDoes: A card under the finder — never over the content — offering to install. On Android it fires Chrome's real install prompt when the browser offers one; on iPhone it opens a sheet with steps. Dismissed once, gone forever; the footer button stays as the way back.
features.whyRelevant: "A bar that covers what somebody came for is an advert, not a help" (index.html:180-181) is a good design-values line.

features.name: Install instructions with iPhone / Android tabs
features.whatItDoes: A bottom sheet with a four-step walkthrough per platform, defaulting to iPhone unless the user agent says Android, plus the note that it has to be Safari on iOS because Chrome on iOS cannot add to the home screen.
features.whyRelevant: Support content.

features.name: Footer: How MySet works, and Add to home screen
features.whatItDoes: Two things reachable from anywhere on the home page. The install button hides itself once the app is installed.
features.whyRelevant: The only inbound link from the home page to /about.

features.name: "For artists" and "For venues" in the home header
features.whatItDoes: Two outlined pills top right of the home page, going to /studio and /venues.
features.whyRelevant: Unlike the artist page's menu these do not change wording for signed-in people.

features.name: /signup and /studio are the same page
features.whatItDoes: Both redirect to studio.html; the artist page's menu switches its href between them purely cosmetically, and the Venue Studio link always points at /venues regardless of whether a venue token exists.
features.whyRelevant: Do not describe /signup as a separate signup flow.

features.name: The Pro plan's "promote" flag (not built)
features.whatItDoes: PLANS lists `promote: true` on Pro, described as "list gigs in cities you don't normally play". There is no code behind it anywhere in the repo; it is in NOT_BUILT and the Studio shows it as "coming", never as "yours".
features.whyRelevant: This is NOT the $10 Featured Shows feature. Two different things with the same word. See traps.

features.name: merch count and showId in the profile payload (unused here)
features.whatItDoes: /api/profile returns how many merch items are switched on and the current showId; the artist page reads neither. They exist for the community page.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/profile.mjs:39-40; no reference to merch or showId anywhere in public/artist.html
features.whyRelevant: Nothing on the artist page sells anything.

features.name: The page falls back to the registered name
features.whatItDoes: If the profile record has no name, the name from the artist registry is used instead, so the page never renders a nameless heading.
features.whyRelevant: Robustness detail.

features.name: There is no follower count, because there is no follow
features.whatItDoes: The profile handler states plainly that only real numbers are shown and there is no follower count because there is no follow feature.
features.whyRelevant: Do not write copy about followers, fans following, or a fanbase you can message. None of that exists on this surface.

trapsForCopy: THERE ARE TWO DIFFERENT KINDS OF 'LIVE' ON THE ARTIST PAGE AND THEY DISAGREE. The pink "Live now — vote the setlist" pill on the cover comes from the artist's SHOW record (show.status === 'live', profile.mjs:38) — the artist has to have started a show in the Studio, or had one auto-start. The "On now" badge in the Upcoming shows list comes purely from the CALENDAR (events.mjs:160 — now is between startsAt and endsAt). So a page can say "On now" on a gig row while showing no Live pill and no Join live button, and vice versa. Never write copy that treats them as one state.

THE COUNTDOWN DOES NOT COUNT DOWN.
