The label is correct when the page loads and then freezes until the page is reloaded — startTick() bails out on line 334 of artist.html because it tests `S`, an object that was removed from boot() on 2026-09-04 (commit 67f1d36) and is now hardcoded null. about.html's own image alt text already says "a live countdown to the next gig", which overstates it. Safe phrasing: "shows how long until the next gig". Unsafe: "a live ticking countdown".

'FANS' IS NOT UNIQUE PEOPLE. It is the sum, across every archived show, of how many phones were in the room that night (profile.mjs:20). The same regular at ten gigs counts ten times. It also counts a phone that merely opened the voting page and stamped presence, not just people who voted (_lib.mjs:752-755). Honest phrasings: "people in the room, added up across every night", "total attendance". Dishonest: "your fanbase", "unique fans", "people who follow you". There is no follow feature at all (profile.mjs:12).

'SHOWS' COUNTS NIGHTS MYSET WAS USED, NOT GIGS PLAYED. It is the length of the archived-show index (profile.mjs:15). A night that was never started, or that had no song, no vote and nobody in the room, is refused by the archiver and never appears (_history.mjs:107-123). So an artist who plays four gigs but only runs MySet at two shows "2". Do not say "every gig you've played".

A STAT TILE WITH A ZERO VANISHES ENTIRELY, it does not show 0 (artist.html:413, compact() returns '' for 0 at line 302). A brand-new artist's page shows Joined, possibly Songs, and the Community button — three cells in a row built for six. Any screenshot or mockup showing five populated tiles is showing an experienced account.

'SONGS' IS THE LIVE COUNT, AND ON THE FREE PLAN IT CANNOT EXCEED 50. It counts library songs with active !== false (profile.mjs:32); the free plan's `featured` limit is 50 songs live to the audience at once (_plan.mjs:20), while everyone can STORE up to 2,000 (_plan.mjs:133). "Your whole library on your page" would be wrong for a free artist with 300 songs.

THE VERIFIED TICK IS THE ONLY PLAN-GATED THING ON THIS ENTIRE PUBLIC SURFACE, and it needs BOTH the registry flag and a currently-paid plan — `verified && planOf(who) !== 'free'` (profile.mjs:27). A comped plan that lapses drops the tick on the next page load with nothing firing. And the framing in the code is precise and worth keeping: paying opens the door to being CHECKED, it does not buy the tick (_verify.mjs:185-188).

THE ARTIST TICK AND THE VENUE TICK ARE EARNED COMPLETELY DIFFERENTLY. A venue's needs a paid plan, a sign-in email on the venue's own domain, the venue's website naming the venue, and three different artists with gigs there vouching (_verify.mjs:7-30, 204-205). An artist's needs a paid plan, working Stripe card payments, a photo of an ID with a legal name and date of birth, and either Stripe's identity check matching or Perry looking at it (_verify.mjs:314-328). Same green chip, same glyph, two totally different stories.

THE VERIFIED TICK DOES NOT APPEAR IN THE CITY FEED. The feed rows carry only name, slug, venue, times and address (events.mjs:154-161, 80-85). The tick exists on the artist page, the community page and the venue page only. Do not imply a verified act stands out in the listings.

'PROMOTE' MEANS TWO DIFFERENT THINGS IN THIS CODEBASE AND ONLY ONE IS REAL. The Pro plan's `promote` flag ("list gigs in cities you don't normally play") is in NOT_BUILT — there is no code behind it anywhere (_plan.mjs:74, 112-130). The $10 Featured Shows spot IS built and shipped, is gated only by a feature flag, and is available to artists on ANY plan including free — handleFeature checks the flag and Stripe and nothing else (admin.mjs:1404-1470). Never write "featured listings are a Pro feature".

FEATURED SHOWS SITS BEHIND A FEATURE FLAG THAT DEFAULTS ON BUT CAN BE SWITCHED OFF GLOBALLY AT ANY MOMENT (_flags.mjs:38-49). With it off there is no Promote button, the endpoint refuses so nobody can be charged, and the Featured section is not rendered — but spots already paid for keep their record and reappear the moment it comes back. It was shipped 2026-09-05 as an experiment Perry wanted to test, with an explicit removal plan: if nobody buys, delete the flag AND the feature.

CANCELLING A PROMOTED GIG SPENDS THE $10. The feed renders a featured row only when the occurrence still exists, so deleting the gig makes the paid spot silently stop appearing and there is no refund (events.mjs:130, _featured.mjs:36-38). The refund path only exists for a payment that lands after the hold expired and the night filled, or a duplicate purchase.

THE GIG COUNTS IN THE COUNTRY/CITY PICKER ONLY LOOK AT THE FIRST 40 OWNERS IN A CITY (events.mjs:181, `ids.slice(0, 40)`), while the actual feed loops over every owner with no cap (events.mjs:68). In a busy city the number beside the city name will UNDER-count what the feed then shows. Do not describe the picker counts as exact.

THE FEED IS SEVEN DAYS, HARD-CODED (WINDOW_DAYS = 7, events.mjs:8). The artist page's own list looks 90 days ahead but the server returns at most 60 occurrences and the page renders at most 24, with only 3 visible until "See N more" is tapped (artist.html:359, 439, 452-456; events.mjs:44-50). "All your upcoming gigs" is a stretch; "the next three months" is closer.

AN ARTIST ONLY APPEARS IN A CITY'S FEED IF THE GIG HAS BOTH A COUNTRY AND A CITY FILLED IN (_events.mjs:180-181). And a ONE-OFF gig only keeps them listed until seven days after it happened, whereas a REPEATING gig keeps them in that city indefinitely (_events.mjs:182-185). "Add a gig and you're in your town's listings" needs the city caveat.

'TONIGHT' AND 'TOMORROW' ARE COMPUTED IN DIFFERENT TIMEZONES ON THE TWO PAGES. The city feed labels days in the GIG's timezone, and groups a whole city's night by the first row's timezone (events.mjs:89-92, 169-175). The artist page computes them from the VIEWER's own clock (artist.html:289-297). A traveller can see the same gig labelled differently on the two pages.

SHARING AN ARTIST LINK GIVES A GENERIC PREVIEW CARD. artist.html's OpenGraph tags are static — og:title is just "MySet", og:description is "Live music. You pick what gets played.", og:image is the stock /img/band.jpg (artist.html:21-23). The artist's name and photo are only set in JavaScript after load (line 495), which link unfurlers do not run. Do not claim "share your page and your photo shows up".

EVERY ARTIST WITHOUT PHOTOS GETS THE SAME STOCK BAND PICTURE. /img/band.jpg is the default for both the cover AND the avatar (_profile.mjs:50; artist.html:387, 395). A page that has never been filled in still looks furnished — which is good for screenshots and misleading in a demo.

THE ARTIST PAGE SELLS NOTHING. No merch, no tips, no ticket sales through MySet. /api/profile returns a merch count but artist.html never reads it — merch lives on the /:slug/community page and is a Plus/Pro feature (_plan.mjs:68, 90, 108). "Tickets ↗" on a gig row is just an outbound link to whatever URL the artist pasted (artist.html:450).

THERE IS NO GLOBAL ARTIST SEARCH. The only way to reach an artist page from the home page is to pick their country, pick their city, and have them playing there within seven days (index.html:396-424). The search box on the results filters the week already on screen and nothing else. Someone who knows an artist's name but not their city cannot find them.

THE ARTIST PAGE'S BIG BUTTON ALWAYS LINKS TO THE VOTE PAGE, even when nothing is on and the label reads "See the setlist" (artist.html:321, 406). It is never disabled. Do not describe it as only appearing during a show.

THE BIO IS 700 CHARACTERS AND THE TAGLINE IS 120 (_profile.mjs:90-91). There are exactly five link slots — Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube Music, Instagram, Website — in a fixed order, with no custom links (artist.html:350). Do not describe it as a link-in-bio tool.

MEDIA EMBEDS ARE THREE PROVIDERS ONLY: YouTube (including Shorts and playlists), Spotify, Apple Music (_embeds.mjs:92-93). No SoundCloud, no Bandcamp, no Vimeo, no MP3 upload. And every stored embed is re-validated on read — anything that can no longer produce a valid src is silently dropped from the page (_profile.mjs:109-114).

NOTHING THIRD-PARTY LOADS UNTIL SOMEBODY TAPS PLAY (artist.html:499-535). That is a genuine speed and privacy claim worth making, but it also means the page shows a poster image, not a playing widget, and for Spotify and Apple Music a non-subscriber gets a 30-second preview — which the page itself admits in fine print (artist.html:488-489). Do not promise full-track playback.

THE PAGE IS CLIENT-RENDERED AND SHOWS A BLACK SPLASH UNTIL BOTH FETCHES FINISH (artist.html:233-236, 354-363). There is no server-side HTML for search engines beyond the shell. Any SEO claim about artist pages ranking is unsupported by this code.

'src': 'ms-k3f9qz' IN THE /api/events RESPONSE IS AN ANTI-CLONE PROVENANCE MARKER, not a feature (_canary.mjs:36-42). It must never be explained, referenced or described publicly — a marker is only evidence while nobody knows to strip it. Note it appears on /api/events but NOT on /api/profile.

NEITHER OF THESE FILES HAS CHANGED SINCE THE LANDING PAGE WAS LAST EDITED (artist.html last touched 2026-09-04 commit 456feda; index.html 2026-09-05 commit 81f5b44; about.html 2026-09-05 commit 9e9fde4). But Featured Shows landed in that same 81f5b44 on 2026-09-05 and the landing page has never mentioned it — it is the biggest gap on this surface. The Fans stat tile and the artist verified tick both arrived 2026-09-04 (67f1d36) and are also unclaimed.

appCatalogue.surface: Community pages, posts, photos and CLIPS (/:slug/community and /v/:slug/community)
appCatalogue.summary: The community page is the one place in MySet where the audience writes rather than votes: a public page per artist (/:slug/community) and per venue (/v/:slug/community) where anyone who was in the room can rate the night 1–5 stars, write up to 500 characters, attach up to three photos, paste a YouTube/Instagram/TikTok link, and — newest of all — upload one 30-second video clip straight off their phone, with its sound. Nobody signs in; the only identity is a device id minted in localStorage that never leaves the server (public/community.html:185-188, netlify/functions/_community.mjs:9-12). Above the feed sits the owner's merch rail with real Stripe checkout. The owner reads and moderates the same feed from the Artist Studio's Profile tab or the Venue Studio's Merch tab: reply once per post, pin, hide (free on every plan, and hiding deletes the photos and clip), or delete for good (Plus for artists, Pro for venues). Everything the room does here — reading, posting, photos, clips, hearts, reports — is free on every plan.
appCatalogue.structure: One scrolling page, no tabs, rendered client-side from a single GET to /api/community (public/community.html:203-284). Top to bottom: a brand bar with a hamburger that offers the Artist Studio and Venue Studio (and switches its wording to "Open your Studio" if a token is in localStorage, public/community.html:189-194); the owner's avatar, name (linking back to /:slug or /v/:slug), a green "✓ Verified" tick, and a Share button; a horizontal snap-scrolling Merch rail if the owner has items on; the composer ("Say something") with five tappable stars, a 500-character textarea with a live counter that turns orange at 480, a night picker (artists only), an optional name field, a video-link field, "＋ Add photos" (up to three, shrunk on the phone), "＋ Add a clip" (one, up to 30s, with a progress bar), and a Post button that stays disabled until something is entered; then the feed, "What fans said · N", newest first with pinned posts on top; each post card shows name, stars, the night's label as an orange tag, the words, a 1/2/3-up photo grid that opens a full-screen lightbox, the clip player, the embedded or linked video, the owner's reply in an accent-tinted box, a heart with a count, a relative timestamp, and a ⋯ menu. The ⋯ menu is two different menus: on somebody else's post it offers "Report it"; on your own it offers "Edit it" (only inside 24 hours) and "Delete it" (public/community.html:572-590). Buying merch opens a bottom sheet with a quantity stepper and a "Pay $X" button that goes to Stripe Checkout and returns to the same page with a green receipt card pinned above the feed. Pull-to-refresh works (public/pull.js via public/community.html:173, 690). Fans arrive from three places only: the "Community" tile on an artist's public page (public/artist.html:414), the "Community" nav item on a venue page (public/venue.html:345), and a "Say something about tonight →" link on the voting page that appears ONLY after a show has ended (public/vote.html:618).
appCatalogue.design: Same "MySet dark-first" system as the rest of the app: a black first paint with three animated bars and the word MySet as a splash (public/community.html:13-30, 152), painted inline before app.css so a phone opening a new tab never flashes white. Rounded surface cards on a soft ground, a coral→orange gradient (#FF375F → #FF7A45) as the one accent, pill buttons, spring-eased taps (stars scale to 1.2, hearts to 1.15). Light and dark both honoured via prefers-color-scheme. Photos are square in a 3-up grid, 4:3 when there is only one, and tap to a near-black lightbox. Clips are black-backed rounded players capped at 70vh, with a poster frame and preload="none"; while a clip is fetching, the same three bars from the boot splash animate over it, so the wait reads as MySet thinking rather than a broken video (public/community.html:108-128, 518-543). The clip upload shows a real byte-accurate progress bar with a percentage (public/community.html:132-134, 345-351, 399-417). Reduced-motion is respected everywhere the bars animate. Copy is plain and lower-case-friendly: "How was the night?", "Just in general", "Nothing here yet — say something about a night."

features.name: An artist's community page
features.whatItDoes: A public page at /:slug/community where fans rate the night, post, and read each other. No sign-in of any kind.
features.whyRelevant: This is the only fan-writes surface in the whole product and it is free on every plan.

features.name: A venue's community page
features.whatItDoes: The same page for a bar or club at /v/:slug/community. Resolved from the venue registry; the feed is keyed posts_v_<vid>.
features.whyRelevant: Venues get a review page of their own — a distinct pitch from the artist one.

features.name: Posting without an account
features.whatItDoes: A fan never signs in. A device id is minted in localStorage on first visit and is the only identity a post carries; it is never returned to any page.
features.whyRelevant: The zero-friction promise. But it is also why every limit below is soft.

features.name: Rate the night 1–5 stars
features.whatItDoes: Five tappable stars in the composer; tapping the same star again clears the rating. Stars alone, with no words, count as a post.
features.whyRelevant: The headline verb of the page — 'rate the night'.

features.name: 500 characters, with a live counter
features.whatItDoes: The textarea is capped at 500 and the counter turns accent-coloured at 480. The server truncates to 500 as well.

features.name: Your name is optional
features.whatItDoes: A 30-character name field. Left blank, the post shows as 'Someone'. Nothing verifies the name.

features.name: Say which night you were at
features.whatItDoes: A dropdown of the artist's real gigs — every calendar gig from the last 120 days up to tonight, one per venue-and-date, newest first, capped at 40, plus archived nights the calendar never had. Default option is 'Just in general'. The chosen night becomes an orange tag on the post.
features.whyRelevant: Reviews are tied to a real, verifiable night rather than a vague vibe.

features.name: Venue pages have no night picker
features.whatItDoes: pickableNights runs for artists only; a venue GET returns shows: [] and a venue POST forces show to ''. So on a venue page there is no dropdown and no 'one post per night' rule.

features.name: Up to three photos per post
features.whatItDoes: A file input (multiple) that shrinks each photo on the phone to 1024px longest side and steps JPEG quality down until it is under ~400KB, shows 58px thumbnails with an ✕ to remove, and refuses a fourth.

features.name: Photos are checked by their bytes, not their label
features.whatItDoes: The server reads the actual JPEG/PNG/WebP file signature and refuses anything else, and refuses anything over 900KB, with a sentence a person can act on.

features.name: Tap a photo to see it full screen
features.whatItDoes: A near-black overlay lightbox; tap anywhere to close.

features.name: Photos are served from /api/img and cached for a year
features.whatItDoes: Each photo gets its own slot (c<postid>_0..2), served with an immutable one-year cache in the browser AND durably at Netlify's edge, so a photo is read out of storage once per version rather than once per viewer.

features.name: A 30-second clip from the night, with its sound
features.whatItDoes: One video clip per post, up to 30 seconds and up to 25MB, uploaded straight off the phone before the post is written. Nothing on the phone re-encodes it, so the audio is never at risk.
features.whyRelevant: The newest thing in the repo (rewritten 2026-09-06 11:57, commit f80f71d — AFTER the landing page's last edit at 2026-09-05 21:59) and the landing page has never mentioned video at all.

features.name: Big clips go up in pieces, raw, with a progress bar
features.whatItDoes: Three-step protocol: begin mints the clip id and says how many 4MB pieces to expect; each piece is POSTed as raw bytes with XMLHttpRequest so the bar can move byte by byte; end joins them and validates the whole file. Each piece gets three attempts with backoff before the upload gives up.
features.whyRelevant: This is what makes 25MB possible at all; base64-in-JSON capped clips at ~3MB.

features.name: The clip comes from the phone's own camera or camera roll
features.whatItDoes: A plain <input type="file" accept="video/*">. MySet never records in the browser — the site's Permissions-Policy blocks camera and microphone outright.
features.whyRelevant: Copy must not say 'record a clip in MySet' — you pick or shoot it in the phone's own camera app.

features.name: Every clip gets a still frame
features.whatItDoes: The phone grabs a frame at min(1s, duration/3), scales it to 640px and sends it as the poster. It is stored in a normal photo slot (k<10>), so it is served and cached by the same code as every other photo. Optional — a clip with no poster still plays, it just shows a black box.

features.name: Clips only download when somebody taps play
features.whatItDoes: Every clip in the feed is preload="none" behind its poster, so scrolling past a clip costs nothing. This is a deliberate cost control, not a nicety.

features.name: Three bars while a clip loads
features.whatItDoes: The boot-splash bars animate over a clip that is fetching, and come down the moment it can play, errors, or after 25 seconds. Wired so 'suspend' and 'stalled' never hide them.

features.name: /api/vid answers byte ranges so iPhones can play
features.whatItDoes: Serves a clip with accept-ranges, real 206 slices, correct suffix-range handling and a 416 with the real size for an unsatisfiable range. Without it iOS Safari plays nothing.

features.name: A clip is cached for a year at the edge
features.whatItDoes: Clip ids are minted once and never reused, so the URL is immutable; served with a one-year browser AND durable Netlify edge cache.

features.name: The composer preview plays the original file, with sound
features.whatItDoes: After upload, the draft shows a player pointed at a blob: URL of the file on the phone — no round trip — plus a 'Remove clip' chip.

features.name: A clip that is too big or too long is refused, with the actual number
features.whatItDoes: Size is checked on the phone before a byte is read, again at begin (413), and again on the joined bytes; length is checked on the phone when the duration is readable and again on the server from the MP4 mvhd box. Every message names the real size or length and says what to do.
features.whyRelevant: Nothing shrinks or trims any more. A long clip is a refusal, not a fix.

features.name: A clip nobody posted is deleted after two hours
features.whatItDoes: Every upload is noted as pending before the first byte lands; the post clears it; a cron drains one owner per ring on an hourly watermark and deletes anything over two hours old that no post claims.

features.name: At most 40 clips going up at once per page
features.whatItDoes: begin refuses with 429 'Too many clips going up at once here — try again in a few minutes.' when the pending list is at 40.

features.name: The old single-body clip upload (action:'clip')
features.whatItDoes: Accepts a whole clip as a base64 data URL inside the community JSON body. Still implemented, still tested, still reachable — but no page calls it any more; community.html only talks to /api/clipup.
features.whyRelevant: INVARIANTS.md 0dq still describes this as the clip path. It isn't any more.

features.name: Paste a YouTube, Instagram or TikTok link
features.whatItDoes: A separate field from the clip. YouTube embeds inline in a 16:9 iframe rebuilt from a literal youtube-nocookie template; Instagram and TikTok render as a '▶ Watch on … ↗' pill link. Anything else is refused with 'Videos can be a YouTube, Instagram or TikTok link.'
features.whyRelevant: A link and a clip are two different features and both are kept. The landing page mentions neither.

features.name: Three posts a day per phone
features.whatItDoes: Enforced inside the write, not just in the page, and again at the clip upload door so nobody uploads 25MB only to be refused. Message: 'That's three posts today from this phone — come back tomorrow.'

features.name: One post per night per phone
features.whatItDoes: If the same device already posted about the same show, the second is refused: 'You've already posted about that night — one per show.' Artists only.

features.name: A soft per-network daily ceiling
features.whatItDoes: 150 posts a day from one network hash per page — wide enough that a whole bar on one wifi never hits it. 'This network has posted a lot today. Try again tomorrow.'

features.name: The feed keeps the last 200 posts
features.whatItDoes: Older posts fall off the list once 200 is exceeded.
features.whyRelevant: The record is dropped but its photo and clip bytes are NOT deleted — they stay in storage and stay fetchable by URL.

features.name: One heart per phone per post
features.whatItDoes: Optimistic tap, then confirmed by the server; unlike takes it back. Liker hashes live in a separate document so a burst of hearts does not fight the composer. The page remembers which posts this phone liked.

features.name: Report a post
features.whatItDoes: One report per device. It is a count the owner sees in their Studio, never a takedown — nothing is auto-hidden. Toast: 'Reported — thanks'.
features.whyRelevant: Do not write 'reported posts come down'. They never do automatically.

features.name: Change what you wrote, for 24 hours
features.whatItDoes: Your own post only, words and stars only — photos and the clip are left alone and the sheet says so. The Edit button is only drawn inside the window the server also enforces; after that it says 'The day for changing this one has passed — you can still take it down.' An edited post shows '· edited'.

features.name: Take your own post back, any time
features.whatItDoes: No time window — deleting your own words is always allowed. Confirms, then deletes the record, the photos, the clip and the like hashes.

features.name: The owner replies, once per post
features.whatItDoes: One reply per post, up to 500 characters, shown in an accent-tinted box labelled 'The artist' or 'The venue'. Saving an empty reply removes it.

features.name: Pin a post to the top
features.whatItDoes: Pinned posts sort first for the public and for the owner, with a 'Pinned' chip. Toggled from the Studio.
features.whyRelevant: There is no limit of one — any number of posts can be pinned, despite the Studio copy saying 'pin one'.

features.name: Hide any post, on any plan, instantly and undoably
features.whatItDoes: The post vanishes for the public and stays visible to the owner marked 'hidden', so the decision can be undone. Free forever, deliberately, so every artist can take something offensive off their page the second they see it.

features.name: Hiding a post deletes its photos and its clip
features.whatItDoes: Because /api/img and /api/vid are edge-cached and know nothing about hiding, hide removes the bytes for good. The words stay and can be un-hidden; the pictures and the clip cannot come back. The Studio says so in the confirm dialog before the tap.
features.whyRelevant: Added 2026-09-05 12:46 (99f0db8). 'Undo it' is only half true — the media is gone.

features.name: Delete a post for good — Plus for artists
features.whatItDoes: Erases the record, the photos, the clip and the likes permanently. Refused on Free with a 402 and the same words the Studio shows; the founder bypasses the gate. Greyed as '✕ Plus' in the Artist Studio rather than hidden.

features.name: Delete a post for good — Pro for venues
features.whatItDoes: Same action on the venue side, gated on the venue being on a paid plan, refused with 402 'Deleting a post for good is a Pro feature'.
features.whyRelevant: The Venue Studio does NOT grey this button — a free venue sees a plain '✕' and only finds out when the server refuses (public/venue-studio.html:1050).

features.name: The owner reads the whole feed in their Studio
features.whatItDoes: Artist Studio → Profile tab shows the last 30 posts with stars, report counts, photo counts, the night, and the owner's own reply. Venue Studio shows the same on the Merch tab.

features.name: The owner never sees who posted
features.whatItDoes: Both the public and the owner shapes strip the device id entirely. Reports are a count; there is no way to identify or block a person.

features.name: Crew and managers can moderate, with limits
features.whatItDoes: postReply, postHide and postDelete are 'community' capabilities in the artist Studio's role table; postPin is not listed, so anyone signed in can pin. On the venue side crew may postList/postReply/postHide/postDelete.

features.name: Merch on the community page
features.whatItDoes: A snap-scrolling rail of up to 12 items with a square picture, title, price and blurb. Each card shows one of three buttons: 'Buy · $X' when the owner can take money and the item is at least $1, 'Get it ↗' when the item has an outside link, or a flat 'Ask at the show'.

features.name: Merch is Plus for artists, Pro for venues
features.whatItDoes: The rail is empty on a free plan — items are never deleted when a plan lapses, just not shown. The founder always sees his.

features.name: Buying merch with Stripe Checkout
features.whatItDoes: A bottom sheet with a 1–5 quantity stepper, then Stripe Checkout on the owner's own connected account. Price comes from the stored record, never the request. Pickup items ask for no address; posted items ask Stripe for one. Fine print: 'Paid to <name> through Stripe. MySet never sees your card.'

features.name: The receipt when you come back from Stripe
features.whatItDoes: The return is verified with the server, never trusted from the URL, and a green 'Paid — thank you' card is inserted above the feed. A lost return is retried for 24 hours from a pending record in localStorage; cancelling shows 'Payment cancelled'.

features.name: One money gate decides whether Buy exists
features.whatItDoes: canBuy is true only when Stripe is configured AND the artist's show payments are ready (or it is the founder); for a venue it mirrors the venue's own Stripe readiness. If false, no Buy button is drawn anywhere on the page.

features.name: The verified tick on a community page
features.whatItDoes: A green '✓ Verified' badge beside the owner's name. For an artist it requires the registry flag AND a paid plan; for a venue it requires the flag AND a paid venue plan.

features.name: Share the page
features.whatItDoes: Uses the native share sheet where it exists, otherwise copies the link and toasts 'Link copied'. Strips the query string.

features.name: 'Say something about tonight' after the show ends
features.whatItDoes: The voting page shows a link straight to the community page, carrying ?show=<showId>, but ONLY once the show has ended. While a show is live there is no route from the voting page to the community page.
features.whyRelevant: The single most important funnel into this page, and it is invisible for the whole gig.

features.name: The Community tile on the artist and venue pages
features.whatItDoes: A permanent CTA in the artist page's stats row, and a nav item on a venue page. The city/what's-on home (index.html) never links to a community page at all.

features.name: The honesty line under the feed
features.whatItDoes: 'Posts come straight from fans' phones and aren't checked first. The artist can hide anything.' Nothing is pre-screened, filtered or auto-moderated anywhere in the code.

features.name: No notifications for fans
features.whatItDoes: 'You won't get a notification — come back and look.' Push exists in MySet but only for the artist's Studio; the audience is never pushed to.

features.name: Pull to refresh
features.whatItDoes: The shared MySet pull-to-refresh reloads the feed. There is no live polling and no auto-refresh on this page.

features.name: Community posts are in the account export
features.whatItDoes: The artist's and venue's 'download everything' export includes the whole community feed in the owner shape (hidden posts and report counts included, device ids excluded).

features.name: Leaving takes the clips with it
features.whatItDoes: The key list for account deletion enumerates every post photo, every posted clip and its poster, and every still-pending clip — so nothing is left behind that list() could never find.

features.name: Nothing on this surface is behind a feature flag
features.whatItDoes: The only two flags in the repo are voteFinal and featuredShows, both defaulting on and neither touching the community page, posts, photos or clips.

features.name: Clips are the expensive end of MySet
features.whatItDoes: A 25MB clip watched 100 times is ~$0.33 of Netlify bandwidth — more than ten entire three-hour gigs, which cost about 2.8 cents each. Caching saves compute, never bytes.
features.whyRelevant: If clips become a marketing headline, the unit economics change materially and there is no plan gate on them at all.

trapsForCopy: THE LANDING PAGE HAS NEVER HEARD OF VIDEO. public/about.html says only 'fans rate the night, post photos, and you reply' (line 609). It never mentions the 30-second clip, the pasted YouTube/Instagram/TikTok link, editing your own post, or taking it back. The clip rewrite landed 2026-09-06 11:57 (commit f80f71d), after about.html's last edit at 2026-09-05 21:59 (commit 9e9fde4).

'Post a video' means two different things and both exist. A CLIP is a file uploaded from the phone, up to 30 seconds and 25MB, played inside MySet with its sound (public/community.html:251-255). A LINK is a pasted YouTube/Instagram/TikTok URL — YouTube embeds, the other two are just links out (netlify/functions/_community.mjs:74-102). One post can carry one of each. Do not merge them into one claim.

MySet does not record video. The clip comes from the phone's own camera or camera roll through a plain file input, and the site's Permissions-Policy blocks camera and microphone outright (netlify.toml:99). Never write 'record a clip in MySet' or 'hit record'.

Nothing shrinks or trims a clip any more. Before 2026-09-06 the phone re-encoded every clip; that code is deleted (public/community.html:314-341). A clip over 25MB or over 30 seconds is REFUSED with its actual size or length and told to trim it in the phone's own app. Do not promise 'we'll compress it for you'.

The 30-second limit is not enforced for every file. The server reads the duration out of an MP4's mvhd box only; a WebM, a fragmented MP4, or anything whose duration reads back as Infinity on the phone gets no length check at all (netlify/functions/_video.mjs:143-157, public/community.html:482). The hard, always-true limit is 25MB of bytes. Say 'up to 25MB' if you need a limit that is always true.

'Hide, and undo it' is only half true. Hiding a post deletes its photos and its clip permanently (netlify/functions/_community.mjs:295-303). Un-hiding brings back the words, never the pictures. The Studio warns about this before the tap; marketing copy that says 'hide it and change your mind later' will be wrong for any post with media.

Hiding is free forever; DELETING for good is Plus for artists (netlify/functions/_plan.mjs:73, admin.mjs:1287-1291) and Pro for VENUES (netlify/functions/venueadmin.mjs:548-549). Two different plan names for the identical action. The Venue Studio also fails to grey the button — a free venue sees a plain '✕' and only learns it is gated when the server refuses (public/venue-studio.html:1050).
'Pin one' is the Studio's wording, not the code's. postPin sets a per-post boolean with no limit (netlify/functions/_community.mjs:304) — an owner can pin every post on the page.

'One heart per phone' holds up to 500 likers. Past MAX_LIKERS the hash is not stored but the count still increments, so on a very popular post the same phone can add hearts repeatedly (netlify/functions/_community.mjs:228).

A report is a count, never a takedown. Nothing is auto-hidden, auto-flagged or reviewed by anyone. The owner just sees a number in their Studio (netlify/functions/_community.mjs:245-261). Do not imply moderation happens without the owner acting.

Nothing is checked before it appears. The page says so itself: 'Posts come straight from fans' phones and aren't checked first' (public/community.html:281). There is no profanity filter, no queue, no AI review.

Nobody is notified. Fans get no notification of a reply — the composer says 'come back and look' (public/community.html:257). Push exists only for the artist's Studio; the audience is never pushed to.

The 'one post per night' rule only exists on ARTIST pages. Venue pages have no night picker and force the show field empty (netlify/functions/community.mjs:89, 143), so on a venue page a phone can post three unrelated times a day with nothing tying them to a date.

The night picker reads the CALENDAR, not the archive — every gig from the last 120 days, up to 40 entries, one per venue-and-date (netlify/functions/community.mjs:16-32). A show run outside a calendar entry appears only if it was archived. It is not 'every show you've ever played'.

The 'Say something about tonight' link on the voting page appears ONLY after the show ends (public/vote.html:610-618). During the gig there is no path from the voting screen to the community page. And its ?show= parameter carries a showId, while the picker's keys are usually eventId@date — so the night is usually NOT pre-selected when a fan follows that link.

Editing your own post is 24 hours, words and stars only. Photos and the clip cannot be changed or added by an edit, and the sheet says so (public/community.html:595; netlify/functions/_community.mjs:175-198). Deleting your own post has no window at all.

Merch on the community page is Plus for artists (netlify/functions/_plan.mjs:68) and Pro for venues (netlify/functions/_venues.mjs:130-131). When a plan lapses the items are hidden, never deleted. A Buy button additionally needs Stripe payouts to be live — otherwise the card falls back to an outside link or a flat 'Ask at the show' (public/community.html:228-230).

A venue CAN sell through MySet. Older material says venues have no payout account; venueadmin now accepts a merch item if the venue has either an outside link OR Stripe ready (netlify/functions/venueadmin.mjs:505), and pay.mjs has a full venue merch branch (lines 33-70).

Everything the ROOM does here is free on every plan — reading, posting, stars, photos, clips, hearts, reports. There is no plan gate and no feature flag anywhere on the fan side of this page. Clips in particular are unlimited by plan and are the most expensive thing MySet serves (netlify/functions/_video.mjs:50-62).

A YouTube link loses its timestamp, and a playlist-only YouTube link produces a broken embed. parseVideo keeps only the video id and drops start/list/shorts (netlify/functions/_community.mjs:82), so a ?t= link starts from zero and a list-only URL renders an iframe pointed at 'videoseries?list=undefined'. A YouTube Short also renders letterboxed in a 16:9 box.

/community.html with no slug is the FOUNDER's page, not 'a generic one'. publicArtist falls back to DEFAULT_ARTIST ('perry-idyll') when no ?a= is given (netlify/functions/_lib.mjs:1016-1031), and both Studios link there when an artist has no slug yet (public/studio.html:3275, 3463).

The feed keeps the last 200 posts and older ones fall off (netlify/functions/_community.mjs:164) — but their photo and clip bytes are not deleted and stay fetchable by URL. Do not claim posts are kept forever, and do not claim old media is cleaned up.

The repo's own docs are stale on this surface. INVARIANTS.md 0eb / 0eg / 0ei / 0eq all describe the deleted canvas re-encoder and the separate audio-mixing path, and 0dq still names action:'clip' as the upload route — which no page calls any more (public/community.html only talks to /api/clipup). Read the code, not the invariants, for anything about clips.

appCatalogue.surface: The venue side — public venue page (/v/:slug), Venue Studio (/venues), and the venue half of the server
appCatalogue.summary: MySet's venue side is a genuinely separate second product living inside the same app: its own registry (`venues`), its own sign-in realm and token tag, its own studio, and its own two-tier plan ladder. A bar signs in with an email code at myset.vip/venues, names the place plus a city and country, and instantly gets a public page at myset.vip/v/<slug> whose "what's on" is assembled — with no data entry and no backfill — by matching artists' self-listed gig venue names against the venue's own name inside its own town. On top of that free base the venue adds its own recurring events (quiz night, DJ, the football), a menu, offers, opening hours, amenities, photos, a community page it moderates, and printable QR codes; it reads per-night and per-act audience numbers taken from show history it never had to collect, and it receives booking enquiries from signed-in artists with real numbers attached. As of 2026-09-04/05 it also has self-serve Stripe billing for a $20/mo Pro tier, its own Stripe Connect payout account, merch sales, an orders list, a Stripe-sourced earnings statement with CSV export, staff roles, device session management, a data export and a 30-day undoable account deletion. Perry's landing page (/about) describes only the free auto-filling listing half; roughly half of what shipped in the last three days has never appeared in the marketing copy at all.
appCatalogue.structure:
Two public routes and one studio, all served by netlify.toml redirects (netlify.toml:57-66): /v/:slug -> public/venue.html, /v/:slug/community -> public/community.html, /venues -> public/venue-studio.html (there is NO public venue directory — "For venues" links straight into the sign-in door, public/index.html:246,310,411).

PUBLIC PAGE (public/venue.html:315-455) is one long scroll, rendered from a single GET /api/venue?v=<slug> (netlify/functions/venue.mjs:20-47): cover photo with an "on now" pill -> name + Verified/Unverified chip + address + "N artists confirmed it" line -> action pills (Directions, Community, Call, WhatsApp, Menu) -> "On now"/"Next up" -> About -> What's on, grouped by night, max 14 day-groups -> Offers -> Menu highlights -> Good to know (amenities) -> Opening hours with today highlighted -> Photos -> Find them (links) -> Who plays here -> the "Play live?" card (public/venue.html:460-506), which is the artist-facing pitch/vouch surface and changes shape four ways depending on whether an artist token is in localStorage, whether they have already pitched, and what the venue answered.

VENUE STUDIO (public/venue-studio.html) is a dark, six-tab single page, tab persisted in localStorage as `myset.vtab` (public/venue-studio.html:357,623). Header carries the venue name (links to the public page), an Upgrade/plan button and a Verified/Unverified pill (public/venue-studio.html:1377-1393). Tabs (public/venue-studio.html:1394-1400): Page (verification checklist, cover photo, basics, place, contact + social links, amenities, opening hours, photo slots) | What's on (auto-filled live music, your own events, "who wants to play here") | Numbers (people/votes/nights, busiest night, by act, by night) | Menu (menu link + up to 24 highlights + up to 6 offers) | Merch (merch items, Stripe Connect setup, orders, earnings, community moderation) | Settings (plan, slug, verification summary, QR codes, who can sign in, sessions, export, delete). A sign-in gate replaces the whole app when no token (public/venue-studio.html:379-416); a "being deleted" bar and a "card didn't go through" bar sit above every tab (public/venue-studio.html:1401).

The door: POST /api/venueauth with action start -> verify -> (claim if new). Everything else the studio does is POST /api/venueadmin with an action name; the venue id is always taken from the token, never the body (netlify/functions/venueadmin.mjs:19-28).
appCatalogue.design:
Two deliberately opposite skins. The public venue page is the light consumer skin shared with the rest of myset.vip: system font, --grad coral gradient (#FF375F -> #FF6B45), soft card shadows, pill buttons that scale on :active with a spring curve, a black first-paint splash with three animating bars that is hidden on first render rather than a timer (public/venue.html:203-216, 286). It respects prefers-color-scheme, uses aspect-ratio 16/10 covers with a bottom veil gradient, and reads as a Google-Business-listing-meets-Apple-Maps card stack. The Venue Studio is the dark back-office skin (#000 ground, #1C1C1E surfaces, --accent #FF456E), pinned header + a horizontally scrollable pill tab bar whose sticky offset is MEASURED not guessed (public/venue-studio.html:74, 1412-1417), bottom sheets that can be dismissed by drag, flick, backdrop, Escape or a visible ✕ (public/venue-studio.html:1548-1556).

Two design rules carry marketing weight. First, locked features are SHOWN greyed, never hidden — /lock.css is shared by both studios, and there are two distinct lock states: a clickable "Pro feature" veil that scrolls you to the plans, and a non-clickable "Coming soon" veil for things designed but not built (public/venue-studio.html:687-732). "Has it" means "has as much as the top plan gives", so a numeric limit like 3-of-12 photos reads as locked (public/venue-studio.html:698-714). Second, verification is presented as a five-line CHECKLIST with the specific blocker named in a toast, never a yes/no (public/venue-studio.html:1423-1511). Photos are shrunk and centre-cropped on the phone before upload — cover to 1400px at 1.6:1, gallery to 800px square (public/venue-studio.html:1777-1799). Every internal link paints a leaving splash before navigating so there is never a white flash (public/venue-studio.html:562-584).

features.name: Sign in with an email and a 6-digit code
features.whatItDoes: No password. Type an email, get a code that works for ten minutes, you are in. Same button for a brand-new venue and a returning one.
features.whyRelevant: Removes the single biggest friction in getting a bar owner signed up.

features.name: A venue account can never reach an artist account
features.whatItDoes: Venues live in their own registry with their own token tag ('v|'), their own one-time-code realm and their own session store. The same email address can run an artist page and a venue page and neither can touch the other's setlist, votes or money.
features.whyRelevant: A real trust claim a bar owner cares about, and it is structural rather than a permission check.

features.name: Claiming: name, city, country, and the page exists
features.whatItDoes: After the code, a new venue types the venue name plus a city and country and the public page is created immediately, with the slug auto-picked from the name and the profile seeded so the map link works before they press Save.
features.whyRelevant: This is the 'claim your venue — free' promise the landing page already makes.

features.name: Reserved and collision-safe page addresses
features.whatItDoes: A slug under 3 characters gets 'bar' appended, reserved words (admin, studio, venues, community, merch...) are refused, and a taken name gets a number suffix up to 500.

features.name: Change your page address
features.whatItDoes: Owner can rename myset.vip/v/<slug> from Settings. The old slug is released and the new one claimed atomically; a clash is refused with a message.

features.name: The what's-on tab fills itself from artists' calendars
features.whatItDoes: Nothing stores a link between a gig and a venue. The public page matches on the venue NAME (normalised, 'the' stripped, containment only when the shorter name is distinctive) inside the venue's own city and country, across every artist indexed in that city. A venue that signs up today already has its whole diary.
features.whyRelevant: The headline venue feature and already the centrepiece of about.html's venue section.

features.name: 60 days ahead, 60 artists per city, 200 rows
features.whatItDoes: The public page looks 60 days ahead, reads at most 60 artists indexed in that city, and returns at most 200 rows; the page renders at most 14 day-groups and reports a truncation flag the page never uses.
features.whyRelevant: A hard ceiling nobody has written copy against — a busy city could silently drop acts.

features.name: "Listed as" — the artist's own spelling is shown back to the venue
features.whatItDoes: In the Studio each auto-matched gig shows the exact venue name the artist typed, so a venue can see why a near-miss did or didn't match.

features.name: The page says out loud that the artists listed it, not the venue
features.whatItDoes: A fine-print line under what's-on: shows are listed by the artists from their own calendars, times can change, check with the venue.

features.name: The venue's own events, entered once
features.whatItDoes: Quiz night, a DJ, the football, a full-moon party. Title, date, start and end time, an optional one-liner, and a repeat rule (once / weekly / every 2 weeks / monthly / yearly). Place is never asked for — the server fills it from the profile.
features.whyRelevant: Already on about.html; the recurrence-as-one-record design is the substance behind 'entered once'.

features.name: A weekly event is ONE record, forever
features.whatItDoes: Events are stored as rules and expanded on read, so a residency needs no maintenance and there is no job to run. Up to 200 event rules per venue.

features.name: Cancel just one night of a repeating run
features.whatItDoes: The ✕ on an occurrence adds that date to a skip list; Edit changes the whole run. The Studio spells the difference out.

features.name: A venue's own events appear in the local what's-on feed
features.whatItDoes: Venue-run events go into the same city index as artists' gigs, tagged 'At the venue', and their row on the city feed links back to /v/<slug>.
features.whyRelevant: The only route by which a venue itself becomes clickable in the public city feed.

features.name: Changing your city rewrites your events so they don't vanish
features.whatItDoes: Editing the venue's name, city or country rewrites every stored event's place and reindexes the city feed, so events don't keep pointing at the old town.

features.name: Events are refused until the city and country are set
features.whatItDoes: eventSave returns an error telling them to fill in the Page tab first, because the city is what puts the event in the local feed.

features.name: Artists ask for a spot from your page, with real numbers attached
features.whatItDoes: A signed-in artist sends a 400-character enquiry from the venue's public page. The venue sees the artist's name, message, and their real totals: nights played, people in the room, votes cast, songs in the library — plus a link to their MySet page.
features.whyRelevant: Already on about.html as 'acts come to you, with receipts'.

features.name: Only a signed-in artist can send an enquiry
features.whatItDoes: There is deliberately no open contact form. An artist with no MySet token sees a 'get your MySet page — it's free' card instead of a message box.

features.name: One enquiry per artist per venue — asking again just updates it
features.whatItDoes: Idempotent by artist id. Re-sending identical text is not recorded as a change; the artist gets a 'Change my message' button rather than a second row in the venue's inbox.

features.name: Keen / pass / undo, and no email is ever shared
features.whatItDoes: The venue taps Keen or ✕. The artist sees the answer on their own page and in their studio; neither side gets the other's email address. Both sides can undo back to 'new'.

features.name: 120 enquiries kept per venue, 60 shown
features.whatItDoes: Past 120 stored pitches new ones are refused with 'this venue has a lot of enquiries in'; the studio renders the most recent 60.

features.name: The green Verified tick
features.whatItDoes: A verified venue shows a green ✓ Verified chip; everyone else shows a grey 'Unverified listing' chip and a fine-print line inviting whoever runs it to claim it.
features.whyRelevant: about.html says 'your page works whether you verify it or not' but never says the tick itself is a paid feature.

features.name: Verification needs all five things, and any one alone is just a claim
features.whatItDoes: Paid plan AND a website on the page AND the claiming email on that website's domain AND the website's own text naming the venue AND three different artists with a gig there confirming it. The town being named on the site is reported as a bonus and never required.

features.name: The verification checklist tells you exactly which step is missing
features.whatItDoes: Five numbered lines with ticks, an 'N of 5 done' headline, the claiming email spelled out against the required domain, and a toast that names the single blocker rather than saying 'see above'.

features.name: MySet fetches your homepage and looks for your name in the words on it
features.whatItDoes: An https-only fetch with SSRF protection (every resolved address checked against private ranges, three redirect hops max, 512KB cap, 8s timeout, non-HTML refused). Script, style and comment text is stripped before the name search, so a name that only exists in an image or is drawn by JavaScript will not be found — and the UI says so.

features.name: Saving a website runs the check by itself
features.whatItDoes: Pressing Save on the Page tab with a website filled in silently runs the verification check and only speaks up if it wins. The check never runs on page load, so a stranger's server is not hammered.

features.name: Artists tap "Yes, I play here" to help a venue get its tick
features.whatItDoes: An artist can only vouch for a venue they already have a gig listed at, in the same town. Three different artists are needed. The public page shows a progress bar and the count; hitting three re-runs the whole verdict.
features.whyRelevant: The anti-fraud story is genuinely good: ten vouches means ten accounts each with their own gig history.

features.name: "N artists who play here confirmed it" on the public page
features.whatItDoes: Shown to everyone as soon as at least one artist has confirmed, with the vouching artists' names sent back (up to 12). Adds '— one of the things the green tick needs' while unverified.

features.name: The domain check uses the address that CLAIMED the page, not whoever is signed in
features.whatItDoes: A barman added on Tuesday cannot verify the venue off his own domain. The Studio explains this when the signed-in address is not the claiming one.

features.name: Gmail, Hotmail and friends never count as a venue domain
features.whatItDoes: A hard list of consumer mail domains is rejected before any comparison, and the site must be reachable over https on a public address.

features.name: Perry can verify a venue by hand
features.whatItDoes: Founder-only toggle over every venue in the registry, stamped verifiedVia:'owner'. The Studio and the public page both render 'Checked by MySet by hand' for it. This is the route for a bar with no website.

features.name: The tick goes when Pro goes
features.whatItDoes: Two independent belts: the founder's plan setter clears `verified` when a venue drops to free, and shapeVenue ANDs verified with paid on every read, so a stale stored flag can never show a tick on a free page.

features.name: Numbers: people, votes and nights, by night and by act
features.whatItDoes: Totals across every MySet show that ran at the venue, a busiest-night callout, a ranked by-act list with an average-people-per-night figure, and a reverse-chronological by-night list capped at 40 rows.
features.whyRelevant: about.html's 'you learn who fills the room' — and the average-per-night is explicitly called the number that matters.

features.name: What each act earned is not in the venue's numbers, ever
features.whatItDoes: Money is absent from the venue stats payload entirely, not even as a total, and the Studio says so in plain words.
features.whyRelevant: A trust line that matters to artists as much as to venues.

features.name: Any act can switch their numbers off from their own studio
features.whatItDoes: shareStats defaults to on. An artist who turns it off is excluded from the venue's stats entirely and counted only as an anonymous 'N acts have switched sharing off'.
features.whyRelevant: A copywriter promising venues 'see every act's numbers' would be wrong.

features.name: "People in the room" means phones that opened the voting page
features.whatItDoes: The headline number is the show's room count (falling back to peak voters), not people who tapped and not a headcount — and the Studio states this under the figure.

features.name: Menu: a link to the full menu plus up to 24 highlights
features.whatItDoes: A URL (https only), a one-line note about the food, and up to 24 items each with a section, name, price and note. Sections become headings on the public page; the full menu stays behind the link.

features.name: Offers — up to six
features.whatItDoes: Happy hour, two-for-one, a free shot for anyone who votes: a title, a detail line and a when. They get their own section on the public page with a % badge.

features.name: Opening hours, including after midnight
features.whatItDoes: Seven days, each open/closed with times, saved the instant a time input changes. The public page highlights today's row. Closing after midnight is explicitly fine.

features.name: 22 "Good to know" chips
features.whatItDoes: House PA / backline, live music most nights, sea view, dance floor, dog friendly, step-free access, cash only and 15 more. One tap toggles each. The Studio tells venues House PA is the one artists look for first.

features.name: A Directions button that opens the right map app
features.whatItDoes: The server builds an Apple link and a Google link from coordinates, an address, or a pasted maps link, and the page picks by user agent. A pasted link that isn't a real map link is dropped and the venue is told so instead of it looking saved.

features.name: Call and WhatsApp buttons
features.whatItDoes: A phone number renders as a tel: link and a WhatsApp number as a wa.me link, both stripped to characters a dialler understands.

features.name: Website, Instagram, Facebook and a Google Maps listing
features.whatItDoes: Four link fields, each host-checked (Instagram and Facebook must be on their real domains, the Google one must pass the map-URL parser), https only, tracking parameters stripped, private hosts refused.

features.name: Three photos free, twelve on Pro — plus a cover on any plan
features.whatItDoes: The cover photo is uncounted and free to every venue. Gallery slots p0-p2 are free; p3-p11 are shown greyed with a Pro lock and the server returns a 402 naming the slot number and the plan's cap if one is attempted anyway.
features.whyRelevant: The cap existed in the plan table for weeks and was only actually enforced on 2026-09-05.

features.name: Clearing photo 2 doesn't move photo 3
features.whatItDoes: Photo slots are addresses, not a list — blanks in the middle are preserved and only trailing empties are dropped, so the Studio never draws one photo in another's box.

features.name: Photos are shrunk and centre-cropped on the phone
features.whatItDoes: Cover to 1400px wide at 1.6:1, gallery to 800px square, cover-fit from the middle so nothing is squashed, JPEG at 0.82 before it goes over the wire.

features.name: A community page fans post to, free on every plan
features.whatItDoes: myset.vip/v/<slug>/community. Fans rate the night with stars, post text, up to three photos and a video clip. The venue replies once per post, pins one, hides anything, and deletes for good on Pro.
features.whyRelevant: Shipped 2026-09-04 and about.html's venue section does not mention it at all.

features.name: Hiding is free and undoable; deleting for good is Pro
features.whatItDoes: Every owner on every plan can take an offensive post off the page instantly and put it back. Permanent erasure is gated at 402 with a message that says hiding is free and instant. Hiding also deletes the post's photos and clip on the way in — so un-hiding brings back the words, not the pictures.

features.name: Fans cannot tag which night a venue post is about
features.whatItDoes: Night selection is an artist-only feature; for a venue page the show field is forced empty and no pickable nights are returned.

features.name: Merch on your community page — a Pro feature
features.whatItDoes: Up to 12 items with a name, blurb, price, photo and an on/off switch. On free the whole list is locked behind a Pro veil and the server refuses saves at 402; items already added stay saved and reappear when Pro comes back.

features.name: Venue merch shows on the community page only, never on the venue page
features.whatItDoes: shapeVenue returns merch, but public/venue.html has no merch section at all — the shop lives at /v/<slug>/community.
features.whyRelevant: Easy for copy to imply a shop on the venue page itself.

features.name: Venues get their own Stripe payout account
features.whatItDoes: Stripe Connect Express onboarding from the Merch tab, with a country picker (22 countries) that Stripe cannot change later. Money from merch lands directly in the venue's own account; MySet never sees bank details. A Stripe dashboard link once it is live.
features.whyRelevant: Landed 2026-09-04; two in-repo code comments still say a venue has no payout account.

features.name: 10% on free, 2% on Pro — with Stripe's card fee shared
features.whatItDoes: MySet's cut on merch a venue sells through the app, taken as an application fee on a direct charge, and reduced by half of Stripe's estimated card fee (never below zero). The Studio shows the exact percentage and an honest note that the split is an estimate until the charge settles.

features.name: An item needs either a buy link or working card payments
features.whatItDoes: merchSave refuses an item with no link until Stripe is set up, naming both ways out. Items priced under $1 are never sold through MySet — the buyer is told to ask at the bar.

features.name: An orders list with buyer and shipping details
features.whatItDoes: Every paid order lands with a title, quantity, amount, pickup-or-post and a date; a Details sheet pulls the buyer's name, email and postal address live from Stripe; Done/Undo marks it fulfilled.

features.name: A venue's own earnings statement, and a CSV for the bookkeeper
features.whatItDoes: Twelve months from Stripe: paid to you, fees, yours, month by month with payment counts and the Stripe/MySet fee split, plus a downloadable CSV. Never goes back further than the day the venue joined. Owner only.
features.whyRelevant: Shipped 2026-09-05 and appears nowhere in marketing.

features.name: Two venue plans: Free and Pro at $20/month
features.whatItDoes: A full plan sheet listing every line of both tiers, the transaction fee called a transaction fee, and a working Stripe Checkout upgrade. Pro buys twelve photos, merch, delete-for-good, the green tick and the 2% rate.
features.whyRelevant: about.html never mentions a paid venue tier exists.

features.name: Leaving Pro asks twice and offers half price for a month, once
features.whatItDoes: A confirm sheet naming what is lost, then a one-time 50%-off-for-a-month retention offer, then the downgrade. A paid month always runs to its end.

features.name: Invoices, receipts and card management
features.whatItDoes: An in-app invoice list read from Stripe and a link into Stripe's billing portal to change the card. Only shown once there is a Stripe customer, so a free or comped venue never sees a dead link.

features.name: A "your card didn't go through" banner with a grace date
features.whatItDoes: Sits above every tab when billing is past due, explains it is usually an expired card, says nothing on the page has changed, and gives the date everything keeps working until.

features.name: Locked features are shown greyed, never hidden — in two different states
features.whatItDoes: A clickable 'Pro feature' veil that scrolls to the plans, and a non-clickable 'Coming soon' veil for things designed but not built. A numeric limit counts as locked unless it matches the top plan's.

features.name: Tips for your staff — designed, NOT built
features.whatItDoes: A tip jar on the venue's page going to the team rather than the act. Listed in VENUE_NOT_BUILT, so it is greyed as 'Coming soon' even for a venue paying for Pro, and there is no endpoint behind it.
features.whyRelevant: The Pro tier list literally says 'Coming soon, included: tips for your staff' — a copywriter must not turn that into a shipped feature.

features.name: Votes for what plays between the sets — designed, NOT built
features.whatItDoes: When no band is on, the room votes for what comes out of the venue's speakers. In VENUE_NOT_BUILT; greyed as 'Coming soon' on every plan.

features.name: Two printable QR codes: your page, and MySet
features.whatItDoes: Tap for a full-size printable card with a caption ('Connect with our performers') and the plain URL underneath, plus a 20x-scale link for printing. Only MySet's own URLs can ever be encoded and the slug is resolved server-side so a made-up one cannot be turned into a printable code.
features.whyRelevant: about.html's 'one code on the tables' — there are two offered, and the venue one points at the venue page, not a voting page.

features.name: Invite the acts to list their gigs here
features.whatItDoes: A share sheet with myset.vip/studio, telling the venue to give the acts the exact venue name and city so their gigs land automatically, and pointing them at the venue page where they tap 'I play here'.

features.name: Up to five sign-in addresses per venue
features.whatItDoes: The owner adds a manager or a barman by email; anyone added can sign in with their own code. The last remaining address can never be removed and the owner's row can never be deleted by anyone else. Removing someone kills their live sessions.

features.name: Three roles: owner, manager, crew — and everything new is owner-only by default
features.whatItDoes: Crew can read and reply to community posts and mark orders done. Managers can additionally edit the page, events, menu, offers, photos, merch and moderation. Money, plan, slug, staff and sessions are owner-only, and any action not explicitly listed is owner-only by construction.
features.whyRelevant: Shipped 2026-09-05 to close a real hole: a barman added on Tuesday could previously rename the page, link the payout account and sign the owner out.

features.name: There is no way to make anyone a manager
features.whatItDoes: The Settings field is labelled 'Add a manager or barman' but addStaff sends no role, so the server defaults every new sign-in to 'crew'. The roleSet endpoint exists but has no UI — and even called directly it applies the change and then returns a 400 'unknown action', because roleSet is missing from the action allow-list it falls through to.
features.whyRelevant: Never claim a venue can appoint managers — in the shipped UI every added person is crew.

features.name: Pinning a community post is accidentally owner-only
features.whatItDoes: The Studio shows a Pin button to everyone, but 'postPin' is absent from both CREW_OK and MANAGER_OK, so a manager or barman tapping Pin gets a 403 telling them to ask whoever owns the page.

features.name: Where you're signed in, and sign out one device or all of them
features.whatItDoes: Every phone and tablet with a live sign-in, labelled by device, with the date and the address used. Sign out this one, sign out one other, sign out our other devices, or sign out everywhere including this one. Signing out actually kills the token server-side, and the local clear happens whatever the network does.
features.planGate: owner (revokeAll); any role for own signOut

features.name: Download everything MySet holds about your venue
features.whatItDoes: One JSON file: the account row and its sign-in addresses, the full profile, every event, the community feed and the order list — with every buyer's device id stripped out.

features.name: Delete the page: offline today, gone in thirty days, undoable the whole time
features.whatItDoes: Two confirm screens then typing DELETE. The public page stops answering immediately and the city index is emptied, the subscription is cancelled that day, and nothing is erased for 30 days — the slug is held too, because it is on a Google listing and a printed menu. Undo restores everything including the calendar.

features.name: A page on its way out is read-only, not locked out
features.whatItDoes: While deletion is pending everything returns 423 with 'undo that in Settings and everything comes straight back' — except read, export, plan and undelete, so the owner can always reverse it.

features.name: Perry can set any venue's plan by hand
features.whatItDoes: Founder-only action to comp a venue onto Pro or drop it to free, which also clears a verified tick on the way down. Also a founder-only list of every venue with slug, city, verification state and join date.

features.name: Venues appear in the Google Sheet export
features.whatItDoes: A 'Venues' tab with name, id, page, email, city, country, plan and verification, plus paying-venue counts in the growth tab. Founder-only and off until env vars are set.

features.name: Fans can post video clips on a venue's community page
features.whatItDoes: The clip upload endpoint resolves a venue owner from ?v=<slug> exactly as it does an artist, so venue community pages take clips too — and a leaving venue's unattached clips are cleaned up.

features.name: There is no public list of venues
features.whatItDoes: /venues goes straight to the Venue Studio sign-in. A venue is discoverable through the city what's-on feed only via a row it owns (its own event) or an artist's gig row, and a venue page is not itself indexed anywhere as a venue.
features.whyRelevant: about.html's 'people searching what's on tonight find you' is only literally true for venue-run events.

trapsForCopy: THE TICK IS A PAID FEATURE. Verification requires a paid plan as check number one (netlify/functions/_verify.mjs:185-205, 300-301). about.html's venue section says 'your page works whether you verify it or not' but never says the tick itself costs $20/month. And the framing matters: paying does not buy the tick, it opens the door to being checked — the other four checks still have to pass.

THERE IS A $20/MONTH VENUE PRO TIER AND IT IS SELF-SERVE TODAY. about.html says only 'Claim your venue — free'. Stripe Checkout for venue Pro works (netlify/functions/venueadmin.mjs:415-420, netlify/functions/_billing.mjs:52). Two places in the shipped product still say the opposite — public/venue-studio.html:746-749 ('Venue Pro is NOT self-serve — there is no billing behind it') and the verification checklist at public/venue-studio.html:1456-1458 and the toast at :1504 ('Not self-serve yet: message us'). Those are stale strings, not the behaviour. Never repeat them.

THE PUBLIC PAGE TELLS ARTISTS 'NO WEBSITE NEEDED' AND THAT IS WRONG. public/venue.html:490 says three artists confirming 'does it — no website needed'. The verdict requires the website AND the domain email AND the site naming the venue AND the paid plan AND the three artists (netlify/functions/_verify.mjs:204-205). Vouches alone verify nothing. The no-website route is Perry checking it by hand (netlify/functions/admin.mjs:363-375).

THE AUTO-FILL MATCHES CITY AND COUNTRY AS EXACT STRINGS. The venue NAME is normalised (netlify/functions/_venues.mjs:197-208) but the city and country are compared with === (netlify/functions/venue.mjs:84) against a city index keyed on the raw typed strings (netlify/functions/_events.mjs:174-175). 'Koh Phangan' and 'koh phangan' are different towns to this code. That is why the Studio says the city has to match how artists write it (public/venue-studio.html:1105) — do not write copy implying it is fuzzy or forgiving.

THE AUTO-FILL NEEDS ALL THREE OF NAME, CITY AND COUNTRY OR IT RETURNS NOTHING AT ALL (netlify/functions/venue.mjs:71). A venue that claims a page and stops before filling in the country sees an empty what's-on and no explanation on the public page.

VENUE MERCH DOES NOT APPEAR ON THE VENUE PAGE. It only appears on /v/<slug>/community (public/community.html:222-231). public/venue.html renders no merch section at all, even though the API sends it (netlify/functions/_venues.mjs:430).
'WHO PLAYS HERE' ONLY APPEARS IF MORE THAN ONE ACT MATCHES (public/venue.html:445). A venue with exactly one regular act gets no such section.

A VENUE WITH NO EVENTS OF ITS OWN IS NOT CLICKABLE IN THE CITY FEED. On public/index.html the venue name is plain text in the 'where' line and the whole row links to the ARTIST's page (public/index.html:467,473; netlify/functions/events.mjs:83-84). Only a venue-run event produces a row that links to /v/<slug>. So 'locals looking for something to do find you' is true through your own events, and only indirectly through artists' gigs.
THERE IS NO PUBLIC VENUE DIRECTORY. /venues is the Venue Studio sign-in page (netlify.toml:51-53). Nobody browses a list of bars on MySet.

'ADD A MANAGER OR BARMAN' ONLY EVER ADDS A BARMAN. The Studio sends no role, so everyone lands as 'crew' (public/venue-studio.html:1735; netlify/functions/venueauth.mjs:163-167). The roleSet endpoint has no UI and, called directly, applies the change and then returns a 400 'unknown action' because it is missing from the allow-list at netlify/functions/venueauth.mjs:223. Do not promise venues they can appoint managers.

CREW CAN REPLY TO COMMUNITY POSTS BUT CANNOT HIDE ONE (netlify/functions/venueadmin.mjs:37-38). And nobody except the owner can PIN one, because 'postPin' is on neither list even though the Studio shows the button to everybody (netlify/functions/venueadmin.mjs:37-43 vs public/venue-studio.html:1047).

TIPS AND BETWEEN-THE-SETS VOTING DO NOT EXIST. They are in VENUE_NOT_BUILT (netlify/functions/_venues.mjs:140) and are greyed 'Coming soon' even on Pro. The Pro plan list in the Studio literally reads 'Coming soon, included' (public/venue-studio.html:804) — a copywriter lifting that bullet without the 'coming soon' half would be selling something with no code behind it.

MONEY IS NOT IN THE VENUE'S NUMBERS AND NEVER WILL BE (netlify/functions/_vstats.mjs:12-15). Do not write 'see what each act earned'. Also, any artist can switch their numbers off entirely (netlify/functions/_vstats.mjs:41), so 'every act's numbers' is not guaranteed.

'PEOPLE IN THE ROOM' MEANS PHONES THAT OPENED THE VOTING PAGE, not a headcount and not people who voted (netlify/functions/_vstats.mjs:53; public/venue-studio.html:1244). The Studio says this plainly and marketing must not upgrade it to attendance.

THE VENUE NUMBERS ONLY EXIST FOR NIGHTS WHERE MYSET WAS ACTUALLY RUNNING. They come from show history the artist created (netlify/functions/_vstats.mjs:22-45); a venue whose acts have never run a MySet show sees an empty Numbers tab with 'nothing to count yet' (public/venue-studio.html:1235-1237).

THE THREE-FREE-PHOTO CAP WAS ONLY ENFORCED ON 2026-09-05 (netlify/functions/venueadmin.mjs:331-347). Any venue that uploaded more than three before that has photos the record can still hold but the free plan will not let them replace. The cover photo is separate and free on every plan.

TWO CODE COMMENTS SHIPPED IN PRODUCTION SAY 'A VENUE HAS NO PAYOUT ACCOUNT' (netlify/functions/venueadmin.mjs:482-486 and public/venue-studio.html:1017-1019). They are stale. Venues have had full Stripe Connect payouts since 2026-09-04 (netlify/functions/venueadmin.mjs:380-404). Trust the endpoints, not the prose around them.

THE 2%/10% TRANSACTION FEE IS ON MERCH SOLD THROUGH THE APP ONLY — a venue has no votes or tips to sell (netlify/functions/pay.mjs:33-38). And the 'Stripe's fee shared evenly' line is an ESTIMATE at checkout, not an exact split; the real fee is only known after the charge settles (netlify/functions/_connect.mjs:69-74).

THE PAYOUT COUNTRY CANNOT BE CHANGED LATER. Stripe Express fixes it at account creation and the picker offers 22 countries only (netlify/functions/_connect.mjs:88-99; public/venue-studio.html:933-937,962).

EMAIL SIGN-IN IS OFF WITHOUT RESEND_API_KEY — the door returns a 503 'Email sign-in isn't switched on yet' (netlify/functions/venueauth.mjs:46), and the Studio surfaces 'codes can't go out' (public/venue-studio.html:1335). Do not promise instant sign-up unconditionally.
MAXIMUM FIVE SIGN-IN ADDRESSES PER VENUE (netlify/functions/venueauth.mjs:162), and the last one can never be removed (netlify/functions/venueauth.mjs:178).

THE PUBLIC PAGE'S HORIZON IS 60 DAYS, 60 ARTISTS PER CITY AND 200 ROWS, RENDERED AS AT MOST 14 DAY-GROUPS (netlify/functions/venue.mjs:17-18,40,46; public/venue.html:382). Do not write 'your whole diary, forever'.
A VENUE COMMUNITY POST CANNOT BE TAGGED TO A NIGHT — night picking is artist-only (netlify/functions/community.mjs:89,136,143).

HIDING A POST DELETES ITS PHOTOS AND CLIP. Un-hiding brings back the words only (netlify/functions/_community.mjs:295-303; the confirm text at public/venue-studio.html:1049 says so). 'Undoable' is true for the text and not for the pictures.

THE VENUE'S OWN EVENTS AND ARTISTS' GIGS ARE DIFFERENT THINGS ON THE PAGE. A venue event has a title and is tagged 'At the venue' and does not link anywhere; an artist's gig shows the act's name and links to their MySet page (public/venue.html:362,365,386-392). Only the artist row is clickable.

THE THREE-ARTIST BAR IS THREE, NOT FIVE OR TEN. MIN_VOUCHES is 3 (netlify/functions/_verify.mjs:30). public/venue.html:485 carries a dead fallback of 10 that would only show if the server sent nothing — never quote 10.
THE TESTIMONIALS IN THE VENUE PLAN SHEET ARE PLACEHOLDERS, marked as such in the data and in the visible text (public/venue-studio.html:807-813). Nothing there is a real quote from a real bar.

appCatalogue.surface: Plans, billing, payouts, fees and the ledger (MySet)
appCatalogue.summary: This is MySet's whole money surface: a three-tier artist plan ladder (Free/Plus $10/Pro $20) sold through real Stripe Billing subscriptions, a Stripe Connect Express payout system that makes each artist the merchant of record for their own tips/vote-packs/merch, a platform cut taken as a Stripe application fee (10% free / 2% Plus / 0% Pro), a separate $10-per-night "Featured show" placement bought by artists on any plan, and a read-only reporting layer that buckets Stripe balance transactions into monthly statements and a founder-only P&L. It is used by artists (in the Studio's Settings and Money tabs), by venues (Venue Studio, one Pro tier at $20), and by the founder alone for promo codes, feature flags, venue plans and MySet's own books. The headline finding: the landing page's three "honest notes" are now materially out of date — Plus/Pro checkout exists and is reachable (admin.mjs:79-85), and Connect onboarding is built and reachable for any artist (admin.mjs:1105-1123), so "card payments aren't on yet" and "Plus and Pro can't be bought yet" are both false as of the code. Several in-repo code comments (_pay.mjs:4-32, venue-studio.html:746-749, admin.mjs:308-309) are stale in the same direction and must not be trusted.
appCatalogue.structure:
Three artist-facing places, one venue-facing place, one founder-only place.

STUDIO → SETTINGS TAB ("Your plan"): a founder's letter explaining why there is a limit at all (studio.html:2321-2344), one green "Upgrade your plan" button opening a full-screen Plans sheet listing all three tiers in full with the transaction fee in orange (studio.html:3559-3578), a never-blank status line under it ("Free, forever" / "Renews 3 Oct · Card, invoices and receipts ↗" / "Pro, on the house until…") (studio.html:3720-3729), a promo-code box, and — for the founder only — code minting, flag switches, the venue list and the ID review queue. Upgrading leaves the site for Stripe Checkout and returns to /studio?sub=done&cs=…, which is confirmed server-side (studio.html:3615-3633). Leaving a paid plan is a two-step: "Are you sure you want to lose your … benefits?" then a one-time 50%-off-one-month retention offer (studio.html:3589-3607).

STUDIO → MONEY TAB: top card is "Getting paid" — either a country picker plus "Start with Stripe", or "Stripe still needs a few details" plus "Check again", or a green "Card payments are on ✓" with a Stripe dashboard link (studio.html:1551-1578). Below it: tonight's numbers, the fan feedback, "All payments · last 180 days" read live from Stripe with a red banner and a one-tap "Deliver them now" recovery for any undelivered purchase (studio.html:2138-2166), merch orders, "Your earnings · last 12 months" with a CSV download, then (founder only) "MySet's books" with hand-entered costs, then greyed "coming soon" previews of the four unbuilt Pro features.

STUDIO → GIGS TAB: a "★ Promote a gig" button and a sheet listing upcoming gigs with "2 of 3 spots left" per night; $10, Stripe Checkout, back to /studio?promoted=… (studio.html:1357-1430).

VENUE STUDIO (/venues): the same plan sheet with two tiers (Free / Pro $20), the same retention flow, the same Connect card, plus merch and the verification checklist.

FOUNDER-ONLY: /moneymodel, an interactive projections dashboard served by a function from outside the published folder behind a four-digit passcode (moneymodel.mjs:6-43, netlify.toml:12-13, 22-32).

A locked feature is never hidden — it renders greyed under a veil with a lock pill that says either "Plus feature" (tappable, scrolls to the plans) or "Coming soon" (not tappable), and one function decides both (studio.html:1274-1316).
appCatalogue.design: Everything money-shaped is one-tap and leaves the app for Stripe rather than collecting anything itself — MySet never sees a card or a bank detail (Express hosts the whole KYC flow, _connect.mjs:131-161).
