The consistent visual grammar: a "sec" strip header with a kicker on the left and a number on the right, then a list of rows, then a wide button. Plan cards list every tier in full every time, never "everything in Plus", and put the transaction fee in an orange <span class="fee"> and call it a fee (studio.html:3494-3549). Locked things are greyed with a padlock, never removed (Perry's rule), with the reason line sitting under the veil rather than inside it because a 43px row clips text (studio.html:1309-1315). Refusals name the plan and promise nothing is deleted: "Separate setlists are a Plus feature — everything you already have keeps working." (admin.mjs:736); "Deleting a post for good is a Plus feature — you can hide it on any plan, and hiding is instant and undoable." (admin.mjs:1291). The failed-card banner is deliberately suppressed over a live show unless the artist is in Settings, because a card warning at 11pm on stage is the wrong pixel at the wrong moment (studio.html:3691-3694). Money buttons are never shown to a room that cannot pay: canTakeMoney rides on every audience poll for free by reading a mirror on the show record (_pay.mjs:52-54, _connect.mjs:244-289). The room-size number is written as a soft ceiling, never a door: "a bigger night still runs, just a little calmer" (studio.html:3522).

features.name: Three artist plans — Free, Plus $10/mo, Pro $20/mo
features.whatItDoes: One table defines every limit and the platform's cut for each tier. Prices are in cents and the billing module reads them, so the pricing page and Stripe cannot drift.
features.whyRelevant: The prices and the cut ladder (10% / 2% / 0%) are the core commercial claim.

features.name: Four shows a month on Free

trapsForCopy: THE LANDING PAGE'S THREE HONEST NOTES ARE NOW TWO-THIRDS WRONG. Note 1 ("MySet is early, one real gig") still stands. Note 2 (about.html:654-657, "Card payments aren't on yet… no other artist can take money through MySet") is false: Stripe Connect Express onboarding is built and one tap from the Studio (admin.mjs:1105-1123, _connect.mjs:131-180, studio.html:1551-1613). Note 3 (about.html:658-660, "Plus and Pro can't be bought yet. There's no checkout") is false: planCheckout opens a real Stripe subscription Checkout (admin.mjs:79-85, _billing.mjs:120-161). The mid-page caveat at about.html:415-418 repeats note 2. Only the fourth sentence of note 3 — that promote/analytics/presskit/branding are unbuilt — is still accurate (_plan.mjs:130).

"2% cut" IS NOT "YOU KEEP 98%". These are direct charges, so Stripe's own ~2.9% + 30c is charged to the ARTIST on top of MySet's fee (_connect.mjs:30-35). On a $5 vote pack a Plus artist pays ~45c to Stripe and 10c to MySet. On Pro, "0% cut" still means Stripe takes ~2.9% + 30c. The Studio is required by code to say this (_connect.mjs:314-319); the landing page's Plus and Pro bullets (about.html:630, 640) do not.

THE FEE SPLIT IS VENUES ONLY. splitFee: true appears on both venue rows (_venues.mjs:131-132) and on NO artist row (_plan.mjs:17-111). Never write that MySet shares Stripe's card fee with artists. And even for venues it moves no money today — venue merch is Pro-only at 2%, and half of Stripe's fee exceeds 2% of anything under about $29, so the fee is already zero at checkout (_feesplit.mjs:42-47).

"PROMOTE" MEANS TWO COMPLETELY DIFFERENT THINGS. The Pro plan flag `promote` — "List shows in cities you don't normally play" — is in NOT_BUILT and is greyed as Soon for everybody including Pro (_plan.mjs:130, about.html:645). The "★ Promote a gig" button in the Studio is the $10-per-night Featured show, which is LIVE, available to Free artists, and not plan-gated at all (admin.mjs:1452-1500). Conflating them in copy would either oversell an unbuilt feature or hide a live one.

THE $10 FEATURED SHOW IS A REVENUE LINE THE LANDING PAGE HAS NEVER HEARD OF. Three spots per city per night, first come first served, on any plan, behind a flag that defaults ON (_flags.mjs:38-49, _featured.mjs:40-41). It shipped 2026-09-05 in commits 81f5b44 and 99f0db8, the same day the landing page was last edited. It also has no "paid placement" disclosure in the public city feed (index.html:485-486) — so do not describe that feed as purely organic.

FREE'S 10% CUT DOES NOT APPLY TO MERCH. Merch is a Plus feature and the checkout refuses it on Free (pay.mjs:120-121), so a free artist's 10% only ever touches tips and vote packs. The landing page's Plus bullet "2% cut instead of 10% — tips, vote sales and merch stay yours" (about.html:630) implies free artists sell merch at 10%. Same trap on the venue side: venue Free's 10% row is unreachable because venue merch is Pro-only (_venues.mjs:131, pay.mjs:46).

THE FOUNDER'S EXPERIENCE IS NOT THE PRODUCT. isPlatformOwner bypasses the gig cap, the room cap, the merch gate, the pricing gate and the moderation gate, charges on the platform account with NO application fee, and never sees the Get-paid card (_plan.mjs:154-161, _lifecycle.mjs:42, 55, pay.mjs:168-181, studio.html:1554). Two comments in the repo disagree about whether he is comped to Pro or reads as Free (_plan.mjs:120-123 vs admin.mjs:1703-1704) — the code truth is that the OWNER BYPASS, not a plan row, is what gives him everything.

PLUS DOES NOT ADD SIGN-IN SEATS. Free and Plus are both 1 seat; only Pro has 5 (_plan.mjs:65, 89, 107, enforced at auth.mjs:391-398). The landing page correctly lists "Five sign-ins for your band" only under Pro — keep it that way.

A LAPSED PLAN DELETES NOTHING, BUT TWO THINGS GO DARK. Merch comes off the community page (community.mjs:73) and the verification tick disappears (profile.mjs:22-27), both AND-ed with the plan on every public read. Songs, gigs, history, photos, setlists and community posts all stay. "Nothing gets deleted" is safe to say; "nothing changes" is not.

THE ROOM SIZE IS A BILLING LINE, NOT A DOOR. Nobody is ever turned away past 200/1,000/2,000 — the poll interval lengthens and the leaderboard shortens (show.mjs:32-43). Never write "up to 200 people" as a hard limit; the Studio's careful phrasing is "a bigger night still runs, just a little calmer" (studio.html:3522). Pro's number came DOWN from 3,000 to 2,000 on 2026-09-05 (commit 9e9fde4) because the load arithmetic was wrong.

VENUE PRO IS SELF-SERVE, WHATEVER THE COMMENTS SAY. venue-studio.html:746-749 says "Venue Pro is NOT self-serve — there is no billing behind it", admin.mjs:308-309 says "There is no venue self-serve billing yet", and the venue verify toast says "message us to switch it on" (venue-studio.html:1504). All three are stale: the Buy button is at venue-studio.html:820 and the endpoint at venueadmin.mjs:415-420. Equally, _pay.mjs:4-38 still carries a long comment insisting Connect "is not built" and "returns false for everyone today" — the code directly beneath it reads a real connect document. Never quote a comment on this surface.

THE REFERRAL FREE MONTH IS BUILT AND UNADVERTISED — AND CONDITIONAL. rewardReferrer gives the referrer 30 days when a referral goes paid (_plan.mjs:216-242), but it is called only from finishCheckout, the browser's return trip (_billing.mjs:214-217), and NOT from the subscription webhook. If the new subscriber closes the tab, the referrer gets nothing. The Studio's invite card never mentions the month at all (studio.html:2414-2419).

ONLY 22 COUNTRIES CAN GET PAID, AND THE CHOICE IS PERMANENT. PAYOUT_COUNTRIES is an explicit allow-list (_connect.mjs:94-95) and an Express account's country cannot be changed afterwards (admin.mjs:1109-1114). Do not imply worldwide payouts.

MYSET DOES NOT DO REFUNDS FOR FANS. The only automatic refund anywhere is for a Featured-show spot that could not be given (_featured.mjs:320). Tips, vote packs and merch are refunded by the artist in their own Stripe dashboard (studio.html:2165). The strong claim available here is DELIVERY — "a payment taken is a payment delivered", with three independent recovery paths (_pay.mjs:56-148) — not refunds.

MONEY BUTTONS ARE OWNER-ONLY AND BOOKS ARE OWNER-ONLY. A band mate on one of five Pro seats can run the show but cannot open the Stripe portal, change the plan, burn the retention offer, start Connect onboarding, buy a Featured spot, or see the earnings statement (admin.mjs:1578-1590). "Five sign-ins for your band" should not be read as five people who can see the money.

THE PAST-DUE BANNER HAS A LIVE COPY BUG. studio.html:3705 reads PLAN.plans.free.gigsPerMonth and .cutPct, but shapeLimits emits gigs and cut (admin.mjs:393-407), so the day-before-downgrade warning renders "undefined shows a month" and "MySet's cut goes back to undefined%". Worth fixing before anyone screenshots it.

appCatalogue.surface: Accounts, sign-in, sessions and security (artist + venue)
appCatalogue.summary: MySet has exactly one kind of account: an artist page, or a venue page. Fans never sign in anywhere — vote.html and community.html have no email field at all, only a random device id in localStorage (public/vote.html:287-289) — and that is the load-bearing design decision the whole product rests on. Artists sign in with an email and a six-digit code (no password anywhere, no Google/Apple/OAuth), and on top of that there are four more doors that most artists will never see: a Face ID / Touch ID passkey, eight one-time recovery codes, a per-page "studio code" typed with the page name, and the founder's master ADMIN_CODE env var. A session is a 30-day signed token carrying a device id, so "sign out" genuinely revokes; there is a device list, a per-device sign-out, seats for a band (1 on Free and Plus, 5 on Pro), owner/member/crew roles, a two-code flow to move your sign-in address, and a delete that goes dark on day one and only erases 30 days later. Almost all of this landed in three commits on 2026-09-05 (931d18d, 7ee4827, 81f5b44) — the landing page has never heard of any of it.
appCatalogue.structure:
TWO ENTRY POINTS. myset.vip/studio (and /signup, which is the same file — netlify.toml:41-44) is the Artist Studio; myset.vip/venues is the Venue Studio. Both are single HTML files that render a sign-in "gate" until a token exists.

THE ARTIST GATE (public/studio.html:940-1016) has four modes drawn into one div. Mode "start" is the default and is NOT a single email box — it stacks, top to bottom: an optional "Sign in with Face ID" button (only rendered when this browser has a remembered page name), an email box with "Email me a code", then a second pair of boxes — page name + studio code — with "Unlock with code", then a text link "Lost your email? Use a recovery code". Mode "code" is the six-digit box. Mode "name" is one box, "What should we call you?", with the button "Create my page". Mode "recover" is page name + XXXX-XXXX.

THE SIGN-UP PATH IS EXACTLY THREE SCREENS: email → code → name. There is no fourth step, no card, no page-address picker, no plan choice. The page address is derived from the name by pickSlug (_auth.mjs:91-103) and the toast says "Welcome — your page is myset.vip/<slug>". After that you land in the Studio's Live tab with an empty library.

INSIDE, EVERYTHING ACCOUNT-SHAPED LIVES IN THE SETTINGS TAB (public/studio.html:2394-2520), in this order: Your public page (rename), Codes to print, Invite another musician (referral link), "Who can sign in" (the seats list + add box, greyed at the plan cap), "Signing in" (four rows: Password — you don't have one · Face ID · Studio code · Recovery codes), Starting by itself, Show, "Your account" (your sign-in address + Change · Where you're signed in · Download my data · Invoices), then Sign out of this device / Sign out everywhere, then Delete my account, then "If something looks wrong" (Reload / Clear what's stored on this phone).

THE VENUE STUDIO is a thinner twin: email → code → name + city + country (public/venue-studio.html:392-400, four fields not three). It has sessions, sign-out, seats and account export/delete — and no passkeys, no recovery codes, no studio code and no email change.
appCatalogue.design:
Everything is one file per surface with inline CSS and JS, deliberately (netlify.toml:110-116 explains why 'unsafe-inline' is still in the CSP). The gate is a centred card with a big black primary button, a hairline "or" divider between doors, and 12.5px grey helper text. The six-digit box is 26px with .3em letter-spacing and `autocomplete="one-time-code"`, so iOS offers the code from the SMS/mail banner. Recovery codes render in a monospace block at 1.9 line-height inside a bottom sheet, because they get copied or written down.

Two interaction rules worth stealing for copy. First, locked things are shown, never hidden — the seats box greys with a caption "Your plan has 1 sign-in. Pro has 5." (studio.html:2434-2439) rather than disappearing. Second, destructive things take two screens: delete is a sheet saying "Keep my account" / "Yes, delete my account", then a second sheet that makes you type DELETE (studio.html:3644-3656).

The tone is plain and non-shaming throughout: "No password to forget — we email you a code each time", "You don't have one", "That's the only way in — add another address first." Security emails are plain paragraphs, not code boxes — sendNotice (_auth.mjs:295-316) exists because sending a "your address changed" mail through the code template produced an email that was a giant empty box.

Sessions show a device CLASS ("iPhone · Safari"), never a raw User-Agent and never an IP or a city (_session.mjs:116-125). The current device is labelled "This phone". The whole system is designed to add zero reads to the audience poll — revocation is a normally-absent `dead` map on a registry row the verifier already holds (_session.mjs:22-35).

features.name: Sign up in three steps: email, a six-digit code, your name
features.whatItDoes: Type an email, get a six-digit code, type the code, type your name. That creates the artist, the page address and the first sign-in in one atomic write, and drops you into the Studio.
features.whyRelevant: The landing page's central setup claim. Mechanically it is true — three fields and no fourth step — but see trapsForCopy for the two things that can stretch the two minutes.

features.name: One button for both signing in and signing up
features.whatItDoes: There is no separate sign-up form. The same 'Email me a code' button serves new and returning artists; whether an account exists is only answered after you prove you own the inbox.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/auth.mjs:47-67 (identical response either way); auth.mjs:79-82 (needName is decided at verify, not at start); public/studio.html:988-989
features.whyRelevant: Removes a decision from the funnel, and it is a real privacy property: the door cannot be used to discover which emails have MySet accounts.

features.name: There is no password
features.whatItDoes: MySet never sets, stores or asks for a password. Settings has a permanent row saying so: 'Password — You don't have one.'
features.whyRelevant: Answers 'what's my password / forgot password' before it is asked, and is a genuine security posture claim.

features.name: No Google or Apple sign-in
features.whatItDoes: Deliberately absent. Email plus a code was chosen over OAuth so there is no consent screen, no Google Cloud project, no verification review, and it works for people with no Google account.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/_auth.mjs:6-9 (the reasoning); verified absent — no OAuth code path exists in netlify/functions/ except the Google Sheets service account in _sheets.mjs
features.whyRelevant: Never imply a social sign-in exists. A copywriter reaching for 'sign in with Google' would be inventing it.

features.name: The code works for ten minutes, once
features.whatItDoes: A six-digit code expires after ten minutes and is burned the moment it succeeds. Five wrong guesses kill it too.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/_auth.mjs:11-14 (CODE_TTL, MAX_TRIES); _auth.mjs:249-263 (checkCode burns on success and at the try cap); the email itself says it at _auth.mjs:278
features.whyRelevant: Exact numbers a copywriter can safely quote; they are stated in the sign-in email and on the code screen.

features.name: Five codes per address per hour
features.whatItDoes: A sixth code request inside an hour is silently dropped — the server still answers 'sent' and no email goes out.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/_auth.mjs:15 (MAX_SENDS=5), _auth.mjs:233-245; the silent path is netlify/functions/auth.mjs:64
features.whyRelevant: A support and copy hazard: somebody who keeps tapping 'resend' is told a code is coming and gets nothing. Never write 'tap again if it doesn't arrive'.

features.name: Every sign-in door answers the same for a stranger
features.whatItDoes: An unknown email, an unknown page name, a locked-out page and a wrong code all get byte-identical responses, so none of the doors can be used to find out who has a MySet account.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/auth.mjs:11-14, 47-67 (email door), auth.mjs:137-142 (passkey door), auth.mjs:166-170 (recovery door); netlify/functions/_lib.mjs:993-996 (studio-code door); auth.mjs:304-305 (email change)
features.whyRelevant: A real, tested security property most small SaaS gets wrong. SECURITY.md:57 lists it as one of the things that would surprise a reviewer.

features.name: Your page address is chosen for you from your name
features.whatItDoes: Signing up does not ask for a URL. pickSlug turns the name into a free slug, appending 2, 3, 4… on a clash, skipping a reserved list and anything already used as an artist id.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/_auth.mjs:91-103 (pickSlug), _auth.mjs:65-72 (cleanSlug + RESERVED), _auth.mjs:129 (aid derived from slug); the client never sends a slug — public/studio.html:1093
features.whyRelevant: Keeps the three-step claim true. Do not write 'pick your address' as a signup step — it is a Settings action afterwards.

features.name: Rename your page and the old address still works
features.whatItDoes: Changing your page name keeps the old name pointing at the same page for ever, and nobody else can claim it while it is held — so printed QR codes and Instagram bios keep landing in the right room.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/auth.mjs:436-461 (setSlug writes a.oldSlug); netlify/functions/_auth.mjs:74-83 (artistBySlug reads it); public/studio.html:3784-3789; the Studio says so at studio.html:2397
features.whyRelevant: A specific, unusual, physical-world benefit — printed table tents outlive a rename — that no competitor bothers to say out loud.

features.name: Invite another musician with your own link
features.whatItDoes: Settings hands you myset.vip/signup?ref=<yourslug>, counts how many signed up through it, and lists their names. The referrer is recorded at signup and never editable afterwards.
features.whereInCode: public/studio.html:2414-2419 (the link and the count); netlify/functions/_auth.mjs:132-137 (referredBy recorded); netlify/functions/auth.mjs:465,472-473 (invited/invitedNames)
features.whyRelevant: There is a real reward attached: a referral going paid gives the referrer a free month (_plan.mjs:218-241) — but only through the promo-code path today.

features.name: Where you came from survives the trip to your inbox
features.whatItDoes: ?ref= and ?src= (or utm_source/utm_medium, or the referring host) are stashed in localStorage on the first visit and read back at 'claim', because signing up means leaving for an email and coming back with a bare URL.
features.whereInCode: public/studio.html:1072-1084 (firstTouch); public/studio.html:1085-1092 (read at claim); netlify/functions/_auth.mjs:110-120 (cleanSource rejects anything URL-shaped)
features.whyRelevant: Means a landing-page A/B test can actually be measured. Also a privacy promise in code: no full URL, no query string, no path is ever kept.

features.name: Stay signed in for thirty days
features.whatItDoes: A session token is an HMAC of email|expiry|revision|deviceId, good for 30 days, kept in localStorage. No cookie.
features.whyRelevant: The honest counterweight to 'a code every time' — you do not type a code at every gig, only about once a month.

features.name: See every phone and laptop you're signed in on
features.whatItDoes: A sheet listing each live sign-in as a device class ('iPhone · Safari'), when it signed in, and which email it used. The one you are holding says 'This phone'.
features.whyRelevant: Answers 'did somebody else get into my page?' — which ACCOUNTS.md:127 says was previously unanswerable.

features.name: Sign one device out, instantly
features.whatItDoes: Kills a single session server-side by adding its device id to a kill list on the account row; the token stays validly signed and the verifier refuses it.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/auth.mjs:257-263; netlify/functions/_session.mjs:78-104 (killSessions); _auth.mjs:216-218 (the check on every request)
features.whyRelevant: Before 2026-09-05 'sign out' cleared localStorage and told the server nothing, so a copied token worked for the rest of its 30 days (_session.mjs:9-14). This is a fixed hole, not a new toy.

features.name: Sign out my other devices
features.whatItDoes: One button kills every session except the one you are on.
features.whyRelevant: The realistic version of 'I left it signed in on the bar's iPad'.

features.name: Sign out everywhere, including this one
features.whatItDoes: Bumps the account's revision counter, which invalidates every token ever issued for the page. Confirmed with a browser confirm() that warns you will need a code to get back in.
features.whyRelevant: Note the revision is now PER ARTIST. It used to be one global counter, so any signed-up stranger could sign out every artist and every venue on the platform (_auth.mjs:205-212).

features.name: Twenty devices, then the oldest is properly signed out
features.whatItDoes: Past twenty live sessions the oldest is evicted from the list AND killed, so the list never says a device is gone while its token still works. Past twelve kill-list entries the whole account is signed out instead of quietly un-revoking one.
features.whyRelevant: A band on a Pro page with five people and several devices each can hit this. 'More revocation than was asked for is the safe way to fail.'

features.name: "Last opened Settings", not "last used"
features.whatItDoes: A session's freshness timestamp moves at most once an hour, and only when the Studio calls the sessions or team endpoints — so it is deliberately labelled by what it actually measures.
features.whyRelevant: Do not write 'see when each device was last used'. The number only moves when Settings is opened, and the code says printing it as 'last used' would be a number that lies. The sessions sheet does not currently render it at all.

features.name: Sign in with Face ID, Touch ID or Windows Hello
features.whatItDoes: Add a passkey from Settings. The private key never leaves the phone; MySet keeps only the public half. Up to eight devices per account, each with a label and a 'last used' date, each removable.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/_passkey.mjs (whole file; MAX_KEYS=8 at :46, register at :188-223); netlify/functions/auth.mjs:226-253; public/studio.html:3878-3938; Settings row at studio.html:2454-2460
features.planGate: owner only — auth.mjs:211-215 puts passkeyStart/Finish/List/Forget in OWNER_ONLY
features.flagGate: none — the gate is browser support (PKSUPPORTED, studio.html:3878)
features.whyRelevant: The strongest single sign-in claim MySet has, it is real, it is tested against a real P-256 key pair (test/passkeys.mjs), and the about page has never mentioned it. Written with no npm dependency at all.

features.name: The Face ID button on the sign-in screen
features.whatItDoes: A one-tap door on the gate. It needs to know WHICH page before it can ask the phone, so the button only renders once this browser has a remembered page name.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/auth.mjs:133-159; public/studio.html:977-984 (conditional render), studio.html:3940-3964 (passkeySignIn); the page name is remembered at studio.html:3889
features.planGate: none to use; only an owner can have created the key
features.whyRelevant: The button is invisible to a brand-new signup and to anyone who has never opened the Settings tab on that browser — 'myset.slug' is only written inside loadPasskeys(), which only runs on a tap into Settings, not on a reload that lands there (studio.html:938 vs 1615).

features.name: A copied passkey is refused
features.whatItDoes: If an authenticator's signature counter goes backwards, sign-in is refused with 'That key looks copied.' Counters that are zero on both sides — which is what iCloud and Google synced passkeys always report — are allowed.
features.whyRelevant: The kind of detail that proves the passkey implementation is not a toy, if a technical reader ever asks.

features.name: Eight one-time recovery codes
features.whatItDoes: Generate eight XXXX-XXXX codes in a no-0/O, no-1/I/L alphabet, shown exactly once with a Copy button. Settings shows a live count: '6 of 8 unused'. Making new ones kills the old set immediately.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/_session.mjs:190-234 (makeRecovery/recoveryStatus/useRecovery); netlify/functions/auth.mjs:281-286; public/studio.html:3966-3984; Settings row at studio.html:2464-2466
features.planGate: owner only — recoveryMake is in OWNER_ONLY (auth.mjs:211). recoveryStatus is not.
features.whyRelevant: This is MySet's honest answer to 'what if I lose my email', and the landing page does not mention it. The alphabet choice exists because these get written on the back of a setlist in a dark room.

features.name: Sign in with a recovery code when your inbox is gone
features.whatItDoes: On the gate, 'Lost your email? Use a recovery code' takes your page name and one code. It burns the code, signs every other device out, gives this device a fresh session, and emails everyone on the account that it happened.
features.whyRelevant: Note it also opens the OWNER's session, not the session of whoever's recovery code it was, and it signs the whole band out. That is a support-visible consequence.

features.name: A studio code for when email is slow
features.whatItDoes: Set an 8+ character code for your page. Then the gate's third door — page name plus code — gets you in from any phone without waiting for an email. Stored hashed. A deny-list refuses 'password', repeated characters, and your own page name.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/_lib.mjs:953-964 (MIN_CODE=8, weakCode), _lib.mjs:966-1006 (requireArtist's code door); netlify/functions/admin.mjs:1958-1969 (setCode); public/studio.html:3810-3831; the gate boxes at studio.html:994-999
features.planGate: owner only — 'setCode' is in admin.mjs OWNER_ONLY (admin.mjs:1581)
features.whyRelevant: Exists because Perry could not get into his own Studio during a gig on 2026-08-30 (_lib.mjs:899-903). That story is the reason, and it is a good one. Note it grants FULL OWNER rights (_lib.mjs:1002).

features.name: The founder's master key
features.whatItDoes: The ADMIN_CODE environment variable signs in as the founding artist, is checked before any lockout, and cannot be shut out.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/_lib.mjs:979-984; the Studio tells only the founder it exists — public/studio.html:3816-3818
features.whyRelevant: Never mention on a marketing page. It also means the founding account has a door no other artist has.

features.name: Ten wrong tries locks the code doors for fifteen minutes
features.whatItDoes: Ten failures inside fifteen minutes shuts the studio-code door AND the recovery-code door for that page for fifteen minutes. A locked-out page answers exactly like a wrong code.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/_lib.mjs:931-951 (LOCK_TRIES=10, LOCK_WINDOW/LOCK_FOR=15min, codeLocked/noteCodeFailure); used by netlify/functions/auth.mjs:169-171 and _lib.mjs:998,1004
features.whyRelevant: The lock is ONE shared counter per page (lock_<aid>). Fumbling recovery codes locks you out of the studio code too, and vice versa. Email sign-in is unaffected.

features.name: Move your account to a new email address
features.whatItDoes: Two proofs, never one: a code to the new address and a code to the old one (or a recovery code instead of the second). The old inbox is warned the moment the request is made, not at the end. One change per 24 hours.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/auth.mjs:288-368; public/studio.html:3986-4011; the 24-hour rule at auth.mjs:301-302
features.whyRelevant: Before this there was literally no way to do it on Free or Plus, because the documented workaround was add-then-remove and that needs Pro seats. Unavailable if you signed in with the studio code — the flow needs an inbox to move (auth.mjs:297).

features.name: Five sign-ins for your band
features.whatItDoes: Add other email addresses that can sign in to the same page. Free and Plus allow one; Pro allows five. Over the cap the add box is greyed with 'Your plan has 1 sign-in. Pro has 5.' and the server answers 402.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/_plan.mjs:65,89,107 (seats: 1 / 1 / 5); netlify/functions/auth.mjs:387-411 (the add + cap); public/studio.html:2430-2445 (the greying); public/about.html:641 claims it

features.name: Owner, member and crew
features.whatItDoes: Three roles. Owner does everything including money and access. Member runs the page and the show but never moves money. Crew is tonight only — run the show and see the requests. An unrecognised role falls back to crew.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/_session.mjs:236-263 (the CAN table); enforced at netlify/functions/admin.mjs:1594-1600 and auth.mjs:211-218; roleSet at auth.mjs:371-384

'Crew' is unreachable through the app.

features.name: Money and the account are the owner's alone

features.name: You can never remove the last way in
features.whatItDoes: Removing sign-in addresses refuses if it would leave none ('That's the only way in — add another address first'), refuses the owner's row, and refuses your own address with a pointer to 'change my sign-in address' instead.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/auth.mjs:412-431; the venue twin at netlify/functions/venueauth.mjs:178-181

features.name: An activity log for the account
features.whatItDoes: Every sign-in, code sent, seat added or removed, role changed, recovery code made or used, address moved, passkey added or removed, and deletion started or cancelled is recorded — capped at 100 entries, never an IP, never a fan id, never an amount.

features.name: Download everything MySet holds about you
features.whatItDoes: One button produces a JSON file with the account, profile, show, songs, gigs, setlists, songs-to-learn, every archived night, tips, orders, community posts and feedback. A fan's device id is never in it.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/_account.mjs:26-48 (exportArtist); netlify/functions/admin.mjs:116-119; public/studio.html:3634-3642; Settings row at studio.html:2492
features.planGate: owner only — accountExport is in admin.mjs OWNER_ONLY (admin.mjs:1580), despite CAN.member listing 'export' (_session.mjs:252)
features.whyRelevant: A GDPR-shaped promise that is actually kept, and it keeps working while an account is mid-deletion (admin.mjs:1558).

features.whatItDoes: Sheet one: 'Keep my account' / 'Yes, delete my account'. Sheet two: type DELETE. The server refuses anything else.
features.whereInCode: public/studio.html:3644-3663; netlify/functions/admin.mjs:124-126 (confirm !== 'DELETE' is refused, and non-owners are refused)
features.whyRelevant: Perry asked for exactly this. It replaced a single sheet that erased everything inside one request with no undo.

features.name: Thirty days to change your mind, and nothing is moved
features.whatItDoes: On day one the page, the voting screen and the community page go dark, the plan is cancelled so you stop being charged, any running show is filed, and the calendar leaves the city listings. Not one document is copied or erased. A banner on every tab says the date and offers 'Undo, keep my page'. A cron erases it a month later.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/_account.mjs:80-153 (DELETE_GRACE_MS=30 days, startDeletion, cancelDeletion); netlify/functions/_lib.mjs:1016-1031 (publicArtist 404s the page); public/studio.html:3678-3688 (leavingBar); the purge at netlify/functions/autocron.mjs:60-71
features.whyRelevant: 'Nothing is deleted, everything comes back with one tap' is a strong trust line, and the landing page does not have it. Sessions are deliberately NOT killed, so the owner can always get back in to undo.

features.name: Your page address is held while you're leaving
features.whatItDoes: During the thirty days nobody else can take your page name, because QR codes on bar tables point at it. There is a separate deliberate link in the banner — 'Free up my page address now' — with a warning that undoing would then need a new address.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/_account.mjs:96-102 (the reasoning), _account.mjs:155-168 (freeSlug), _account.mjs:138-142 (it comes back on undo if nobody took it); public/studio.html:3670-3676, 3686
features.whyRelevant: Same physical-world reasoning as the rename. Undo tells you honestly if the address was taken while it was free.

features.name: An account on its way out is read-only, not locked out
features.whatItDoes: While a deletion is pending, every Studio action except undo, export, the plan, the billing portal and the tax ledger answers with 423 and one sentence that tells you the way back.
features.whyRelevant: Somebody thirty days out can still pull their tax records, which is exactly what they come back for.

features.name: The founding account cannot be deleted
features.whatItDoes: startDeletion and deleteArtist both refuse the DEFAULT_ARTIST id outright.
features.whyRelevant: Also means publicArtist short-circuits for the bare address with no lookup at all (_lib.mjs:1018-1023) — a cost decision hanging off an identity fact.

features.name: MySet emails everyone on the account when something serious happens
features.whatItDoes: Plain-text notices go out for: a recovery code being used (to every address on the page), an address-change request (to the OLD inbox, at request time, while there is still time to act), the change completing (to both), and a deletion starting (to everyone, with the date).
features.whyRelevant: Warning the old inbox at REQUEST time rather than at the end is the specific choice that stops a stolen session walking off with the page.

features.name: The sign-in code email
features.whatItDoes: A single large code on a grey card, addressed by artist name, saying it works for ten minutes and once. Sent through Resend.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/_auth.mjs:266-291; the from address is process.env.AUTH_FROM with a fallback to 'MySet <onboarding@resend.dev>' at _auth.mjs:268
features.flagGate: none — but the whole email door 503s if RESEND_API_KEY is unset (auth.mjs:54-55)
features.whyRelevant: MYSET.md:1030-1033 and :1123-1124 say AUTH_FROM is not set, so codes go out from Resend's shared onboarding@resend.dev rather than a myset.vip address — a deliverability and trust risk for the first stranger who signs up. The code confirms the fallback exists; whether the env var is now set cannot be read from the repo.

features.name: Fans never make an account
features.whatItDoes: No sign-up, no email, no password, no app. A phone gets a random id in its own localStorage and that is the entire identity. Nothing on the fan-facing pages asks for an email address.
features.whereInCode: public/vote.html:287-289 (fanId), vote.html:21 ('No app, no account'); public/community.html:185-188; verified: zero 'email' matches in vote.html, artist.html, index.html, community.html
features.whyRelevant: Already the landing page's biggest claim (about.html:374-375, 673-674) and it is completely true in code. SECURITY.md:56 puts it as 'there is no fan database to breach'.

features.name: A fan can put a name on a community post, and nowhere else
features.whatItDoes: The community page has one optional 'Your name (optional)' box on the post composer. It is a display label typed each time, not an account.
features.whyRelevant: The only place a fan volunteers anything about themselves. It is not stored against a person and does not persist as an identity.

features.name: A merch buyer's name and email come live from Stripe, and are never stored
features.whatItDoes: Opening an order's detail asks Stripe for the buyer's name, email and shipping address on the spot. MySet keeps none of it.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/admin.mjs:1310-1325; the export strips the device id at netlify/functions/_account.mjs:44
features.whyRelevant: The one nuance to 'we never know who your fans are' — for a merch order, the artist can see who bought it, because a shipping address has to come from somewhere. Stripe holds it, not MySet.

features.name: Venues sign in the same way, in their own world
features.whatItDoes: Email plus a six-digit code in a separate realm: separate registry, separate token tag ('v|…'), separate code key. The same address can run an artist page and a venue page without either reaching the other.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/venueauth.mjs:1-91; the token tag at netlify/functions/_venues.mjs:104-113, 151-181; public/venue-studio.html:417-441
features.whyRelevant: Venue signup is FOUR fields, not three: email → code → name + city + country (venue-studio.html:392-400). The 'two minutes, three steps' copy is the artist path only.

features.name: Five sign-ins for a venue, on every plan
features.whatItDoes: A venue can add up to five email addresses regardless of plan — the cap is hard-coded, not a plan limit.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/venueauth.mjs:162 (mine.length >= 5); VENUE_PLANS has no seats key at all — netlify/functions/_venues.mjs:130-133
features.whyRelevant: Do not copy the artist ladder across. A free venue gets what only a Pro artist gets.

features.name: The Venue Studio has no passkeys, no recovery codes and no way to move its email
features.whatItDoes: A venue gets sessions, sign-out, seats, rename, export and delete — and nothing else. Its only door is a code to an address in the registry.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/venueauth.mjs (no passkey/recovery/emailChange actions exist); confirmed absent from public/venue-studio.html; ACCOUNTS.md:334 lists 'passkeys in the Venue Studio' as item 1 of what is next
features.whyRelevant: A venue that loses its inbox has no self-service way back in. Never write account-security copy that covers 'artists and venues' in one sentence.

features.name: Changing a venue person's role reports failure after succeeding
features.whatItDoes: venueauth's roleSet performs the mutation, then falls through to a final allow-list that does not contain 'roleSet', so it answers 'unknown action' — after the role has already changed.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/venueauth.mjs:123-136 (the mutation), then venueauth.mjs:223-224 (the fall-through refusal)
features.whyRelevant: Nothing in public/ calls it, so nobody has hit it — but it is not a safe thing to describe as working.

features.name: Venues can take their data and leave, with the same thirty days
features.whatItDoes: Export as JSON, and a marked deletion with a thirty-day window purged by the same cron, keyed v_<venueId>.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/_venueaccount.mjs:22-43 (export), :88-127 (startVenueDeletion / cancelVenueDeletion); the shared queue at netlify/functions/_account.mjs:173-190
features.planGate: none stated in venueadmin for these
features.whyRelevant: Until 2026-09-05 a venue could sign up, put a page up, take money and pay for Pro, and had no way out except emailing Perry.

features.name: Clear what's stored on this phone — without signing out
features.whatItDoes: Throws away every service-worker cache and tells the worker to unregister, then reloads. It deliberately leaves the sign-in token alone, because in an installed app with no address bar this is the only way to fix a stale copy mid-gig.
features.whyRelevant: 'You stay signed in' is stated twice on purpose. Good support copy; not a marketing feature.

features.name: The site's own hardening
features.whatItDoes: HSTS preloaded for a year across all subdomains, a Content-Security-Policy whose connect-src is 'self' so a stolen token has nowhere to send itself, nosniff, SAMEORIGIN framing, and camera/mic/location/payment all denied.
features.whyRelevant: Real and unusual for a project this size. The comment at netlify.toml:110-116 is honest that the policy does not stop an injected inline script, only its ability to load or exfiltrate anything.

features.name: None of this is behind a feature flag
features.whatItDoes: The flag system has exactly two flags — voteFinal and featuredShows — and neither touches sign-in, sessions, roles or deletion.
features.whyRelevant: Everything catalogued here is on for everyone right now; there is no switch to worry about when writing copy.

features.name: Session timezone and "installed app" label are accepted and never sent
features.whatItDoes: The server records a session's timezone and can label a device as 'installed app' — but neither Studio sends body.tz or body.standalone, so tz is always empty and the installed-app label can never be produced. The sessions sheet does not render tz either.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/auth.mjs:24-26 and venueauth.mjs:21-23 accept them; _session.mjs:123 uses standalone; grep confirms no tz/standalone in any sign-in call in public/studio.html or public/venue-studio.html
features.whyRelevant: Do not write 'see the timezone each device signed in from'. It is always blank.

features.name: The "Welcome, your page is…" toast on the code screen never fires
features.whatItDoes: verify returns isNew from a pending name that is never set, because issueCode is only ever called without one. The client's isNew branch is unreachable; the real welcome comes from the claim path instead.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/auth.mjs:88 (isNew: !!got.name); netlify/functions/_auth.mjs:226,242 (pendingName); all four callers pass null or nothing — auth.mjs:63,306,307 and venueauth.mjs:49; public/studio.html:1106
features.whyRelevant: Harmless, but it means the only welcome message a new artist sees is the one after typing their name.

trapsForCopy: THE THREE-STEP SIGN-UP CLAIM IS TRUE, THE ONE-BOX SCREEN IS NOT. 'email, a six-digit code, your name' (about.html:700, 713-715) matches the code exactly — three screens, three fields, no card, no plan choice, no URL picker (studio.html:1054-1097). But the FIRST screen is not just an email box: it also shows a page-name box, a studio-code box, an 'Unlock with code' button, a 'Lost your email? Use a recovery code' link, and sometimes a Face ID button (studio.html:976-1001). Never describe the sign-in screen as one field.

TWO MINUTES DEPENDS ON AN EMAIL ARRIVING FROM onboarding@resend.dev. If RESEND_API_KEY is unset the whole email door answers 503 with 'Email sign-in isn't switched on yet' (auth.mjs:54-55), and MYSET.md:1030-1033 says AUTH_FROM is still unset, so codes go out from Resend's shared sending domain rather than myset.vip. Do not add 'the code arrives instantly' or 'check your inbox' confidence the deliverability does not yet support.

'RESEND THE CODE' IS NOT SAFE ADVICE. After five code requests for one address in an hour the server silently stops sending and STILL answers 'sent' (_auth.mjs:15, auth.mjs:64). The Studio then shows the code screen as if a code is coming. Any copy that says 'didn't get it? tap again' walks somebody into a dead end.

SEATS ARE THE ONLY THING PLUS DOES NOT BUY. Free and Plus are both seats:1; only Pro has five (_plan.mjs:65, :89, :107). 'Five sign-ins for your band' is correct in the Pro column and would be wrong anywhere near Plus.

ROLES EXIST IN CODE AND NOWHERE IN THE APP. Owner / member / crew are real and enforced (_session.mjs:250-263, admin.mjs:1594-1600), but there is no interface to pick one: addTeam sends no role so every added address becomes a 'member' (studio.html:3790), and nothing in public/ ever calls roleSet. Do not write 'give your sound engineer crew access' — a person cannot be made crew through the product.

CREW IS NOT ACTUALLY LIMITED TO TONIGHT. The capability gate only fires for actions listed in CAPABILITY (admin.mjs:1596-1599); the comment at admin.mjs:407-412 says everything else needs nothing but a session. 'clearSetlist', 'newShow' and 'resetVotes' are not in that table, so a crew sign-in can wipe the library or reset a show. The role table's promise is stronger than the code's.

SECURITY.md IS WRONG ABOUT DEFAULT-DENY. SECURITY.md:54 says 'both admin surfaces gate on an allow-list — anything not named is owner-only'. That is not what admin.mjs does. What IS default-deny is an unrecognised ROLE STRING falling back to crew (_session.mjs:261-262). Two different claims; only the second is safe to make.

ACCOUNTS.md SAYS MEMBERS CAN EXPORT. THEY CANNOT. CAN.member includes 'export' (_session.mjs:252) and ACCOUNTS.md:150 repeats it, but accountExport is in admin.mjs's OWNER_ONLY set (admin.mjs:1580), which is checked first. Export is owner-only in practice.

THE ACTIVITY LOG HAS NO SCREEN. Every sign-in, seat change, role change, recovery code and address move is recorded (_session.mjs:176-188) and the only reader is an API action nothing in public/ calls. An artist cannot see their own account history today. Never promise it.

THE FACE ID BUTTON IS INVISIBLE TO NEW SIGNUPS. It only renders when this browser already has a remembered page name (studio.html:977), and that is written inside loadPasskeys(), which only runs when somebody TAPS into the Settings tab — a reload that lands on Settings does not call it (studio.html:938 vs 1615). So 'sign in with Face ID' is a second-visit feature, and only after a Settings visit.

ONLY THE OWNER CAN ADD A PASSKEY, AND A PASSKEY ALWAYS OPENS THE OWNER'S SESSION. passkeyStart/Finish/List/Forget are all in OWNER_ONLY (auth.mjs:211-215) and passkeySignInFinish resolves the owner's address regardless of whose thumb it was (auth.mjs:150-156). It is not a per-band-member convenience.

A RECOVERY CODE SIGNS THE WHOLE BAND OUT. Using one bumps the account revision, killing every other device, and emails every address on the page (auth.mjs:172-191). Fine as a rescue, wrong to describe as 'a quick way back in'.

THE STUDIO CODE AND THE RECOVERY CODES SHARE ONE LOCKOUT. Ten failures in fifteen minutes on either door shuts both for fifteen minutes, because both use lock_<artistId> (_lib.mjs:936-951, auth.mjs:169-171). Email sign-in is untouched by it.

THE STUDIO CODE GRANTS FULL OWNER RIGHTS AND CARRIES NO EMAIL. requireArtist returns role 'owner' for a correct studio code (_lib.mjs:1002), so anyone holding it can do everything — but me.email is null, which means 'change my sign-in address' refuses with 'Sign in with your email first' (auth.mjs:297) and 'sign out this device' has no session to kill (auth.mjs:267).

DELETE DOES NOT DELETE ON DAY ONE, AND NOTHING IS MOVED. The page goes dark immediately and billing stops, but not one document is copied or erased for thirty days (_account.mjs:80-105). The safe line is 'nothing is erased'; the unsafe line is 'we archive your data', because there is no archive.

THE PURGE IS ONE ACCOUNT PER HOUR. autocron runs every two minutes but only attempts a purge on an hourly watermark and only takes one account per run (autocron.mjs:64-71, _account.mjs:173). 'Erased on day 31' is approximately, not exactly, true.

DELETING DOES NOT SIGN YOU OUT, ON PURPOSE. Sessions survive and the revision is not bumped, because the owner has to be able to get back in and undo (_account.mjs:103-105). Do not write 'your account is locked' — it is locked DOWN (423 on everything but undo, export, plan and ledger), never locked out.

THE VENUE SIDE IS A DIFFERENT PRODUCT. Venue signup is four fields not three (venue-studio.html:392-400), venue seats are five on every plan including free (venueauth.mjs:162), and venues have no passkeys, no recovery codes and no way to move their sign-in address (ACCOUNTS.md:334 lists it as next). Any sentence covering 'artists and venues' together on account security will be wrong for one of them.

SIGNUP IS COMPLETELY OPEN. Anyone who can receive an email can create an artist page in three steps — no invite, no approval, no cap (auth.mjs:92-112, and the comment at _auth.mjs:207 says so plainly). Do not write 'apply' or 'request access'.

THE SESSIONS LIST SHOWS A DEVICE CLASS, NOT A LOCATION. 'iPhone · Safari' and a sign-in date, never an IP, never a city, and the timezone field is always empty because no client sends it (_session.mjs:116-125; no tz in any sign-in call in either Studio). And the freshness number is deliberately called 'last opened Settings' because that is all it measures (_session.mjs:29-34).

FANS REALLY DO HAVE NO ACCOUNT — WITH ONE FOOTNOTE. There is no email field anywhere on vote.html, artist.html, index.html or community.html, and a phone is only a random localStorage id (vote.html:287-289). The footnote: a merch buyer's name and email are readable live from Stripe on the order detail screen (admin.mjs:1319-1323), because a shipping address has to come from somewhere. MySet stores none of it.

ALMOST ALL OF THIS IS NEWER THAN THE LANDING PAGE'S UNDERSTANDING. Sessions, roles, recovery codes, the email change, the thirty-day delete and passkeys all landed on 2026-09-05 in commits 931d18d, 7ee4827 and 81f5b44. about.html's last edit (9e9fde4, same day) was about room sizes and mentions none of them — a grep for 'passkey', 'recovery', 'session' and 'delete' in public/about.html returns nothing.

appCatalogue.surface: The show engine, polling and feature flags
appCatalogue.summary: This is the live machinery of a gig: one Netlify Blobs document per artist holding the show state, twelve sharded fan documents holding every vote, one read-only endpoint (/api/show) that every phone in the room polls, one write endpoint (/api/vote), and the lifecycle module that starts and ends a night — by the artist's tap or by the calendar, with no request behind it. Fans are anonymous (a random id in localStorage, no sign-in); the artist drives it from the Studio's Live tab, which polls every 4 seconds. The defining design decision on this surface is that a plan's audience number is a BILLING line and not a turnstile: a room over its ceiling is never closed and never refuses a vote — it slows its own polling and shortens the board instead. Feature flags are a separate, tiny global document read on the hot poll and cached 60 seconds in module scope; there are exactly two flags and both default ON.
appCatalogue.structure: Three surfaces sit on one engine. (1) The fan's voting page at /:slug/vote (public/vote.html): a header with the artist and a credit pill, "Playing now" hero with a Lyrics button, an open/paused strip, "Up next" (top 3 by votes), an optional request/birthday card, search + sort + genre chips, the main votable list, an "Already played" list at replay price, and a bottom dock with More votes / Tip. Tapping a song opens a bottom sheet with a quantity stepper and a plain-English rules list; Confirm casts. (2) The artist's Live tab in the Studio (public/studio.html:1870-1948): a Voting Open/Paused toggle, three stat tiles (votes now, voting/in-room + networks, tips), Now playing with a private chart button, the requests panel, Start/End the show, "Start top voted — <title> (<votes>)", a queue of up to 12 with per-row Start, and Played with Reset votes. (3) The server: /api/show returns everything the room sees plus two self-tuning dials (nextPollMs, board) and the flags in force; /api/vote takes a cast. A fourth surface is gone — public/stage.html is now a 9-line meta-refresh to /studio.html (public/stage.html:5) and has no route in netlify.toml.
appCatalogue.design: The fan page is a single self-contained HTML file, no framework, no external fonts or scripts (CSP is default-src 'self', netlify.toml:123). Dark, iOS-flavoured: rounded cards, a red-pink accent, a skeleton shimmer on first paint (public/vote.html:307-312), a "rise" entrance once (public/vote.html:685), haptic buzz on every meaningful tap (public/vote.html:292), a credit pill that bumps when the number changes (public/vote.html:697-699), confetti + a triple buzz on a successful purchase (public/vote.html:966-977), dancing equaliser bars on the Playing-now card. Everything destructive or costly happens in a bottom sheet with a grab-handle drag-to-dismiss and Escape-to-close (public/vote.html:860-870). Pull-to-refresh is a shared script used by all seven pages (public/pull.js) because an installed home-screen app has no address bar. The tone throughout is plainly written and non-technical: refusals read "That one isn't on tonight's list" and "Those votes are cast — they stay with the song" (curly apostrophes are deliberate — they are the app's own copyright fingerprint, netlify/functions/_canary.mjs:26-28). The engine's pacing is invisible by design: at an ordinary gig the board moves within about three seconds and nothing on screen mentions polling at all.

features.name: The live board every phone reads
features.whatItDoes: One public endpoint, /api/show, returns the whole state of the night — who's playing, the ranked songs, this fan's own votes and credits, what's already been played, requests, the flags in force. It is the only thing the voting page reads.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/show.mjs:10-176; routed by netlify.toml:15-18; called at public/vote.html:316
features.whyRelevant: This is the product's heartbeat — 'the queue moves while you watch' is this endpoint.

features.name: The board refreshes itself every three seconds, then eases off
features.whatItDoes: The page re-asks the server every 3 seconds while anything is moving, 10 seconds after 2 unchanged ticks, 25 seconds after 6, and a terminal 60 seconds after 20 — with ±20% random jitter so a whole room doesn't fire on the same instant. Any tap, screen-on, vote or pull-to-refresh drops it straight back to 3 seconds.
features.whereInCode: public/vote.html:1076-1114 (rungs at :1098-1105, jitter at :1112), tick at :1115-1125, wakeUp at :1132-1137, listeners at :1150-1151
features.whyRelevant: 'It updates itself every few seconds' is the honest claim; 'real-time' / 'instantly' / 'live sync' would be wrong — there are no websockets anywhere in this repo.

features.name: A packed room slows itself down instead of melting
features.whatItDoes: The server counts the phones actually in the room and hands back nextPollMs with every response: 3s up to 200 people, 5s to 1,000, 10s to 3,000, 20s above that. The page obeys it and every rung of its own ladder stretches with it. Nobody has to decide anything at 11pm and no deploy is needed.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/_lib.mjs:852-858 (pollFloorFor); sent at netlify/functions/show.mjs:169; clamped and applied at public/vote.html:323 and :1045
features.whyRelevant: Already claimed on the landing page as 'refreshes a little slower' for oversized rooms (public/about.html:622-623). It is real and it is server-side.

features.name: A big room sees the top of the chart, not all of it
features.whatItDoes: Past 200 phones the response carries only the top songs — 40 up to 1,000 people, 25 up to 3,000, 15 above that — instead of the whole library.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/_lib.mjs:866-872 (boardLimitFor); applied at netlify/functions/show.mjs:86-91; sent at :170
features.whyRelevant: Already on the landing page (public/about.html:623). It is the visible consequence of an oversized room.

features.name: Your own song stays on your board even when it is 90th
features.whatItDoes: When the board is shortened, anything this particular fan voted for is appended back on regardless of its rank, so a voter can always find their pick.
features.whyRelevant: A trust detail worth a sentence: in a voting app, a vanished vote reads as a lost vote.

features.name: The page says out loud when the board is short
features.whatItDoes: Renders 'Big room tonight — showing the top N. Songs you voted for stay on your list wherever they are.' whenever the server sent a board limit.
features.whyRelevant: Supports the claim above; too small to sell on its own.

features.name: Nobody is ever turned away at the door
features.whatItDoes: Going over the plan's audience number does not close the room, refuse a vote or make anybody a spectator. There is deliberately no head-count check in the vote path at all. The room slows and the board shortens; that is the whole penalty.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/vote.mjs:81-92 (the explicit non-check); netlify/functions/show.mjs:32-43; whole rationale + tests in test/roomsize.mjs:1-16 and :119-131
features.whyRelevant: This is a genuine differentiator and it is already half-claimed at public/about.html:622-623. It can be stated flatly: a room over its plan still runs.

features.name: Tonight's room size is fixed when the show starts
features.whatItDoes: The plan's audience number is read once, when the show goes live, and written onto the show record — so an artist who upgrades mid-set does not have the room change size underneath them, and the polling path never pays a lookup for it. It applies from the next show.
features.planGate: free 200 / plus 1,000 / pro 2,000 (netlify/functions/_plan.mjs:63, :88, :106); Infinity only for the founder
features.whyRelevant: Explains the honest small print on an upgrade: a bigger room starts at your next gig, not mid-song.

features.name: The 'this room is over its plan' signal that nothing displays
features.whatItDoes: /api/show sends room:{cap, in, over}. No page anywhere reads room.cap or room.over — the fan page never mentions it and the Studio's Live tab shows only voting/in-room counts. The code comments and the tests say the artist 'is told afterwards'; no such telling exists in the codebase.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/show.mjs:168 emits it; no consumer — grep finds it only in tests (test/roomsize.mjs:95, :107, :150-151) and the Studio Live tab has no cap awareness (public/studio.html:1880-1884)
features.whyRelevant: Do not write 'and we let you know afterwards' — nothing does.

features.name: How many phones are in the room
features.whatItDoes: Every phone stamps itself once per show the first time it opens the voting page (never on a profile view). The count is distinct phones, not distinct networks — forty people on one bar wifi count as forty. The network is stored only as a salted hash, never the address.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/_lib.mjs:721-745 (rationale + clientIp/roomHash), :765-775 (markPresence), :810-815 (countInRoom); presence is only sent with in=1 from public/vote.html:316
features.whyRelevant: Backs the landing page's '21 of 26 in the room' screenshot claim (public/about.html:390).

features.name: The presence stamp is written once and then skipped
features.whatItDoes: The poll checks the already-merged fan bag and only writes a presence stamp when it is genuinely missing or the network changed — removing about 27% of the billed duration of ~99.9% of all polls.
features.whyRelevant: Cost engineering, not a user-facing feature.

features.name: '40 phones on 3 networks' in the Studio
features.whatItDoes: The Live tab shows voting/in-room plus the number of distinct networks, which is the only defence against one phone rotating its id to inflate the count.
features.whyRelevant: Real but obscure; not a selling line.

features.name: Casting a vote
features.whatItDoes: POST /api/vote with a fan id, a song, a quantity and an intent. The server checks the show isn't ended, the voting window is open, the song exists, it isn't the song playing right now, it is actually on offer tonight, and the fan can afford it — then appends one entry per vote to the fan's record.
features.whyRelevant: The core act of the product.

features.name: Put several votes on one song at once
features.whatItDoes: The vote sheet has a −/+ stepper: a fan can stack up to 20 votes on a single song in one Confirm (the page caps at 20 or whatever they can afford; the server's own hard ceiling is 50). Before this a fan with five votes had to tap five times and could not say how strongly they wanted something.

trapsForCopy: VOTES ARE FINAL, AND THE LANDING PAGE'S OWN DEMO SAYS OTHERWISE. voteFinal defaults to TRUE (netlify/functions/_flags.mjs:34) — a fan cannot take a vote back; the sheet says 'Once you confirm, that's final' (public/vote.html:448). But the interactive demo on /about lets you tap a Voted button to un-vote and get the credit back (public/about.html:768). Either the demo or the copy is wrong, and the demo is the one that contradicts production.

'REAL-TIME' AND 'INSTANT' ARE BOTH WRONG. There are no websockets and no server-sent events anywhere in this repo. The board is polled: 3 seconds when things are moving, easing to 10, then 25, then 60 (public/vote.html:1098-1105). Safe phrasings: 'updates itself every few seconds', 'the queue moves while you watch'. Unsafe: real-time, live sync, instantly, push.

IN A BIG ROOM A POCKETED PHONE CAN GO MINUTES BETWEEN REFRESHES. The rungs are multiples of the server floor, so at a 3,000+ room (floor 20s) the terminal rung is floor x 20 = 400 seconds — about six and a half minutes (public/vote.html:1105). Any tap or screen-on wakes it instantly, but 'never more than a few seconds out of date' is false at scale.

THE ROOM CEILING IS A BILLING LINE, NOT A DOOR. Free 200 / Plus 1,000 / Pro 2,000 (netlify/functions/_plan.mjs:63, :88, :106). Going over refuses nobody and blocks no vote — there is deliberately no head-count check in the vote path (netlify/functions/vote.mjs:81-92). Never write 'up to 200 people can vote' or 'your room is limited to'. Write 'the night still runs; it just refreshes slower and shows the top of the board'.

NOTHING ACTUALLY TELLS THE ARTIST THEY WENT OVER. The code comments and tests both say the artist 'is told afterwards', and /api/show emits room.over (netlify/functions/show.mjs:168) — but no page reads it. The Studio's Live tab shows in-room counts only (public/studio.html:1882). Do not promise a notification, a report, or an after-the-gig warning about room size.

THE ROOM SIZE IS FIXED WHEN THE SHOW STARTS. Upgrading mid-set does not enlarge tonight's room; the plan's number is stamped onto the show record at start (netlify/functions/_lifecycle.mjs:143-147). And a show that began before room caps existed is simply uncapped forever.

THE SHORT BOARD ONLY TRUNCATES THE UNPLAYED LIST. The 'Already played' section is built separately and is never limited (netlify/functions/show.mjs:100-105), so in a huge room the played list is still complete while the votable list is 15 long. Do not say 'we show the top 15 songs'.

AUTO-END IS THREE HOURS AFTER THE CALENDAR GIG'S SCHEDULED END, NOT AFTER YOU STOP PLAYING (netlify/functions/_auto.mjs:31, :149). Gigs default to 180 minutes long (netlify/functions/_events.mjs:40), so a 8pm gig with no duration set auto-ends around 2am. It is deferred if a song started in the last 45 minutes, and there is a six-hour hard backstop.
AUTO-START CAN BE UP TO TWO MINUTES LATE. The cron rings every two minutes (netlify/functions/autocron.mjs:95). Say 'within a couple of minutes of your gig's start time', not 'exactly at'.

AUTO-START WON'T FIRE AT ALL IF NO SONGS ARE SWITCHED ON, if the artist turned auto-start off, if the free gig cap is spent, or if the artist already started and ended tonight by hand (netlify/functions/_auto.mjs:133-145). It is a helper, not a guarantee.

THE FREE PLAN'S SHOW CAP IS PER CALENDAR MONTH IN UTC, RESETTING ON THE 1st (netlify/functions/_lib.mjs:131, netlify/functions/_plan.mjs:21-33). It is four a month, not one a week — it was briefly weekly on 2026-09-03 and changed straight back, so older docs may say otherwise.

'SET YOUR OWN VOTE RULES' IS A PLUS FEATURE, BUT THE DEFAULTS ARE FREE. A free artist runs on 5 free votes, a 5-vote replay price and the standard packs, and the ROOM's experience is identical (netlify/functions/admin.mjs:1699-1709). Only the artist's ability to change the numbers is gated. Never imply a free artist's audience gets a worse night.

REQUESTS AND BIRTHDAY SHOUT-OUTS ARE OFF BY DEFAULT (netlify/functions/_lib.mjs:180-183). The buttons are not rendered at all until the artist switches them on. Don't show them in a screenshot captioned as the default fan experience.

REQUESTS COST VOTES, NEVER MONEY, and a declined request refunds automatically — but ONLY within the same show. A request from an earlier show is deliberately not refunded, because its credits already refreshed (netlify/functions/_requests.mjs:167-177).
THERE IS NO ENCORE FEATURE. The only 'Encore!' in the app is the label on the $20 tip tile (public/vote.html:937). Every other use of the word is metaphor in code comments.
THERE IS NO STAGE OR BIG-SCREEN VIEW. public/stage.html redirects to the Studio (public/stage.html:5) and has no route. Never mention projecting the queue on a screen behind the band.

FANS INSTALL NOTHING AND SIGN IN TO NOWHERE — but that means identity is a random id in the browser's own storage (public/vote.html:287-290). Clear the storage, use a private window, or switch phone, and the votes and any bought credits are gone. Don't promise votes 'follow you'.

THERE IS NO OFFLINE MODE AND NO QUEUED-VOTE-WHEN-BACK-ONLINE. A failed poll is swallowed silently with no banner (public/vote.html:325); a failed vote retries once then says 'Couldn't reach the room — try again' (public/vote.html:533-534). The service worker deliberately never caches anything under /api (public/sw.js:10-12).

A SHOW IN 'pre' STATE IS INCONSISTENT: the fan page greys out voting (public/vote.html:574-575), but the server will actually accept a vote — /api/vote only refuses when the show is 'ended' or the window is shut (netlify/functions/vote.mjs:46, :80). Requests, by contrast, do check for 'live' (netlify/functions/_requests.mjs:70). Don't write 'nothing can be voted until you go live'.

THE FAN CAN STACK UP TO 20 VOTES ON ONE SONG IN ONE CONFIRM (public/vote.html:427-428); the server's hard ceiling is 50 (netlify/functions/vote.mjs:16). The landing demo's one-tap-one-vote model understates the product.

'FREE VOTES COME BACK EVERY TIME A NEW SONG STARTS' IS EXACTLY TRUE — but so does the artist's manual 'Reset votes', and so does changing the free-vote count or the replay price, both of which wipe the round on purpose (netlify/functions/admin.mjs:1834, :1949). The fan sees credits reappear without a song having started.
PUSH NOTIFICATIONS ARE ARTIST-ONLY AND REQUIRE THE STUDIO TO BE INSTALLED. The audience is never pushed to (public/sw.js:31-36). Don't say 'we'll ping your fans'.

FOUR PLAN FLAGS ARE DESIGNED AND NOT BUILT — promote, analytics, presskit, branding (netlify/functions/_plan.mjs:130). Anything on a pricing table describing earnings-by-venue analytics, a press kit, custom branding or cross-city promotion is describing something with no code behind it. (The separate $10 Featured-shows purchase IS built and IS live, behind the featuredShows flag — do not confuse it with the unbuilt `promote` tier flag.)

BOTH FEATURE FLAGS DEFAULT ON AND ONLY THE PLATFORM OWNER CAN FLIP THEM (netlify/functions/admin.mjs:176, :190). They are not artist settings and must never be described as customer-facing options. A flip also takes up to 60 seconds to reach every warm server (netlify/functions/_flags.mjs:67).

THE PROOF NUMBERS ON /about ARE ONE PUB NIGHT — 8 people, 21 votes (public/about.html:486-489). The show engine records the whole round, not just the winner (netlify/functions/admin.mjs:1748-1753), so richer numbers exist, but nothing bigger has been played. Don't extrapolate.

appCatalogue.surface: History, numbers, analytics and the warehouse — what a night records, what an artist can show a venue, and the Google-Sheet export
appCatalogue.summary: This is MySet's memory of a gig. When a show ends (or a new one starts, or the calendar ends it), `archiveShow` freezes one document per night — songs played in order with their votes, everything the room asked for and never got, how many phones were in the room, how many networks they were on, how many people voted, and what the night took in card payments read straight from Stripe (netlify/functions/_history.mjs:83-241). Those nights drive four different audiences: the artist's own Money tab in the Studio, the public stat row on their myset.vip page, the numbers a venue sees about its own room, and a nine-tab Google Sheet export for the founder. The sheet is fully built and completely OFF in production — its three env vars have never been set (verified against Netlify: production holds only ADMIN_CODE, AUTH_FROM, RESEND_API_KEY, STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET). The Pro plan feature actually called "analytics" (earnings by venue/night/song) is in NOT_BUILT and shows as a greyed "Coming soon" card with invented sample numbers (netlify/functions/_plan.mjs:130, public/studio.html:1336).
appCatalogue.structure:
Five places a number appears, from most private to most public.

1. STUDIO → MONEY TAB (artist, signed in). Top: "Tonight so far" (or "Last show — finished") with songs played, votes, taken. Then "Past shows" — one tappable row per night showing date, venue, city, songs/votes/people and the night's takings on the right; a search box appears only once there are more than three nights (public/studio.html:2095-2135). Tapping a row opens the full night: two rows of three big numbers (songs/votes/people, then taken/vote packs/tips), the tips with their notes, "What you played" numbered in order with vote counts, "Wanted but never played" (top 15), and a "↺ Re-check the money in Stripe" button (public/studio.html:2040-2090). Under the list: "Look for missing shows" (the heal). Below all of that: All payments (last 180 days, live from Stripe), Your earnings (12-month statement + CSV, owner only), MySet's books (founder only P&L + costs editor + CSV), and the greyed "Your numbers" coming-soon card.

2. STUDIO → LIVE TAB. Three live tiles while a show runs: "Votes now", "Voting · in room" rendered as `21/26` plus a networks count, and "Tips" (public/studio.html:1880-1884). This is the only place the room count is visible in real time.

3. PUBLIC ARTIST PAGE (/:slug). A five-cell stat strip under the name: Joined · Shows · Fans · Votes cast · Songs, plus a Community link (public/artist.html:409-415), served by netlify/functions/profile.mjs:29-33.

4. VENUE STUDIO → NUMBERS TAB. Three tiles (people in the room, votes cast, nights), a line naming how many acts and since when, a "Busiest night" callout, a "By act" leaderboard ranked by people with an average-per-night badge and a link to each artist's page, and "By night" (last 40) (public/venue-studio.html:1232-1267). Built by netlify/functions/_vstats.mjs.

5. THE GOOGLE SHEET (founder only, currently off). Nine tabs — Guide, Artists, Shows, Songs, Requests, Ratings, Gigs, Venues, Growth. Four are snapshots rewritten each run, three are append-only logs, Growth is one row per sync, Guide is written once in plain English (netlify/functions/_warehouse.mjs:90-100, 139-155). Driven by a nightly cron at 03:20 UTC and by an "Update the sheet now" button on a card in Settings.
appCatalogue.design:
Dark-first Studio; the numbers are the visual anchor. Stat tiles use a monospace face (`class="mono"`) at ~23px with an 11.5px muted caption, three across, so three numbers read as one row rather than three cards. Money figures get the accent colour (`class="mono acc"`), everything else stays ink — so "taken" pops out of a row of grey counts. The live in-room tile is a deliberate fraction, `21` big with `/26` smaller and muted, captioned "Voting · in room" plus a networks suffix — the design says "voters out of people here" without a sentence.

Every number is accompanied by an honesty line in muted 12px: "Couldn't reach Stripe for this one — the money figures may be stale", "$3.00 came in during this window but isn't tagged to a show", "10 songs played, but the titles weren't logged — the Studio wasn't open that night". The interface refuses to let a blank or a zero pass as a fact.

Locked features are shown, never hidden (Perry's rule). An unbuilt Pro feature renders its real card, veiled, with a padlock pill reading "Coming soon" rather than "Pro feature", and the reason line sits *under* the veil rather than inside it (public/studio.html:1304-1315). The greyed card still contains fully-written example rows — "The Ugly Duckling · $184 over 6 nights" — which look like data and are not.

Venue Numbers is the same tile language in the Venue Studio, with two standing captions doing product work: "Phones that opened the voting page in your room, not just people who tapped", and "What each artist earned is not here and never will be — that's their business."

The public artist stat strip is a flat five-cell grid with no chrome, numbers compacted (1.2k), and any zero-valued cell is dropped entirely rather than shown as 0 (public/artist.html:413) — so a brand-new artist's page shows Joined and Songs and nothing else.

features.name: A night is filed the moment you end the show
features.whatItDoes: Ending a show, starting a brand-new one, or the calendar ending it for you snapshots the whole night into one permanent document before anything wipes the tally.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/_history.mjs:83-241; called from netlify/functions/_lifecycle.mjs:121 (new show) and :182 (end show); the scheduler calls the same two doors at netlify/functions/_auto.mjs:130,162
features.whyRelevant: This is the mechanism under "every gig you play is counted from the first song". It is real and it runs on every plan.

features.name: A night where nothing happened is not a night
features.whatItDoes: A show that never went live, or went live with no song started, no vote cast and no phone in the room, is refused and never appears in history or as "Shows: 1".
features.whyRelevant: It is the anti-inflation guard, and it is genuinely load-bearing now that a calendar gig can start a show by itself. But it is weaker than it sounds — see traps.

features.name: Ending the show twice keeps the fuller night
features.whatItDoes: Re-archiving the same showId replaces the stored snapshot only when the new one has more songs or more votes; otherwise it just refreshes the money. No number in the list row is ever allowed to go down.
features.whyRelevant: Explains why the founder's own numbers changed under him between two screenshots — it is a fix, not a bug, but it means published figures move.

features.name: What you played, in order, with the votes each song won
features.whatItDoes: The night's detail page lists every song started from the Studio, numbered, with the artist, the time it started, whether it was a replay, and the votes it had when it won.
features.whyRelevant: It is the setlist you actually played, recorded without typing it. Note the honest fallback when the Studio was not open.

features.name: Wanted but never played
features.whatItDoes: Sums every song the room voted for across every round of the night and lists the ones that never got played, ranked. It is the answer to "what should I learn next".
features.whyRelevant: It is the most distinctive thing in the archive and it survives even when the song log does not — the founder's one real gig has 16 of these and zero played rows.

features.name: Phones in the room, not just phones that tapped
features.whatItDoes: Counts every device that opened the voting page during that show (stamped once per device per show), separately from how many of them voted; also counts how many distinct networks those phones were on.
features.whyRelevant: "How many people were in the room" is the number a venue cares about, and MySet measures it rather than asking. The networks count is the sanity check against one phone rotating its id.

features.name: How many people actually voted
features.whatItDoes: The high-water mark of distinct phones that cast at least one vote, taken across every round of the night as well as at the end.
features.whyRelevant: This is the "8 people voted" on the landing page today.

features.name: Every vote of the night, not just the winning ones
features.whatItDoes: Sums the whole vote count in each round (not only the votes the winner had) plus anything left uncast at the end, because votes are wiped every time a song starts.
features.whyRelevant: "21 votes cast" comes from here. Older archived nights only have the winner's count, so the field falls back.

features.name: The night's top song
features.whatItDoes: Records the single song with the most votes that night, falling back to the most-wanted-but-unplayed if nothing was started from the Studio.
features.whyRelevant: It is stored but is only surfaced today in the Sheet's Shows tab, not in the Studio's own night view.

features.name: What the night took, read from Stripe
features.whatItDoes: At archive time MySet asks Stripe for every paid checkout in that night's window on that artist's own account, and stores gross, vote-pack money and count, tip money and count, the twelve most recent tips with their notes, and anything untagged.
features.whyRelevant: It is a cache of Stripe, never a second ledger, and it says out loud when Stripe could not be reached. But card payments only work for artists with Stripe Connect finished — see the payments caveat the page already carries.

features.name: Money in the window that isn't tagged to a show
features.whatItDoes: Payments taken during the night that carry no show tag are reported separately, on the night view and in the list row, labelled as predating show tracking.
features.whyRelevant: It is a window figure and must never be summed across nights. The founder's one real gig carries $3.00 here — which is the only card money MySet has ever taken from a room.

features.name: Re-check the money in Stripe
features.whatItDoes: A button on any past night that re-pulls Stripe for that night's window and rewrites the stored money block and the list row's total.
features.whyRelevant: Only useful if the night was archived while Stripe was unreachable. Not a selling point.

features.name: Look for missing shows
features.whatItDoes: A repair button that goes back through every showId the artist has ever archived, plus any whose index write failed, plus (for the founding artist only) the pre-multi-tenancy flat keys, and rebuilds the list.
features.whyRelevant: It exists because nights genuinely went missing. Never advertise it — it is a plaster on a leak, and it has a side effect (see traps).

features.name: The heal runs itself once per artist
features.whatItDoes: The first time an artist ever opens the Money tab, the repair runs automatically and stamps the index so it never runs again unless the button is tapped.
features.whyRelevant: This is what silently rewrote the founder's public numbers on 4 September — see traps.

features.name: 400 nights kept in the list, every night kept on disk
features.whatItDoes: The searchable list keeps the most recent 400 nights and records how many it dropped and the oldest it still holds; the full detail documents and a permanent append-only list of every showId ever archived are never trimmed.
features.whyRelevant: 400 nights is five-plus years of gigging. Not a limit anyone will hit, and not worth mentioning.

features.name: Find a night by venue, city, weekday or date
