features.whatItDoes: A search box over past shows that matches venue name, city, the formatted date, and the day of the week — so "friday ugly" finds it.
features.whyRelevant: Nice detail, but it only renders once the artist has more than three archived nights (public/studio.html:2118) — so nobody on the platform has ever seen it.

features.name: Tonight so far
features.whatItDoes: A live preview of the running show's songs, votes and takings at the top of the Money tab, before the night is filed; the row is hidden from Past shows only while the show is actually live.
features.whyRelevant: You can watch the night's numbers accumulate before you end it. Skips the Stripe call entirely when the show has no start time, so it is cheap.

features.name: Your public page carries your real numbers
features.whatItDoes: myset.vip/yourname shows Joined, Shows, Fans, Votes cast and Songs, computed from the archive on every page load. Zero-valued cells are dropped rather than shown.
features.whyRelevant: This is the artefact the whole "stop telling venues you draw a crowd" argument rests on. It is real, public and needs no login. But three of the five numbers are computed in ways a copywriter will misread — see traps.

features.name: "Songs" on the public page is the library, not songs played
features.whatItDoes: The Songs figure counts how many songs are currently featured to the audience, not how many were performed.
features.whyRelevant: The founder's page says 66 Songs and he has played eleven. Never present this number as performance data.

features.name: A venue sees what happened in its own room
features.whatItDoes: The Venue Studio Numbers tab totals people, votes and nights across every MySet act who has played there, with a by-act leaderboard (ranked on people, with an average-per-night badge), a by-night list of the last 40, and a busiest-night callout.
features.planGate: none — free venues get it too (netlify/functions/_venues.mjs:130-133 has no analytics flag)
features.whyRelevant: The landing page already claims it (public/about.html:533). It is real, built and free. It has also never displayed a single number in production — see traps.

features.name: A venue never sees an artist's money
features.whatItDoes: Money is not in the venue stats payload at all, not even as a total, and the page says so out loud.
features.whyRelevant: A strong, provable trust claim — enforced in the payload, not just hidden in the page.

features.name: The artist can switch venue sharing off
features.whatItDoes: A toggle in the Studio that removes the artist entirely from every venue's numbers. Default on. Owner-only to change. The venue is told how many acts have switched off, but not who.
features.whyRelevant: "It's your data and you get the switch" is a real, enforced promise, and the hidden-count line means the venue is not misled by an absence.

features.name: A venue's numbers assemble themselves from artists' own records
features.whatItDoes: No new tracking: the venue's city index names the artists, and their archived nights are matched to the venue by fuzzy name comparison (exact, or a distinctive short name contained as a whole word in a longer one).
features.whyRelevant: Supports the existing claim at public/about.html:568-571 that a venue page fills itself in. But matching is by typed venue name — see traps.

features.name: "Want to perform here?" sends your numbers, not a bio
features.whatItDoes: An artist asks a venue for a spot from the venue's public page; the venue's inbox shows the artist's nights, people, votes and songs beside the message, and no email is exposed either way.
features.whyRelevant: The landing page already promotes this at public/about.html:495-497. It is built and reachable. It uses the same people formula as the public page, so it carries the same bug.

features.name: "Your numbers" — earnings by venue, best night, money songs
features.whatItDoes: Nothing. It is a greyed card in the Money tab showing three example rows behind a "Coming soon" veil.
features.planGate: pro (PLANS.pro.analytics = true, _plan.mjs:109) — but listed in NOT_BUILT so it is greyed as "Coming soon" on every plan including Pro
features.whyRelevant: The word "analytics" in the plan table means THIS, and it does not exist. Its sample figures ($184 over 6 nights, Thursdays average 31 people, Wonderwall 12% of votes) are invented and must never be quoted.

features.name: Your press kit
features.whatItDoes: Nothing. A greyed Pro card promising myset.vip/you/press with average room, votes and nights played, plus a PDF.
features.whyRelevant: The single most tempting thing on this surface to over-claim. The public artist page is the closest thing that exists today.

features.name: List shows in cities you don't normally play
features.whatItDoes: Nothing. A greyed Pro card. The landing page already correctly labels it "Soon" (public/about.html:645).
features.whyRelevant: Already handled honestly on the current page — keep it that way.

features.name: Your earnings — twelve months, downloadable
features.whatItDoes: A month-by-month statement built from Stripe's balance transactions (fans paid, Stripe's cut, MySet's cut, yours, paid out), cached per closed month, with a "Check again" force-recompute and a CSV download.
features.planGate: none by plan — but OWNER-only per account (netlify/functions/admin.mjs:1578-1590) and it returns `enabled:false` until the artist has a Stripe account
features.whyRelevant: A real, shipped feature nobody has used, because no artist on the platform has finished Stripe Connect. Every figure is Stripe's, never recomputed.

features.name: A venue's own earnings statement
features.whatItDoes: The same twelve-month statement, scoped to the venue's own Stripe account, in the Venue Studio's Merch section.
features.whyRelevant: Venues had nothing before; still nothing to show, since no venue sells anything yet.

features.name: MySet's books — a real P&L
features.whatItDoes: Founder-only. Came in, went out, kept, per month, from Stripe's balance transactions on the platform account, with a hand-entered costs editor across six categories and a CSV download. Splits the founder's own gig takings out of the company's revenue.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/_ledger.mjs:279-372 (platformSplit), :398-421 (books); netlify/functions/admin.mjs:1365-1392 (`if (!isFounder) return bad(...)`); public/studio.html:3341-3378; ACCOUNTING.md
features.whyRelevant: Never mention. It is Perry's own accounting, not a product feature.

features.name: All payments, last 180 days, live from Stripe
features.whatItDoes: Lists every paid checkout this app created for this artist, flags any the app failed to deliver, and offers a one-tap recovery that hands over what was bought.
features.whyRelevant: The "nobody can pay and get nothing" safety net. Real, and buyer emails are shown to the artist here.

features.name: The whole platform as a Google Sheet
features.whatItDoes: Nine tabs — Guide, Artists, Shows, Songs, Requests, Ratings, Gigs, Venues, Growth. Four rewritten each sync, three append-only logs, one time series, one plain-English guide written once.
features.whyRelevant: Platform data, not an artist's own; the code comment says so explicitly. Not a customer feature.

features.name: The sheet has never actually run
features.whatItDoes: The whole export is a clean no-op until GSHEET_ID, GSHEET_EMAIL and GSHEET_KEY exist in Netlify. Verified today: production holds only ADMIN_CODE, AUTH_FROM, RESEND_API_KEY, STRIPE_SECRET_KEY and STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/_sheets.mjs:52-65; netlify/functions/_warehouse.mjs:405-406; tools/prod.py:90-92 says the same
features.flagGate: none — it is env-var gated, not flag gated
features.whyRelevant: Anything derived from "the sheet says" is derived from a spreadsheet that does not exist.

features.name: Shows tab — 24 columns per finished gig
features.whatItDoes: Date, started, artist, venue, city, minutes, songs played, votes, phones in room, networks, people who voted, voted %, top song, money, from votes, from tips, vote sales, tips, money source, asked-for-and-not-played, average stars, plan, show id.
features.whyRelevant: The richest per-night record MySet produces — and it is unreachable today.

features.name: A permanent per-song play-and-vote tally
features.whatItDoes: Because a song's vote count is destroyed when the next song starts, each night's contribution is stored under its showId in a separate document and re-summed each sync — so "votes all time" survives and a re-archived night replaces rather than double-counts.
features.whyRelevant: This is the only "which song does the room actually want" analytic that exists in code anywhere. It lives in the off spreadsheet, not in the app.

features.name: Growth tab — one row per sync
features.whatItDoes: Running totals of artists, paying artists, venues, paying venues, nights played, votes, phones, money, songs, requests, ratings, average stars and gigs booked, plus a column that says when a cap bit.
features.whyRelevant: Deliberately running totals, not deltas, so a chart line means something. Never run.

features.name: The sheet updates itself at 03:20 UTC
features.whatItDoes: A scheduled function calls the same sync the button does, no earlier than an hour after the last run, logged never thrown so a failure waits for tomorrow rather than retrying.
features.whyRelevant: It runs every night in production and logs "sheetcron: sheet is off".

features.name: A cap defers, never drops, and says so
features.whatItDoes: One sync covers at most 400 artists, 40 new nights each and 5,000 rows a tab; when a cap bites the run reports it in plain English and the remaining rows come next time. Watermarks commit per tab, immediately after that tab's rows land.
features.whyRelevant: Engineering rigour, not marketing.

features.name: A song called "=1+1" cannot execute in the sheet
features.whatItDoes: Any cell beginning = + - or @ is written with a leading apostrophe so Sheets shows it as text.
features.whyRelevant: Security detail, no marketing value.

features.name: No fan is identified anywhere in the export
features.whatItDoes: Phones are counted, never named. There is no device id in any tab, and no per-transaction money row.
features.whyRelevant: A genuine, code-enforced privacy claim: the audience never signs in, and the deepest internal export still cannot name one.

features.name: The room rates MySet, one device per week
features.whatItDoes: An "enjoying this?" prompt to the audience: 1–5 stars plus their own words, tagged with the show; at most one per device per week, enforced on the server; nothing stored without stars.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/_feedback.mjs:19-60; shown to the artist public/studio.html:1522-1537
features.whyRelevant: "What the room said" appears in the Money tab and the average per show lands in the Sheet's Shows tab. There are zero ratings in production today.

features.name: Download my data
features.whatItDoes: One JSON file with the account, profile, songs, gigs, setlists, songs-to-learn, community posts, ratings, tips and orders — and the show history list.
features.whyRelevant: Real and reachable. But it exports the history LIST ROWS only — not the per-night setlist, the wanted-but-never-played list, or the money breakdown. "Everything MySet holds about you" overstates it.

features.name: A gig on your calendar starts and ends the show for you
features.whatItDoes: A scheduler rings every two minutes and starts or ends shows from the artist's own calendar; a night started that way is archived exactly like a tapped one.
features.whyRelevant: It is why the nothing-happened guard matters, and it is how the founder's empty 4 September night got recorded — the show auto-started (`startedBy: 'schedule'`) and one phone turned up.

features.name: myset.vip/moneymodel — the passcode-gated projections dashboard
features.whatItDoes: A financial model of what MySet costs and earns at scale, served by a function from outside the published folder behind a four-digit passcode (2068 by default; FINMODEL_CODE is not set in production), noindexed, cookie remembered 30 days.
features.planGate: none — a shared passcode, not an account gate
features.whyRelevant: Added AFTER the landing page's last commit (f343b11, 2026-09-06) and live now — but it is a courtesy lock, not a vault. Never link it, never quote its projections as facts.

features.name: tools/prod.py — read production without anyone's password
features.whatItDoes: Reads the live blob store through the already-signed-in Netlify CLI: who is on the platform, plans, verification, whether Stripe is connected, and every key in the store.
features.whyRelevant: This is how the real numbers in this report were established.

features.name: tools/actuals.py — which nights actually happened
features.whatItDoes: Walks production history and applies five rules to separate real gigs from tests: nobody there, one phone and no votes, ten-plus phones on one network in under 30 minutes (a load test), shorter than 30 minutes, longer than 12 hours. Also measures account-wide deploys and, from bandwidth marks, polls per phone-hour.
features.whyRelevant: It is the only honest arbiter of "how many gigs has MySet run", and its answer today is ONE. It disagrees with every number the app itself displays.

trapsForCopy: THE HEADLINE ANSWER — WHICH NUMBERS ARE RIGHT. The landing page is right and both screenshots are wrong. MySet has run exactly ONE real gig: 30 August 2026, The Ugly Duckling Irish Pub, Koh Phangan, 2 hours 11 minutes, 10 songs, 21 votes, 8 people voting, $3.00 taken. `tools/actuals.py` run against production today returns `"shows": 1, "people": 8.0, "hours": 2.19` and lists six other archived nights as not-nights. The page's "one real gig — the eight people and twenty-one votes" (public/about.html:486-487, 652-653) is the only figure on this surface that is currently true.

THE SCREENSHOT SHOWING "2 shows, 10 audience, 23 votes, 66 songs" IS ALREADY ON THE LANDING PAGE. It is `/Users/perryidyll/Docs/MySet/public/about/profile.jpg`, dated 2 September 2026 and referenced at public/about.html:433. It is a stale snapshot of the founder's own public page, not new evidence. Today the same live page (curl https://myset.vip/api/profile) returns `{"shows":3,"votes":27,"people":4,"songs":66}` — so the picture on the marketing page contradicts the page it is a picture of, in three of five numbers.

WHY THE NUMBERS MOVED, EXACTLY. (a) "Shows" went 2→3 because a calendar-auto-started show on 4 September was filed with 0 songs, 0 votes and 1 phone — the nothing-happened guard passed it because one phone counts as something (netlify/functions/_history.mjs:114,120). (b) "Votes" went 23→27 because the 30 Aug 19:28 show was re-archived on 4 September with a richer snapshot (2 songs, 6 votes) replacing an earlier poorer one (netlify/functions/_history.mjs:161-164). (c) "Audience" went 10→4 — a REGRESSION. The repair job writes `room: st.room || 0` (netlify/functions/_history.mjs:324), turning "this night predates the head-count" into a hard zero; the public page's fallback is `x.room ?? x.peakVoters` (netlify/functions/profile.mjs:20), and `0 ?? 8` is 0. So the one real gig's 8 voters now count as zero people on the public page, on the venue pitch (netlify/functions/_pitch.mjs:100) and in venue stats (netlify/functions/_vstats.mjs:53). `tools/actuals.py:170` uses `room if room > 0 else peak` and gets it right — the app does not.

THE OTHER LANDING-PAGE SCREENSHOT IS A LOAD TEST. `/about/studio.png` (public/about.html:389-390, alt text "21 votes, 21 of 26 in the room") shows a Studio belonging to "Sam Cole", not Perry. Those figures are `hist_samcole_show-1788179016366` in production: 21 votes, 21 voters, 26 phones — all 26 on ONE network, over in 4 minutes, generated by tools/loadsim.py. Sam Cole is not in the artists registry at all. The page removed one seeded screenshot for exactly this reason (see the CSS comment at public/about.html:196-198) and left this one, two sections above the "we're not going to dress it up" honesty block. `/about/fills.png` (public/about.html:580) is also seeded Sam Cole data.

"SONGS" ON THE PUBLIC PAGE IS THE LIBRARY, NOT PERFORMANCES. 66 is how many songs are featured to the audience (netlify/functions/profile.mjs:32). The founder has played eleven songs on MySet, ever. Never write "66 songs played".

A NIGHT'S LENGTH IS TIME-BETWEEN-BUTTONS, NOT SET LENGTH. `endedAt` is `Date.now()` at the moment of archiving (netlify/functions/_history.mjs:127), so it is when the artist pressed End or started the next show. One production night reads 107.9 hours (30 Aug → 4 Sep) because nobody ended it. Never quote an average gig length from history data.

"EVERY NIGHT IS RECORDED" IS TRUE; "EVERY SONG" IS NOT. The one real gig has `"playedUnlogged": true` and an empty played array — 10 songs played, zero titles logged, because the Studio was not open. The UI is honest about this ("the titles weren't logged", public/studio.html:2084) but a headline that promises a setlist record would be wrong for the only gig MySet has actually run.

THE VENUE NUMBERS TAB IS REAL, FREE, AND HAS NEVER SHOWN A NUMBER. Only one venue exists in production (Idyll Studios, unverified, Perry's own) and the only artist's shows are all at "The Ugly Duckling Irish Pub", which does not match — so venueStats returns zeros and the page renders "Nothing to count yet" (public/venue-studio.html:1235). Matching is by the venue NAME the artist typed into their own show/calendar (netlify/functions/_venues.mjs:200-208), plus the artist having to be listed in that venue's city. Two artists spelling the bar differently split the count.

THE PRO PLAN'S "ANALYTICS" DOES NOT EXIST. `analytics` is in NOT_BUILT (netlify/functions/_plan.mjs:130) and renders as a "Coming soon" veil on every plan including Pro. The sample rows inside it — "The Ugly Duckling · $184 over 6 nights", "Thursdays average 31 people", "Wonderwall pulled 12% of all votes" (public/studio.html:1338-1340) — are invented placeholder text and read exactly like real data. Same for presskit, branding and promote. The current page handles this correctly at public/about.html:645; keep it.

THE GOOGLE SHEET IS SWITCHED OFF IN PRODUCTION AND ALWAYS HAS BEEN. Verified against Netlify's production context: GSHEET_ID, GSHEET_EMAIL and GSHEET_KEY do not exist. The nightly 03:20 UTC cron runs and logs "sheet is off" (netlify/functions/sheetcron.mjs:53-55). Nine tabs of code, zero rows ever written. It is also founder-only platform data by design, so it is not an artist-facing feature under any circumstances (netlify/functions/admin.mjs:211-214).

NO CARD MONEY HAS EVER COME THROUGH A CONNECTED ARTIST ACCOUNT. The only money in any archived night is $3.00 of UNTAGGED payment on the founder's own gig, recorded as `unattributed` because it predates show tagging (netlify/functions/_history.mjs:59). Its `gross` is $0.00. `unattributed` is a window figure and must never be summed across nights — the code says so at netlify/functions/_history.mjs:200-205.

"THE BOOKS ARE OWNER-ONLY" IS TRUE FOR THE STATEMENT AND FALSE FOR THE NIGHTLY TAKINGS. Earnings, books and their CSVs are gated to the account owner (netlify/functions/admin.mjs:1578-1590). But /api/history has no role check at all (netlify/functions/history.mjs:8-9) — any signed-in seat, including a 'crew' member who can otherwise only run the show, can read every past night's gross, its vote-pack and tip totals, and the tip notes. Do not write "only you can see what you earned".

"DOWNLOAD EVERYTHING MYSET HOLDS ABOUT YOU" OVERSTATES THE EXPORT. It carries the history index ROWS only (netlify/functions/_account.mjs:43) — not the per-night setlist, not the wanted-but-never-played list, not the money breakdown or the tip notes. Those exist on disk and are not in the file.

THE PAST-SHOWS SEARCH ONLY EXISTS AFTER FOUR NIGHTS. `${H.shows.length>3?...}` at public/studio.html:2118. Nobody on the platform has ever seen it. Same class of thing: "Tonight so far" is titled "Last show — finished" once the show ends, and the archived row is only hidden from the list while the show is genuinely live (netlify/functions/history.mjs:57-65).

"A NIGHT WHERE NOTHING HAPPENED IS NOT A NIGHT" IS WEAKER THAN IT SOUNDS. The guard passes if there is ANY of: a song, a leftover vote, one phone in the room, or a now-playing song (netlify/functions/_history.mjs:120). One phone that opened the voting page and never tapped is enough to file a night and add 1 to the public Shows count — which is precisely what the 4 September record is.

TWO PIECES OF IN-REPO DOCUMENTATION ARE STALE ON THIS SURFACE. INVARIANTS.md:1097 and the comment at netlify/functions/_warehouse.mjs:70-72 both say the song tally is "bounded to the same 100 shows _history.mjs itself keeps" — the history index now keeps 400 (netlify/functions/_history.mjs:213) while KEEP_SHOWS is still 100 (_warehouse.mjs:75). And tools/prod.py:90-92 asserts "there is NO Google Sheet and never was", which is true today but is a hard-coded sentence, not a check.

NOTHING ON THIS SURFACE IS FEATURE-FLAGGED. The only two flags that exist are voteFinal and featuredShows (netlify/functions/_flags.mjs:27-50), neither of which touches history, analytics or the warehouse. Any "we're testing this" framing would be wrong here.

NOTHING ON THIS SURFACE HAS CHANGED SINCE THE LANDING PAGE'S LAST EDIT — with one exception. Diffing 9e9fde4..HEAD, no history, warehouse, sheet or stats file was touched. The one new thing the page has never heard of is myset.vip/moneymodel: a passcode-gated (2068, hard-coded — FINMODEL_CODE is not set) financial projections dashboard added in f343b11 and live now. It is noindexed and explicitly "not a vault" in its own header comment. Do not reference it, do not link it, and do not quote its projections.

appCatalogue.surface: Admin, moderation and the founder-only surface
appCatalogue.summary: There is no separate admin app. The founder's console is a handful of extra cards that appear inside the ordinary Artist Studio when the signed-in artist id happens to equal the hard-coded string `perry-idyll` (netlify/functions/_lib.mjs:118, _plan.mjs:154) — a review queue, feature-flag switches, a Google Sheet panel, promo-code minting, a venue list with a verify toggle, and MySet's own profit-and-loss. Alongside that sits one genuinely separate page, myset.vip/moneymodel, a whole-business projections dashboard served from outside the published folder behind a four-digit passcode (netlify/functions/moneymodel.mjs). Moderation is a different thing entirely and belongs to every artist and venue, not to the founder: hiding, pinning and replying to fan posts is free on every plan, permanently deleting one is a paid feature, and fans can report a post but a report is only a number the owner sees. The whole surface is used by exactly one person for the admin half and by every page owner for the moderation half.
appCatalogue.structure: The founder console has no URL of its own. Sign in to /studio as `perry-idyll` and three extra cards render at the top of the Settings tab — the ID review queue, the feature-flag switches, the Google Sheet panel (public/studio.html:2227-2229) — plus two more further down that tab: the promo codes he hands out and the full venue list with Verify/Un-verify buttons (public/studio.html:2358-2385). A sixth card, MySet's own books, renders at the bottom of the Money tab under the artist's own earnings statement (public/studio.html:2168, :3341). Every one of those cards is drawn only when `PLAN.owner` is true, which is a flag the server puts in the plan payload (netlify/functions/admin.mjs:68), and every one of the endpoints behind them refuses independently (netlify/functions/admin.mjs:176). The money model is the only genuinely separate screen: myset.vip/moneymodel serves a passcode form, a correct code sets a 30-day cookie and the dashboard is streamed from finance/model.html, which lives outside public/ and is bundled into the function (netlify.toml [functions.moneymodel]). Moderation lives in the artist's Community section of the Profile tab (public/studio.html:3463) and the mirrored venue one; the fan's side is a "⋯ → Report it" item on somebody else's post on the community page (public/community.html:588). The audience feedback loop starts on the voting page as an iOS-style star sheet and surfaces as a read-only "What the room said" card in the Studio's Money tab.
appCatalogue.design: Deliberately plain and unbranded — the founder cards use exactly the same list/row/button components as the rest of the Studio, with no admin chrome, no separate nav, no red "danger zone" styling. The ID review queue is three lines and two buttons ("Approve" / "No"), and the ID photo is deliberately not shown in it (public/studio.html:1496-1521). The flag switches carry a one-line plain-English "what off means" under each name and a standing instruction above them: "Both answers work. Run a gig each way, keep the better one, then delete the loser." The money model page is the exception and is a proper designed artefact: an accent-red passcode gate with a monospace letter-spaced code field, then a full dashboard with KPI tiles, five charts, a scale ladder, month-by-month projections and up to 20 saved scenarios. It ships its own Content-Security-Policy in the function's headers and rewrites the Chart.js CDN link and the Google Fonts stylesheet to local /vendor/ copies so nothing external loads (netlify/functions/moneymodel.mjs:60-72). Everything on this surface is `x-robots-tag: noindex, nofollow` and `cache-control: private, no-store`.

features.name: There is no admin app
features.whatItDoes: The founder's console is not a separate site, page or login — it is six extra cards that appear inside the normal Artist Studio when the signed-in artist id equals the hard-coded constant 'perry-idyll'.
features.whyRelevant: A copywriter who hears 'admin panel' will imagine a product surface. There is nothing to show and nothing to sell.

features.name: Founder status is one hard-coded string
features.whatItDoes: Every founder-only power in the app resolves to `aid === 'perry-idyll'`. There is no roles table for platform staff, no second admin, and no way to grant it.
features.whyRelevant: MySet is a one-person platform in code as well as in the story. Nothing here scales to a support team without new code.

features.name: Feature-flag switches
features.whatItDoes: Lists every declared runtime flag with its description, its 'what off means' sentence, its code default, the global setting and the value currently in force.
features.whyRelevant: Explains how Perry A/B tests product opinions across real gigs rather than shipping and undoing.

features.name: Flip a flag globally or for one artist
features.whatItDoes: Turns a named flag on, off, or back to the global answer, either for everyone or for a single artist id. Unknown flag names are rejected with an own-property check so `toString` cannot be persisted as a flag.
features.whyRelevant: Per-artist overrides exist, so two artists can be running different product behaviour on the same night.

features.name: Flag: voteFinal (default ON)
features.whatItDoes: Votes cannot be taken back once cast. Off means a second tap removes the vote and refunds it, which was the behaviour before 2026-09-02.
features.flagGate: voteFinal, default true (in code, not in the flags document)
features.whyRelevant: 'Your vote is final' is a real product behaviour today, but it is a switch one person can move between gigs, not a law.

features.name: Flag: featuredShows (default ON)
features.whatItDoes: Whether artists can pay $10 for one of three Featured spots on a city's listing for a night. Off means no Promote button, the endpoint refuses so nobody can be charged, and the Featured section is not rendered — but spots already paid for keep their record and reappear when it is switched back on.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/_flags.mjs:38-49; admin.mjs:1404-1424 (handleFeature reads the GLOBAL value only, never a per-artist override)
features.planGate: none — any plan including free can buy a spot
features.whyRelevant: A live, chargeable feature that is on trial with an explicit kill date in its own removal plan: if nobody buys, the flag AND the feature get deleted.

features.name: Flags are cached for 60 seconds
features.whatItDoes: The flags document is held in module scope with a 60s TTL because it is read on the hot audience poll; flipping a flag takes up to a minute to reach every warm server instance.
features.whyRelevant: A flag flip is not instant. Never describe it as a live toggle a room would see immediately.

features.name: Artist ID review queue
features.whatItDoes: Lists every artist waiting for a human decision on their verification tick — the legal name they typed, their page address, the name their account goes by, how strongly the two names matched, whether the date of birth matched, and when they asked.
features.whyRelevant: The verified tick on an artist page is, for some artists, a decision one human makes by hand.

features.name: The ID photo is never shown in the queue
features.whatItDoes: The review card deliberately does not render the ID image — the artist's own page is opened in another tab to see it — and the image slot 'idcheck' is deliberately absent from the servable SLOTS list so /api/img refuses it.
features.whyRelevant: A real privacy posture worth claiming: the ID is not browsable, not indexed, not part of a dashboard.

features.name: Approve or turn down an ID, and the photo is deleted either way
features.whatItDoes: Approving sets the artist's verified tick; rejecting can also UNDO a previous approval. Either decision deletes the ID photo, and the delete is verified by re-reading the slot — if it fails, the response says so rather than swallowing it.
features.whyRelevant: 'We delete your ID the moment we decide, and we check that it went' is a stronger and truer claim than 'we keep it secure'.

features.name: Approving re-runs the checks rather than trusting the queue row
features.whatItDoes: Before setting the tick, the server re-verifies that the artist is on a paid plan, has card payments live, and has an ID on file — and names which one is missing. An unknown artist id is a 404, not a cheerful ok.
features.whyRelevant: The tick genuinely cannot be handed out to an artist who has not met the conditions, even by mistake.

features.name: Automatic verification when Stripe already knows them
features.whatItDoes: An artist can get the tick with no human involved if they are on a paid plan, have card payments live, Stripe's own identity check has passed, their typed legal name strongly matches Stripe's, and their typed date of birth matches exactly. Any weakness sends it to the human queue. Nothing reads the photo — no OCR, no face comparison.
features.planGate: plus or pro — checks.paidPlan requires plan === 'plus' || 'pro' (_verify.mjs:353)
features.whyRelevant: The tick is a paid feature and the identity work is Stripe's, not MySet's. Both are worth saying plainly.

features.name: The date of birth is compared and thrown away
features.whatItDoes: The DOB is used once to answer one question against Stripe's verified record; only a boolean survives. The legal name is also dropped when the decision is made.
features.whyRelevant: A concrete, checkable privacy claim rather than a generic one.

features.name: Every venue in the system, in one list
features.whatItDoes: Lists every venue page ever claimed — id, slug, name, city, country, whether verified, how it was verified, when it was created — newest first.
features.whyRelevant: Platform-wide data in a page an artist otherwise owns. Never describe the Studio as showing only your own data without qualifying it.

features.name: Verify or un-verify a venue by hand
features.whatItDoes: Toggles a venue's tick and stamps it as verified 'by owner'. A venue with an email at its own website verifies itself automatically; everyone else waits for this button.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/admin.mjs:363-375; public/studio.html:2378 (copy: 'the rest are your call')
features.whyRelevant: A venue tick is either an automatic domain proof or one person's judgement — and the page already says so honestly.

features.name: Set a venue's plan by hand
features.whatItDoes: Sets a venue to free or Pro, because there is no venue self-serve billing checkout. Dropping a venue to free also strips its verified tick, on the reasoning that the tick is part of Pro and a purchased trust signal must stop when the purchase does.
features.whyRelevant: Venue Pro cannot currently be bought by a venue — a comment at admin.mjs:308 says so outright. Do not write venue pricing as self-serve.

features.name: Mint a comp code
features.whatItDoes: Creates a code with a plan (plus/pro), a discount percentage 1-100, a length in months 1-60, and a maximum number of uses (0 = unlimited).
features.whyRelevant: This is how early artists actually get Plus and Pro today, alongside the real Stripe checkout.

features.name: List and switch off codes
features.whatItDoes: Shows every code with its terms and how many times it has been used, and toggles a code on or off. Revoking is reversible.

features.name: Redeem a code (the artist's side)
features.whatItDoes: Any artist can type a code into Settings. A 100% code comps the plan outright with an expiry date; anything less is recorded as a discount to be applied at the next subscription checkout, because there was no billing to halve when this was written.
features.planGate: none — but OWNER_ONLY in admin.mjs:1579, so a band mate on a Pro seat cannot redeem
features.whyRelevant: A partial-discount code does not reduce anything today; it is stored as `discountPct` and becomes a Stripe coupon at checkout (_billing.mjs).

features.name: One free month to whoever referred them
features.whatItDoes: When a referred artist goes to a comped plan, the artist who referred them gets 30 days added to their plan (and is bumped to Plus if they were free). Paid at most once per referral, guarded by a `referralPaid` marker.
features.whyRelevant: Today it fires only on a 100% promo redemption — the comment at _plan.mjs:216-217 says billing will call it too 'when it exists', and billing now exists but does not call it. Do not promise 'refer a friend, get a free month' for paid signups.

features.name: MySet's own profit and loss
features.whatItDoes: A twelve-month P&L for the company: what came in (subscriptions plus MySet's cut of what fans paid artists, after Stripe's own fee), what went out (typed in by hand), and what was kept. Every revenue figure is read from Stripe balance transactions and only added up, never computed.
features.planGate: owner — double-gated: OWNER_ONLY role check at admin.mjs:1585 AND isFounder at admin.mjs:1365
features.whyRelevant: This is the founder's company accounts sitting inside the same app artists use. Never describe it as an artist feature.

features.name: Type in what a month cost
features.whatItDoes: Records hosting, email, domain, software, contractor and other costs per month by hand, because nothing can read a Netlify bill. Each figure carries who typed it and when. Entering zero removes the line.

features.name: The founder's gig money split out of the company's
features.whatItDoes: Perry's own vote packs and tips were taken on the platform Stripe account before Connect existed, so one balance holds his takings AND every artist's subscription. A splitter tags each balance transaction by its session metadata and returns his half separately from MySet's.
features.whyRelevant: Explains why the founder's own earnings card carries an extra sentence nobody else's does (studio.html:3322).

features.name: Download the company books as a spreadsheet
features.whatItDoes: The P&L as a CSV with different column headings from an artist's statement — Revenue / Stripe fees / Net received / Refunds / Costs / Profit / Transactions.

features.name: Google Sheet connection status
features.whatItDoes: Says whether the export is set up, whether Google is answering, the sheet's title, how many of the nine tabs are present, when it last ran and how many times.
features.whyRelevant: It is built but off until three environment variables are set in Netlify — the card renders 'Not connected yet' with a walk-through pointer until then.

features.name: Update the sheet now
features.whatItDoes: Walks the whole store and writes nine tabs of platform data — artists, songs, gigs, venues, shows, requests, ratings, growth, guide. Takes seconds, so it is a button somebody taps and never sits on a path a room is waiting for. A failure returns a sentence, not a 500.
features.planGate: owner — owner-only because the sheet holds EVERY artist's rows (admin.mjs:211-214)
features.whyRelevant: The reason it is founder-only is stated in code and is not about trust: it is platform data, not one artist's own.

features.name: The sheet updates itself nightly
features.whatItDoes: A scheduled function at 03:20 UTC runs exactly what the button runs. A second call inside the hour is a no-op. Failures are logged, never thrown, so a Google outage waits for tomorrow instead of being retried.

features.name: What the export deliberately leaves out
features.whatItDoes: No per-transaction money (Stripe is the source of truth; only each night's total lands), and never a fan's device id — counts of phones, yes; which phone, never.
features.whyRelevant: A real, checkable statement about what MySet does not collect about an audience.

features.name: myset.vip/moneymodel — the business projections dashboard
features.whatItDoes: An interactive model of the whole business: dials for artists, plan mix, gigs, room size and spend; KPI tiles, five charts, the formula line by line, four show sizes on every host, a scale ladder, month-by-month growth, and up to 20 saved scenarios with automatic summaries.
features.whyRelevant: It is on the production domain and reachable by anyone who knows the address and the four digits. It is not a customer feature and must never be linked from marketing.

features.name: The money model's four-digit passcode
features.whatItDoes: The dashboard lives outside the published folder so nothing leaves the server until the code is given. A correct code sets a 30-day HttpOnly cookie carrying a hash of the code, not the code. `?signout=1` clears it.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/moneymodel.mjs:39 (CODE falls back to '2068' when FINMODEL_CODE is unset), :43 (stamp), :104-132
features.whyRelevant: The file itself calls this 'a courtesy lock, not a vault' and says anything that would ruin the business if seen does not belong on it.

features.name: The money model moved address on 6 Sep
features.whatItDoes: It launched on 5 Sep at /financialmodel and was renamed to /moneymodel the next day; the old address 301s so a saved link still lands.
features.whyRelevant: This is NEWER than the landing page's last edit (9e9fde4, 2026-09-05 21:59), so about.html has never heard of it — correctly, since it should not.

features.name: The founder's recovery key
features.whatItDoes: An `ADMIN_CODE` environment variable that authenticates as the founding artist with owner role from any device, checked before any artist's own studio code so a lockout can never shut him out of his own platform.
features.whyRelevant: It cannot be read back — Netlify masks it — which an earlier session mistook for a broken key (tools/prod.py:11-18).

features.name: Reading production with no password
features.whatItDoes: A local script that reads the live Blobs store through the already-signed-in Netlify CLI: a health report, every key in the store, or one document pretty-printed. Read-only by design; it cannot act as an artist.
features.whyRelevant: Full owner-level read access to everything the app has ever stored exists outside the app entirely. Relevant to any privacy claim about who can see what.

features.name: Hide a fan's post — free on every plan
features.whatItDoes: Takes a post off the public page instantly and reversibly. Every artist and every venue can do it on any plan, on the reasoning that an owner must be able to remove something offensive the second they see it.
features.whyRelevant: The safety floor of the whole community feature, and it is deliberately not a paid feature.

features.name: Hiding also deletes the post's photos and clip
features.whatItDoes: Photos and clips are served by URL and the image endpoint does not know whether a post is hidden, so hiding removes the bytes. The words stay and can be un-hidden; the pictures do not come back. The Studio says this out loud in the confirm dialog before the tap.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/_community.mjs:266-272 (the reasoning), :296-303 and :313-316 (the deletes); public/studio.html:3471-3472 (the confirm text)
features.whyRelevant: Hiding is described everywhere as 'undoable' — it is undoable for the words only. The media is gone for good. That asymmetry is easy to get wrong in copy.

features.name: Deleting a post for good is a paid feature
features.whatItDoes: Permanently erasing a fan's post — record, photos, clip and likes — requires Plus or Pro for an artist, and Pro for a venue. Refused server-side with a 402 in the same words the Studio shows before the tap.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/admin.mjs:1287-1292; _plan.mjs:161 (moderateAllowed), :90 and :108 (moderate: true on plus and pro), :74 (false on free); venueadmin.mjs:542-551 (Pro on the venue side); public/studio.html:3484 (canDelete)
features.planGate: plus (artist) / pro (venue) — with a founder bypass, _plan.mjs:161
features.whyRelevant: The wording matters: what a paid plan buys is erasing, not moderating. Moderating is free.

features.name: Pin a post, and reply to it once
features.whatItDoes: The owner can pin posts to the top of their community feed and leave exactly one reply per post, in their own words. Both are free on every plan.
features.whyRelevant: One reply per post is a deliberate cap, not a limitation to apologise for.

features.name: A fan can report a post — and it is only a count
features.whatItDoes: A '⋯ → Report it' item on somebody else's post. One report per device. It increments a number the owner sees next to the post in red; it never hides or removes anything on its own.
features.whyRelevant: There is no automated takedown, no queue, and nobody at MySet ever sees a report. It goes to the artist. Never imply platform moderation.

features.name: The owner's view of their feed
features.whatItDoes: Shows hidden posts as well as visible ones, plus the report count for each — and still never shows a device id.
features.whyRelevant: Reinforces the 'audience never signs in' posture: even the artist cannot identify who posted.

features.name: A fan can edit their own post for 24 hours
features.whatItDoes: Long enough to fix a typo the morning after; short enough that a five-star review cannot quietly become a one-star one months later under a reply the artist already wrote. Deleting your own words has no window.

features.name: MySet asks the room what it thought
features.whatItDoes: An iOS-style 'Enjoying MySet?' sheet on the voting page: five stars and an optional note. Never before an hour of accumulated VISIBLE use, never more than once a week, never again once answered, and never mid-vote, over another sheet, or between songs.
features.whyRelevant: The only time MySet ever asks an audience member for anything, and the restraint around it is the story.

features.name: The weekly rating limit is enforced on the server too
features.whatItDoes: At most one rating per device per week and nothing stored without a star count, checked in the function as well as in the page, because a browser-side limit is a suggestion. A rejected rating never looks like a failure to the fan.

features.name: 'What the room said' in the Studio
features.whatItDoes: A read-only card in the Money tab showing the average out of five, how many people rated, and up to six recent notes. Deliberately placed next to the money.
features.whereInCode: public/studio.html:1522-1540 (fbCard), :2168; netlify/functions/_feedback.mjs:66-76 (shapeFeedback — notes only, never a device id)
features.whyRelevant: The average survives trimming because the running total is kept separately from the list of notes; only the last 200 notes are kept.

features.name: Three roles: owner, member, crew
features.whatItDoes: One table says what a role means. Owner: money, plan, payouts, access, the page address, recovery codes, export, deletion. Member: the page and the show, sees money totals but never moves money. Crew: tonight only — run the show and the requests. An unrecognised role string falls back to crew.
features.planGate: none — but seats are 1 on free and Plus, 5 on Pro (_plan.mjs:65, :89, :107)
features.whyRelevant: Roles exist and are enforced, but only Pro has more than one seat, so for almost everyone today there is exactly one role: owner.

features.name: Moderation is a member capability, not an owner one
features.whatItDoes: postReply, postHide and postDelete map to the 'community' capability, which members have and crew do not. So a band mate on a Pro seat can moderate the community page; the sound engineer running the screen cannot.
features.planGate: pro for a second seat to exist at all

features.name: Money and the account are the owner's alone
features.whatItDoes: Fourteen actions are refused for anyone but the owner even on a five-seat Pro page: every billing action, the Stripe portal, invoices, plan changes, the retention offer, promo redemption, export, deletion, payout setup, ID upload, the studio code, both statements, the books, and buying a featured spot. planGet is deliberately NOT on the list, because a member needs the limits or every locked control renders live on first paint.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/admin.mjs:1566-1590 (OWNER_ONLY); auth.mjs:211-217 (the parallel list on the auth door)
features.whyRelevant: A specific and defensible security story: a band mate could otherwise have opened the owner's card details or created the payout account with the wrong country, which Stripe will never let anyone change afterwards.

features.name: Recent account activity
features.whatItDoes: A per-account log of sensitive events — sign-outs, revoked sessions, passkeys added and removed, recovery codes made, deletion started and cancelled — capped at 100 entries. Readable by owner and member, refused for crew.

features.name: Leaving takes two screens and then thirty days
features.whatItDoes: Typing DELETE marks the account, takes the public page offline the same day and cancels the billing on the spot. Nothing is erased for a month, and one tap in Settings brings it all back. Every sign-in address on the account gets an email with the exact date. The founding account cannot be deleted this way.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/admin.mjs:120-151; _account.mjs:110 and :193 (the founder refusal); _lib.mjs:1010-1030 (publicArtist returns null so every public endpoint 404s)
features.whyRelevant: A real, unusual guarantee: no document moves for thirty days, so undo restores everything rather than reconstructing it.

features.name: An account on its way out is read-only, not locked out
features.whatItDoes: While an account is marked for deletion, every action except six answers with the same sentence and a 423. The six are: read your plan, undo the deletion, export your data, free up your page address, open the billing portal, and read or download your earnings statement — because somebody leaving has thirty days to take their tax records with them.

features.name: The thirty-day erase runs itself
features.whatItDoes: A two-minute cron does the purge on an hourly watermark, one account per ring, so a purge date can never eat a ring a show was waiting on.

features.name: Clips uploaded and never posted are collected
features.whatItDoes: Every hour, one owner's unposted clips older than two hours are deleted, on the reasoning that a 3MB blob nothing points at is worth collecting and nothing about it is urgent.

features.name: Take your account with you
features.whatItDoes: Returns the artist's data as a JSON payload. Owner-only and a 'member' capability of its own ('export').

features.name: Show venues my numbers (on by default)
features.whatItDoes: A venue can see how many people were in their own room and how many votes were cast, by night and by act, for artists who leave this on. Money is never in that payload at all, not even as a total. On by default; owner-only to change.
features.whyRelevant: Default-on data sharing with a third party. The default and the money exclusion both need saying.

features.name: Four Pro features are designed and not built
features.whatItDoes: `promote`, `analytics`, `presskit` and `branding` are plan flags with no code behind them anywhere in the repo. They are shipped to the Studio in a `soon` list and greyed as 'coming' on every plan INCLUDING Pro — and including for the founder, who is comped to Pro and would otherwise see four dead ends presented as his.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/_plan.mjs:112-130 (NOT_BUILT); admin.mjs:393-407 (shapeLimits ships `soon`); public/studio.html:1287-1310 (isSoon before PLAN.owner); test/limits.mjs:146-163 asserts both directions
features.planGate: pro on paper; nothing turns them on
features.whyRelevant: The landing page already marks these Soon. The list is enforced by a test that also asserts anything NOT in it is genuinely enforced somewhere, so it cannot rot in either direction.

features.name: The four unbuilt features have full marketing cards in the Studio
features.whatItDoes: analyticsCard, presskitCard and brandingCard render fully designed previews with example figures ('The Ugly Duckling · $184 over 6 nights', 'Thursdays average 31 people', 'Wonderwall pulled 12% of all votes') behind a lock.
features.whyRelevant: TRAP: those numbers are illustrative placeholders inside a locked preview, not real data from any gig. They must never be quoted as evidence.

features.name: Pay $10 to feature a gig in a city
features.whatItDoes: Three spots at the top of a city's listing for one night, $10 each, first come first served. The slot is HELD before checkout so a double tap finds its own hold; a payment that arrives after the night filled up is refunded in full and the message says so.
features.planGate: none — NO plan gate; a free artist can buy a spot. Owner-only within the account (admin.mjs:1586-1588)
features.whyRelevant: This is a live, paid, any-plan feature that is completely separate from the unbuilt Pro `promote` flag, despite both being about promoting gigs in cities.

features.name: Turning the featured flag off cannot look like a refund
features.whatItDoes: With the flag down nothing new may be bought and the endpoint refuses — but spots already paid for are still listed and reappear the moment it is switched back on.

features.name: Founder bypass: merch
features.whatItDoes: Selling merch from the community page is a Plus feature, but the founder is allowed regardless of plan, because his account predates the registry and the plan lookup returns 'free' for him.
features.whyRelevant: Anything seen working on Perry's own page may be working because of a bypass, not because the plan allows it.

features.name: Founder bypass: permanent post deletion
features.whatItDoes: Same shape as merch — the founder can delete a post for good without a paid plan.
features.whereInCode: netlify/functions/_plan.mjs:159-161; admin.mjs:1288-1291; public/studio.html:3480-3484 (the page mirrors the server bypass)

features.name: Founder bypass: setting your own prices
features.whatItDoes: Changing the free-vote count, the pack prices, and what a replay or a song request costs is a Plus feature; the founder is exempt. The code calls the bypass 'load-bearing, not a courtesy'.

features.name: Founder bypass: the show cap and the room ceiling never apply
features.whatItDoes: The free plan's four-shows-a-month limit and the per-plan audience ceiling are both skipped entirely for the founder.
features.whyRelevant: The one artist playing six or seven nights a week on MySet is the one artist the cap does not apply to.

features.name: Founder bypass: card payments work without Stripe Connect
features.whatItDoes: Every money button in the app asks one question — has this account finished Connect onboarding — and the founder's account answers yes unconditionally, because it predates Connect and charges on the platform account directly.
features.whyRelevant: This is the true shape of the honest note on the landing page — but see the traps: other artists CAN now onboard.

features.name: PLAN.owner unlocks every gated control in the page
features.whatItDoes: The Studio's one availability function returns true for every flag when PLAN.owner is set, except anything in the `soon` list. So the founder sees the whole Studio ungated.
features.whereInCode: public/studio.html:1280 (if(PLAN.owner) return true), preceded by :1279 (isSoon wins)
features.whyRelevant: Screenshots taken from the founder's Studio show a Studio no paying customer has.

features.name: A venue's own earnings statement
features.whatItDoes: The same reporting layer artists get, scoped to the venue's connected Stripe account, for a venue that takes tips or sells merch. Owner-only by construction — it is on neither the crew nor the manager list, and anything not on those lists is owner-only.
features.planGate: none — but Stripe Connect must be live for the venue

features.name: Your earnings — the artist's own statement
features.whatItDoes: Twelve months of gross taken, Stripe fees, MySet's fee, net, refunds and payouts, downloadable as a CSV to hand to an accountant. Never goes further back than the day the account was created, so a new artist does not see twelve rows of zero.
features.whyRelevant: Every figure comes straight from Stripe balance transactions and is only summed, never computed. That is a strong claim and it is true.

trapsForCopy: THE LANDING PAGE IS WRONG ABOUT CARD PAYMENTS. about.html:415-418 and :654-657 say payments 'run on the founder's own gigs today' and 'no other artist can take money through MySet'. Stripe Connect onboarding is built and reachable: payStart / payDashboard / payStatus in admin.mjs PROFILE_ACTIONS (admin.mjs:1535-1540), _connect.mjs in full, and connectReady reads a real `connect_<aid>` document with `chargesEnabled` (_pay.mjs:33-38). The founder clause at _pay.mjs:35 is a BYPASS for an account that predates Connect, not the only path. The stale comment at _pay.mjs:30-32 ('Returns false for everyone today because Connect is not built yet') is itself out of date — read the code under it, not the comment.

THE LANDING PAGE IS ALSO WRONG THAT PLUS AND PRO CANNOT BE BOUGHT. about.html:658-660 says 'There's no checkout, so nobody is being charged for anything.' Stripe Billing shipped 2026-09-04 (commit 6fae274): planCheckout, planFinish, planChange, planPortal, planInvoices, planSync and a retention offer, all in admin.mjs:79-113 over _billing.mjs. Products and prices are created on first use so a fresh Stripe account works without anything being clicked in a dashboard.

'PROMOTE' MEANS TWO DIFFERENT THINGS AND ONLY ONE IS REAL. The Pro plan flag `promote` — 'list gigs in cities you don't normally play' (_plan.mjs:74) — is in NOT_BUILT and has no code anywhere. Featured Shows — $10 for one of three spots at the top of a city's night — IS built, IS charged, and is NOT plan-gated at all: a free artist can buy one (admin.mjs:1404-1529, _featured.mjs:40-41). Never merge these two into one sentence.

'HIDING IS UNDOABLE' IS ONLY TRUE OF THE WORDS. Hiding a post permanently deletes its photos and its clip (_community.mjs:296-303, :313-316) because the media endpoints cannot know a post is hidden. Un-hiding brings back the text and nothing else. The Studio's own confirm dialog says this (studio.html:3472); marketing copy must not soften it to 'hide it and put it back'.

MODERATION IS FREE; ERASING IS PAID. postHide, postPin and postReply are free on every plan for artists and venues (admin.mjs:1281-1296). Only postDelete is gated — Plus for an artist, Pro for a venue (admin.mjs:1287-1292, venueadmin.mjs:548-550). Writing 'moderation tools are a Plus feature' would be false and would also break the safety promise the code is built around.

A REPORT IS A NUMBER, NOT A TAKEDOWN, AND NOBODY AT MYSET SEES IT. reportPost only increments a counter shown to the page owner (_community.mjs:245-263). There is no platform moderation queue, no automated hiding, no trust-and-safety review. Never imply MySet reviews reported content.

THE FOUNDER'S STUDIO IS NOT THE CUSTOMER'S STUDIO. Six extra cards render only for him (studio.html:1246, :1458, :1497, :2358, :3342), and PLAN.owner returns true for every gated feature (studio.html:1280). Any screenshot or demo recorded from Perry's account shows a product no paying customer has — including merch on free, permanent deletion on free, custom pricing on free, no show cap, no room ceiling and live card payments without Connect.

THE FREE PLAN'S NUMBERS ARE 4 SHOWS A MONTH AND 200 PEOPLE IN A ROOM, and the room ceiling is NEW (added 2026-09-05, commits 421d5ac / 9e9fde4). Free 200, Plus 1,000, Pro 2,000 (_plan.mjs:63, :88, :106). Pro was briefly written as 3,000 and was deliberately brought down; the code says 'sell what the app can do, not what the margin could afford'. Do not resurrect 3,000, and do not describe any plan's room as unlimited.

myset.vip/moneymodel IS ON THE PRODUCTION DOMAIN AND IS NOT A CUSTOMER FEATURE. It is the whole business model with revenue, cost and break-even projections, behind a four-digit passcode that falls back to '2068' in code when FINMODEL_CODE is unset (moneymodel.mjs:39). The file itself calls this 'a courtesy lock, not a vault'. It must never be linked, screenshotted, or mentioned in anything public — and it is newer than the landing page's last edit, so about.html has never referenced it.

THE FOUNDER-ONLY ENDPOINTS CHECK THE ARTIST ID, NOT THE ROLE. admin.mjs:176 gates flagList, flagSet, sheetStatus, sheetSync, idQueue, idApprove, idReject, venuePlan, promoList, promoCreate, promoRevoke, venueList and venueVerify on isPlatformOwner(aid) alone. None of those thirteen is in admin.mjs's OWNER_ONLY set (:1578-1588) or the CAPABILITY map (:414-423), so any sign-in on the founder's own account — including a 'crew' one — reaches them. `books` and `bookCost` ARE double-gated (OWNER_ONLY at :1585 plus isFounder at :1365). Do not describe the founder console as protected by roles.

PROMO CODES BELOW 100% DO NOTHING UNTIL CHECKOUT. redeemPromo comps the plan outright only at 100%; anything less just records `discountPct` and `pendingPlan` for a future subscription checkout to turn into a Stripe coupon (_plan.mjs:203-205). A '50% off' code does not lower a bill today.

'REFER A FRIEND, GET A FREE MONTH' ONLY FIRES ON A COMPED CODE. rewardReferrer is called from exactly one place — a 100% promo redemption (_plan.mjs:208). Its own comment says billing will call it 'when it exists'; billing now exists and does not call it. A referral that converts into a real paid subscription pays nobody.

THE GOOGLE SHEET IS BUILT BUT OFF. sheetStatus renders 'Not connected yet' until three environment variables are set in Netlify and the sheet is shared with a service address (studio.html:1474-1477, _warehouse.mjs:632-643). It is also founder-only for a stated reason that is not about trust: the sheet holds every artist's rows, so it is platform data (admin.mjs:211-214).

THE VERIFIED TICK HAS TWO PATHS AND ONE OF THEM IS A HUMAN. An artist can be verified automatically only if they are on a paid plan, have card payments live, Stripe's identity check has passed, AND both their typed legal name and date of birth match Stripe's record (_verify.mjs:404-475). Everything else goes to a queue only Perry sees. And nothing in the app ever reads the ID photo — no OCR, no face match (_verify.mjs:392-399). Venue ticks are different again: a domain-matched email verifies instantly, everyone else waits for Perry (admin.mjs:360-362).

A VENUE CANNOT BUY VENUE PRO. There is no venue self-serve billing checkout; the founder sets a venue's plan by hand, and dropping a venue to free strips its tick (admin.mjs:308-331). _billing.mjs mentions venue owners as `v_<vid>` but the purchase path an artist has does not exist for a venue in admin.mjs.

FLAGS ARE NOT INSTANT AND CAN BE PER-ARTIST. The flags document is cached for 60 seconds in every warm server instance (_flags.mjs:67), and flagSet accepts an artistId so two artists can be running different behaviour the same night (admin.mjs:195-205). The one exception is Featured Shows, which deliberately reads the GLOBAL value only so an artist cannot be sold a spot no city would render (admin.mjs:1406-1410).

'DELETE YOUR ACCOUNT' NEVER MOVES A DOCUMENT FOR THIRTY DAYS. The page goes dark the same day and billing stops on the spot, but nothing is erased until a cron purges it a month later, so undo is a restore rather than a rebuild (admin.mjs:120-151, autocron.mjs:60-71). During those thirty days the account is read-only, not locked out — six actions still work, including downloading the earnings statement (admin.mjs:1558-1559). The founding account is refused outright (_account.mjs:110, :193).

'SHOW VENUES MY NUMBERS' IS ON BY DEFAULT. shareStats defaults to true and the code reads `!== false` everywhere (admin.mjs:164-173). Money is never in the venue payload at all, not even as a total (studio.html:2389-2390). Both facts need stating together; the default-on half is the one a privacy-minded reader will care about.

THE FOUR 'SOON' CARDS IN THE STUDIO CONTAIN INVENTED EXAMPLE FIGURES. 'The Ugly Duckling · $184 over 6 nights', 'Thursdays average 31 people', 'Wonderwall pulled 12% of all votes' (studio.html:1336-1340) are placeholder illustrations inside a locked preview for a feature with no code behind it. They are not measurements and must never be quoted as proof.

THE AUDIENCE RATING PROMPT IS DELIBERATELY RARE. It waits for an hour of VISIBLE use accumulated across visits, asks at most once a week, never asks again once answered, and never appears mid-vote, over another sheet, or between songs (vote.html:335-370). The server enforces the weekly limit independently (_feedback.mjs:43-48). If you write about it, the restraint is the point.

THERE IS NO PLATFORM SUPPORT TEAM IN THE CODE. Founder status is the literal string 'perry-idyll' (_lib.mjs:118) and there is no way to grant it. Alongside that, a local script reads the entire production store through the signed-in Netlify CLI (tools/prod.py). Any claim about who can see a user's data has to account for both.

appCatalogue.surface: The app shell — PWA/install, service worker, offline, pull-to-refresh, performance, security headers and SEO
appCatalogue.summary: MySet has no native app and no build step: eight hand-written single-file HTML pages sit on Netlify's CDN, share exactly two external files (`/app.css` 3.4 KB gzipped and `/pull.js` 2.8 KB gzipped), and talk to Netlify Functions over `/api`. On top of that sits a deliberately timid PWA layer — three web manifests (fan / Artist Studio / Venue Studio), one service worker registered by every page, and one shared pull-to-refresh gesture — plus a security-header block in `netlify.toml` that is unusually strict for a site this small. The audience never installs anything: a fan scans a QR, a web page opens, and the voting page is ~31 KB gzipped in total. Installing is offered only to artists and venues (for home-screen launch and iPhone push alerts) and, oddly, to fans on the public what's-on home page. The whole surface is engineered around one scenario — a cheap phone on bad bar wifi at 10pm — which is why navigations are network-first, nothing is precached, the poll rate backs off, and there are two "if it looks broken" escape hatches in the Artist Studio.
appCatalogue.structure: There is no shell in the SPA sense — every page is a standalone document that boots itself. Entry points: `myset.vip/` (index.html, what's-on home, carries the install banner), `/about` (about.html, the landing page), `/:slug` (artist.html), `/:slug/vote` (vote.html), `/:slug/community` and `/v/:slug/community` (community.html), `/v/:slug` (venue.html), `/studio` and `/signup` (studio.html), `/venues` (venue-studio.html), and `/moneymodel` (a passcode-gated function, netlify.toml:23-30). `/stage.html` is now only a meta-refresh redirect to the Studio (public/stage.html:5-9) — a dead surface. Real files always beat the pretty-URL rules, and the `/:slug` catch-all sits last so `/moneymodel` and `/about` are not swallowed by it (netlify.toml:23-79). Every page carries: a `<link rel=manifest>`, an inline SVG favicon data-URI, a `<script src="/pull.js">` loaded blocking, and a late non-blocking `navigator.serviceWorker.register('/sw.js')` after `load`. The three public app pages (artist, venue, community) additionally paint a black `html{background:#0D0B0C}` from an inline style before any external file and then swap `app.css` in via `rel=preload`; both Studios paint `html{background:#000}` and load no `app.css` at all. index.html, about.html and vote.html still load `app.css` render-blocking. The Studios show an animated boot screen with rotating lines and a hard failsafe (studio.html:4244 at 6s, venue-studio.html:593 at 7s), and paint a full-screen "leave" splash on every internal link so a navigation never flashes white (studio.html:4211-4233).
appCatalogue.design: One accent (#FF375F → #FF6B45 gradient), an Apple-family system font stack, soft shadows and a spring easing curve, all defined as CSS custom properties in app.css:5-39. Public pages follow the phone's light/dark setting (app.css:40-51, plus per-scheme `theme-color` metas); both Studios are always dark by choice and have no `prefers-color-scheme` block anywhere, which is why the locked-feature veil in lock.css is hard-coded dark (lock.css:26-33). `prefers-reduced-motion` is honoured globally (app.css:190-193), in the pull spinner (pull.js:41), in the boot bars, and in the landing page's scroll reveals (about.html:268-270). The brand mark is three bars of unequal height — used as the favicon, the app icon, the intro animation on the home page, and the boot animation in both Studios. The landing page's reveal animations are scoped to a `.anim` class added by an inline script (about.html:36, 263-267), so if JavaScript never runs the content is visible rather than stuck at `opacity:0`. Locked premium features are shown greyed with a pill over them rather than hidden, with two honest states — `.lock` (a higher plan turns it on, tappable) and `.lock.soon` (designed and not built, not tappable on any plan including Pro) — lock.css:20-33.

features.name: Every page installs the service worker
features.whatItDoes: All eight pages register /sw.js on the window load event, HTTPS only, with the error swallowed.
features.whereInCode: public/index.html:614-616, public/about.html:822-824, public/vote.html:1159-1161, public/artist.html:547-549, public/venue.html:566-568, public/community.html:694-696, public/studio.html:4258-4260, public/venue-studio.html:1843-1845
features.whyRelevant: Just reading the landing page installs a service worker on the reader's phone; that is what makes the second visit instant.

features.name: Nothing is stored ahead of time
features.whatItDoes: The worker calls skipWaiting on install and precaches nothing at all, so there is no versioned shell that can go stale.
features.whyRelevant: This is the deliberate opposite of most PWAs and is the reason a bad deploy is fixed by the next deploy.

features.name: Pages always come from the network first
features.whatItDoes: A navigation is fetched fresh; the cached copy is only used when the fetch throws. A successful page is put in the cache for that fallback.
features.whyRelevant: Nobody is ever shown a stale version of the app, which is a real claim but the opposite of 'works offline'.

features.name: Votes and payments never come from a cache
features.whatItDoes: Any request whose path starts with /api/ is passed straight through untouched.
features.whyRelevant: A cached vote would be a lost vote. Underpins any trust claim about voting.

features.name: CSS, JS, images and fonts load instantly on repeat visits
features.whatItDoes: Anything matching .css .js .png .jpg .jpeg .webp .svg .woff/.woff2 .webmanifest is served from cache immediately and refreshed in the background.
features.whyRelevant: The concrete mechanism behind 'the page is tiny' on a second load — app.css and pull.js cost zero network.

features.name: The 'No connection' page
features.whatItDoes: When a navigation fails and nothing is cached for it, the worker synthesises an inline HTML 503 that says 'MySet needs the internet for the live bits.'
features.whyRelevant: This is the entire extent of 'offline'. MySet does not work offline and its own fallback page says so out loud.

features.name: Old caches are thrown away on upgrade
features.whatItDoes: On activate, every cache whose name is not the current one is deleted and the worker claims all open clients immediately.
features.whyRelevant: Cache is named myset-runtime-v3; bumping the name is the only eviction there is.

features.name: The worker can be told to stand down
features.whatItDoes: Posting the string 'myset-unregister' to the worker unregisters it, deletes every cache and reloads every open copy of the app.
features.whyRelevant: The last-resort escape hatch. Only the Artist Studio has a button that sends it.

features.name: Stripe and embeds are never touched
features.whatItDoes: Non-GET requests and any cross-origin request return before the handler does anything.
features.whyRelevant: Payments and YouTube/Spotify/Apple embeds bypass the worker entirely.

features.name: MySet installs as an app (fan)
features.whatItDoes: Fan manifest: name 'MySet — the room picks the next song', start_url /?src=pwa, scope /, standalone, portrait, theme #FF375F.
features.whyRelevant: This is linked from vote.html, artist.html, venue.html and community.html — so a fan CAN install MySet, which sits awkwardly beside 'no app to install'.

features.name: The Artist Studio installs as its own app
features.whatItDoes: Separate manifest, id /studio, start_url /studio?src=pwa, black background, dark theme #161413.
features.whyRelevant: An installed Studio opens straight into the Studio, not the city feed. It is also the precondition for iPhone alerts.

features.name: The Venue Studio installs as its own app
features.whatItDoes: Separate manifest, id /venues, start_url /venues?src=pwa.
features.whyRelevant: Venues get the same home-screen treatment as artists — but none of the Studio's other shell features (see below).

features.name: Long-press shortcuts on the installed icon
features.whatItDoes: The fan manifest declares two shortcuts — 'Artist Studio' → /studio and "What's on near me" → /.
features.whyRelevant: Android-only in practice; the two Studio manifests declare no shortcuts.

features.name: The installed app is locked to portrait
features.whatItDoes: All three manifests set "orientation": "portrait".
features.whyRelevant: An artist propping an iPad sideways gets a rotated portrait app, not landscape.

features.name: App icon and maskable icon
features.whatItDoes: Two 512×512 PNGs: one 'any', one 'maskable'. No 192px icon exists anywhere.
features.whyRelevant: Verified 512×512 on disk. Some Lighthouse/store checks still want a 192px entry.

features.name: The installed fan app's splash is always light
features.whatItDoes: The fan manifest sets background_color #F5F5F7 with no dark alternative, even though every public page has a full dark palette.
features.whyRelevant: A dark-mode phone launching the installed fan app flashes light grey before the dark page paints.

features.name: "Saved MySet to your home screen yet?" card
features.whatItDoes: A dismissible card on the public home page offering install; hidden when already installed or once dismissed (localStorage key myset.a2hs).
features.whyRelevant: This is the ONLY page that asks a fan to install. The voting page never does.

features.name: Real one-tap install on Android/Chrome
features.whatItDoes: beforeinstallprompt is captured and deferred; the card's button then says 'Install' and fires the real browser prompt. Otherwise it says 'How' and opens instructions.
features.whyRelevant: iOS has no such API, which is exactly why the fallback is a tabbed instruction sheet.

features.name: Step-by-step install instructions with iPhone/Android tabs
