trapsForCopy: "Nothing for your fans to install" is true of VOTING and not of the site. The public home page at myset.vip actively offers a fan an install banner and a footer 'Add to home screen' link (public/index.html:273, 279, 508-546), and vote.html/artist.html/venue.html/community.html all link the fan web-app manifest (public/manifest.webmanifest). The honest form is: nothing to install to vote — a fan scans and taps; a fan CAN save MySet to their home screen if they want to.

MySet does not work offline. The service worker's offline fallback literally says 'MySet needs the internet for the live bits' (public/sw.js:99-105). Nothing is precached (public/sw.js:17-20 and INVARIANT 0ax at INVARIANTS.md:974-979), and /api is never cached (public/sw.js:89). The only offline behaviour is a page you already loaded coming back from cache with a dead board.

"The page is tiny" is true and provable — vote.html is 24.5 KB gzipped, plus app.css 3.4 KB and pull.js 2.8 KB, so about 31 KB — but the Artist Studio is 81.5 KB gzipped (274 KB raw, 4,263 lines) in ONE file. Do not let a 'tiny' claim be read as covering the artist's own tool.

PERFORMANCE-PLAN.md:53 says the Studio is '197 KB raw, ~45 KB gzipped'. It was already 211 KB / 63 KB when that line was written and is now 274 KB / 81.5 KB. Do not quote any number out of that document.

"It backs off politely when the room goes quiet" (about.html:686) describes the polling ladder, which was rewritten on 2026-09-05 at 22:39 — forty minutes AFTER the landing page's last edit. The rungs are now 3s / 10s / 25s / 60s with ±20% jitter, the floor is set by the server based on room size (3s under 200 people, up to 20s past 3,000), and above the default floor another person's vote no longer wakes your phone (public/vote.html:1046-1123). The claim survives; the mechanism behind it is newer than the sentence.

"If a phone drops out it picks up where it left off" is true of state — the fan id lives in localStorage (vote.html:287-290), a failed vote is retried once with the same idempotent cast id (vote.html:523-535), and an unconfirmed payment is re-claimed for 26 hours (vote.html:1013-1018). It is NOT true of feedback: there is no offline banner or stale indicator anywhere on the voting page. The board just stops moving silently.

"Everyone's on their own phone and their own data, so you're not sharing one connection" (about.html:685) is a claim about the venue, not about MySet. Nothing in the code makes phones avoid the venue wifi. What IS in the code is that each phone talks only to Netlify's CDN over HTTPS, with HSTS preloaded (netlify.toml:64-68).

Alerts on the artist's phone are real Web Push and free on every plan — but they depend on VAPID keys being set as Netlify environment variables (netlify/functions/admin.mjs:1637-1642). If they are not, the Studio says 'Not switched on yet'. This repo cannot tell you whether they are set in production; check before claiming it works.

iPhone alerts do not work in a browser tab at all. The Studio must be added to the home screen first, and the code refuses to even offer the button otherwise (public/studio.html:3140-3141, 3152, 3195-3197). Any 'know the moment someone requests a song' line needs that condition attached for iPhone.

The Venue Studio gets none of the Artist Studio's shell extras: no push notifications, no 'Reload the Studio', no 'Clear what's stored on this phone'. It has the manifest, the service worker and pull-to-refresh, and that is all (public/venue-studio.html has no match for Notification/PushManager/hardReset/location.reload).

There is no stage or big-screen display. public/stage.html is a 605-byte meta-refresh to the Studio (public/stage.html:1-9) and has not been meaningfully edited since 2026-08-17. Do not describe a projector or TV view.

'Branding — your colours and logo on the audience pages' appears on the Pro plan card but is in NOT_BUILT (netlify/functions/_plan.mjs:130). It is greyed as 'coming' even for Pro. There is no white-label or themed fan page.

An artist sharing their own MySet link gets a generic preview: og:title 'MySet', og:description 'Live music. You pick what gets played.' and og:image /img/band.jpg — a relative path to a stock band photo (public/artist.html:21-23). The artist's real name is only set later by JavaScript (artist.html:495), which social scrapers do not run. Do not show a mocked-up rich link preview as if it is what MySet produces today.

Every app page ships an empty
and renders client-side (public/artist.html:249). There is no robots.txt, no sitemap.xml and no canonical URL anywhere except the dead stage.html. Do not claim SEO benefits, discoverability, or 'your page shows up in search'.

The security headers in netlify.toml apply to the static pages in public/ only. Function responses do not receive them — moneymodel.mjs restates the whole CSP itself and says so in a comment (netlify/functions/moneymodel.mjs:69-81). 'Every page is protected by the policy' is not quite right.

The CSP explicitly does NOT stop an injected inline script — script-src still carries 'unsafe-inline' because every page is one self-contained file (netlify.toml:88-98, INVARIANTS.md:1579-1582). What it stops is that script loading anything or sending anything out. Copy that says 'blocks malicious scripts' overstates it.

INVARIANT 0cl (INVARIANTS.md:1311-1315) says 'Video is a link, never an upload.' That is now false: as of 2026-09-06 fans upload real video clips up to 25MB and 30 seconds, chunked in 4MB pieces (netlify/functions/clipup.mjs:25-146, netlify/functions/_video.mjs:63-66). The invariants file has not caught up. Trust the code.

Netlify's Image CDN resizing is on the ARTIST page only — one line, public/artist.html:284. venue.html, community.html and index.html serve the original bytes. Do not claim site-wide automatic image optimisation.

Room size is not a hard limit and must never be described as one. Free 200 / Plus 1,000 / Pro 2,000 (netlify/functions/_plan.mjs:63, 88, 106) is a billing line: over it the room slows and the board shortens, nobody is refused a vote, and the artist is told afterwards (netlify/functions/show.mjs:32-46, test/roomsize.mjs:1-16). Pro was cut from 3,000 to 2,000 in the same commit that last touched the landing page.

Past about 200 phones a fan stops seeing the whole setlist — the board is trimmed to the top 40/25/15 (netlify/functions/_lib.mjs:865-871) with an on-screen note. Their own voted songs always survive the cut. If copy promises 'they see your whole setlist', add 'in a normal room'.

The three-bars logo used in the favicon, the app icon, the intro animation and both boot screens is the same mark. Only two icon files exist, both 512×512 (public/icons/). There is no 192px icon, no monochrome badge, and the installed fan app's splash background is hard-coded light grey (#F5F5F7, public/manifest.webmanifest:10) even on a dark-mode phone.
The installed apps are locked to portrait (all three manifests, line 9). Do not show a landscape tablet mock-up of the Studio.

'Print it once. It's good forever' (about.html:378) holds because renaming a page keeps the old slug resolving (netlify/functions/auth.mjs:452-453). But the QR points at the artist PAGE (https://myset.vip/{slug}, netlify/functions/qr.mjs:20), not straight at the voting screen — a fan lands on the profile and taps 'Join live', which only appears while a show is running (public/artist.html:389, 406-407).

The service worker caches successful navigations regardless of Cache-Control, because the Cache API ignores it. That includes /moneymodel, which the function marks 'private, no-store' (netlify/functions/moneymodel.mjs:75 vs public/sw.js:96). Not a fan-facing issue, but do not describe the worker as 'respecting no-store'.

finding.claimText: This file is sent to your browser because it has to be, in order to run… the data, the money, the accounts — are on the server, where they are authorised per request and where you cannot see them.
finding.evidence: True of accounts and money: netlify/functions/admin.mjs:1543-1545 opens with `const me = await requireArtist(req); if (!me) return bad('unauthorized', 401);` before any artist-side write, netlify/functions/venueadmin.mjs:24 does the same for venues, and netlify/functions/pay.mjs:77-80 refuses with 503 unless `canTakeMoney(aid, show)` (_pay.mjs:52-54) passes. Plan gating is genuinely server-side, not client-side: admin.mjs:1706-1708 re-checks `limits.pricing` on the server for freeCredits/packs/replayCost/askSet. But three endpoints mutate stored data with no session at all, deliberately: netlify/functions/vote.mjs (no auth import; identity is `cleanFanId(body.fan)`, a random string the browser minted at vote.html:287-289), netlify/functions/feedback.mjs:4-5 ("Public, like /api/vote — the audience never signs in (INVARIANT 9g), so this is anonymous by design"), and netlify/functions/community.mjs:114 (`const me = sha(String(fan)).slice(0,10)`). So "authorised per request" holds for everything with an account behind it and not for the audience path.
finding.proposedFix: …are on the server, where the accounts and the money are checked on every request and where you cannot see them. The audience never signs in, so their votes are checked against tonight's show rather than against a person.

check.correctedStatus: ACCURATE — no change needed (the sentence is a source-code notice, not marketing copy, and its claim holds on every path including the audience path)
check.correctedEvidence: public/about.html:6-9 (the sentence, inside the HTML copyright comment); public/about.html:373-375 and 672-674 (visible copy: "the fans never make an account", "No app, no account, no email, no password"); netlify/functions/vote.mjs:41-42,45,52-53,58,80,99-101,115,119-120 (per-request server checks on an anonymous vote); netlify/functions/_feedback.mjs:43-48 ("One per device per week, server-side"); netlify/functions/_community.mjs:186-190 and 205-207 (ownership proved inside the write against the stored device id); netlify/functions/pay.mjs:80 and 85 (canTakeMoney backstop; "price is whatever the artist set — never what the client claims") — and pay.mjs imports no session helper at all
check.reasoning:
Four independent problems with the finding, any one of which sinks it.

1. The accuser swapped "authorised" for "authenticated". The sentence says the data, money and accounts are "authorised per request" — i.e. each request's permission is decided on the server at request time, not in the file you are reading. It never claims every request carries a session. An anonymous vote IS authorised per request, against state the browser cannot touch: the artist must resolve (vote.mjs:41-42), the show must not be ended (:45), the song must be on tonight's list (:52-53) and still on offer (:115), the voting window must be open (:80), the cost comes from the artist's server-side pricing (costOf, :58), the cast must be affordable against server-held credits (:119-120: `creditsUsed(me, show) + need > total` → 402), and the cast id is de-duplicated inside the mutation (:99-101). Same for the two other endpoints cited: feedback is rate-limited "One per device per week, server-side" (_feedback.mjs:43-48) and validated 1–5 stars (:36); community edit/delete prove ownership *inside the write* against the stored value, with the code saying so explicitly — "the id arrives from a phone and proves nothing on its own" (_community.mjs:186-190, 205-207). Nothing on the audience path is decided client-side. That is exactly what the sentence asserts.

2. The accusation is internally inconsistent. It offers netlify/functions/pay.mjs:77-80 as proof the claim is TRUE — but pay.mjs has no session gate either; it imports no auth helper (grep: no requireArtist/requireVenue/requireSession/readSession in the file). What makes pay.mjs count as "authorised" is precisely a per-request check against server state (canTakeMoney, and "price is whatever the artist set — never what the client claims", pay.mjs:85). Apply that same standard consistently and vote.mjs, feedback.mjs and community.mjs pass it too. The accuser used one rule for the money endpoint and a stricter one for the audience endpoints.

3. One cited line does not say what it is claimed to say. community.mjs:114 (`const me = sha(String(fan)).slice(0,10)`) is not an identity bypass — it is the hash key for the "three clips per phone per day" rate-limit counter checked before an expensive upload (community.mjs:108-117). It is a server-side limit being enforced, i.e. evidence FOR the sentence, not against it. And feedback.mjs:4-5 is a code comment; the accuser read the comment as the behaviour, when the behaviour one call deeper (_feedback.mjs:41-59) is a CAS-guarded, server-enforced write.

4. The condition the accuser applies is one the page never implies — and the page explicitly denies it, twice, in the visible copy. about.html:373-375: "No app, no sign-up, no email, no password — the fans never make an account". about.html:672-674: "They scan a code, a web page opens, they vote. No app, no account, no email, no password. That is the single most important design decision in MySet." No reader can take "the accounts" in the hidden comment to include the audience when the page they are reading says in bold that the audience has none. Note also that the disputed sentence is inside an HTML comment — a copyright/anti-reuse notice addressed to someone viewing source, whose whole point is "copying this file gets you nothing, because the enforcement is not in it". That point is true of the audience path too: vote.html cannot mint credits, open the window, change replay pricing, or make a song votable.

Severity check the other way: is it worse or wider? No. I looked for a path where a client-supplied value decides a limit or a price and found the opposite each time — plan pricing is re-checked server-side (admin.mjs:1706-1708), pack prices come from `show.packs` not the body (pay.mjs:86), and the money gate fails closed (pay.mjs:162).

The proposed fix would also make the notice worse: it adds two sentences of product explanation to a copyright comment, restating a fact the visible page already makes twice, and it introduces a false contrast ("checked against tonight's show rather than against a person") that implies fan credits and post ownership are not checked per person — they are (vote.mjs:119-120 keys on the fan record; _community.mjs:189 compares the stored device id).
check.betterFix: None — leave public/about.html:6-9 exactly as written. If the reviewing agent still wants belt-and-braces against a literalist reading of a comment no visitor sees, the only defensible edit is a one-word tightening that costs nothing and claims nothing new: "…are on the server, where every request is authorised there and where you cannot see them." Do not add the audience sentence: it puts product copy inside a legal notice, duplicates about.html:672-674, and its "rather than against a person" clause is itself inaccurate about credits and post ownership.

finding.claimText: MySet — the room picks the next song
finding.evidence: The room's votes rank the queue; a person still presses play, and can press a different one. netlify/functions/admin.mjs:1785-1808 (`playTop`) ranks the votable pool and sets `show.nowPlaying = pool[0].id` — that is the room's winner. But admin.mjs:1771-1783 (`play`) sets `show.nowPlaying` to whatever song id the artist names, with no reference to votes. In the Studio both are one tap: public/studio.html:1923-1924 is the big "Start top voted — <title> (<n>)" button, and public/studio.html:1931 puts a "▶ Start" on every single queue row. There is no auto-advance anywhere in admin.mjs. So the room decides the order and the artist executes it — the fan page's "Winning — plays next" (public/vote.html:631) is a prediction the artist normally honours, not a lock.
finding.proposedFix: The headline can stand — the mechanism under it is real and an artist who could not override the room would not use this. If a clarifier is wanted it belongs a line down, not in the H1: "One tap starts whatever won."

check.betterFix: No change to the page. Specifically, do NOT add the proposed line — it is already on the page twice. If a future editor wants to strengthen anything, the only honest upgrade is the reverse of what was suggested: the page could say that the artist can start any song in the queue, not just the winner (public/studio.html:1931 puts "▶ Start" on every row, backed by admin.mjs:1771-1783 `play`). But that is an addition, not a correction — the current copy never claims otherwise, and the FAQ at about.html:676 already concedes artist discretion ("Then you play what you were going to play anyway"). Leave as is.
check.correctedEvidence: public/about.html:291 (the actual H1: "The room picks<br>the next song.<br><em>You just play it.</em>"); about.html:386; about.html:455; about.html:676; netlify/functions/_lib.mjs:694-702 and 790-797; netlify/functions/show.mjs:78,100; netlify/functions/stage.mjs:68-77; netlify/functions/admin.mjs:1785-1808
check.correctedStatus: ACCURATE — no change needed (the proposed clarifier is already present on the page, in the H1 and twice in body copy)
check.reasoning:
The finding is refuted on four independent grounds, three of them fatal. 1. IT AUDITS THE WRONG LINE. about.html:19 is not a headline at all — it is `MySet — the room picks the next song` (mirrored at :21 as og:title). The finding calls it "the H1". The page's actual H1 is at public/about.html:291 and is three lines: "The room picks
the next song.
You just play it." The artist's hand is not missing from the headline — it is the emphasised third line of it, set in italics as the payoff. The whole premise ("a clarifier belongs a line down, not in the H1") collapses: the clarifier IS the H1's last line. 2. THE PROPOSED FIX IS ALREADY ON THE PAGE, VERBATIM IN SUBSTANCE, TWICE. The accuser suggests adding "One tap starts whatever won." about.html:386 already reads "One tap starts the top song and hands everybody fresh votes." about.html:455 already reads "Why: the queue is ranked live, and one tap starts the winner." Adding the proposed line would be a third copy of the same sentence. 3. IT APPLIES A CONDITION THE PAGE NEVER IMPLIED. "Picks" is a choosing verb, not an executing verb. Nothing in the title, description (:20, :22), sub (:292) or body claims the song starts by itself; the word "automatically" appears nowhere, and the FAQ at :676 openly says the artist may just play what he was going to play. The finding measures the page against a claim of automation that the page does not make. 4. THE MECHANISM IS STRONGER THAN THE FINDING ALLOWS. I confirmed the accuser's code reading is mechanically correct — admin.mjs:1771-1783 `play` takes any song id, admin.mjs:1785-1808 `playTop` starts the ranked winner, studio.html:1923-1924 and :1931 are both one tap, and there is no auto-advance. But the finding misses that MySet goes out of its way to make the room's pick authoritative rather than advisory: rankSongs and votable in _lib.mjs (694-702, 790-797) are a single shared definition, with the comment "Used by show, stage and playTop so the audience can never be shown a winner the Studio won't start." show.mjs:78/100 (fan payload), stage.mjs:68-77 (big screen) and playTop (admin.mjs:1794-1799) all rank through it, and callers may narrow but "none of them may widen it." So vote.html:631's "Winning — plays next" cannot name a song the artist's own button would refuse to start. The room's ordering is a hard, non-divergent server fact; only the instant of execution is a human tap — exactly what the H1 says with "You just play it." Net: the underlying code observation is true, but it is not a discrepancy with the page. Every element of the proposed remedy is already shipped. Downgrade from AMBIGUOUS/minor to ACCURATE/no action.

finding.claimText: Free
finding.evidence: PLANS.free in netlify/functions/_plan.mjs is genuinely $0 with no expiry (`planOf` only downgrades, never lapses free) and no card anywhere in signup. But it carries three real limits the bare word does not carry: `gigs: 4` shows per calendar month, `audience: 200` phones in a room, and `cut: 0.10` — the platform's share of tips and vote sales. The page's own Free column states all three (public/about.html:607 "4 shows a month — up to 200 people in the room at each", public/about.html:611 "10% of money taken through the app", styled `li.no`, i.e. as a limitation). A reader could take the unqualified "Free" in a search snippet as "MySet never takes a cut", which is false at 10% — though honest note 2 (public/about.html:654-657) records that today the cut applies to nobody, because no artist but the founder can take money at all.
finding.proposedFix: Your fans vote from their phones on what you play next. Free for about a gig a week, no app for them to install, and it takes about two minutes to set up.

check.correctedStatus: OK — "Free" at public/about.html:20 is accurate as written; no change needed there. The real defect on this page is next door and is NOT minor: honest notes 2 and 3 (public/about.html:654-661) are both false against the code, and the accusation leans on note 2 as its mitigation.
check.correctedEvidence: public/about.html:20 (the full meta description, not a bare word); netlify/functions/_plan.mjs:19 (free price: 0); netlify/functions/_plan.mjs:137-142 (planOf never lapses free); netlify/functions/_auth.mjs:134 (new artist created plan:'free'); netlify/functions/_lifecycle.mjs:41 and :54 (gigCapFor / roomCapFor — the 4-gig and 200-phone ceilings are capacity, not price); netlify/functions/pay.mjs:167-168 (no Connect account → 503 'payments-not-configured', so a non-onboarded artist can never be cut); netlify/functions/_connect.mjs:78-86 (feeCents only fires on a direct charge); public/about.html:591 and :607-611 (the page's own "Everything the room sees is free. Always." plus all three free-tier limits stated in the Free column). Contradicting the accusation's mitigation: netlify/functions/admin.mjs:1105-1122 (payStart → ensureAccount/onboardingLink, open to any signed-in artist) with public/studio.html:1574,1600; and netlify/functions/_billing.mjs:121-160 (startCheckout, mode:'subscription') wired at netlify/functions/admin.mjs:44,77-84 (planCheckout) and driven from public/studio.html:3565 (startCheckout('plus'|'pro')), webhooks at netlify/functions/webhook.mjs:69-74.
check.reasoning:
The accusation misquotes the artifact. Line 20 does not say the bare word "Free". It says: "Your fans vote from their phones on what you play next. Free, no app for them to install, and it takes about two minutes to set up." The grammatical subject is "Your fans", and the clause immediately after "Free" is "no app for THEM to install" — three items in one list, all about getting the room in: it costs nothing, they install nothing, setup is two minutes. On the natural reading the referent is the room, and that is unconditionally true in code and undisputed by the accuser. The page says the same thing in its own words at about.html:591, "Everything the room sees is free. Always."

Even on the artist reading, "Free" is literally true. PLANS.free is price: 0 (_plan.mjs:19); a new artist is written into the registry as plan:'free' (_auth.mjs:134); planOf only ever downgrades, so free never lapses (_plan.mjs:137-142); and auth.mjs contains no Stripe call at all — sign-up is an email code or a passkey, no card. There is no code path by which a free artist is charged a subscription.

The three "limits" are not a price. gigs: 4 (_plan.mjs:33, enforced _lifecycle.mjs:41) and audience: 200 (_plan.mjs:63, enforced _lifecycle.mjs:54) are capacity ceilings on a free tier. Nothing in the word "Free" implies "unlimited" — that condition is the accuser's addition, not the page's implication. And cut: 0.10 is a revenue share on money the artist opts into taking: feeCents only produces a fee on a direct charge (_connect.mjs:78-86), and pay.mjs:167-168 refuses with 503 'payments-not-configured' unless the artist has completed Stripe Connect onboarding. An artist who never onboards pays MySet nothing, forever. A <meta name="description"> is a ~155-character SERP snippet, not a pricing table; the pricing table is on the same page and states all three limits explicitly (about.html:607, 611, the last one styled li.no).

The proposed fix is also weaker than the line it replaces, on the accuser's own terms. It still omits the 10% cut and the 200-person cap, so a reader could STILL read the snippet as "MySet never takes a cut" — the exact harm the finding is built on goes unaddressed. It reframes the sentence from the fan to the artist, spending the snippet's strongest and most literally-true claim (the room pays nothing) on a hedge. And it grows the description from 131 to 154 characters, right at Google's truncation edge, so "it takes about two minutes to set up" is the part likely to be cut.

Where the accusation does real damage is its mitigation, which is a stale doc read as behaviour — the specific error the brief warns against. It cites honest note 2 ("no other artist can take money through MySet, which also means the 10% above currently applies to nobody"). That is false: Stripe Connect onboarding is fully built and open to any signed-in artist (admin.mjs:1105-1122, Studio UI at studio.html:1574/1600), and pay.mjs:161-186 creates a direct charge on that artist's account with feeCents applied. The 10% is live code. Honest note 3 ("Plus and Pro can't be bought yet. There's no checkout, so nobody is being charged for anything") is also false: _billing.mjs:121-160 creates a subscription-mode Checkout Session, admin.mjs:77-84 exposes it as planCheckout, studio.html:3565 renders an "Upgrade to Plus/Pro" button that calls it, and webhook.mjs:69-74 handles the subscription events. So the page tells a visitor nobody can be charged while the Studio will in fact run a live Stripe subscription checkout. That is the finding worth writing up — at about.html:654-661, not at line 20.
check.betterFix:
Leave public/about.html:20 exactly as it is. If anything is touched in the meta area, the og:description at line 22 is the tighter of the two and neither is wrong.

Redirect the effort to public/about.html:654-661, where the page is actually contradicted by the code:

Note 2 currently claims no other artist can take money and that the 10% applies to nobody. Replace with something true, e.g. "2 · Getting paid runs through Stripe. Connect your own Stripe account in the Studio and tips, vote packs and merch are paid straight to you, with MySet's 10% (2% on Plus, 0% on Pro) taken off the top. Until you connect one, nothing on your page can take a card — and MySet takes nothing."

Note 3 currently claims there is no checkout and nobody is being charged. Replace with something true, e.g. "3 · Plus and Pro are live subscriptions, billed monthly through Stripe from inside the Studio; cancel any time. The four Pro extras marked Soon are on the way, not shipped; everything else listed above is built and running today."

Both replacements need re-verifying against _billing.mjs and _connect.mjs before they ship, because whoever wrote the current notes was describing the app as it was, not as it is.

finding.claimText: <meta name="twitter:card" content="summary_large_image" />
finding.evidence: The card will render large; it will not show the product. public/about.html:13-29 contains no twitter:image, no twitter:title, no twitter:description, no og:url and no og:type, so X falls back to og:image — the only image offered is public/about/vote.png at 640×1385 (confirmed with sips), an aspect ratio of 0.46:1 against summary_large_image's ~1.91:1. A centred crop keeps roughly 640×335, about y=525 to y=860 of the file. I opened the PNG: that band contains the "Voting open" strip, the "UP NEXT" header and the first Up-next row. The "Sam Cole" header, the whole "PLAYING NOW / Hey Jude" gradient card and the Lyrics button all fall outside it. Roughly three-quarters of the image height is discarded.
finding.proposedFix: Cut a 1200×630 card at /about/card.png — the headline over the phone shot, not a phone shot on its own — and add three tags beside the existing ones: <meta name="twitter:image" content="https://myset.vip/about/card.png" />, <meta property="og:url" content="https://myset.vip/about" />, <meta property="og:type" content="website" />. Leave og:image on vote.png for the platforms that letterbox rather than crop.

check.reasoning:
I could not refute this. I re-checked every load-bearing fact myself rather than trusting the accuser.

WHAT I CONFIRMED PERSONALLY
1. The head is exactly as described. public/about.html:12-29 contains only: og:title (21), og:description (22), og:image = https://myset.vip/about/vote.png (23), twitter:card = summary_large_image (24). No twitter:image, no og:url, no og:type.
2. Nothing rewrites it. netlify.toml has NO build command (publish = "public", functions only), so about.html ships byte-for-byte; /about is a plain 200 rewrite to /about.html (netlify.toml:47-49). I grepped every .html and .js in public/ for `meta[property=`, `querySelector('meta`, and og/twitter writes — zero hits. There is no other code path that supplies a card image.
3. The image really is that tall. `sips` on public/about/vote.png returns 640 x 1385, ratio 0.462:1.
4. I did the crop rather than imagining it. I made a centred 640x335 cut (1.91:1) and opened it. The accuser's band is right: it holds the bottom sliver of "Voting open", the "UP NEXT" header, row 1 "Wish You Were Here / Pink Floyd / Winning - plays next" and the top of row 2 "Landslide". The "Sam Cole / Live - The Lantern" header, the whole PLAYING NOW / Hey Jude gradient card and the Lyrics button are all outside it. 335/1385 = 24% of the height kept.
5. Not blocked from crawlers - there is no robots.txt, and the only X-Robots-Tag noindex in netlify.toml:125-128 is scoped to /stage.html.

WHERE THE ACCUSATION IS WEAKER THAN STATED (two corrections)
A. "It will not show the product" is too strong. The band that survives the crop is the ranked vote queue with a numbered #1 and the words "Winning - plays next". That is arguably the single clearest frame of the product in the whole file. What the crop actually costs is identity and context - the artist name and the PLAYING NOW card - not the product idea. Rewrite the finding as "the card loses the brand and the now-playing frame", not "shows nothing".
B. Half the cited evidence is inert. Missing twitter:title and twitter:description cause no defect at all - X falls back to og:title/og:description, which are both present. og:url and og:type are likewise inferred by every major crawler from the request URL. So two of the three tags in the proposed fix (og:url, og:type) fix nothing visible; only twitter:image (or a re-cut og:image) changes what renders. Listing four "missing" tags makes the defect look four times bigger than the one tag that matters.

WHERE IT IS WIDER THAN STATED (the part the accuser missed)
about.html is the ONLY page on the site with a working absolute og:image, and the only page with a twitter:card at all. Meanwhile:
- public/artist.html:23 sets og:image="/img/band.jpg" - a RELATIVE path. Open Graph requires an absolute URL; crawlers do not reliably resolve it, so artist pages - the URLs fans actually paste into a group chat - most likely share with no image. finding.claimText: Loaded BLOCKING, not deferred, on purpose: every page calls MySetPull() from an inline script…
finding.evidence: "Every page" has one exception. finding.proposedFix: Loaded BLOCKING, not deferred, on purpose: every page that loads this file calls MySetPull() from an inline script, and a deferred script runs AFTER all of those — so `defer` here makes MySetPull undefined at the moment it is called and the gesture silently never arms.

check.reasoning:
I checked every file myself. The accuser's raw fact is right — public/stage.html carries no `<script src="/pull.js">` and no MySetPull() call — but it does not falsify the sentence, for four independent reasons.

2. stage.html is not a page. It is 605 bytes (public/stage.html:1-9): a `<meta http-equiv="refresh" content="0; url=/studio.html">`, a `<link rel="canonical" href="/studio.html">`, one fallback anchor, and `location.replace('/studio.html')`. netlify.toml:126-128 stamps it `X-Robots-Tag = "noindex, nofollow"`. It has no app.css, no UI, no scroller, and replaces itself before first paint. Treating a redirect tombstone as a counterexample to "every page" is like counting a 301 rule as a page. A pull-to-refresh gesture on it would be meaningless.

3. The sentence is scoped more tightly than the accuser noticed. It reads "so `defer` **here** makes MySetPull undefined at the moment it is called". "Here" anchors the whole claim to this script tag, and the failure mode it describes can only exist on a page that loads pull.js and then calls the function. stage.html is outside the domain of discourse, not an exception inside it. The invariant the comment encodes is stated the same way in INVARIANTS.md:1259-1263 and enforced by the sibling comments at studio.html:535, venue-studio.html:348, artist.html:253, venue.html:243, community.html:208 ("pull.js must stay before MySetPull() (INVARIANT 0cf)").

Worth flagging what the accuser missed while chasing this: there IS a real off-by-one in the same subject matter, and it is not on the landing page. Three places claim pull.js is used by "all seven pages" — public/pull.js:12, MYSET.md:890, INVARIANTS.md:1246 — when eight files load it (community.html was evidently added after that line was written). finding.claimText: 4KB, same origin, and the service worker serves it from cache, so blocking costs nothing measurable.
finding.evidence: Both halves are wrong. (a) `ls -l public/pull.js` → 5,996 bytes, i.e. 5.9 KB — the comment understates it by about 50%. (b) public/sw.js:18-20 states rule 4 outright: "NOTHING is precached at install. Precaching is what makes a service worker ship a stale shell…", and the install handler at public/sw.js:29 is `self.addEventListener('install', () => self.skipWaiting())` — nothing else. The cache is `myset-runtime-v3` (public/sw.js:26) and it is populated only by stale-while-revalidate on a request that has already happened. So on a first visit — which is the visit a landing page exists for — pull.js is a blocking network round trip, not a cache hit. The comment tells a future reader not to bother measuring, when a cold-profile measurement is exactly what is missing.
finding.proposedFix: 6KB, same origin, and the service worker caches it after the first request — so this costs one round trip on a cold load and nothing on any load after it.

check.reasoning:
The finding does not hold up as stated. (a) is wrong in direction, and (b) is right about the mechanism but wrong about the consequence.

(a) BYTE COUNT — the accuser measured the wrong quantity. public/pull.js is 5,996 bytes on disk, but Netlify serves .js compressed. I measured it myself: `gzip -c public/pull.js | wc -c` -> 2,806 bytes (2.7 KB); brotli would be lower. A sentence about what BLOCKING costs is a sentence about transfer size, and the transfer size is UNDER the stated 4 KB, not ~50% over it. The proposed fix "6KB" is the disk figure, which never crosses the network — it makes the comment less accurate about the cost being described, not more. History supports the original number too: at 117661d (2026-09-03), the commit that wrote this comment, pull.js was 5,054 bytes raw / 2,402 gzipped; 931d18d later added 16 lines. "4KB" was a fair round number for the compressed payload then and still overstates it today.

(b) SERVICE WORKER — the mechanism is exactly as described, and I confirmed each line: sw.js:29 is `self.addEventListener('install', () => self.skipWaiting())` and nothing more; rule 4 at sw.js:18-20 states nothing is precached; CACHE = 'myset-runtime-v3' at sw.js:26 is populated only by the stale-while-revalidate branch at sw.js:112-121; about.html:822-823 registers the worker on `load`. So on a genuinely first visit there is no controlling worker and pull.js is fetched from the network. The clause "the service worker serves it from cache" is therefore loosely worded — it is true of every visit after the first, not of the first.

BUT the sentence's conclusion — "blocking costs nothing measurable" — survives the cold load anyway, and the accuser did not check this. The line immediately above the script is `<link rel="stylesheet" href="/app.css">` (about.html:29). app.css is 11,117 bytes raw / 3,462 bytes gzipped — LARGER on the wire than pull.js, and itself render-blocking. The browser's preload scanner discovers both in the same head parse and fetches them concurrently over the connection already open for the HTML document. pull.js is therefore not an additive serial round trip, which is what "a blocking network round trip" implies; the measurable difference between `blocking` and `defer` here is bounded by max(0, t_js - t_css), which is ~0 given the CSS is the bigger, equally blocking asset. (This part is standard browser fetch behaviour rather than a repo fact; the sizes and the head ordering are file-verified.)

WIDER THAN STATED, in one respect: the identical comment is triplicated at about.html:33, index.html:34 and vote.html:32, so any reword must land in all three or they drift.

FRAMING: this is an HTML comment in the document head — a note to a future developer, not copy any visitor reads. Auditing it as a landing-page claim is a category slip, and "cosmetic" still overstates its distance from the marketing surface.

What genuinely warrants a touch-up is one imprecise clause (cache-on-first-visit) and a number that would be better stated as a compressed size. That is a wording polish, not a FALSE claim.
check.correctedStatus: IMPRECISE — not FALSE. Severity: trivial (internal head comment, not visitor-facing copy). Half (a) is refuted outright: the served payload is 2.7 KB gzipped, under the stated 4 KB, so the comment overstates rather than understates the network cost, and the proposed "6KB" is the wrong metric. Half (b) is a correct mechanism read but the stated consequence does not follow: the cold-load blocking cost is parallel to a larger render-blocking stylesheet on the same connection, so "blocking costs nothing measurable" holds even on a first visit. Only the clause "the service worker serves it from cache" deserves an edit, for being silent about the first visit.
check.correctedEvidence: public/about.html:29-34 (stylesheet on the line above the blocking script; the comment itself); public/pull.js — 5,996 bytes on disk, 2,806 bytes gzipped (measured); public/app.css — 11,117 bytes on disk, 3,462 bytes gzipped (measured, larger on the wire and render-blocking); public/sw.js:18-20, :26, :29, :112-121 (no precache, runtime cache filled only by stale-while-revalidate); public/about.html:822-823 (worker registered on `load`); duplicated comment at public/index.html:34 and public/vote.html:32; git 117661d and 931d18d (pull.js was 5,054 bytes / 2,402 gzipped when the comment was authored)
check.betterFix:
Reword the last sentence in all three files (public/about.html:33, public/index.html:34, public/vote.html:32) to:

"~3KB gzipped, same origin, fetched in parallel with the stylesheet above it — and served from the service worker's cache on every visit after the first — so blocking costs nothing measurable."

This fixes the one real imprecision (it no longer implies a cold visit is a cache hit), states the number that actually crosses the network instead of the disk size, and keeps the load-bearing reason the claim is true — the blocking is concurrent with a larger render-blocking asset, not serial after it. Do not adopt "6KB": it is the on-disk size of a file Netlify never sends uncompressed, and in a sentence about the cost of blocking it is simply the wrong quantity.

finding.claimText: The link is repeated by the venues section and the footer, so it costs nothing here.
finding.evidence: The link is not repeated. public/about.html:280 is `href="#venues"` — an in-page jump to the section at public/about.html:505. The three later venue links all go somewhere else: public/about.html:575 "Claim your venue — free" → /venues, public/about.html:718 "I run a venue" → /venues, public/about.html:724 "Venue Studio" → /venues. netlify.toml rewrites /venues to /venue-studio.html with status 200, so those three navigate away to the Venue Studio app. `grep -n '#venues' public/about.html` returns one hit — line 280. What the comment is right about in substance is that nothing is lost: the section at :505 is still reachable by scrolling on a 320px screen, and a venue owner still has three routes to the Venue Studio. It is the stated reason that is wrong.
finding.proposedFix: On a 320px screen the nav link plus the pill run 13px past the edge. The venues section is still there to scroll to, and the footer has a link to the Venue Studio, so what this costs is a jump link, not the content.

check.reasoning:
The accuser's raw grep is correct, but the status FALSE does not survive.

What I verified myself:
- public/about.html:280 is the only `href="#venues"` in the file. `grep -c '#venues' public/about.html` = 1. There is no JS scroll handler (no scrollIntoView, no getElementById('venues')) that creates a second one.
- public/about.html:65 `.nav .navlink{display:none}` inside `@media(max-width:359px)`, and :280 is the only .navlink element, so below 360px the nav route does disappear.
- The three venue links exist as stated: :575 "Claim your venue — free", :718 "I run a venue", :724 "Venue Studio", all `href="/venues"`, and netlify.toml:51-54 rewrites /venues -> /venue-studio.html status 200. I also opened public/venue-studio.html: logged out it renders a gate with a claim flow (:399 "Create your page", :411 gate markup), so those links land a venue owner on the venue product, not a dead end.

Why the finding still fails:

1. The load-bearing clause is true and the accuser concedes it. The sentence is "The link is repeated ... so it costs nothing here." The operative claim is "it costs nothing here," and the accuser's own text says "What the comment is right about in substance is that nothing is lost." A comment whose conclusion is correct is not FALSE.

2. The comment names exactly the right two places. It says the link is repeated "by the venues section and the footer." The venues section (:505) does contain a venue link, at :575 inside it. The footer (:724) does contain a venue link. Both named locations check out. What differs is href and label, not existence — the nav link is a jump to the section, the other two are routes to the app. "The link" read as the venue route rather than the literal anchor string makes the sentence true. The accuser has read "link" as "this exact href" and the comment as a behavioural assertion, when it is a designer's note about what a 320px reader can still reach.

3. The accuser's own proposed fix restates the original's substance. Their replacement — "the footer has a link to the Venue Studio, so what this costs is a jump link, not the content" — says the same thing as the comment it replaces. That is a wording preference, not a correction.

4. Severity is over-stated even at "cosmetic." This is a CSS comment. It renders nothing, gates nothing, and no user or crawler ever sees it. Cosmetic implies a visible blemish; there is none.

The one genuine improvement available is precision: the comment blurs "the anchor" with "the route." That is worth a word, not a status of FALSE.

finding.claimText: @media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){ .anim .up{…} *{animation-duration:.01ms!important} }
finding.evidence: The reveal is properly killed (public/about.html:269). What survives is more than the claim guessed. (a) The rule clamps animation-duration but not transition-duration, so every CSS transition still runs at full length: public/about.html:59 `.pill{transition:transform .2s var(--spring)}`, :93 `.big{transition:transform .22s}`, :143 `.vb{transition:transform .22s…}`, :245 `details[open] summary::after{transform:rotate(45deg)}` on a .25s transition. finding.proposedFix: Add transition-duration to the clamp and give the counter its own check. CSS at :268-271 → @media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){ .anim .up{opacity:1;transform:none;transition:none} *{animation-duration:.01ms!important;transition-duration:.01ms!important} }. And at the top of count() at :794 → if (matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion:reduce)').matches) { el.textContent = to + suffix; return; } — with the comment: a number spinning for a second is animation, whatever the CSS says.

The page concedes the tap itself 116 lines later at public/about.html:407 ("One tap starts the top song and hands everybody fresh votes"), which is the honest version.

check.reasoning:
The accusation rests on a single sentence that is false in code: "the artist must, at minimum: start the show ... and end it."

The accuser wrote "There is no auto-advance in netlify/functions/admin.mjs" and stopped there. But admin.mjs:1667-1669 carries a comment pointing straight at the module they missed: "STARTING AND ENDING A NIGHT live in _lifecycle.mjs, because the calendar can now do both without a request behind it (_auto.mjs)." They audited one file and never opened the one that file names.

What _auto.mjs actually does: a gig on the artist's calendar starts its show at the gig's start time if the artist hasn't (_auto.mjs:144), and ends it three hours after the scheduled end if the artist hasn't (_auto.mjs:162). autocron.mjs:95 rings this every two minutes as a genuine Netlify scheduled function. It is default-ON — _auto.mjs:133 only bails on an explicit `show.autoStart === false`, and stage.mjs:52 confirms the default with `show.autoStart !== false`. The Studio's own copy says so at studio.html:1915 and 1920. So two of the three "mid-set actions the phrase denies" are not required of the artist at all in the default configuration.

The third alleged burden, the approval queue, is opt-in: show.mjs:139-142 returns `asks.song: null` unless `show.requests.on`, and the page already discloses this in the same breath ("they only exist if you switch them on"). Applying an optional feature's cost to a headline is a condition the page never implied.

Two smaller sloppiness signals: the "One tap" disclosure is at about.html:386, not :407, and it is 95 lines after the hero, not 116.

What genuinely survives is the per-song tap — playTop/play require an artist action, confirmed at admin.mjs:1790-1800. But the hero's own mechanism is literally true there: playTop ranks the pool by vote count and starts the winner, so "The room picks the next song" is exact. "You just play it" is the contrast to choosing, and the very next line spells that out — "You don't guess any more." The claim being made is decision-relief, not zero-interaction, and the page pays the tap off plainly 95 lines later in the beat literally titled "You stop guessing."

Per Perry's standing calibration (mechanism literal, framing is his), the mechanism under this hero is true and the compression is ordinary headline framing. Combined with the fact that the accuser's stated basis for the finding is refuted by code they did not read, this is not a minor overstatement — it is a finding that should not have been raised.

One honest caveat that does not rescue it: auto-start needs a gig on the calendar (_auto.mjs:105-107) and at least one active song (_auto.mjs:141), so an artist with an empty calendar does tap "Start the show." Start is therefore not universally automatic — but it is not universally manual either, and the accusation asserted the manual case as the only case.

finding.claimText: You don't guess any more.

Empty queue: public/vote.html:644 renders "No votes yet — Pick a song below and you'll set the queue" and :645 "Nothing on the list yet". Paused voting: public/vote.html:621 renders "Voting paused", set from the Studio's Voting box at public/studio.html:1873 ("Paused — nobody can vote until you re-open"). In both, the Studio's "Start top voted" button falls back to "nothing left" (public/studio.html:1924). The page answers this honestly in the FAQ 400 lines below — public/about.html:689-693, "Then you play what you were going to play anyway and nothing is worse than before" — which is the sentence the hero should not be contradicting.
finding.proposedFix: You're not guessing on your own any more.

check.correctedEvidence: public/studio.html:1867-1868 and :1924; netlify/functions/admin.mjs:1795-1802 and :1811; netlify/functions/stage.mjs:61-63; public/studio.html:1879-1881; public/about.html:292-293
check.reasoning:
I read every line cited and the gates behind them. The accusation fails on the facts, not on taste.

1) "In both states the Studio's 'Start top voted' button falls back to 'nothing left'" — FALSE, in both states.
public/studio.html:1867 builds the pool as `songs.filter(x=>!x.now&&canVote(x)&&(!x.played||x.votes>0))` and :1868 takes `top=startPool[0]`. There is no vote condition on unplayed songs. With zero votes and a normal setlist, `top` is a real song and the button at :1924 reads "Start top voted — <Title> (0)". The server mirrors this exactly: netlify/functions/admin.mjs:1795-1801 filters votable, not-now-playing, and (not played OR holding replay votes), and only then :1802 `if (!pool.length) { err = ['nothing left in the pool', 409] }`. "Nothing left" is the EXHAUSTED-SETLIST state, not the no-votes state and not the paused state. The accuser read the fallback string and inferred a trigger it does not have.

2) "Paused voting leaves the artist guessing exactly as before" — FALSE. netlify/functions/admin.mjs:1811 is the entire pause implementation: `case 'window': show.windowOpen = !!body.open; break;`. It flips one flag. It does not touch votes. Every vote already cast is still standing, still ranked, still on the artist's screen — the Studio's "Votes now" tile (public/studio.html:1879) and the ranked Queue rows with their counts (public/studio.html:1927-1932) render identically whether the window is open or shut. Pausing is the artist holding a finished result, which is the opposite of guessing. And it is artist-initiated: the artist tapped "Paused" themselves (public/studio.html:1875-1876). A feature the user deliberately switched off does not falsify a claim about the feature.

3) The empty-queue state is not "guessing exactly as before" either. netlify/functions/stage.mjs:61-63 sends `voters` AND `room: room.phones`, commented "phones in the room tonight, not just phones that voted". public/studio.html:1880 renders that as "Voting · in room" before a single vote exists. In the very state the accuser says is information-free, the artist can see how many people are actually in the room with the page open. That is real data the pre-MySet artist never had.

4) The page's sentence is more careful than the accuser noticed. public/about.html:292-293 is one sentence in three clauses: "Your fans vote from their own phones on what you play next. They don't install anything. You don't guess any more." The claim is explicitly conditioned on the antecedent — fans voting. It never says "you don't guess even when nobody votes." The supporting section at public/about.html:384-386 keeps the same discipline: "One screen tells you what's winning, how many people are in the room, and what they've asked for" — a literal description of the Live tab, all three of which are true.

5) The FAQ is not a confession. public/about.html:675-679 answers "What if nobody votes?" That is a zero-usage question, not a broken-state question. Every product has an empty state before first use; a hero line is not contradicted by the first thirty seconds of a session. Reading the FAQ as the page admitting the hero is false only works if you first accept limbs 1-3, and those don't hold.

What survives: nothing load-bearing. "Any more" is an absolute, and a brand-new show at t=0 has no votes on the board. But that is the ordinary empty state of every product, it resolves the moment one person taps, and the artist still has the room count while it lasts. Downgrade to no-finding.

One caution for the parent: this is exactly the class of edit Perry vetoed on 2026-09-06 — rewriting his framing when the mechanism underneath it is true. The proposed replacement is also weaker prose: "You're not guessing on your own any more" invites "then who's guessing with me?" and trades a clean promise for a hedge that answers a question nobody asked.
check.betterFix: No change. Ship the line as written. If Perry independently wants the absolute softened for his own taste (not for accuracy), the minimal edit that keeps the promise intact is "You stop guessing." — but that already appears at public/about.html:384, so repeating it in the hero costs the section its payoff. Leave public/about.html:293 alone.

finding.claimText: See how it feels
finding.evidence: The demo is genuinely interactive — public/about.html:330 `<section id="try">`, real buttons and a real re-sort at :735-770 — but the interaction it teaches is not the app's, in three ways. (a) Vote finality. public/about.html:768 `if (mine.has(id)) { mine.delete(id); row.n--; left++; }` — a second tap takes the vote back. The shipped default is the opposite: FLAGS.voteFinal.default is true in netlify/functions/_flags.mjs ("ON as of 2026-09-02, at Perry's decision"), so public/vote.html:632 renders "Your vote — tap to add more", never "tap to change", and public/vote.html:412-423 openVote refuses the un-vote path when finality is on. (b) One tap versus a sheet. The demo votes on the tap; the real page opens a confirmation sheet with a quantity stepper (public/vote.html:412-423 → drawVoteSheet). (c) Free votes. The demo starts on 3 (public/about.html:339 "3 votes left"); the shipped default is `freeCredits: 5` (netlify/functions/_lib.mjs:176). So the visitor learns that votes are changeable, instant and three — and all three are wrong.
finding.proposedFix: Fix (a) in the demo rather than the copy — make a second tap add a vote, the way the room does. Then the lede at :333 can stay as it is. If the demo has to keep the toggle, the lede must say so: "This is the real thing, running on this page. Vote and watch the queue move. In the room a vote sticks once you confirm it — here you can take it back and try again."

The accuser's file:line citations are all real — I checked each one and none is a comment misread as behaviour. But the finding as framed does not hold.

(1) Zero allowance — does not hold. The sentence says 'a few free votes', deliberately unnumbered. The default is 5 (_lib.mjs:181). Setting it to 0 requires the artist reading this very page to be on Plus/Pro (admin.mjs:1706-1707, _plan.mjs:66) and to deliberately do it in their own back office. The page is not hiding this from them: about.html:625 sells it as a Plus feature in plain words — 'Set your own vote rules — how many free votes each person gets'. A page cannot be accused of omitting a condition it names 271 lines further down and charges $10/month for.

(2) Replay cost — does not hold. The sentence makes no claim about what a vote costs; it is about the allowance and its refresh. And again the page states it outright at :625: 'and what it costs the room to replay a song you've already played'. costOf (_lib.mjs:712, default 5 at :181) is disclosed, not concealed.

(3) Voting can be closed — this one is backwards. The sentence's subject is the moment a song starts. Both admin.mjs:1782 ('play') and :1808 ('playTop') set `show.windowOpen = true` on the SAME mutation that sets resetVotes, and :2001 then runs clearAllFanVotes. So the exact event the sentence describes clears the vote.mjs:80 condition the accuser raises. The only route back to a closed window mid-gap is the artist deliberately flipping it afterwards (admin.mjs:1811). vote.mjs:46 ('The show has ended') is not a gap at all — there is no next song to contest. The page's claim is more precisely engineered than the accuser noticed.

(4) Finality — real in code (_flags.mjs:28-29 default true; vote.mjs:107) but it is not a claim line 354 makes. Line 354 says nothing about taking votes back. What DOES contradict finality on this page is the demo's own click handler at :768 — `if (mine.has(id)) { mine.delete(id); row.n--; left++; }` — which un-votes and refunds. That is the real finding, and it is a behaviour discrepancy in a widget, not an omission in a sentence.

The proposed fix is worse than the status quo on two counts I verified on the page itself. First, 'gets five free votes' contradicts the widget it sits directly under: about.html:740 seeds `left = 3` and :337/:755 render '3 votes left'. A reader would see 'five free votes' printed beneath a counter reading three. Second, hard-coding five makes the accuser's own point (1) worse — 'a few' stays true when a Plus artist sets 3 or 7; 'five' becomes false. Third, 'Once you confirm one it stays with the song' would sit inches above a demo that demonstrably hands the vote back, so the page would contradict itself inside one visual block.

Default to refuted stands: I could not confirm the stated problem at the stated location.

I could not refute the factual core, and I tried three ways.

The number really is stale. _lib.mjs:176 and :390 both say 5. A free artist cannot move it: admin.mjs:1706 puts 'freeCredits' behind canPrice, _plan.mjs:69 sets pricing:false on free, and studio.html:2241 wraps the chips in lock('pricing'). The history claim holds exactly as stated — d03c033 had freeCredits: 3, and 0b357b5 flipped it to 5 on 2026-09-02, three days after about.html was written against it.

I also could not dismiss it as set dressing. The page demonstrably does mirror real defaults in its numbers: the alt text at :404 says "three votes each" for requests and birthdays, and _lib.mjs:182-183 sets both costs to 3. So the 3 in the widget was tracking the product, not decorating it.

But "major" is too strong, for three reasons the accuser did not weigh.

First, no prose on the page is falsified. The only sentences about the allowance — :354 and the live version at :761 — say "Everyone in the room gets a few free votes." That is true of five. The page never tells the reader a number in words. The lede at :333 says "This is the real thing, running on this page", and the sentence after it defines what "the real thing" is pointing at: "Vote and watch the queue move." It is a claim about the interaction, and that claim is honest — the queue really does reorder. The invented songs and the invented starting counts of 5/4/2/1 sit under the same sentence and nobody would call those discrepancies.

Second, 3 is a legal room. studio.html:2241 offers 1, 2, 3, 5, 10 as chips and a free-text field up to 999, so a Plus or Pro artist can genuinely run a room on three votes. The page is showing a configuration the product supports, not one it forbids.

Third, the accuser's own premise is a little too tidy. "Five is what every free room gets" is not quite right: admin.mjs:1839 handles 'unlimited' outside the canPrice list, and studio.html:2249-2251 exposes that switch to everyone with the note "Free on every plan — it is your show, not a price." So a free artist can hand the room unlimited votes. There is no single universal number to be wrong about.

Net: a real drift worth fixing, of the same weight as a screenshot showing an old default — worth correcting, not worth calling the page misleading. And the fix needs the fifth song or it costs more than it repairs.

The proposed fix, however, is wrong: '(x.at || Infinity)' sends every unstamped seeded row to the BACK of a tie, while a just-tapped song gets a finite Date.now() and sorts to the FRONT — so tapping Landslide still dethrones Wish You Were Here, and Fast Car still jumps Tennessee Whiskey.
