Line 758 in full reads: "Out of votes — in the room you could buy a few more, or wait: the next song refreshes everyone." The accusation quotes only up to the comma. The proposed fix's payoff clause — "or wait: the next song refreshes everyone" — is the second half of the existing line, verbatim, bold tag and all. The fix therefore "adds" nothing the page does not already say; its only real change is swapping the buy clause for artist-side onboarding jargon. SECOND — WRONG SPEAKER. Line 758 is not a marketing claim in the page's own voice. It is the `dfoot` string of the interactive fan demo (about.html:734-762: SEED = "Wish You Were Here", "Landslide"…, `left = 3`, tap-to-vote, spring reorder). It is written in the phone's voice to someone play-acting as a fan in a room — "in the room YOU could buy a few more" — describing what the audience-side product does, not what the reader's own unconfigured account will do on night one. And it is hedged: "could", not "can". THIRD — THE PAGE ALREADY DISCLOSES THIS, TWICE, MORE BLUNTLY THAN THE FIX WOULD. about.html:415-418 volunteers "One caveat, up front: card payments are the part still being built"; :654-657 is a dedicated honest note, "2 · Card payments aren't on yet." A reader cannot come away from this page believing card payments are switched on by default. This is the accuser applying a condition the page never implied while missing the page's own, louder disclosure of the same condition. FOURTH — THE PROPOSED FIX WOULD MAKE THE PAGE SELF-CONTRADICTORY AND BREAK THE DEMO. It injects "Connect a payout account and they can buy a few more, too" into a fan's-eye demo footer: "you" the fan becomes "they" the artist mid-sentence, and back-office setup language lands in the one place on the page that is supposed to feel like standing in the room holding a phone. Worse, it asserts Connect onboarding as an available path — which flatly contradicts about.html:654-657 still sitting a hundred lines below saying no other artist can take money at all. The fix creates a contradiction rather than resolving one. AND THE REAL PROBLEM IS WORSE, WIDER, AND POINTS THE OTHER WAY. The accuser's own premise — that Connect onboarding is the gate — is correct and is exactly what the page fails to say. Stripe Connect Express is BUILT AND LIVE: any signed-in artist can hit admin.mjs:1105 'payStart', which creates an Express account (_connect.mjs:141) and returns a Stripe-hosted onboarding link (_connect.mjs:162); studio.html:1551-1576 renders the "Set up card payments / Start with Stripe" card to every non-founder; webhook.mjs:51 syncs charges_enabled back; pay.mjs:173 creates the charge on the artist's own account with application_fee_amount from PLANS[*].cut at :64 and :209. INVARIANTS.md:218 states it outright: "0r0. DIRECT CHARGES … 0r below is now implemented (_connect.mjs)." So about.html:654-657 is stale and now FALSE — "Until that's finished no other artist can take money through MySet" is not true, and "the 10% above currently applies to nobody" is contradicted by pay.mjs:64 charging it. Same for :415-418. The page is not overselling payments; it is talking a prospective artist out of a shipped feature and misstating its own fee. That is the major finding, and it sits on different lines. ONE TRAP WORTH NAMING, because I nearly fell into it and it may be what produced this finding: netlify/functions/_pay.mjs:5-9 carries a long header comment insisting Connect is not built and inviting you to "grep the tree for application_fee_amount … and you will find nothing." That comment is stale. Grep the tree and you find it twice in pay.mjs. Reading that comment as behaviour is exactly the failure mode this audit is supposed to catch.
check.betterFix: Leave public/about.html:758 as written — it is a hedged, fan-voice line in a demo, and the page discloses the payments caveat elsewhere. Fix the two stale disclosures instead. 1) public/about.html:654-657, replace honest note 2 with: "2 · Card payments need a five-minute setup. Before your room can tip you or buy votes, you connect a payout account through Stripe from your Studio — Stripe handles the ID checks and MySet never sees your bank details. Until that's done, everything that doesn't involve a card works from the moment you sign up. MySet's cut (10% on free) comes off card payments only." 2) public/about.html:415-418, replace the caveat paragraph with: "One thing to set up: before the money buttons appear in your room, you connect a payout account through Stripe in your Studio. It takes about five minutes and MySet never sees your bank details." 3) Separately, and this is a truth issue rather than a copy one: about.html:640-645 and the plans block should be checked against _plan.mjs NOT_BUILT, and _pay.mjs:5-9's stale header comment should be corrected so the next reader is not misled the way this finding's author was. Both are outside this line's scope but should be filed. Note for whoever writes this: the honest-notes block is Perry's own framing and its plainness is the point. Keep the three-note shape and the "here's where the edges are" tone; only the facts inside note 2 are wrong.

finding.claimText: ${sorted[0].t} is winning, so that's what plays next
finding.evidence: The top of the board is a recommendation the artist can ignore. netlify/functions/admin.mjs:1770-1783 the 'play' action takes an arbitrary body.song and starts it, with no check that it is the winner; only :1790-1808 'playTop' starts the ranked leader. The Studio offers both side by side: public/studio.html:1923-1924 the big 'Start top voted' button, and :1926-1931 a queue where every one of the top twelve rows carries its own '▶ Start'. Nothing forces the winner to be honoured. The fan page makes the same strong claim to the room (vote.html:632 'Winning — plays next'), so the page is not out of step with the product — but neither is enforced, and the hero at about.html:291 ('The room picks the next song. You just play it') rests on it.
finding.proposedFix: Line 760: '${sorted[0].t} is winning — that's the one at the top of your screen when you finish this one.'

check.reasoning: The accusation misquotes the line and misreads who the line is talking to. Three things I checked myself: 1. THE QUOTE IS TRUNCATED. about.html:760 does not end at "plays next". The full string is: `${esc(sorted[0].t)} is winning, so that's what plays next — whenever the next request is taken.` The accuser dropped the trailing clause. That clause is doing real work: "whenever the next request is TAKEN" names a human act by someone else, at an unspecified moment. It is not an automation promise. The sentence is more carefully worded than the accuser noticed, and the accuser's proposed fix mostly re-adds a hedge the sentence already carries. 2. THE LINE IS THE FAN'S VIEW, AND IT REPRODUCES THE SHIPPED APP VERBATIM. about.html:330-334 frames this block as "Try it — right here / Tap a song … This is the real thing, running on this page … That's exactly what forty people do at once." The reader is seated as a fan casting votes, and the string only renders once the visitor has voted (about.html:757-762, the `mine.size` branch). Its live counterpart is vote.html:631, `Winning — plays next` — the same claim, in the same seat. So the landing page is an accurate reproduction of the product's own fan-facing UI, which is precisely the test this audit applies. The accuser concedes this ("the page is not out of step with the product") and then reports it as a page defect anyway. If the claim is too strong it is too strong in the app, and the edit belongs in vote.html, not about.html — editing about.html alone would make the demo stop matching the product. 3. THE PAGE'S ARTIST-FACING CLAIMS ARE ALREADY ACCURATE AND ALREADY PERMISSIVE. about.html:385-386 says "One screen tells you what's winning … One tap starts the top song and hands everybody fresh votes." That is exactly admin.mjs:1785 `playTop` plus its `resetVotes = true` — an offer of one tap, never a statement that other taps do not exist. The hero at :291 is "The room picks the next song. You just play it," and its own sub at :292-293 is "Your fans vote … You don't guess any more" — not "you don't choose any more." The claim that the hero "rests on" line 760 is the accuser's inference, not a code fact. The code facts the accuser cites are true and I confirmed each: admin.mjs:1771-1773 `case 'play'` takes `body.song` with only an empty check (`if (!id) { err = ['no song', 400]; return false; }`) and no winner check; :1785 `playTop` is the ranked path; studio.html:1923 is the big `act('playTop')` button and :1926-1931 is a queue literally headed "Queue — tap ▶ to start" with a per-row `act('play',{song:…})`. Overriding is a designed, first-class affordance. None of that contradicts anything the page says. One genuinely wider thing I noticed while in there, unrelated to marketing and NOT an upgrade of this finding: `case 'play'` at admin.mjs:1771-1773 never checks that `body.song` exists in `show.songs`. `logPlay` falls back to `sg.title || id` and `show.nowPlaying` is set to whatever string arrived. An authenticated artist can put an arbitrary id into nowPlaying and into the play log. Low impact (same-artist scope only), but worth a separate look.
check.correctedStatus: ACCURATE (no change needed on about.html). The finding as filed rests on a truncated quote and on judging a fan-seat demo by an artist-seat standard. At most this is a note against the app's own copy at vote.html:631, severity trivial — not a landing-page discrepancy.
check.correctedEvidence: public/about.html:760 (full string, incl. the dropped "— whenever the next request is taken"); public/about.html:330-334 and :757-762 (the demo is the fan's seat, and the line renders only after the visitor votes); public/vote.html:631 (the shipped app says the same thing, so the page matches the product); public/about.html:385-386 vs netlify/functions/admin.mjs:1785 (the artist-facing claim is playTop, and is stated as an offer); netlify/functions/admin.mjs:1771-1773 and public/studio.html:1923, 1926, 1931 (the override paths — real, but contradicted by nothing on the page)
check.betterFix:
Change nothing on about.html. Line 760 already hedges the timing and already mirrors the app word for word; the accuser's replacement ("that's the one at the top of your screen when you finish this one") is actively worse in three ways — it says "your screen" and "when you finish" to a reader the page has deliberately seated as a FAN, not the artist; it duplicates a hedge the sentence already has; and it trades the demo's one payoff line for a sentence about screen furniture.

If Perry does want the "plays next" promise softened, the edit belongs at public/vote.html:631 — that is the string a real paying room actually reads — changing `Winning — plays next` to `Winning — up next`, which is what the panel above it (vote.html:626, "Up next") already calls itself. Then, and only then, mirror it into about.html:760 so the demo keeps matching the product. Doing about.html alone would break the one property that makes this page honest.

finding.claimText: None of them need you.
finding.evidence: Nothing in MySet advances a song by itself. Starting a song is only ever an artist tap: public/studio.html:1923 renders the button as onclick="act('playTop')", and each queue row has its own ▶ Start at studio.html:1931. The server side is admin.mjs:1771 (case 'play') and admin.mjs:1783 (case 'playTop') — both reached only from POST /api/admin. The only automation in the whole app is show START and show END from the calendar: netlify/functions/_auto.mjs imports exactly `startShow, endShow` (_auto.mjs:5) and calls them at _auto.mjs:144 and _auto.mjs:130/162. Grep for playTop or nowPlaying in _auto.mjs and autocron.mjs returns nothing — there is no auto-advance mode, and no flag for one (_flags.mjs declares only voteFinal and featuredShows). Beat 3 needs the artist too: ASK_ACTIONS = ['askList','askAccept','askDone','askDecline'] (admin.mjs:951), each fired by a button in the Studio's request rows (studio.html:2624-2626). So of the five beats, two require the artist repeatedly, all night.
finding.proposedFix: Replace the H2 at line 365 with: "Five things happen. Your part is one tap between songs."

check.correctedStatus: FALSE, severity MODERATE (downgraded from major) — the overclaim is real, but it is one beat not two, the page corrects itself two lines later, and the proposed fix is incomplete because it leaves line 366 standing.
check.correctedEvidence: public/about.html:365 (H2) and :366 (the lede "Everything below runs itself while you're on stage"); public/about.html beat 2 body "One tap starts the top song and hands everybody fresh votes"; public/about.html demo footer (~line 354) "Starting a song gives everybody theirs back"; public/studio.html:1923 (act('playTop')) and :1931 (act('play',{song})); netlify/functions/admin.mjs case 'play' with show.nowPlaying/resetVotes at :1782 and case 'playTop' resetVotes at :1808; netlify/functions/_auto.mjs:5 (imports only startShow, endShow) and :133 (autoStart); netlify/functions/admin.mjs:951 ASK_ACTIONS; netlify/functions/_lib.mjs:182 requests:{on:false,cost:3}; public/studio.html:2276 "Both are off until you switch them on"; netlify/functions/_flags.mjs FLAGS (voteFinal, featuredShows only); netlify/functions/_plan.mjs:130 NOT_BUILT
check.reasoning:
I tried to refute this and could not. The code facts check out under my own reading: play and playTop are reachable only as artist taps (studio.html:1923, 1931 -> admin.mjs 'play'/'playTop', resetVotes at :1782/:1808), _auto.mjs imports exactly startShow and endShow (:5) and only ever starts or ends a show, there is no auto-advance flag (_flags.mjs declares only voteFinal and featuredShows), and no autoAccept/autoPlay/autoAdvance exists anywhere in functions or public (I grepped). Critically, the page contradicts its own H2 in the same section: beat 2's body says "One tap starts the top song and hands everybody fresh votes." So "None of them need you" is not defensible as written.

But the accusation is over-graded and wrong in three places.

1. It is ONE beat by default, not two. The accuser says "two of the five beats require the artist repeatedly, all night." Requests ship OFF: _lib.mjs:182 sets requests:{on:false,cost:3}, and studio.html:2276 tells the artist "Both are off until you switch them on" — which is exactly what about.html beat 3 already discloses ("they only exist if you switch them on"). Beat 3 asks nothing of an artist who never opted in. So by default exactly one of the five beats needs the artist.

2. Severity is moderate, not major. The page names the tap three times inside the same stretch of copy: the demo footer ("Starting a song gives everybody theirs back"), the section lede at 366 ("You start the show and play"), and beat 2 itself. Nobody finishes this section believing songs advance themselves. That makes it a headline overclaim the page immediately walks back — a copy-consistency defect — not a false capability claim that leaves a reader misinformed about what they are buying.

3. The proposed fix is broken and would make the page worse. It replaces only the H2 at 365 and leaves line 366 untouched: "Everything below runs itself while you're on stage." That is the SAME claim in more mechanical words ("runs itself"), and it is the stronger of the two. Swapping 365 to "Your part is one tap between songs" while 366 still says everything runs itself puts a flat contradiction one line under the new headline. 365 and 366 have to move together — the accuser did not notice the lede at all.

One smaller correction: "The only automation in the whole app is show START and show END" is too sweeping. autocron.mjs also heals the index, purges, and sweeps clips (:58-81); decline refunds votes automatically (admin.mjs:877-885); a play resets the room's votes automatically (:1782). None of these advance a song, so the load-bearing part of the accusation stands — but the wording as filed is not accurate.
check.betterFix:
Fix 365 AND 366 together, keeping Perry's contrast (no maths in the gap, no jar, no chasing) rather than flattening it: line 365:

Five things happen. Your part is one tap.

line 366:

You start the show and play. Between songs you tap the top-voted song — the rest runs itself while you're on stage.

This is literally true against the code: one tap per gap (admin.mjs 'play'/'playTop', which is also what refreshes the room's votes at :1782/:1808), beats 1, 4 and 5 need nothing, and beat 3 only exists if the artist switched requests on (_lib.mjs:182). It also stops the H2 fighting beat 2's own "One tap starts the top song," and it keeps the tap framed as the artist's moment of control instead of as a chore. If Perry wants the punchier headline, "Five things happen. Four of them without you." is also true by default and keeps the rhythm — but the lede at 366 still has to lose "Everything below runs itself."

finding.claimText: Everything below runs itself while you're on stage.
finding.evidence: Three of the five beats fail the test. (a) Beat 2 is artist-triggered — see the evidence on night-1-2-03; the song does not change until a tap reaches admin.mjs:1783. (b) Beat 3's mechanic is OFF by default: netlify/functions/_lib.mjs:181-182 sets `requests: { on: false, cost: 3 }` and `birthdays: { on: false, cost: 3 }` in defaultShow(), and the Studio's own Settings copy says so — "Both are off until you switch them on" (studio.html:2276). (c) Beat 4's card payments are gated to the founder: _pay.mjs:53-55 canTakeMoney returns true only for isPlatformOwner or an artist whose show.pay.ready mirror is set, and _pay.mjs:34-38 connectReady returns false for everyone but the founder because Connect is not built. The page admits (c) itself at L415-418 and (b) at L399, which makes the blanket sentence at L366 contradict its own beats two lines later.
finding.proposedFix: Replace the lede at line 366 with: "You start the show, play, and tap the winner in each gap. The rest below happens without you."

check.betterFix:
Fix the heading and the lede together — the heading is the more false of the two and the accuser left it standing. Replace about.html:365-366:

  h2:   "Five things happen. One tap is your whole job."
  lede: "You start the show and play. Between songs, one tap starts the winner — everything else below happens on its own."

Do NOT bolt beat 3's toggle or beat 4's Connect caveat into this lede. Both are already disclosed in their own beats (L399 "they only exist if you switch them on"; L415-418 "card payments are the part still being built"), and the accuser's fix leaves the contradicting h2 at L365 in place while making the sell-line heavier than it needs to be.

Separately, and NOT part of this finding: beat 3's "Say no and their votes come straight back, automatically" (about.html:400-401) is not unconditionally true. admin.mjs:880-884 refunds nothing when the declined request came from an earlier show, on purpose ("those credits have already refreshed, so refunding would mint votes"). That is a real, undisclosed carve-out and a better finding than two of the three legs the accuser raised.
check.correctedEvidence: public/about.html:365-366 (the h2 + lede), 386-387 (beat 2's own "One tap starts the top song"), 399 ("they only exist if you switch them on"), 415-418 (the payments caveat); netlify/functions/admin.mjs:1771-1799 (only 'play'/'playTop' move the song; grep for autoplay/autoAdvance/autopilot across netlify/functions/*.mjs and public/studio.html returns nothing); netlify/functions/_lib.mjs:181-182 (requests/birthdays default off); netlify/functions/_pay.mjs:34-38, 53-55 (Connect gate); public/studio.html:1923-1924 (the button is labelled "Start top voted", not "Play"); netlify/functions/admin.mjs:880-884 (the decline refund is NOT unconditional).
check.correctedStatus: MISLEADING, severity minor (not FALSE/major)
check.reasoning:
One of the three legs holds; the other two do not test the sentence they are aimed at.

LEG (a) HOLDS, and I confirmed it independently rather than taking the cite. admin.mjs:1771-1799 is the only place show.nowPlaying moves, under actions 'play' and 'playTop', both artist-initiated. I grepped netlify/functions/*.mjs and public/studio.html for autoplay/auto_play/autoAdvance/auto-advance/autopilot and got zero hits — there is no second code path that advances a song on its own. I also checked the charitable reading, that "you start the show and play" might be naming the tap: it is not. The Studio's own label for the tap is "Start top voted" / "▶ Start" (studio.html:1923-1924), while "Start the show" (studio.html:1895) is a separate button that only flips status pre→live. So the lede names one artist action and the product needs two. Beat 2 admits the second one plainly two paragraphs later — "One tap starts the top song" (about.html:386) — which is what makes this an internal contradiction rather than a lie to the reader.

LEG (b) DOES NOT HOLD. The default is real (_lib.mjs:181-182, confirmed, and show.mjs:140-141 gates the fan card on it), but flipping a toggle in Settings is a pre-show setup act, not on-stage work, so it does not falsify "runs itself while you're on stage". More to the point, the same beat says it out loud at about.html:399 — "they only exist if you switch them on". A reader cannot be misled by a fact the paragraph volunteers. The accuser's second cite, studio.html:2276, is Studio marketing copy, not a gate — using it as evidence of app behaviour is reading copy as code.

LEG (c) DOES NOT HOLD against this sentence. The _pay.mjs gates are exactly as described (34-38, 53-55), but they are an availability problem, not a "does it run itself" problem — when payments are on, the fan buys or tips with zero artist involvement, which is what the beat claims. And about.html:415-418 discloses the gate in the same beat, in the same voice, unprompted. Citing a page's own inline caveat as proof the page is dishonest inverts the test.

So the accusation is right about the mechanism and wrong about the scale: it triples the count by folding in two disclosed facts, and the residue is a lede that overstates for two paragraphs before its own body copy corrects it. That is a copy-tightness defect, minor.

Where the accuser under-read: L365, the h2 "Five things happen. None of them need you", is the flatter falsehood — it admits no exception at all, where the lede at least carves out "you start the show and play". The fix must touch both lines or the contradiction survives. And the accuser missed a genuinely undisclosed carve-out one beat over (see betterFix).

finding.claimText: You start the show and play.
finding.evidence: Starting IS one discrete action: studio.html:1894 renders a single "Start the show" button posting act('status',{status:'live'}), which admin.mjs:1670-1677 routes to startShow() in _lifecycle.mjs:112. But that is not the artist's whole workload. Every song after the first needs a tap (studio.html:1923 / admin.mjs:1783) — there is no auto-advance. If requests are switched on, each one needs +Add, Did it, or ✕ (studio.html:2624-2626, admin.mjs:951). Ending the show is a tap behind a confirm() (studio.html:1917). The Voting Open/Paused control is a live surface the artist can also touch (studio.html:1872-1875). No re-authentication is needed mid-show (the Studio token lives in localStorage, studio.html:544) and the Live tab keeps polling on its own every 4s while visible (studio.html:4246), so those two falsifiers do not fire — the tap-per-song does.
finding.proposedFix: Covered by the line-366 rewrite proposed for night-1-2-05: "You start the show, play, and tap the winner in each gap. The rest below happens without you."

check.reasoning:
The accuser's core mechanism is real — I confirmed there is no auto-advance anywhere (admin.mjs 'play'/'playTop' are the only paths that move a song, both artist-initiated; grep for autoAdvance/autoplay/advance across netlify/functions/*.mjs and studio.html returns nothing relevant). But OVERSTATED/major does not survive, for four reasons.

1. THE PAGE ALREADY SAYS IT — inside the very block line 366 introduces. Line 366 is a lede for the five beats that follow. Beat 2, twenty lines below at about.html:386, reads "One tap starts the top song and hands everybody fresh votes." The demo footer above it (about.html:355) says "Starting a song gives everybody theirs back — so every gap is a fresh contest." The Transformation section repeats it at about.html:455: "the queue is ranked live, and one tap starts the winner." A reader is told about the tap-per-song three times, once unavoidably within the section. Nothing is concealed, so the reader-harm that would make this major is absent.

2. TWO OF THE THREE SUPPORTING CLAIMS ARE WRONG IN THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION. The accuser says "Starting IS one discrete action" and "Ending the show is a tap behind a confirm()". Both are incomplete. _auto.mjs is titled "SHOWS THAT START AND END THEMSELVES": _auto.mjs:144 calls startShow(aid,{fresh:true,by:'schedule',occKey,eventId}) when a calendar gig reaches its start time, and _auto.mjs:130 and :162 call endShow(aid,{by:'schedule'}) three hours after the gig's scheduled end (END_GRACE_MS, _auto.mjs:31); autocron.mjs rings every two minutes. _lifecycle.mjs:149/186 stamp startedBy/endedBy, and studio.html surfaces it verbatim — "Started by itself for the gig on your calendar. It ends by itself three hours after that gig's end time, unless you end it first," and "Nothing says 'live' to fans until you tap this — or until a gig on your calendar reaches its start time." So on starting and ending, the page's "You start the show" UNDERSTATES the automation rather than overstating it. The accuser read those two as artist workload without checking for a scheduler.

3. THE VOTING OPEN/PAUSED CITATION IS NOT WORKLOAD. studio.html:1872-1875 is an optional control, and starting any song already sets show.windowOpen = true in admin.mjs's 'play' case. The artist never has to touch it for the night to run. Listing it as evidence inflates the workload count.

4. THE REQUESTS CITATION APPLIES A CONDITION THE PAGE ITSELF DISCLOSES. about.html:399 says requests "only exist if you switch them on." The accuser conditions his own claim on "if requests are switched on" — which is exactly the page's own carve-out, not a gap in it.

WHAT DOES SURVIVE, smaller and aimed elsewhere: there is a genuine internal inconsistency, but it lives one line UP, at the H2 (about.html:365) "Five things happen. None of them need you." Beat 2 is one of those five and it does need a tap — and beat 3 needs one too when requests are on. The H2 is the stronger overclaim; line 366's "Everything below runs itself" inherits the strain from it. That is a minor copy-consistency issue inside a single section, not a major truth defect.

THE PROPOSED FIX IS ACTIVELY HARMFUL AS WRITTEN. Putting "tap the winner in each gap" into line 366 makes the H2 directly above it read as a lie to the same eye, in the same glance, and duplicates about.html:386 word for word in substance. It fixes the weaker line and leaves the stronger falsehood standing two lines above.
check.correctedStatus: ACCURATE as written — downgrade from OVERSTATED/major to a minor copy-consistency note, and re-aim it from about.html:366 to the H2 at about.html:365
check.correctedEvidence: public/about.html:355, :365, :366, :386, :399, :455 (the page's three separate disclosures of the per-gap tap, plus the requests carve-out); netlify/functions/_auto.mjs:31, :130, :144, :162 (scheduled start and scheduled end — startShow/endShow with by:'schedule'); netlify/functions/_lifecycle.mjs:149, :186 (startedBy/endedBy stamped); netlify/functions/autocron.mjs:1-40 (two-minute bell); netlify/functions/admin.mjs ~1670-1677 (status live/ended routed to _lifecycle) and ~940-960 ('play' sets show.windowOpen = true, so the Open/Paused toggle is optional); public/studio.html:1917-1925 (scheduled-start and scheduled-end copy shown to the artist)
check.betterFix:
Do not touch line 366's promise; fix the source of the strain and let the lede bound itself in one clause.

H2, about.html:365 — replace "Five things happen. None of them need you." with:
  "Five things happen. Only one wants a tap."

Lede, about.html:366 — replace "You start the show and play. Everything below runs itself while you're on stage." with:
  "You start the show and play. One tap in each gap picks the winner — the rest below runs itself while you're on stage."

Why this is better than the proposed rewrite: it removes the contradiction at its actual source (the H2) instead of adding a second admission underneath a headline that still denies it; it keeps the four beats that genuinely do run themselves (scan-in, requests-refund, money, after-the-gig) claiming what they can honestly claim; it does not duplicate beat 2 at :386; and it stays inside Perry's compression rather than trading a promise for a caveat.

Optional, and honest in the other direction — the page currently gives away automation it actually has. Beat 2 could add one line, supported by _auto.mjs:144 and :130/:162:
  "Put the gig in your calendar and the show even starts and ends itself."
That is a real, unclaimed feature sitting in the code.

check.reasoning:
I read every file the accuser cites, plus the ones they did not.

WHAT THE PAGE ACTUALLY CLAIMS (public/about.html:373-377). The headline is "They scan, and they're in". The body under it makes four mechanism claims and one durability claim: "No app, no sign-up, no email, no password — the fans never make an account" and "Print it once. It's good forever." Every one of those is true in code. public/vote.html:287-290 mints the fan id as a random localStorage string client-side; boot is `await load(); await handleReturn();` (vote.html:1146-1153); there is no name prompt, consent banner, captcha, age gate or terms click anywhere in the file (I grepped consent|cookie|captcha|terms|age|sign up|password|prompt( — nothing). The profile code is slug-based (netlify/functions/qr.mjs:20 `https://myset.vip/${slug}`), so it genuinely never expires — which is what makes "print it once, good forever" true, and is precisely why the profile code, not a per-show vote code, is the one on the table. The page never says "straight to the vote list", "zero taps" or "no page in between". The accuser is enforcing a condition the copy never asserts.

THE ACCUSER'S OWN EVIDENCE IS WRONG ON A LOAD-BEARING POINT. They state "on that page the only route to voting is a single pill, and it renders only while a show is live", citing artist.html:389. That is false. public/artist.html:405-407 renders the page's PRIMARY call to action, always, in the CTA row directly under the artist's name: `<a class="joinlive ${live?'':'off'}" href="${VOTEHREF}" id="joinBtn">` with the label `Join live` when live (line 407). VOTEHREF is `/slug/vote` (artist.html:266). It is a full-width filled button (`.joinlive{flex:1;...}` artist.html:130), materially more prominent than the corner pill at line 389. So a scanning fan lands on a page whose single biggest button says "Join live" — two entry points, not one, and the accuser missed the main one. Their claimed sequence "scan → page → find a banner → vote" understates the affordance badly.

A SECOND CODE PATH MAKES THE HEADLINE LITERALLY TRUE FOR REAL TABLES. qr.mjs:16-17 and :21 keep the `vote` kind resolving on purpose: "`vote` and `invite` still RESOLVE, because codes printed before this may be on somebody's table". Codes printed under the older scheme land a fan directly on /slug/vote with zero intermediate taps. The Studio no longer offers that kind (studio.html:2991-2993, confirmed), but the copy describes what a fan experiences, and for those tables it is exact.

THE PROPOSED FIX IS WORSE THAN THE LINE IT REPLACES. "They scan, tap the live banner, and they're in" (a) names a UI element that is not what the primary control is called — the main button reads "Join live", not a banner; (b) is wrong for anyone with a legacy vote code; (c) is wrong outside show hours, when the same code lands on the page and the CTA counts down instead; (d) spends the beat's headline on a tap-by-tap that no reader wanted, which is exactly the "show don't tell" discipline this page was rebuilt to obey. It converts a true promise into a fragile, partly-false instruction.

WHAT SURVIVES, HONESTLY. There is one real, minor gap between the compressed headline and the mechanism: during a live show, a fan scanning the table code reaches the voting screen on one tap, not zero. That is a difference of a single tap on a page that never promised zero, and the paragraph doing the actual claiming is exact. Status should be ACCURATE. If Perry ever wants the extra tap acknowledged, it belongs in the body, not the headline, and only if it earns its words.

I checked every gate the accuser cited, and every mechanism fact they state is true. The conclusion drawn from those facts is not.

WHAT I CONFIRMED MYSELF.
1. All three things render in one place with no navigation. studio.html:551 defaults TAB to 'live', and the Live branch at 1869-1939 emits the vote box, the three-stat row, Now playing, asksPanel(), the show controls, "Start top voted", the ranked queue, Played and tips — one continuous body, no sub-tab, no route change.
2. "What's winning" is real and server-authoritative. stage.mjs:72-78 runs rankSongs() and stamps a server-computed `votable` on every song precisely so the Studio's queue and its button label cannot drift from playTop. The Studio then shows the leader twice: in the button (studio.html:1923-1924) and at rank 1 of the queue.
3. "How many people are in the room" is the most carefully worded phrase on the line, and it is exactly right. stage.mjs:61-64 sends `voters` (phones that have voted) and `room: room.phones` with the comment "phones in the room tonight, not just phones that voted." The tile at studio.html:1880-1881 prints voters/room under the label "Voting · in room". The page says "in the room"; the server measures the room. The accuser's proposed swap of "people" for "phones" makes true copy less true — the page is describing the human fact, and the server's own comment calls it the room.
4. Requests really are off by default (_lib.mjs:182, `requests:{on:false}` with the comment that an artist who can't play requests should never be asked for them), only flipped by an explicit admin action (admin.mjs:1932-1934), and only advertised to fans when on (show.mjs:140-146). asksPanel() really does return '' when there are none (studio.html:2609-2610).

WHY THAT DOES NOT MAKE LINE 385 WRONG.
· The condition is disclosed, on the same page, in the very next beat. Line 399-400 reads "Requests cost votes, never money … and they only exist if you switch them on." Beats 1-4 are one numbered narrative in one column; beat 3 is roughly a screen below beat 2 and is titled "They ask for things — properly". The accuser's own fix would insert into line 385 the identical caveat the page already makes ten lines later — a duplication, not a correction, and it drops a caveat into the one line in that beat that carries the rhythm.
· The empty-panel half of the accusation is not an overstatement at all. "One screen tells you … what they've asked for" is not falsified by a night on which nobody asked. A panel that shows nothing when there is nothing to show is the panel working.
· The scrolling half applies a condition the sentence never sets. "One screen" is a claim about there being one place and no navigating between them, which the Live tab satisfies exactly. The page nowhere says "without scrolling", "at a glance" or "above the fold". If below-the-fold content disqualified "one screen", no scrolling page could ever describe itself.
· There is a false-precision error inside the accusation itself: it says "the winner alone is in the button label", implying the standings need a scroll the winner does not. Both live in the same lower region — the button at 1923-1924 sits directly above the queue at 1926-1932. The scroll cost is identical, so the distinction it draws does not exist.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY BE WRONG. If beat 3 did not exist, the requests caveat would belong on line 385 and I would confirm the finding. It exists, and it is adjacent. Under Perry's standing calibration — flag the mechanism, never rewrite his framing when the mechanism under it is true — this is a line whose mechanism is true and whose one condition the page already states in his own voice.

Every code citation in the accusation checks out. Requests and birthdays really are `on: false` in defaultShow (_lib.mjs:181-182), show.mjs really does gate the asks payload and the extra blob read on those flags (show.mjs:112-113, 143-146), and asksPanel really does return '' on an empty list (studio.html:2608-2610). FIRST AND DECISIVE: the caveat is not missing from the page. The accuser states it themselves — "beat 3 at L399 does" carry it — and then treats the absence of a SECOND copy in beat 2 as the defect. SECOND: the accuser applies a condition the sentence never implies. "One screen tells you what's winning, how many people are in the room, and what they've asked for" is a claim about WHERE the information lives — one screen, not three tabs and a spreadsheet — not a claim that all three fields are populated on a fresh account. Applied consistently, the same standard would condemn "what's winning" (a show with no votes yet shows nothing) and "how many people are in the room" (zero until fans scan). finding.claimText: how many people are in the room
finding.evidence: The number is a count of phones, and the code says so. `roomCounts` (_lib.mjs:747-759) walks the fan bag and counts any record that stamped itself on the voting page or took part — `const here = !!f.seenShow || (f.v||[]).length > 0 || f.extra > 0 || f.spent > 0` — returning `{ phones, nets }`. stage.mjs:62-63 puts it on the Studio payload under the comment "phones in the room tonight". `markPresence` (_lib.mjs:765-775) writes one stamp per device per show and the stamp never decays, so a phone left on a table after its owner walks out keeps counting, and two phones for one person count twice. The Studio's own label is the more careful "Voting · in room" (studio.html:1880-1881), which the landing page copy has flattened to "people in the room". Separately worth knowing: `roomCounts` does NOT filter by tonight's showId the way show.mjs's `countInRoom` does (_lib.mjs:810-815), so on a RESUMED show (Start the show rather than Start a new show, which skips carryFans — _lifecycle.mjs:168) devices stamped on an earlier night are still in the denominator.
finding.proposedFix: Line 385: change "how many people are in the room" to "how many phones are in the room".

check.reasoning:
The accusation rests on three planks. I checked all three; two are factually wrong and the third is a taste call the codebase decides against.

PLANK 1 — "the code says phones, the landing page flattened it to people." False as a characterisation of the product. The SERVER itself names this exact metric `people`: netlify/functions/_vstats.mjs:53 does `const people = s.room ?? s.peakVoters ?? 0` where `s.room` is literally `roomCounts(fans).phones` archived at _history.mjs:129,140 — then ships it as `people` at _vstats.mjs:59-63, profile.mjs:31 and _pitch.mjs:106. The APP'S OWN UI labels it "People in the room" (public/venue-studio.html:1240, rendering `S.totals.people`) and "people in the room" (public/venue-studio.html:1216,1221; public/venue.html:466,501; public/studio.html:2594; public/studio.html:2388 "how many people were in their own room"). So "people in the room" is not marketing flattening — it is MySet's established name for this number across the server, the Venue Studio and the Artist Studio. The single label the accuser cites ("Voting · in room", studio.html:1882) is terse because it is a two-word caption under a `21/26` stat tile, not because the product is being careful about phones-vs-humans.

PLANK 2 — "on a RESUMED show, devices stamped on an earlier night are still in the denominator." Wrong, and I traced it. A resume (`fresh:false`, _lifecycle.mjs:169) does NOT mint a new showId (_lifecycle.mjs:126,136 — `show.showId = freshId` only when fresh), so every surviving stamp carries tonight's showId anyway. And a fresh start runs `carryFans`, which REBUILDS or DELETES every fan record: `bag[id] = { v: [], ts: {}, extra: carry, gifted, gr }` or `delete bag[id]` (_lib.mjs:563-565) — `seenShow` does not survive. There is no code path by which a previous night's `seenShow` reaches tonight's `roomCounts`. On that path `roomCounts` and `countInRoom` agree on stamps.

The accuser missed the real divergence, which cuts the other way and defeats their own fix: that same carryFans line keeps a record with `extra: carry > 0`, and `roomCounts`'s presence test (_lib.mjs:753) treats `f.extra > 0` as here. So a fan who bought a vote pack last night and didn't spend it is counted as present from minute zero of a brand-new show, before any device opens the page. Calling that "a phone in the room" is MORE false than calling it a person — it is neither.

PLANK 3 — the non-decaying stamp. True as mechanism (markPresence, _lib.mjs:765-775, writes once per device per show and nothing removes it), but it is not fixed by the proposed edit. A phone left on a table after its owner walks out is not "a phone in the room" either. The fix is non-responsive to the accuser's own strongest evidence, and swapping in "phones" buys a precision the code cannot back while losing the word the rest of the product uses.

Finally, the page never claimed device-level precision. finding.claimText: no email
finding.evidence: MySet itself never asks a fan for an email. Stripe's hosted Checkout page always collects the buyer's email address in payment mode; `customer_email` only prefills it. So a fan doing what beat 4 describes does type an email — into Stripe's form, not MySet's. Today this only bites on the founder's own gigs, because canTakeMoney (_pay.mjs:53-55) is true only for isPlatformOwner or an artist with a ready Connect mirror, and connectReady (_pay.mjs:34-38) is false for everyone else. check.reasoning:
The accusation reads the accounting ledger and calls it the fan's experience. Both of its named legs collapse when you follow what the fan actually holds.

WHAT I READ MYSELF

1. Charge: createRequest debits `me.spent += cost` (_requests.mjs:96). `creditsUsed = votes + spent` (_lib.mjs:718-719), and remaining = (freeCredits + extra) - creditsUsed.
2. Refund: resolveRequest refunds only when `row.showId === show.showId` (_requests.mjs:173), via `me.spent = Math.max(0, spent - cost)` (_requests.mjs:141-143). Both gates are exactly as the accuser describes.
3. THE PART THE ACCUSER MISSED: every song start calls clearAllFanVotes (admin.mjs:1782 for `play`, :1808 for `playTop` — both set `resetVotes = true` unconditionally; fired at admin.mjs:2001), which sets `bag[id].v = []; bag[id].ts = {}; bag[id].spent = 0` (_lib.mjs:521).

So in the accuser's case (b) — decline after the next song has started — the fan's `spent` is 0 AND their vote count is back to full (`total - 0`). The refund returns nothing because there is nothing left to return: the fan already has every vote back. Refunding on top would MINT votes, which is precisely what the INVARIANT 0ac comment at _requests.mjs:167-171 says. Case (a) — a request from an earlier show — is the same thing one show later: those credits refreshed, the fan is whole. Case (c) — the write throwing — self-heals at the very next song start for the same reason.

The page's sentence is "their votes come straight back," which is a promise about the FAN'S OUTCOME, not about which ledger field moved. In every case the accuser names, a free-credit fan ends up holding their votes. The page also sets up this exact mechanism two beats earlier at about.html:384-385 — "One tap starts the top song and hands everybody fresh votes" — so the reader has already been told votes refresh on song start.

THE PROPOSED FIX IS WORSE THAN THE SENTENCE
"the same night" would be actively misleading in both directions. It implies a same-night decline always returns votes — but the accuser's own case (b), the zeroed `spent`, happens the same night. And it implies a next-night decline leaves the fan short, when the fan is fully re-credited. It adds a caveat that is false at both ends.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG (narrower, and the accuser got it backwards)
The accuser wrote "the fan is not out of pocket." That is false for a fan who BOUGHT votes. `paidUsed = max(0, creditsUsed - freeCredits)` (_lib.mjs:499-501) and creditsUsed includes `spent` (_lib.mjs:718-719), so a request whose cost pushes usage past the free allowance is settled out of the fan's purchased balance at the reset: `bag[id].extra -= paid` (_lib.mjs:517-518). Worked example: freeCredits 5, extra 10, fan votes on 3 songs then makes a 3-vote request → creditsUsed 6 → paidUsed 1 → at the next song start extra drops 10→9 and spent→0. A decline after that returns nothing, and one vote the fan paid money for is gone for good. Declined BEFORE the song start, the refund lowers creditsUsed and the paid vote survives.

That is a real defect, but it is a code bug in the settle/refund pair, not a wording problem on the landing page — and it only bites fans who bought votes, which the page itself already flags as founder-gigs-only today (about.html:412-417).

WHY THE SENTENCE IS NOT OVERSTATED. The accusation is that the page promises unconditional landing and the code adds a condition. It does not. The sentence is "a public what's-on feed for YOUR TOWN". The feed is keyed on town (events.mjs:60), so the sentence's own subject presupposes the artist has named one. Naming your town in order to be listed under your town is not a hidden gate; it is the thing the sentence describes. (1) The seven-day window is not a discrepancy. The sentence's own payoff clause is "people looking for something to do TONIGHT find you" — tonight is inside seven days, so the window supports the claim rather than contradicting it. Line 430 promises a town feed; it does not promise canonical geocoding or spelling normalisation. That is a genuine product bug to file on its own, and it is arguably WIDER than the accuser framed it — it degrades the picker for every artist in a town regardless of what any marketing page says — but it is not evidence that this sentence overstates.

ONE CITATION IS A COMMENT, NOT CODE. The accusation offers _plan.mjs:7 as proof the city feed is ungated. Both halves of the accusation are facts about the code, and neither of them makes the sentence overstated.

The geolocation half applies a condition the page never implied. The copy says "a public what's-on feed for your town" — it explicitly scopes the feed to a town, and picking your town from a list is the ordinary way to use a what's-on directory. Nothing in the sentence promises auto-detection, so the absence of navigator.geolocation refutes nothing. (The picker also remembers the last city, so a returning stranger lands on the feed with no interaction at all: index.html:329-336.)

The featured-placement half is real in code but does not touch this claim. The sentence makes no ordering, ranking, or top-billing promise — it claims the gig is listed and that a stranger looking for tonight can find it. A featured spot does not remove anyone from the feed; events.mjs:115-137 moves at most three rows from d.gigs into d.featured on the same night, and :138 counts both in that night's total. The unfeatured gig is still there, still under the right night, still in start-time order. Two further things weaken it as a present-tense description of what a reader would see: index.html:485 renders the "Featured shows" heading only when a spot has actually been sold, so an unsold night shows no paid block at all; and the feature is available to the reader themselves, so it is a product they can buy, not a tax levied on them.

Meanwhile the parts of the claim that could have been false all check out stronger than the copy states. There is no plan gate: reindexCities is called unconditionally after every event save (admin.mjs:489, 496, 517) and indexes any gig with a country and city (_events.mjs:180-186), so a free-plan artist is listed. There is no publish step, no approval, and no private/unlisted profile flag that would keep someone out. The city feed needs no session. The Pro "List shows in cities you don't normally play — Soon" item (about.html:645) gates a different thing entirely and does not gate the home-town listing.

The status should be ACCURATE. The one thing worth carrying forward is broader than the accusation and lives elsewhere on the page: about.html contains no mention of Featured shows, Promote, or $10 anywhere, while a live Stripe charge for it exists at admin.mjs:1452-1465 with the flag defaulting on. That is an omission in the plans/honest-notes section, not an overstatement at line 431.

check.reasoning:
The accusation rests on three factual claims about the code. All three fail when you read the code.

1. "The archived record only exists after an explicit end; _lifecycle.mjs:182 is the only end-show archiveShow call." False twice over.
   (a) The record does not need an archive at all to exist on night one. netlify/functions/history.mjs builds a `live` object — songsPlayed, totalVotes, peakVoters, gross — straight off the running show and the fans blob (history.mjs:44-55), and the file's own header comment at :5-6 says why: "The show currently running is included as a live preview so the artist can see tonight's numbers before he ends it." studio.html:2100-2106 renders exactly that as "Tonight so far", with People/Votes/Taken, during the set. No archive, no end, night one.
   (b) endShow (_lifecycle.mjs:179, archiving at :182) has four callers, and one of them is a cron: _auto.mjs:130 and :162 end and file the show automatically once the gig's end time plus grace has passed. So even the filed record needs no explicit act by the artist — it lands the same night, on its own. (_account.mjs:123 and admin.mjs:1672 are the others.)
   The Freedom card's promise is "you walk out with proof". You end the show as you walk out — or the schedule ends it for you. That is night one, not "builds up as you play".

2. "hist_perry-idyll_2026-08-30-1210 has playedUnlogged: true, so the Studio renders the 'titles weren't logged' branch." The causal link is invented. `playedUnlogged` appears nowhere in the repository — I grepped the whole tree, zero hits — and archiveShow's document shape (_history.mjs:130-146) has no such field. The branch at studio.html:2084 fires on `(H.played||[]).length === 0` with `stats.songsPlayed > 0`. That is reading a data blob's stray key as if it were a gate.
   And even granting the branch: it is the "What you played" section, i.e. song TITLES. The Freedom card never promises a setlist. It promises "how many people were there, what they wanted, what they paid" — and in that same archived night, stats.peakVoters/room still render (studio.html:2065-2067), the requested[] "Wanted but never played" list still renders (studio.html:2086-2091), and requested[] is built from fan votes across every round (_history.mjs:91-101), independent of whether any song was ever started from the Studio. The one document the accuser cites as proof of shortfall in fact still carries all three things the card names.

3. "The money figure needs Stripe Connect that no artist has." The page already says so, in the same reading flow, thirty lines earlier: about.html:415 — "One caveat, up front: card payments are the part still being built. They run on the founder's own gigs today and switch on for everyone once the payouts plumbing is finished." Charging that gate again against the Freedom card double-counts a caveat the page volunteered.

Two further points against the severity.
The sentence is comparative, not absolute: "Three things get EASIER the first night" — not "three things are fully finished". The accuser applies a completeness test the page never invited.
And the accuser's own two "available" items are held to a laxer standard than the third: Ease is credited on the live 4s poll, Excitement is credited on nothing but human reaction. Freedom has a live numbers panel plus an automatic same-night filing, which is more machinery than either.

The one genuine residual, and it is small: the PUBLIC artist page's Shows/people/votes stats are read off the archive index (profile.mjs:15-20), so those specific venue-facing numbers appear once the night is filed rather than mid-set. Still the first night — just at the end of it rather than during. That does not touch "you walk out with proof", which is a Studio claim.

The proposed fix would make the page less true, not more. "The third builds up as you play — and it's the one venues care about" implies the record accrues over multiple nights before it is usable. One night produces one filed show with room count, vote count, top song and the wanted-but-never-played list, automatically. Shipping that fix would introduce an inaccuracy where there is none.

check.reasoning:
The accusation's own remedy ("leave as written") concedes the copy is fine, but its stated reason is wrong and its status label is wrong, so it parks a permanent open item on a sentence that is sound by construction.

1. The claim that there is "no product referent anywhere in the repo" is false. Line 446 is a LEDE, not a standalone assertion. It says "Three things get easier... and they're the three that make the difference." The three things are named immediately below it, and each one carries its own explicit mechanism anchor:
   - public/about.html:452-455 Ease — "Why: the queue is ranked live, and one tap starts the winner."
   - public/about.html:459-463 Excitement — "Why: they voted."
   - public/about.html:467-470 Freedom — "Why: every night is recorded, and it's yours to show."
   So the sentence's referent is three lines away on the same screen, not absent.

2. I checked those anchors in code myself, and all three are shipped and NOT plan-gated:
   - "one tap starts the winner": public/studio.html:1923-1925 renders a "Start top voted — <title> (<votes>)" button calling act('playTop'); the server handles it at netlify/functions/admin.mjs:1684 and :1785, and the ordering rule it uses is the single shared one in netlify/functions/_lib.mjs:790. The queue rows beneath it (studio.html:1927-1931) are vote-ranked with a per-row Start.
   - "every night is recorded": netlify/functions/history.mjs:7-10 gates on requireArtist only — there is no planOf/limitsFor check anywhere in the file. Per-show records carry songsPlayed, totalVotes and peakVoters (netlify/functions/_history.mjs:106, :140, :193, :324). A free artist gets this on night one.
   - The one plan flag that would have broken this, `analytics`, is false on free/plus and listed in NOT_BUILT (netlify/functions/_plan.mjs:75, :91, :130) — but `analytics` is scoped in its own comment to "earnings by venue / night / song", which is a different and richer thing than the raw per-night record. That is the wrong bucket for a sentence that is, by grammatical construction, an authorial value judgement about how a night feels ("a gig you got through" vs "a gig you loved"). It makes no falsifiable product statement, so there is nothing to verify and nothing to leave open. Filing it as UNVERIFIABLE creates a to-do that can never be closed.

4. I looked for a worse or wider problem on this line and did not find one. The only thing in the neighbourhood worth a separate look is the Freedom card's "what they paid" (about.html:468) — card payments are explicitly caveated as founder-only and still being built earlier on the same page (about.html:415-418), so a new artist's night-one record shows $0 there. Every structural claim in the sentence verifies in code I read. All three numbers render (venue-studio.html:1240-1242 from _vstats.mjs:63-64), "by act" renders (byAct list, _vstats.mjs:69), "by night" renders (byNight list, _vstats.mjs:58), and "with the average per night" is literally there — venue-studio.html:1257 computes Math.round(a.people/a.nights) under the label "avg/night". The accuser's data chain is also correct — s.room (_vstats.mjs:52) ← room.phones (_history.mjs:142) ← roomCounts (_lib.mjs:747-760) — but the inference from it is wrong on three counts.

1. It is not a landing-page/app discrepancy. The app itself calls this number "people" everywhere: "People in the room" (venue-studio.html:1240), "${a.people} people" in By act (1255), "people in the room" in the pitch rows (1216), and the artist Studio's own description of the very same venue feature — "how many people were in their own room and how many votes got cast — by night and by act" (studio.html:2388). The landing page uses the product's own word for the product's own metric. Changing about.html to "Phones" would make the marketing page disagree with every screen it describes.

2. The error direction is the opposite of "overstated". roomCounts counts one record per present device; every person in the room who never opens the voting page is invisible, and a couple sharing one phone counts once. The design comment at _lib.mjs:721-734 makes exactly this argument ("A phone is much closer to a person than a network is"). The number is a floor on the head count, so "People" claims less than the room actually held, not more. And the page's promise around it — comparing acts to stop booking on a feeling — is served fine by a consistent proxy.

3. The proposed replacement copy is itself less accurate than what it replaces. "It counts the people who opened the voting page" is wrong: _lib.mjs:754 also counts any record with votes, extra credits or spend, and carryFans (_lib.mjs:559) preserves a record with extra>0 across a fresh show — so a fan who bought a vote pack last month and did not attend tonight still satisfies `here` and counts in tonight's room. (about.html:508), whose lede names the job being replaced: "Update the Facebook page every week." (:509-511). check.reasoning:
The accusation's two load-bearing statements — "The rule is inert at every viewport" and "The dead rule at about.html:106 can go" — are both false. Acting on the proposed fix would cause a visible regression.

WHAT I CHECKED MYSELF

Geometry (confirmed): about.html:102 caps .phone at max-width:300px with 9px padding (:103), and public/app.css:52 sets `*{box-sizing:border-box}`, so the img content box is exactly 282px. about.html:105 sets `width:100%;height:auto`. That part of the accuser's math is correct.

But .phone.tall is used on FOUR images, not one. The accuser only did the arithmetic for the single one at :580 and then generalised. Measured intrinsic sizes with `sips`:
  :389 /about/studio.png  640x1385 -> 282 x 2.1641 = 610.3px  -> EXCEEDS 600, CROPS ~10px
  :403 /about/ask.png     640x1477 -> 282 x 2.3078 = 650.8px  -> EXCEEDS 600, CROPS ~51px (7.8%)
  :433 /about/profile.jpg 780x1500 -> 282 x 1.9231 = 542.3px  -> under, no crop
  :580 /about/fills.png   640x968  -> 282 x 1.5125 = 426.5px  -> under, no crop

So the rule at :106 is live and doing real work on two of the four. I opened ask.png and mapped where the cut lands: at a top-anchored 600px ceiling the visible region ends at image y=1362, and the sticky bottom action bar ("More votes / From $3" and "Tip Sam / Say thanks") begins around y=1357 — so that whole bar is cut away bar a ~5px sliver. That is not an accident; max-height:600px plus object-position:top is the author's deliberate device for normalising four screenshots of very different heights (968 / 1385 / 1477 / 1500) to one visual ceiling. And it fires at essentially every viewport >= ~344px, because .phone sits at its full 300px cap in both the one-column and the two-column (:156, min-width:820px) beat layout.

Deleting :106, as the fix proposes, would let studio.png grow to 610px and ask.png to 651px, un-normalising the beat rail and restoring content the author chose to cut. That is a regression, not a cleanup.

WHAT SURVIVES

Only this, much narrower: on the one element at :580 the `tall` class is a no-op, because fills.png at 426px never reaches the 600px ceiling. Same for :433 (profile.jpg at 542px). That is a redundant class on two elements, not a dead rule.

CATEGORY POINT

This is a landing-page claims audit, and a CSS declaration is not an assertion made to a reader. Nothing here is visible to a visitor as a true-or-false statement, so "status FALSE" is a category error; at worst it is a housekeeping note.

I also confirmed the accuser's one genuinely correct supporting claim: `grep -n "\.phone" public/about.html` and `grep -n phone public/app.css` show no other .phone rule anywhere — :102-109 in about.html is the complete set, and app.css has none.

check.reasoning:
I read the code myself and the kernel of the accusation holds: public/vote.html:709 renders a "Tip <artist> · Say thanks" button in every room unconditionally, :708 renders "More votes" with a real price whenever d.paymentsEnabled, and both run through :944-952 → netlify/functions/pay.mjs:80 into a genuine Stripe Checkout Session. So "Everything the room sees is free. Always." is literally over-broad, and the lede's "none of it ever costs the room a penny" (about.html:593) reads wider than what the code guarantees. That much I could not refute.

But the finding is materially weaker than "AMBIGUOUS / major", on four counts.

1. The price is invisible for every artist alive today. _pay.mjs:52-54 canTakeMoney returns true only for isPlatformOwner or show.pay.ready, and _pay.mjs:33-38 connectReady is false for everyone but the founder because Connect is not built. With paymentsEnabled false, vote.html:708 shows "Ask <artist>" and no figure, and vote.html:918/934 turn both sheets into "Card payments aren't on tonight". So the accusation's "the room is shown money buttons with a price" is true only on the founder's own gigs.

2. The page already discloses fan-facing money, in the same section, without being asked: about.html:627 sells "Price your own vote packs" as a Plus feature, :628-629 sells setting "what it costs the room to replay", and :654-657 states plainly that tips and vote packs exist and currently run only on the founder's gigs. A reader of this section cannot come away believing no money ever moves on a fan's phone. That is a scope-sloppy heading over honest body copy, not a false claim about the product.

3. Three of the four "room-facing plan gates" cited do not support the charge at all. _plan.mjs:20 free.featured:50 is not a cost to the room and is disclosed verbatim at about.html:610 ("50 live to the room at once"). _plan.mjs:66 free.pricing:false locks the DEFAULTS, and the defaults are free (_lib.mjs:176/390 freeCredits 5; replayCost is priced in votes, admin.mjs:1946-1951 clamps 1..20) — admin.mjs:1699-1704 says in code that this gates the artist's back office and the room's night is identical. _plan.mjs:77 branding is in NOT_BUILT (_plan.mjs:130), so it gates nothing that exists, and about.html:644 already marks it "Soon".

4. The real problem is one the accuser missed, and their fix would enshrine it. admin.mjs:1832 clamps freeCredits with Math.max(0, …) and studio.html:2244/3026 accept 0, so a Plus/Pro artist can set the free-vote allowance to zero — after which vote.mjs:118-121 refuses every single vote with 402 'no-credits' until the fan buys a pack. That makes "Nobody ever pays to take part. Always." demonstrably false in a reachable configuration, which is worse than the sentence it replaces. The proposed fix should not ship.

check.reasoning:
I read the files. The finding survives, but not for the reasons given.

WHAT SURVIVES. The word "ever" is an absolute and the code breaks it. Two ways:
(1) Ordinary path — a fan who spends their free credits (default 5, _lib.mjs:390) hits 402 no-credits (vote.mjs:119-121) and the only in-app way past it is the pack sheet at vote.html:919-931 → pay.mjs → a real USD Stripe Checkout. Voting past your allowance costs money.
(2) The path the accuser MISSED, and it is worse than what they found. `freeCredits` is artist-settable and clamps to a floor of ZERO (admin.mjs:1833). The Studio's custom field only rejects n<0 (studio.html:3027), so 0 saves cleanly. At 0 free credits with unlimited off, vote.mjs:120-121 rejects every single vote and _requests.mjs:94-96 rejects every request and shout-out. Taking part at all then requires buying a pack. That is a live, code-level configuration in which participation literally costs money — a far sharper refutation of "none of it EVER costs the room a penny" than "an optional upsell exists." (Gated to Plus/Pro by canPrice at admin.mjs:1707/1831 — a free-plan artist stays at 5 — but Plus/Pro is most of the paying base.)

WHAT I THROW OUT OF THE ACCUSATION.
- The tip sheet (vote.html:933-940) is not evidence. A voluntary tip is not a cost of taking part, and the page never claims tips don't exist — it brags about them at about.html:489 ("100% of it from the room"). Citing tips inflates the finding and would get the whole thing dismissed by anyone who checks.
- "Critical" is too high. Critical implies concealment. The page discloses the pack economy TWICE in its own body: the interactive demo at :758 literally reads "Out of votes — in the room you could buy a few more," and the Plus plan sells "Price your own vote packs" at :627. A reader is not deceived about the existence of paid votes. This is a sentence that overreaches past what the rest of its own page says — a self-contradiction and an overclaim, which is major, not critical.
- The accuser's framing "the same section contradicts itself eleven lines later" is correct but it is a symptom, not the defect. The defect is the single word "ever."

WHAT DEFENDS THE PAGE, and how far it goes. The sentence is more carefully scoped than a hostile read allows: its subject is a feature list ("The voting, the lyrics, the requests, your page, your gig listings"), the heading is "Everything the room sees is free. Always.", and the closer is "What you pay for is your own back office." Read as "no feature is paywalled away from the audience and MySet never bills the audience," it is TRUE — pay.mjs:195-215 puts the platform cut in `application_fee_amount`, deducted from the artist, with nothing added on top of what the fan sees. That defense carries the heading and it carries the last sentence. It does not carry "none of it ever costs the room a penny," because "the voting" is item one in that list and the voting demonstrably can cost money. One word too strong, in a section that is otherwise honest.

The accuser was also right to pre-empt the replay-cost red herring: _lib.mjs:712-713 `costOf` charges 5 VOTES, not cents, so about.html:626 is clean.

The finding SURVIVES, but only on three of the five things the accuser cited, and two of its citations are wrong. I read every gate myself.

WHAT IS REAL (I confirmed these in code, not comments):

1. Merch — genuinely audience-facing and Plus-gated. netlify/functions/_plan.mjs:68 `merch: false` on free, :90 `merch: true` on plus, :108 on pro; the gate is netlify/functions/_plan.mjs:158 `merchAllowed = (aid, limits) => isPlatformOwner(aid) || !!(limits && limits.merch === true)`, applied to the fan-facing payload at netlify/functions/community.mjs:73 `merch: merchAllowed(aid, limits) ? p.merch.filter((m) => m.on) : []`. The rail is drawn at public/community.html:270-271 (NOT :222-223 as the accuser wrote — those are `<script>` tags). Also enforced at the till, netlify/functions/pay.mjs:121.

2. The verified tick — netlify/functions/community.mjs:71 `verified: !!(who && who.verified) && plan !== 'free'`, rendered on the public page at public/community.html:266 as a `✓ Verified` badge. This is the sharpest item and the accuser buried it as an afterthought. It is a public trust marker that switches OFF when a plan lapses, and about.html never mentions verification at all (0 occurrences of "verified" in the file). If anything this piece is UNDERSTATED.

3. `featured: 50` — _plan.mjs:20, really enforced at netlify/functions/admin.mjs:1695 and :833/:925, and it does bound how many songs the room can choose from. Real, though the page itself discloses it on the Free card ("Keep 2,000 songs — 50 live to the room at once").

WHAT IS WRONG IN THE ACCUSATION:

4. `branding` is not evidence of anything. It is in NOT_BUILT (_plan.mjs:130 `export const NOT_BUILT = ['promote','analytics','presskit','branding']`) and there is no code behind it anywhere — grep finds no consumer. The accuser quoted the source comment "your colours and logo on the audience pages" and reported it as behaviour, which is exactly the trap. The page also already marks it honestly: public/about.html:644 lists "Your colours and logo on the fan pages" with a `Soon` chip, and the honest-notes block at :659-661 says the four Pro extras marked Soon are not shipped.

5. `pricing` is the definition of a back-office control, so it argues against the accuser. netlify/functions/admin.mjs:1707 gates only the ARTIST's ability to change `freeCredits`/`packs`/`replayCost`/`askSet`. The defaults are identical on every plan and are free: _lib.mjs:176 `freeCredits: 5`, :179 `replayCost: 5` (five VOTES, not money — see _lib.mjs:713). A free artist's room gets the same five free votes as anyone's. Nothing in the vote path reads the plan.

I also checked a thing the accuser did not raise, which could have looked like a wider problem and is not: the `audience` cap (200/1000/2000) does NOT change the room's night. Degradation is driven purely by head count, not by plan — _lib.mjs:852-858 `pollFloorFor(heads)` and :866-872 `boardLimitFor(heads)` take only `heads`. The stamped `roomCap` (_lifecycle.mjs:53, show.mjs:169) only sets an `over` flag for the artist; _lifecycle.mjs:35-38 states the door is never closed and no vote is refused, and the code matches. So a free artist with 900 people in the room gets the identical experience a Pro artist would.

NET: the headline above the sentence — "Everything the room sees is free. Always." — is TRUE and is the load-bearing claim. The trailing clause "What you pay for is your own back office" is a loose summary that three real, built things contradict: merch, the verified tick, and the 50-song board cap. Two of those three are itemised in plain English on the plan cards three inches below the sentence, so the reader is not deceived about facts; the verified tick is the only one nowhere disclosed. Overstated summary, minor — the accuser's status stands, their evidence needs pruning.

ONE WARNING ON THEIR PROPOSED FIX: "a bigger night" would introduce a NEW inaccuracy. Paying does not make the night bigger — _lib.mjs:852-872 proves the room behaves identically at any head count on any plan, and _lifecycle.mjs:35-38 proves nobody is turned away on free. Do not ship that wording.

Do NOT take the accuser's "rooms of about 200" — 200 is exact and load-bearing (it is the first rung of the ladder), and "about" throws away a true, precise number for nothing. Second, the same bullet needs the opposite treatment on its first half: "4 shows a month" IS hard-refused at show five (_lifecycle.mjs:134, HTTP 402, "That's your 4 free shows this month"), and the card never says so — an artist finds out when the Start button refuses in front of a room. check.reasoning:
I read the gates rather than the comments. There is no turnstile: roomCap is written once at startShow (_lifecycle.mjs:147) and appears in exactly two later places — show.mjs:44 reading it back and show.mjs:168 reporting `room: { cap, in, over }`. A repo-wide grep for `roomCap` returns those lines and nothing else. Nothing refuses a join, a vote or a poll on it. So there is no alternate code path that makes "up to 200" a door.

But the accuser gets two things wrong and misses a third.

Wrong 1 — the causal link. They write that over the cap "the night just slows and the board shortens", citing pollFloorFor/boardLimitFor. Those functions take `heads` and only `heads` (_lib.mjs:853, 867). A Free room of 400 degrades identically to a Pro room of 400. The plan's number does not cause the slowdown, does not trigger it, and is not even shown to anyone: no page in public/ reads `room.cap` or `room.over` — vote.html consumes `nextPollMs` (:323) and `board` (:586, :666), which are computed from the head count. So the cap has zero runtime effect anywhere, which is stronger than "not a door".

Wrong 2 — they undersell the number. "It is not a door, it is a billing line" makes 200 sound arbitrary. It isn't: 200 is exactly the top of the first rung in both ladders — pollFloorFor(200) = 3000ms, the normal refresh, and boardLimitFor(200) = null, the whole board. So "up to 200 people in the room" truthfully names the size at which the night behaves exactly as designed. That is a real, code-backed meaning for the sentence, and it is why I would not soften the number itself.

Missed — the reason the misreading happens. The accuser blames the contrast with the Plus card. That is half of it. The sharper cause is inside the sentence: "4 shows a month" and "up to 200 people" are joined by one em dash in one bullet, and the first half IS a hard door — _lifecycle.mjs:134 refuses the fifth show with a 402 and a scripted refusal string. A reader parses both halves the same way because they are written the same way, one of them correctly. And the gap is two cards wide, not one: Pro at :639 omits the softness too.

So the page's statement is not false, and it is more carefully grounded than the accusation implies — but the finding holds as an inconsistency, and the bigger unstated thing on that line is the hard show cap, not the soft room cap.

I read all four cited gates and both plan tables. Each of the three sub-claims fails, and the accuser's own counter-example turns out to be the same sentence.

1. THE ACCUSER'S CONTROL IS NOT NARROWER — IT IS THE SAME CLAIM. studio.html:3511 reads `['Everything fans touch',': voting, requests, birthday shout-outs, lyrics']`. The headline claim is verbatim the landing page's. Only an appended examples list differs. If "Everything fans touch" were an overstatement, the Studio would be making it too — so this cannot be a page-vs-app discrepancy. It is at most a copy-detail preference.

2. THE `featured: 50` CAP IS DISCLOSED FIVE LINES BELOW, IN THE SAME BULLET LIST. about.html:610 — "Keep 2,000 songs — 50 live to the room at once" — sits inside the identical Free `<ul>` that opens at :605. The Studio does exactly the same: studio.html has `['Everything fans touch', ...]` and `['Keep 2,000 songs',' — 50 live to the room at once']` as adjacent rows of the same TIER_COPY.free array. A bullet cannot overstate a limit that the next-but-four bullet states plainly. Also, "Everything your fans touch" is a claim about which *kinds* of things fans get, not about volume — the accuser is reading a quantity claim into a category headline.

3. `pricing: false` IS EXPLICITLY NOT FAN-FACING, BY THE CODE'S OWN GATE. admin.mjs:1699-1708 gates only the artist actions freeCredits/packs/replayCost/askSet, and the comment on the gate says so: "The DEFAULTS are free — a free artist runs on them, and everything the ROOM experiences works identically (INVARIANT 0w is untouched; this gates the artist's back office)." Fans on a Free artist still vote, still get free votes, still pay to replay, still buy packs. Nothing a fan touches is missing; the artist just cannot re-tune the numbers. And about.html discloses that as Plus in the adjacent column: "Set your own vote rules — how many free votes each person gets, and what it costs the room to replay a song" and "Price your own vote packs". The accuser is applying a condition the page never implied — that "everything your fans touch" means "every knob behind everything your fans touch".

4. THE VERIFICATION TICK IS GATED, BUT THE PAGE MAKES NO CLAIM ABOUT IT. community.mjs:71 and profile.mjs:27 both compute `verified: !!(who && who.verified) && plan !== 'free'` — real, and wider than the accuser said (they missed profile.mjs, which is what /:slug renders via artist.html:399). But about.html never mentions an artist verification tick anywhere — I grepped; the only "verify" on the page is :577, "Your page works whether you verify it or not", which is in the VENUE section, and venue verified is NOT plan-gated (community.mjs:63 passes `!!v.verified` raw). So that line is true. Meanwhile the Studio lists "The verification tick, once you're checked" as a Plus item in the SAME table whose Free column says "Everything fans touch" — the app itself treats the two statements as compatible. A tick is also something fans look at, not something they touch or do.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG NEARBY (not this bullet, and stronger than this finding): about.html's setlist FAQ — "For one night only, build a setlist instead... You can keep twenty of them and attach one to a gig in your calendar" — describes a Plus-only feature with no plan marker. _plan.mjs free has `setlists: false`, and admin.mjs:735-736 refuses: "Separate setlists are a Plus feature". The Studio correctly lists "Separate setlists" under Plus. That is a genuine free-tier overstatement on the landing page; the accused bullet is not.

The proposed fix ("Everything your fans do — voting, requests, birthday shout-outs, lyrics") is harmless and slightly more concrete, but it corrects nothing false, and "do" is weaker than "touch" for the lyrics sheet, which fans read rather than do.
