I tried to break this three ways and could not.

1) Is there another code path that makes the Free bullet true? No. I read the gate at admin.mjs:731-736 in full. Its own comment says only creating a new setlist is gated — "Everything else about setlists keeps working on free — an artist who downgrades can still use, rename and edit the sets they already have." That sounds like a rescue for the page, but it is not: it only helps someone who ALREADY has setlists, i.e. a downgraded paid artist. A new free artist starts from `emptyLists = () => ({ v: 1, lists: [] })` (_lists.mjs:39) — zero lists — and nothing seeds one. So `listNew` is the only door into having a setlist, and it is shut on free. `listRename`, `listDelete`, `listSongs`, `listToggle`, `listUse` (admin.mjs:750-800) are all ungated, but every one of them takes a `body.id` of a list that must already exist. For a free signup the feature is unreachable, not partially available.

2) Is the accuser reading a doc or comment as behaviour? No — the gate is executable code, and I confirmed `planForArtist` (_plan.mjs:146-151) resolves the real registry plan rather than defaulting to a paid one. The only bypass is `isPlatformOwner`, which is Perry himself (_plan.mjs:154), so it cannot rescue the claim for customers.

3) Is the page's sentence more careful than it looks? No, it is less careful. It is a bare bullet inside the Free card's `<ul>` (lines 600-609), with the free-only exclusion in that same list marked `class="no"` at line 608 — so the page has a visual convention for "not included" and did not use it here. Reading "Setlists" as loose shorthand for "the song library" is not available either, because the same page uses "setlist" in its precise product sense at 693-698.

WHERE IT IS WORSE THAN STATED — two things the accuser missed:

(a) The Plus card in about.html (lines 613-635) never mentions setlists at all. I grepped every occurrence of "setlist" in the file: 398, 606, 682, 690, 693-698. So the page does not merely misfile the feature; it deletes it from the paid tier entirely. The Studio's own sheet sells "Separate setlists, one active per night, applied from your calendar" on Plus (studio.html:3524) and Pro (3538). The landing page gives that selling point away for free and gives Plus nothing in return — a conversion loss on top of the false promise.

(b) The FAQ at 693-698 is a second, worse instance the accusation does not cover. It reads: "build a setlist instead — name it, put the songs you want in it... You can keep twenty of them and attach one to a gig in your calendar, so it loads itself when you start the show." That is unqualified how-to prose in a general FAQ, where a reader has no plan card nearby to give any cue that money is involved, and it walks them straight into the 402. (The "twenty" is at least accurate — MAX_LISTS = 20, _lists.mjs:29.) A free artist following that answer literally hits "Separate setlists are a Plus feature" on the very first step.

So: the accusation survives, the one-line fix is right but incomplete, and fixing only line 606 leaves the FAQ still lying and Plus still stripped of a feature it sells.

check.reasoning:
I read the page and the code myself.

1. The FACT is correct. public/about.html:611 says the Free plan pays "10% of money taken through the app". netlify/functions/_plan.mjs:64 sets `cut: 0.10` for free, with the comment "platform share of tips and vote sales", and the header comment at _plan.mjs:8 says in so many words "What free costs is a 10% cut on money that comes through the app". Plus is 0.02 (_plan.mjs:87) and Pro is 0 (_plan.mjs:~90), which is exactly what the page's other two cards claim (about.html:630 "2% cut instead of 10%", :641 "No cut at all — 0%"). Nothing on the page is untrue, so there is no page-vs-code discrepancy here at all — this is a styling opinion, which is a different kind of finding from the rest of the audit.

2. The accusation's central premise does not hold on this page. It says the dash is "the visual grammar of a MISSING feature". It isn't — not here. `class="no"` occurs EXACTLY ONCE in the whole page (about.html:611) and the `.no` rules at :222-223 exist solely to style that one line; grepping public/*.html finds no other plan-list use (the only other `class="no"` in the repo is an unrelated dismiss button, public/index.html:543). The grammar this page actually uses for "you don't have this / it isn't there yet" is a different one: `.soon` at :228-229 (a ◦ bullet, --muted text) plus a literal "Soon" chip in the markup, used at :642-645. So a reader never learns "dash = you don't get it" from anywhere on the page; they just see one dimmed line whose words plainly say what it is. The page even has a deliberate comment at :224-227 explaining that a disclosure must live in the markup, not in ::after — the author was thinking about exactly this problem.

3. The one reading the accuser fears (dash ⇒ "the free plan does NOT take 10%") is closed off twice over by the page itself: the Plus card at :630 says "2% cut instead of 10%", which only parses if Free is 10%, and honest note 2 at :657 says "the 10% above currently applies to nobody" — i.e. the page explicitly treats the 10% as a live charge that is merely dormant because card payments aren't switched on yet.

4. What survives is much weaker than "MISPLACED": the only line on the card that costs the artist money is painted in --faint (#A1A1A6, app.css:17), the lightest text token on the page — the least prominent styling applied to the least welcome fact. That's a fair polish note, and it points the same way the accuser's fix does (make it MORE visible), but it is cosmetic and subjective, not a discrepancy, and I would not ship it as an audit finding of the same kind as a false claim.

One correction to the accuser's proposed fix: it says to style it "in the accent colour like the Studio does". The Studio's `.fee` is `color:var(--accent-2)` (public/studio.html:282), and app.css redefines --ink/--muted/--faint/--accent/--accent-ink for dark mode (app.css:44-46) but does NOT redefine --accent-2 — so copying the Studio rule verbatim ships an unadapted orange in dark mode.

check.reasoning:
I tried four ways to refute this and all four failed.

(1) Is there another code path making Free's silence true — i.e. can a free artist get a second sign-in? No. auth.mjs:391-398 reads `limits.seats` from planForArtist and refuses the add with a 402 when the existing row count for that artistId meets the cap. The count `mine` is every `byEmail` row pointing at the artist, owner included, so on Free the owner's own address consumes the single seat and no second address can ever be added. Crew and member roles do not sidestep it — the role is chosen after the cap check, not before. There is no `isPlatformOwner` bypass on seats the way there is on merch and moderate (_plan.mjs:155-162), so even the founder is bound by it.

(2) Is the accuser reading a doc or a comment as behaviour? No — the accusation cites _plan.mjs:65 and auth.mjs, and I read the enforcement statement itself, not the comment above it. MYSET.md:381 and INVARIANTS.md:1167 agree with the code, but the code stands on its own.

(3) Is the page's sentence more carefully worded than the accuser noticed? This is the strongest refutation available and it still does not carry. The Free card makes no claim of unlimited sign-ins; it simply never mentions them. And a reader can infer *something* from "Five sign-ins for your band" sitting under Pro — the card is cumulative ("Everything in Free", "Everything in Plus"), so a feature named at Pro is conventionally absent below. But that inference gives a direction, not a number: the reader cannot tell whether Free is one, two or four. The page's own house style is what convicts it. Every other ceiling on the Free card is stated with its number in the same breath — "4 shows a month — up to 200 people in the room at each", "Keep 2,000 songs — 50 live to the room at once". A card that is that precise about four limits and silent about the fifth reads as "there is no fifth limit". That is overstatement by omission, which is the status filed.

(4) Is the accuser applying a condition the page never implied? No, and the strongest evidence is internal to MySet: the Studio's plan sheet — the same product copy, for the same reader, one step further into the funnel — prints "One sign-in" in the Free column at studio.html:3518. Whoever wrote that card judged the limit worth naming to an artist. The marketing page does not name it. Same fact, two surfaces, one discloses and one does not.

Severity minor is correct and I would not raise it. Nothing false is asserted, no money changes hands on a misunderstanding (there is no checkout at all yet — about.html's third honest note says so), and the disappointment lands at the moment an artist tries to add a bandmate and gets a clear, honest 402 that names the real ceiling. It is a disclosure gap on a pricing card, not a lie.

Where I improve on the accuser: the omission is wider than the Free card. Plus is also `seats: 1` (_plan.mjs:89) and its card is equally silent, and the Studio names "One sign-in" in the Plus column too (studio.html:3532). Their single Free bullet does technically fix Plus through "Everything in Free", but relying on an inheritance chain for the one limit a paying band is most likely to assume they bought is thin. Two bullets, mirroring what the Studio already does, is the better fix.

I also found a bigger problem two lines above the proposed insertion point, which I have detailed in betterFix: about.html:606 sells setlists as a Free feature while admin.mjs:735-736 refuses to create one below Plus. That is a false claim on a pricing card, not an omission, and it deserves its own finding at a higher severity than this one.

2. Every card already carries an explicit "who it's for" line right under the badge, in the same voice: Free "About a gig a week, run properly" (:601), Plus "For when you're playing more than once a week..." (:617), Pro "For when you're working several towns" (:641). "most artists" is the compressed echo of the Plus one. The section frame is "What it costs" (:588) — the reader's question is which plan to pick, not who else is here.

3. The CSS at :213-215 renders it as an 11.5px uppercase accent-coloured eyebrow on the `.plan.hot` card. That is a badge, not a sentence.

4. Decisive on intent: git blame shows line 615 is original (d03c033) while line 617, the line directly below it, was rewritten by the honesty pass 565bb21 — the commit whose whole purpose was removing false claims from this page, driven by two outside analyses plus its own audit. That commit's diff shows the badge sitting untouched in the middle of an edited hunk, between two lines it did change. The accusation is also self-defeating on the page's own layout. Its strongest evidence — nobody has subscribed, there is no checkout — is what the page itself says in bold at :658-660, in the box rendered immediately beneath the three cards: "Plus and Pro can't be bought yet. There's no checkout, so nobody is being charged for anything." A reader who somehow read the badge as a subscriber count has that reading demolished before they leave the section. Two further points against the finding's weight. The Plus card's actual mechanism claims all check out against _plan.mjs:83-99 — gigs Infinity, audience 1000, cut 0.02, featured Infinity, pricing/setlists/merch/moderate all true, and none of those flags is in NOT_BUILT (:130). Rewriting a recommendation badge because the customer list is currently one person is the courtroom reflex he has already vetoed.

finding.claimText: For when you're playing more than once a week and want the night set up your way.
finding.evidence: The real threshold is four nights per UTC calendar month — netlify/functions/_plan.mjs:33 `gigs: 4`, bucketed by netlify/functions/_lib.mjs:131 `gigMonthOf` and refused at netlify/functions/_lifecycle.mjs:133-134. Four a month is LESS than once a week in every month, so an artist playing exactly weekly is blocked on their fifth night in any month containing five of that weekday, and averages 4.33 nights against a cap of 4. The sentence sets the upgrade point higher than the code does, so the artist who takes it at face value is refused mid-season.
finding.proposedFix: "For when you're playing more than four nights a month and want the night set up your way."

check.correctedStatus: ACCURATE — no change needed to line 617. (Severity of the original finding, if anything survived, would be minor/cosmetic, not major.)
check.correctedEvidence: /Users/perryidyll/Docs/MySet/public/about.html:601,603,617 · /Users/perryidyll/Docs/MySet/netlify/functions/_plan.mjs:33 (gigs: 4) · /Users/perryidyll/Docs/MySet/netlify/functions/_lib.mjs:131 (gigMonthOf = UTC yyyy-mm) · /Users/perryidyll/Docs/MySet/netlify/functions/_lifecycle.mjs:36,133-135 (CAP_REFUSAL, `used >= gigCap` → 402) · /Users/perryidyll/Docs/MySet/netlify/functions/_lifecycle.mjs:39-44 (gigCapFor) · /Users/perryidyll/Docs/MySet/public/studio.html:3510 ("4 shows a month")
check.reasoning:
The accuser's code citations are all correct — I confirmed each one personally. Free is capped at 4 shows per UTC calendar month (_plan.mjs:33), bucketed by gigMonthOf (_lib.mjs:131), and the 5th start is refused with a 402 (_lifecycle.mjs:133-135). No flag or alternate path lifts it; the only exemption is the platform owner (_lifecycle.mjs:41-43).

What fails is the arithmetic the accusation turns on. The cap is bucketed by CALENDAR MONTH, so the sentence has to be read over a month, and over a month the boundary lands exactly where the page puts it. A calendar month is 4.000 to 4.428 weeks. Four shows is therefore between 0.90 and 1.00 per week — never MORE than once a week, in any month, including a 28-day February where it is exactly once. Five shows is 5/4.428 = 1.13 per week at minimum — always more than once a week. So "more than once a week" and "the 5th show in a month" are the same threshold, not two different ones. The code does not set the bar lower than the sentence; they coincide.

The fixed-weekday artist the accuser describes does get refused in the ~4 months a year that contain five of their weekday — but in that month they played 5 nights in ~4.4 weeks, which IS more than once a week. Their yearly average of 4.33 is only relevant if the sentence promises annual averaging, and it doesn't; there is no averaging window in the copy, and the nearest one the page supplies is the month, named explicitly one column to the left.

Two more reasons the finding is weaker than stated. First, it audits the wrong sentence: line 617 is the Plus card's who-is-this-for line, not a statement of the free allowance. The free allowance is stated exactly, as the FIRST bullet on the adjacent Free card — "4 shows a month" (about.html:603) — and the same words appear in the Studio (studio.html:3510) and in the refusal itself, which names the number and says the allowance resets on the 1st (_lifecycle.mjs:36-37). Nobody reaches the 402 without having been shown "4 shows a month" at least twice. That is not an artist "refused mid-season" by a page that hid the number.

Second, the proposed fix makes the card worse: it describes the Plus plan by the Free plan's number, restates a limit already printed one column left, and trades a positioning line for an accounting line on the card meant to sell the upgrade.

One thing the accusation missed that is genuinely under-stated, and belongs to the code rather than the page: startShow counts a gig on the RESUME path too. _lifecycle.mjs:132 only short-circuits when the show is already `live`; a show that was Ended and then resumed ("Resume it instead", admin.mjs:1673 with fresh:false) falls through to countGig at :135 and burns a second night off the month. So an artist who taps End by mistake can reach the cap in fewer than four actual nights. That is a separate finding about lifecycle counting, not evidence that line 617 is wrong.
check.betterFix: Leave about.html:617 as written. If Perry ever wants to tighten the weekly gloss, the sentence to look at is the FREE card's line 601 — "About a gig a week, run properly, and you never pay us anything" — since that is the one inviting the weekly artist to stay free, and it is the one a fixed-weekday player will feel wrong four months a year. Even there it is hedged with "About" and immediately followed by the exact number, so a change is optional; the strongest available version would be "Four nights a month, run properly, and you never pay us anything." The real fix worth spending a change on is the code one: make the resume-after-End path in _lifecycle.mjs:132-135 a no-op for the counter (skip countGig when !fresh), so the free allowance is four NIGHTS rather than four start-taps.

And do not write "MySet takes 2%, Stripe takes 2.9%" as if they were the same kind of thing — MySet's is a percentage of the pack, Stripe's has a flat 30c that dominates on small packs (on a $2 pack Stripe takes ~36c, 18%).
check.reasoning:
I tried to refute this four ways and could not.

1. Is there another code path making the page true? No. I looked for the one that would: `splitFee` at _connect.mjs:83, which subtracts half of Stripe's estimated fee from MySet's cut. If artist plans set it, MySet would be absorbing half the card fee and "stay yours" would be closer to honest. They don't — _plan.mjs:64/87/97 define the artist rows with `cut` only; `splitFee: true` appears solely on the two venue rows at _venues.mjs:131-132. So for artists, MySet's fee and Stripe's fee are strictly additive.

2. Is the accuser reading a comment as behaviour? This was the strongest refutation available, since the quoted passage at _connect.mjs:31-35 is a prose comment. But the behaviour is in executable code, not the comment: pay.mjs:174 passes `stripeAccount: conn.acct` into `checkout.sessions.create`, which is what makes it a direct charge, and pay.mjs:181/209 add `application_fee_amount` separately. Direct charge = connected account pays Stripe's fee. The comment describes the code accurately.

3. Is the accuser applying a condition the page never implied? No — the page's own bullet is doing the implying. "stay yours" is not a hedge; it is an affirmative claim about what reaches the artist, sitting immediately after a percentage.

4. Is the sentence more carefully worded than noticed? The opposite. "2% cut instead of 10%" is precise about MySet and silent about everything else, which is exactly the shape that misleads.

The one real mitigation: the page's own honest note at :655-657 says card payments aren't on for anyone but the founder yet, so no artist is being paid out under a wrong expectation today. But pay.mjs:169-170 fails closed only until an artist completes Connect onboarding — the moment one does, this is live — and the plan cards are the purchase-decision surface regardless. That lowers present harm, not the severity of the copy. Severity stays major.

Where I'd correct the accuser: they framed this as a single-bullet defect at :630. It is a section-wide defect. Pro's "No cut at all — 0% on everything through the app" (:640) is more misleading than the Plus line, because 0% invites "I keep everything" with no counterweight anywhere on the page, and their proposed fix would have left it untouched.

I verified every code fact the accuser cites, and they are all true — but they do not add up to a discrepancy on the page.

WHAT IS TRUE IN CODE (I read all of it):
- netlify/functions/_plan.mjs:65 free seats:1, :89 plus seats:1, :107 pro seats:5.
- netlify/functions/auth.mjs:393-398 is the only seat gate: it counts existing rows in reg0.byEmail for the artist and refuses a new one at limits.seats with "Your plan allows one sign-in. Pro allows five." No other code path grants extra seats (grep for `seats` across netlify/functions/ returns only _plan.mjs, auth.mjs:395-398, and admin.mjs:402 shaping it for the client, plus two comments).
- public/studio.html:3510 and :3532 do put ['One sign-in',''] in the Free and Plus columns.
- "Five sign-ins" appears exactly once in about.html, at line 641, under Pro.

WHY THE ACCUSATION STILL FAILS:

1. The page makes no claim about seats at all — anywhere. There is no false sentence to correct. The finding is an omission-preference dressed as a discrepancy. about.html:604-612 (Free) is equally silent, so if this were an error it would be an error on two cards, not "the Plus card". It is a page-wide convention, consistently applied.

2. The cards are explicit DELTA lists, and the accuser is reading them as full inventories. about.html:620 "Everything in Free" and :638 "Everything in Plus" state the convention out loud. Every other Plus bullet is a thing you GAIN by paying. A seat count is not a gain at Plus, so its absence is the card working as designed. Conversely, Pro listing "Five sign-ins for your band" (about.html:641) as an addition to "Everything in Plus" is, under that stated convention, exactly the disclosure that extra sign-ins are what Pro buys you. The reader is not left with no signal; they are told seats arrive at Pro.

3. The claim "a band reading the Plus card has no way to know" applies a condition the page never sets up: that the about page is the buying surface. It is not. Money is committed in the Studio plan sheet — public/studio.html:3570-3574 renders the tier lists under the heading "Everything in each plan, listed in full" with the CTA (studio.html:3562-3568) in the same card, and startCheckout (studio.html:3580) is reached only from there. The Plus column in that sheet says "One sign-in" (studio.html:3532), directly above "Upgrade to Plus". Nobody can pay for Plus without the exact seat count in front of them. The claimed harm has no path to occur.

4. The finding misreads the page it is quoting. The Plus <ul> at about.html:619-631 contains NINE <li> items, not ten (I counted the block programmatically: Free 9, Plus 9, Pro 8). Minor, but it shows the card was not read closely before being called incomplete.

SOMETHING GENUINELY WORSE THAT I FOUND WHILE CHECKING (not my assigned finding, but it belongs in the same audit and it is a real page-vs-code contradiction, unlike this one): about.html's third honest note says "Plus and Pro can't be bought yet. There's no checkout, so nobody is being charged for anything." That is false in code. Stripe Billing is built and wired: netlify/functions/_billing.mjs (Checkout in subscription mode at :147, upgrades/downgrades/proration/retention), admin.mjs:78-83 action planCheckout, and public/studio.html:3579-3583 startCheckout redirecting to Stripe. A working checkout is one click from the Studio. That is a live, load-bearing false statement about money on the landing page, and it should outrank a missing bullet.

I tried to refute this and could only refute half of it.

SURVIVES (1) — Stripe's fee falls on the artist. This is real behaviour, not a comment read as behaviour. pay.mjs creates the session with `stripeAccount: conn.acct` (line 70, 173) and `application_fee_amount` (64, 209) — a direct charge, so Stripe's ~2.9%+30c comes off the connected account. I checked whether any code path softens it: `splitFee` (which subtracts half of Stripe's estimated fee from MySet's cut, _connect.mjs:83) is set ONLY in VENUE_PLANS (_venues.mjs:131-132). No artist row in PLANS has it. So an artist bears the whole card fee, and about.html:640's "No cut at all — 0% on everything through the app" is the sentence most likely to be misread as "you keep 100%". _connect.mjs:31-35 doesn't create the problem; it predicts it.

SURVIVES, AND IS WORSE THAN STATED (2) — the $10 Featured charge. FEAT_PRICE=1000 (_featured.mjs:40), flag default ON in code (_flags.mjs:38-49), and featureStart (admin.mjs:1452-1497) has NO plan gate — I looked for one specifically. studio.html:1366 draws "Promote a gig · $10" for every signed-in artist on every plan. That is a live Stripe Checkout on the platform account. The accuser files this as an undisclosed caveat; it is stronger than that. about.html:659 says "There's no checkout, so nobody is being charged for anything." That sentence is false as written, not merely incomplete. Note 2 survives untouched (Featured is the artist paying MySet, not taking money), but note 3 does not.

REFUTED (3) — seats. The page never implies more than one seat on Free or Plus. It names "Five sign-ins for your band" only in the Pro column (about.html:641), which is the ordinary way to signal that lower tiers have fewer, and auth.mjs:395's own error text ("Your plan allows one sign-in. Pro allows five.") agrees with the page. This is the accuser applying a condition the page never set.

REFUTED (4) — the gig cap window. The page says "4 shows a month". gigMonthOf (_lib.mjs:131) counts a calendar month, and _plan.mjs:21 says so in as many words. A calendar month IS what "a month" means; the accuser has imagined a rolling-four-weeks reading the page never offered. UTC vs the artist's local timezone shifts the reset by at most a few hours once a month — not a material caveat.

So the finding stands, but "at least three further material caveats" should be two, and the fix has to repair note 3 rather than only append a note 4.

Any signed-in artist can open the Studio today, pick a country from the 22-country allow-list, and be handed a live Stripe onboarding link. (3) "The sentence is more carefully worded than the accuser noticed." It is worded WORSE. "while the payouts plumbing gets built" is present-progressive — a thing still under construction — and the next clause states a consequence as a hard fact: "Until that's finished no other artist can take money through MySet." The accuser's proposed wording, "while payouts get switched on for everyone else", is an improvement but still wrong in mechanism: it implies MySet does the switching on some rollout schedule. check.reasoning:
I tried hard to break this finding and could not.

THE DEFENCE I TESTED FIRST, AND WHY IT FAILS. The best available refutation is contextual: line 657 sits at the end of note 2, whose subject is the card outage, so the sentence could be read narrowly as "the missing payments plumbing doesn't hold anything else up." That reading dies on the words "the moment you sign up." That clause is about the signup state, not about the card outage, and _auth.mjs:134 creates every new artist with plan:'free' — no comp, no trial, no grace period. I then looked for the strongest possible refutation, a runtime kill-switch on plan enforcement: _flags.mjs declares exactly two flags (voteFinal, featuredShows), neither touches plans, and flagValue returns false for any undeclared name. There is no code path that makes the sentence true.

THE FIVE GATES ARE REAL, NOT COMMENTS OR DOCS. I read each one in the handler, not in a doc: listNew 402 at admin.mjs:735-736; the pricing quartet (freeCredits/packs/replayCost/askSet) gated by limits.pricing at 1704-1706; postDelete 402 at 1288-1291 via moderateAllowed; toggleSong 402 against featured=50 at 1852-1856; the second sign-in 402 at auth.mjs:392-398. All five are server-side refusals, all five are listed on the Plus or Pro card inside the same section (lines 620-641), and none of them involves a card.

WHERE THE ACCUSER OVERREACHED — two of the eight items should be struck. (a) The verification tick does not belong in this finding. It is not listed in the pricing section at all; the only "verify" text on the page is line 577, which is inside the VENUES section (505-585) and says "Free. Your page works whether you verify it or not" — a true statement about a venue page still working unverified. The artist tick the accuser cites (studio.html:1174-1195, community.mjs:70) is never sold on this page, so it cannot make this sentence false. (b) The four unbuilt flags are already disclosed, in the very next sentence: they carry a "Soon" chip at lines 641-645 and note 3 says outright that they are "on the way, not shipped." Charging them against note 2 double-counts a disclosure the page already makes honestly. So the count is five, not ten.

WHERE THE ACCUSER UNDERREACHED, WHICH MATTERS MORE. Chasing the setlist gate turned up a bigger problem than the sentence under audit. _lists.mjs:39 starts every artist at lists: [], and admin.mjs:743 — inside the gated listNew — is the only line in the repo that ever pushes one. A Free artist therefore cannot obtain a setlist by any route. Yet line 606 sells "Setlists" as a FREE plan bullet, and the FAQ at 693-698 explains how to build one with no plan caveat at all. The comment at admin.mjs:731-734 rationalises the gate as protecting a downgraded artist's existing sets, which is true and humane, but it quietly conceals that a new free artist has none to protect. That is a false Free-plan bullet, which is a harder claim than a soft reassurance in the honesty block.

ON SEVERITY. I would say high rather than critical. The pricing cards immediately above are accurate about the ladder, and a reader going top-down sees "Plus $10/month — unlimited songs live at once, set your own vote rules, delete a post for good" before reaching line 657. Nobody is charged money on the strength of this sentence. But it is a plainly false statement sitting inside a block whose entire promise is "here is where the edges are," and combined with note 3 it points a reader at the specific wrong conclusion that the paid tier is open until billing ships. A false line in the honesty section costs more trust than the same line elsewhere, which is why I would not soften it below high.

check.reasoning:
The accusation stacks two other findings onto a sentence that does not make either claim, and the sentence's own claim checks out line by line.

WHAT THE SENTENCE ACTUALLY CLAIMS. Note 3 reads: "The four Pro extras marked Soon are on the way, not shipped; everything else listed above is built and running today." Its axis is built vs not-built. It is not a claim about who is entitled to what, and it is not a claim about what can be charged for — because the paragraph directly above it, note 2 (about.html:654-657), already carves the money out: "Until that's finished no other artist can take money through MySet."

LEG 1 OF THE ACCUSATION (the money bullets) IS SELF-REFUTING. The accuser concedes "Note 2 discloses the money half." Three bullets are named — price your own vote packs, merch paid straight to you, the 2% cut. All three are built: pricing at admin.mjs:1705-1709, merch CRUD at admin.mjs:1213-1236, the 2% as a Stripe application_fee at _plan.mjs:83-86. What canTakeMoney (_pay.mjs:52-54) withholds is the ability to CHARGE A CARD, which is exactly and only what note 2 says is missing, eleven pixels higher, inside the same block of honest notes, which a reader reaches in order 1-2-3. A built feature that cannot yet take a card is precisely the state note 2 describes. Charging note 3 as critically false for a thing note 2 discloses is double-counting one disclosure gap as two findings.

LEG 2 (setlists) IS A DEFECT AT A DIFFERENT LINE. Setlists ARE built and running today — admin.mjs:731-736 gates only listNew, and the surrounding comment plus every other list action (listRename, listAll) confirm the feature is live; test/limits.mjs:162-166 asserts in the repo's own suite that setlists and pricing are the two flags that ARE built and are deliberately kept out of NOT_BUILT. So note 3's sentence is TRUE of setlists. What is false is putting "Setlists" in the Free column at about.html:606. Fixing line 660 does not fix that; fixing line 606 does. The accuser's own proposed remedy admits this — it ends "(And fix line 606, per pricing-15, so the sentence becomes true.)" A finding whose fix is another finding's fix is not an independent finding.

I ALSO CHECKED THE SENTENCE ON ITS OWN TERMS, bullet by bullet, looking for anything unmarked that is genuinely not built. Nothing survived. NOT_BUILT holds exactly four flags (_plan.mjs:130) and the page marks exactly four Pro bullets "Soon" (about.html:642-645) — a 1:1 match, and test/limits.mjs:147 pins that list. The two bullets most likely to be vapour both turned out real: Pro's "Five sign-ins for your band" is enforced at auth.mjs:395-398, and Plus's oddly specific "if more turn up the night still runs; it just refreshes a little slower and shows the top of the board" is implemented as documented at show.mjs:33-45. So the page's built/not-built line is drawn exactly where the code draws it.

WHERE THE REAL SECOND PROBLEM IS, AND THE ACCUSER WALKED PAST IT. Note 2 ends (about.html:657): "Everything that doesn't involve a card works the moment you sign up." That sentence IS false, and on the accuser's own entitlement axis. A free artist who signs up this minute cannot create a setlist (admin.mjs:735), cannot set their own prices (admin.mjs:1706), cannot add a merch item (admin.mjs:1226), and cannot delete a post for good (admin.mjs:1291). Not one of those four involves a card. That is a sharper, correctly-located finding than the one filed against line 660 — and it is the sentence a free artist would actually rely on. So the block does have a truth problem; it is one line up from where the accuser pointed, and it needs its own fix rather than a rewrite of a sentence that is already right.

WHAT I VERIFIED MYSELF

1. The gate is real and there is exactly one creation path. netlify/functions/admin.mjs:730 `if (action === 'listNew')`, then admin.mjs:735-736: `if (!isPlatformOwner(aid) && (await planForArtist(aid)).limits.setlists !== true) return bad('Separate setlists are a Plus feature — everything you already have keeps working.', 402)`. netlify/functions/_plan.mjs:67 sets `setlists: false` on free; _plan.mjs:154 `isPlatformOwner = (aid) => aid === DEFAULT_ARTIST` — Perry only, not a general path. I grepped for every writer that can add a set: `grep -rn "lists.push\|listNew"` returns admin.mjs:743 (inside the gated `listNew` branch) and public/studio.html:625 (the client calling it). There is no second route. `emptyLists()` at _lists.mjs:39 returns `{ v: 1, lists: [] }`, so nobody is seeded with one either. A brand-new free artist can create zero named setlists.

2. The app itself is honest — which makes the landing page the outlier. studio.html:616 wraps the "+ New setlist" button in `lock('setlists', …, 'Sets you already have keep working.')`, with a comment at 614-615 saying plainly "The server refuses this on free." The Studio's own plan table lists 'Separate setlists', one active per night, applied from your calendar' under Plus (studio.html:3524) and Pro (3538) — and NOT under Free. The downgrade warning at studio.html:3705 says "you couldn't make new setlists". admin.mjs:398 ships `setlists: !!l.setlists` to the client "so the Studio can say so BEFORE the server refuses."

3. THE FINDING IS WORSE AND WIDER THAN STATED. The accuser found the third of three problems and called it minor. The primary defect is in the pricing card, not the FAQ:
   - about.html:606, in the FREE plan card, unchipped: "Setlists, chord charts, keys and genres". Compare the Studio's equivalent free row, studio.html:3512: "The song sheet: chord charts, keys and genres". The landing page swapped the honest phrase "The song sheet" for the word "Setlists" — turning a truthful item into a direct free-plan feature claim that _plan.mjs:67 contradicts. That is a stronger, plainer contradiction than the FAQ's.
   - about.html:619-631, the Plus card, never mentions setlists at all. So the Plus column cannot correct the Free column, and a reader has no way to learn from the pricing section that separate setlists are paid. The Studio's Plus list does carry it (3524); the landing page dropped it.
   - about.html:695-698, the FAQ, then teaches the reader to do the one gated thing: "build a setlist instead — name it, put the songs you want in it". That is `listNew` exactly. Everything else in that sentence checks out: "keep twenty of them" matches MAX_LISTS = 20 (_lists.mjs:29), and gig-attach is real (studio.html:1721-1730).

REFUTATION ANGLES I TESTED AND REJECTED
   - "Setlist" is overloaded in the Studio (the Setlist tab is the song library, studio.html:1969 "Your setlist — X of Y featured"), so about.html:606 could arguably mean the library. I don't accept it as a defence: the Studio's own free row calls that same thing "The song sheet", and about.html:606 sits next to a separate line (608) already covering the library ("Keep 2,000 songs — 50 live to the room at once"). And the FAQ at 695-698 is unambiguous regardless — naming it and keeping twenty is the gated feature.
   - Downgrade grace doesn't rescue it: rename/delete/edit/use are all ungated (admin.mjs:751-780), so an artist who once paid keeps working. That is precisely why the code's own message says "everything you already have keeps working" — it is a grace clause for lapsed payers, not availability for a new free artist.
   - Owner bypass covers one account.

THE SECONDARY CLAIM (starter pack) DOES NOT SURVIVE. I read the handler: admin.mjs:1972-1983 appends the ~60 starter covers to the library and sets `active` only while `live < featureCap` (featureCap from _plan.mjs `featured`, resolved at admin.mjs:1694-1697). So all sixty are added, fifty go live, and the rest sit inactive — which is literally "add in one tap and edit down". And the page does disclose the ceiling, in the free card at about.html:608: "Keep 2,000 songs — 50 live to the room at once". Asking the FAQ to repeat a limit the pricing card two sections up states in plain numbers is applying a condition the page never implied. Drop that one to NOT AN ISSUE.

ON THE KICKER ITSELF. "Straight answers" at about.html:667 is a section header, not a claim about a feature. The accuser's own proposed fix (leave the kicker, fix what's underneath) is the right shape — I'd keep it. But the defect underneath should not be filed as minor.

check.reasoning:
I confirmed the accuser's MECHANISM but I refute the VERDICT. The finding is real as a fact and dead as a discrepancy, because the accuser stopped reading two lines too early.

WHAT I VERIFIED MYSELF (all read in the files, not in docs):
1. Only three codes exist. studio.html:2991-2993 offers exactly `profile` and `home`; venue-studio.html:1522-1523 offers exactly `venue`. qr.mjs:18-24 is the only generator, and it is a fixed KINDS map — no free-text encoding. `vote` still resolves (qr.mjs:22) but nothing in public/ ever requests it: the only two callers of /api/qr are studio.html:2995 and venue-studio.html:1526, both feeding them from those QRS tables.
2. stage.html contains no QR and no /vote link at all (grep for "qr" and "/vote" returns nothing), so the big screen is not a second path either.
3. The scan therefore lands on artist.html. It has no inline voting — I grepped for vote(, /api/vote, castVote, data-act="vote" in artist.html: zero hits. Voting lives behind two links to VOTEHREF (artist.html:266, 389, 406).
4. There is no auto-forward. No location.replace and no location.href assignment anywhere in artist.html.
So yes: scan, page, tap, vote. The accuser's four steps are correct.

WHY THE FINDING STILL FAILS: the accuser quoted line 672 and did not read line 674 of the same FAQ answer. The answer's own thesis sentence is: 'because anything more than "scan and tap" doesn't happen in a bar.' The page names the tap, in the same paragraph, in quotation marks, as the design standard it is claiming to meet. A reader cannot come away from that answer believing there is no tap — the tap is the thing the answer is bragging about. Line 672 is a compressed lead-in to a sentence that is exactly right.

AND THE ANSWER'S ACTUAL CLAIMS ARE ALL TRUE. The question is "Do my fans have to download anything?" The four load-bearing claims — no app, no account, no email, no password — I checked in vote.html: the fan is minted anonymously client-side (vote.html:287-289, a random id in localStorage), and I grepped vote.html for prompt / nickname / "Your name" / consent / cookie / onboarding — nothing. The accuser is right that there is no gate. So the answer is not overstating anything a fan would actually experience; it is describing a three-beat feeling, not counting taps.

I also checked whether the problem was WIDER and it is not. The other two places about.html describes the scan are clean: line 322 ("the same room, with one QR code on the tables") and the beat headline at 373 ("They scan, and they're in") make no step-count claim at all.

The remaining residue is that "a web page opens" is vaguer than it needs to be — the page that opens is the artist's own page, which is a nicer fact than the sentence currently tells. That is an upgrade opportunity, not a discrepancy. It also runs straight into Perry's standing rule that framing is his when the mechanism under it is true. I would flag it once and leave it.

check.reasoning:
The accusation does not survive, on three separate grounds, and its own counter-evidence is factually wrong.

1. It is not a claim the audit is entitled to grade. Line 674 is a subordinate "because" clause explaining WHY a design decision was made. The claim in that FAQ answer is the question's answer — "Do my fans have to download anything? No — and they never will... No app, no account, no email, no password" — and that claim is verifiably TRUE in code: the fan page derives the room from the URL path (public/vote.html:280-281), mints an anonymous id into localStorage with no input from the person (public/vote.html:287-290), and there is no auth path on it at all; auth exists only for the Studio (netlify/functions/_auth.mjs:5, INVARIANTS.md:328). A rationale for a true claim is not a discrepancy.

2. The "codebase repeating the same belief" point is backwards. public/sw.js:35 and INVARIANTS.md:328 are not the page's source — they are three independent places where the same rule is enforced in shipped behaviour (no push to fans, no fan sign-in, no install). The page is not citing a comment as evidence; the comment and the page are both describing a constraint the code actually honours.

3. The internal-contradiction point is arithmetically wrong in both directions. The accuser says the real flow is "scan, page, tap, vote", so the product sits one tap outside its own standard. But (a) "a web page opens" is not a user step — the browser does it, and the page says so in the immediately preceding sentence, so no reader is misled about the flow; and (b) the accuser undercounted the real taps: voting opens a sheet (public/vote.html:412-423) and requires a second tap on Confirm (public/vote.html:479 → :506). So their reconstruction of the flow is both padded with a non-action and missing a real action. Counter-evidence that is wrong twice cannot downgrade the sentence.

4. The sentence is more carefully worded than the accuser noticed. "scan and tap" sits in scare quotes on the page — it is an explicit shorthand label for the friction class, and the sentence right before it defines that class in literal terms: no app, no account, no email, no password. "Anything more than 'scan and tap'" plainly means anything more than that class of friction, not a tap count. Reading it as a step-count contract applies a condition the page never sets.

The nearest thing to a real observation here — that the product is technically two taps, not one — is a point the accuser did not actually make and that does not bite anyway, because the page never counts taps and does describe the flow honestly one line earlier. Per the standing calibration on Perry's copy (mechanism literal, framing is his), this is framing over a true mechanism.

check.reasoning:
The accusation is built on a truncated quotation and does not survive reading the whole element.

1. THE QUOTE IS CUT MID-PARAGRAPH. The accuser quotes about.html:677 and stops at the full stop. The actual FAQ answer (about.html:676-679, one <div class="a">) reads: "Then you play what you were going to play anyway and nothing is worse than before. In practice one table starts, the rest see them doing it, and it spreads. On the first real gig it ran, eight people voted twenty-one times in a room that had no idea it existed an hour earlier." The generalisation is qualified by its own next clause, which names the sample as one gig. The page never claims or implies a multi-night basis.

2. THE ACCUSER'S OWN EVIDENCE IS THE PAGE AGREEING WITH THEM. They cite about.html:652-653 ("It has run one real gig") as proof the page is wrong. That line is the page voluntarily disclosing the exact fact they say it conceals — and it does it twice, at :652 and again 25 lines later at :678. A page cannot overstate a sample it names twice.

3. THE PROPOSED FIX IS A NO-OP. Their replacement ("On the one night it has run, one table started... eight people voted twenty-one times") is a near-paraphrase of what already stands. It swaps "on the first real gig it ran" for "on the one night it has run" — same disclosure, same numbers — while collapsing the mechanism into the anecdote, which loses information rather than adding honesty.

4. THE MECHANISM IS BUILT AND LIVE, NOT INFERRED FROM ONE NIGHT. "The rest see them doing it, and it spreads" describes shipped behaviour I traced in code. public/vote.html:1122 selects the poll signature: `const sig = FLOOR > 3000 ? stageSig() : signature();`. FLOOR is 3000 by default (:1045) and only rises when the server widens the interval for a large room (:323). So below that threshold every phone uses signature() (:1074), which includes d.totalVotes — meaning one person's vote redraws the board and resets the poll rung on every other phone in the room, immediately. The authors' own comment at :1056-1058 states that crowd acceleration was deliberately kept for small rooms because "in a pub with eight people — where the tally jumping the instant somebody votes IS the product." The sentence describes an engineered, currently-running product behaviour that the one gig then illustrated.

5. THE ACCUSER APPLIES A CONDITION THE PAGE NEVER SET. Reading "in practice" as a claim of statistical frequency across many gigs is the accuser's import. In context it introduces a described mechanism, immediately followed by the single instance evidencing it. Per Perry's standing calibration, framing is his where the mechanism under it is true; here the mechanism is true in code.

The one thing I could not personally verify is the blob-store show list (peakVoters/totalVotes per hist_ key) — I have no read access to production from here. It does not matter: the accuser's single-gig premise is conceded by the page itself and corroborated by MYSET.md:67-69, and the page's wording is already consistent with it. Nothing about the finding is worse or wider than stated; it simply does not hold.
check.betterFix: No fix needed — leave about.html:676-679 exactly as it stands. If anything is touched at all it should be a pure style nit, not a truth fix, and I would argue against even that: the current wording separates the mechanism ("one table starts, the rest see them doing it") from the evidence ("on the first real gig it ran, eight people voted twenty-one times"), which is more informative and more honest than the proposed merge. There IS a bulk import: public/studio.html:1963 renders '⇪ Import songs — CSV, text or Spotify', handled by `openImport()` at :3053 and by `importSongs` at netlify/functions/admin.mjs:1885-1910, which takes up to 300 rows at once. The typing half is accurate — `addSong` (admin.mjs:1862-1878) does no synchronous lookup; genre and lyric enrichment are separate explicit actions (admin.mjs:989, :1001).
finding.proposedFix: "Adding songs takes as long as typing them — or import a CSV, paste a list, or pull one in from a Spotify playlist."

check.reasoning:
The accusation collapses on three counts, and its own wording gives the game away.

1. THE STATUS LABEL IS WRONG. "OVERSTATED" means the page claims more than the code delivers. The accuser writes, in their own finding, "Understates the product rather than overselling it." Nothing here is overstated. Every assertion in the sentence is code-true: `addSong` (netlify/functions/admin.mjs:1862-1878) trims the title, checks the library cap, and pushes — no network call, no lookup, nothing synchronous to wait on. Genre and lyric enrichment are separate explicit actions. The typing claim is exactly right.

2. THE ACCUSER QUOTED HALF A SENTENCE. The finding cites "Adding songs takes as long as typing them" and stops at the comma. The actual line at public/about.html:701-702 reads: "Adding songs takes as long as typing them, and there's a starter pack of around sixty well-known covers you can add in one tap and edit down." The page therefore does NOT tell the reader that typing is the only route — it hands them a one-tap bulk path in the very same breath. And that half is code-true too: STARTER_SONGS in netlify/functions/_lib.mjs:47 holds exactly 62 entries (I counted the rows), appended by the `starterSetlist` handler at admin.mjs:1972-1984. "Around sixty" is honest. The alleged misimpression — reader thinks they must type every song one by one — is not one this sentence can create.

3. THE SENTENCE IS ANSWERING A DIFFERENT QUESTION. It sits inside the FAQ "How long does setting up actually take?" (about.html:700). It is a TIME estimate for a brand-new free signup, not an inventory of every route into the song library. Applying a completeness test to a duration answer is a condition the page never invited.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE: the import feature is real and I confirmed it end to end. The button is at public/studio.html:1963, ungated — it sits in the plain setlist tab with no plan check around it. `openImport()` at studio.html:3058 parses a CSV file, pasted text, or a public Spotify playlist (via `spotifyPeek`), caps the client-side parse at 300 rows (studio.html:3081), and `importSongs` at admin.mjs:1885-1910 re-validates and applies the same rules as a single add. And about.html mentions import NOWHERE — I grepped for import/csv/spotify/paste across the whole file and the only hits are a CSS comment and unrelated body copy. So a real, free-tier feature is absent from the marketing page. That is a genuine observation. But it is an omission from the feature inventory, not a defect in this sentence, and it is not "OVERSTATED."

ONE THING THE ACCUSER'S FIX WOULD MAKE WORSE. Free plan `featured` is 50 (netlify/functions/_plan.mjs:20). An import of up to 300 rows lands with everything past the 50th live song switched OFF — admin.mjs:1902-1908 sets `active: !startsOff` and the note reads "N arrived switched off (your plan features 50 at a time)". The proposed clause bolts "or import a CSV, paste a list, or pull one in from a Spotify playlist" onto the answer aimed specifically at the free two-minute signup, with no mention of that cap. It trades a sentence that is currently true for one that sets a free reader up for a surprise. Their fix is riskier than the copy it replaces.

WIDER LEAD, WORSE THAN THIS ONE (flagging, not claiming — different line, out of my scope): the Free plan card at about.html:605 bullets "Setlists, chord charts, keys and genres" as free, but `setlists: false` on free (_plan.mjs:67) and admin.mjs:735-736 refuses creating a named setlist with "Separate setlists are a Plus feature", 402. That is a real overstatement direction, on the pricing table, where it costs more. Worth its own pass.
check.correctedStatus: ACCURATE — not a discrepancy. The sentence is code-true in both halves. Downgrade to a separate, lower-priority COVERAGE GAP against the Free plan feature list (bulk import is unmentioned anywhere on about.html), severity minor, and drop the "OVERSTATED" label entirely — the accuser's own text says it understates.
check.correctedEvidence: public/about.html:700-702 (full FAQ answer, including the one-tap starter-pack clause the accusation omitted); netlify/functions/admin.mjs:1862-1878 (addSong — no synchronous lookup); netlify/functions/_lib.mjs:47 + admin.mjs:1972-1984 (62 starter songs, appended not replaced — "around sixty" verified); public/studio.html:1963 and :3058-3113 + netlify/functions/admin.mjs:1885-1910 (import is real and ungated); netlify/functions/_plan.mjs:20 and admin.mjs:1902-1908 (free featured cap 50 — why the proposed fix is risky); public/about.html:602-611 (Free plan bullets — where import is actually missing)
check.betterFix:
Leave about.html:701 alone. It is true, it is short, and it already gives the reader a bulk shortcut. If Perry wants import surfaced, put it where a reader is shopping for capability, not in a how-long-does-it-take answer — one bullet in the Free plan list at about.html:602-611, beside "Setlists, chord charts, keys and genres":
  • Import your whole list at once — a CSV, a pasted block of titles, or a public Spotify playlist
    • That is accurate (studio.html:1963 is ungated; admin.mjs:1885 has no plan check), it earns its place in a list whose job is enumerating features, and it costs the FAQ nothing. The neighbouring bullet already discloses "Keep 2,000 songs — 50 live to the room at once", so the free cap is stated once, in the right place, instead of being glossed over inside a setup-time answer.

finding.claimText: you can add in one tap
finding.evidence: It is two taps. public/studio.html:1954 wraps the action in a native dialog — `onclick="if(confirm('Add around 60 well-known covers to your setlist? Nothing you already have is touched.'))act('starterSetlist')"` — so the artist taps the button, then OK. Nothing follows after that: netlify/functions/admin.mjs:1972-1983 writes the songs in one pass with no further prompt.
finding.proposedFix: "…a starter pack of around sixty well-known covers you can add in a couple of taps and edit down."

check.correctedStatus: CONFIRMED but trivial — a literal-precision nit, not an overstatement of what the product does. Severity cosmetic, and the weakest class of finding: the mechanism the sentence describes (no typing, one button, ~57 songs appended in a single pass, nothing existing touched) is completely true. Only the tap count is off by the confirmation dialog. Under Perry's own "this isn't a courtroom" rule — never rewrite his framing when the mechanism under it is true — this is flag-once, his call, not a must-fix.
check.correctedEvidence: public/about.html:702 ("covers you can add in one tap and edit down"); public/studio.html:1954 — the ONLY starter-pack control in the whole app, `onclick="if(confirm('Add around 60 well-known covers to your setlist? Nothing you already have is touched.'))act('starterSetlist')"`; public/studio.html:946-957 `act()` posts once and re-renders, no further prompt; netlify/functions/admin.mjs:1972-1983 appends in one pass and returns; netlify/functions/_lib.mjs:47 STARTER_SONGS = 57 entries, so "around sixty" is accurate; netlify/functions/_plan.mjs:133 MAX_LIBRARY = 2000, so nothing is truncated.
check.betterFix:
Do NOT use "in a couple of taps" — it counts taps out loud, reads as an apology, and makes the sentence worse than the fact it fixes. If it changes at all: "…and there's a starter pack of around sixty well-known covers you can add in one go and edit down." Same cadence, same punch, and it survives the confirm dialog (and any future styled modal) instead of breaking again the moment the button changes.

I checked every escape hatch and none saves "one tap": there is no second starter-pack path (grep for starterSetlist across public/ and netlify/ returns exactly one caller), no onboarding auto-seed (DEFAULT_ARTIST at _lib.mjs:118 is a slug, not a song template), and no plan gate that would make it more taps either (admin.mjs:1694 only computes the feature cap for this action).

Two things I found that are WIDER than the accusation, both in the app rather than the landing page, so out of this audit's scope but worth logging:
1. public/studio.html:1967 — the empty-state row tells a brand-new artist to "tap Add the starter pack at the bottom". The button is labelled "+ Starter pack" and sits at the TOP of the setlist tab (line 1954). Wrong label, wrong place, and it is shown to exactly the person who has never seen the screen before.
2. netlify/functions/admin.mjs:1972-1983 — the free plan features 50 songs (_plan.mjs featured: 50) and the pack is 57, so a free artist gets 50 live and 7 silently switched off. The single-song path sets an explanatory note for this (admin.mjs:844, "Added, but switched off — your plan features N at a time"); the starter-pack path sets none. The artist is never told why seven songs arrived dark. That is a real gap, and unlike the tap count it can actually confuse someone.
check.reasoning:
I opened both files rather than trusting the accusation. The confirm() wrapper is real and unconditional (public/studio.html:1954), it is the only starter-pack control in the app, and nothing follows the OK — admin.mjs:1972-1983 writes the songs in one pass. So a person genuinely taps twice: the button, then OK. The accuser is not reading a comment as behaviour and not applying a condition the page never implied; the page's sentence is not more carefully hedged than they noticed ("in one tap" is a bare numeric claim).

But the finding is as small as a finding gets, and I want to be clear about that rather than let it be scored alongside real problems. The sentence's job is to answer "how long does setting up take?" — its claim is that you do not type sixty songs, you press a button. That claim is exactly true. A native OS confirmation is a safety net, not effort or data entry, and the page makes no promise about dialogs. Nobody buys, skips, or misjudges MySet because of it.

So: not refuted, but the proposed fix is worse than the problem. "A couple of taps" is the kind of edit Perry vetoed on 2026-09-06 — it defends against a charge nobody made and drains the line. "In one go" is accurate, keeps the rhythm, and does not re-break if the confirm is ever replaced by a styled modal (which would still be two taps).

The genuinely more useful output of this check is the pair of app-side issues above — particularly the seven silently-deactivated songs on the free plan, which is a real user-facing gap that the single-song path already handles and this path does not.

finding.claimText: [starter pack presented with no plan or limit caveat]
finding.evidence: A free artist who taps the starter pack gets 62 songs of which only 50 go live. netlify/functions/_plan.mjs:20 sets `featured: 50` on the free row, and netlify/functions/admin.mjs:1976-1981 applies it inside the starter loop — `const on = featureCap === null || live < featureCap;` then `push({ ..., active: on })` — so the last twelve arrive switched off and invisible to the room. Unlike `addSong` (admin.mjs:1880) and `importSongs` (:1910), the `starterSetlist` case sets NO note, so the server says nothing about it; the artist only finds out from the running total at public/studio.html:1966. The page does state the ceiling, but a hundred lines away in the Free column (about.html:610, 'Keep 2,000 songs — 50 live to the room at once'), not here.
finding.proposedFix: "Adding songs takes as long as typing them — or import a CSV, paste a list, or pull one in from a Spotify playlist. There's also a starter pack of around sixty well-known covers you can add in a couple of taps and edit down. Free shows fifty of your songs to the room at a time, so the last few arrive switched off until you swap something out."

check.reasoning: The accuser's code reading is accurate but the page-level conclusion does not follow. Three independent reasons the finding fails as a landing-page discrepancy: 1. THE SENTENCE MAKES NO FALSE CLAIM. about.html:701-702 says "there's a starter pack of around sixty well-known covers you can add in one tap and edit down." STARTER_SONGS (_lib.mjs:47-105) is 62 entries — "around sixty" is right. All 62 ARE added: admin.mjs:1976-1981 pushes every one into show.songs; the featureCap only sets active:false, and an inactive song is still in the library, still editable, still counted toward MAX_LIBRARY. The only thing that refuses a row is the 2,000 library ceiling (admin.mjs:1976), which 62 songs never hits. "OVERSTATED" requires the page to claim something the code doesn't do; nothing here qualifies. This is an omitted-caveat claim wearing an overstatement label. 2. THE PAGE ALREADY STATES THE CEILING, ON THE SAME PAGE, AND STATES IT CORRECTLY. about.html:610 (Free plan card): "Keep 2,000 songs — 50 live to the room at once." Verified: _plan.mjs:20 featured: 50, _plan.mjs:133 MAX_LIBRARY = 2000. about.html is one continuous page; the pricing table is 91 lines above the FAQ answer, not on some other URL. A plan limit belongs in the plan table. Requiring every FAQ answer to re-state it is a standard the page never invited. 3. THE SENTENCE'S OWN FRAMING PRE-EMPTS THE SURPRISE. "edit down" tells the reader the pack is deliberately more than they will keep. The complaint is that twelve songs arrive already off — i.e. twelve fewer to edit down. That is not a broken promise; it is the promise, pre-applied. The accuser's own strongest supporting fact also cuts the other way. They cite studio.html:1966 as where "the artist only finds out." That line renders PERMANENTLY for every free artist — shapeLimits (admin.mjs:393-395) passes featured: 50 through untouched, so the truthiness guard passes — and it reads "50 of 50 featured. Keep as many as you like (up to 2000) — your plan shows 50 to fans at a time. The rest sit switched off." It sits two elements below the "+ Starter pack" button in the same Setlist tab (button at studio.html:1953-1955, caption at 1965-1966). The twelve off songs then render with class "off" and the status word "Hidden" in the list at studio.html:1985. So the disclosure is adjacent to the control, permanent, and per-song — not a buried running total. WHAT IS GENUINELY TRUE AND WORTH KEEPING: admin.mjs:1974-1984 is the only add path that sets no note. addSong sets one at :1880 and importSongs at :1910. syncActive (admin.mjs:36-38) returns null on success, so nothing backfills it. That is a real server-side inconsistency — but it is a Studio polish item, not a marketing-copy defect, and it does not make any sentence on about.html untrue. The only defensible copy nit is unrelated to the plan cap: the button is wrapped in a confirm() dialog (studio.html:1954), so "one tap" is really two. The accuser's own proposed fix quietly corrects this to "a couple of taps" without flagging it. That is worth taking; the plan-cap paragraph they bolt on after it is not — it repeats about.html:610 inside an answer about setup time, and Perry's standing landing-page discipline is against padding an answer with a limit already stated in the plan table.
check.correctedStatus: ACCURATE (page copy). Downgrade from OVERSTATED/minor to NOT A PAGE DISCREPANCY. Reclassify the surviving substance as a separate non-landing-page code nit: "starterSetlist is the only song-add path that returns no note when rows arrive switched off (admin.mjs:1974-1984 vs :1880 and :1910)."
check.correctedEvidence: public/about.html:701-702 (the sentence — every claim true); public/about.html:610 ("Keep 2,000 songs — 50 live to the room at once", the caveat, same page); netlify/functions/_plan.mjs:20 (featured: 50) and :133 (MAX_LIBRARY = 2000, so :610 is exact); netlify/functions/_lib.mjs:47-105 (62 starter songs = "around sixty"); netlify/functions/admin.mjs:1976-1981 (all 62 pushed to show.songs; cap sets active:false, never refuses); netlify/functions/admin.mjs:393-395 (shapeLimits passes featured: 50 to the Studio unchanged); public/studio.html:1953-1955 (starter-pack button) and :1965-1966 (the permanent "50 of 50 featured … the rest sit switched off" caption two elements below it); public/studio.html:1985 (off songs render as "Hidden"); netlify/functions/admin.mjs:36-38 (syncActive returns null on success — confirms no note is backfilled).
check.betterFix:
Leave about.html:701-702 substantively as written. The only change worth making is a one-word accuracy fix, because the button is behind a confirm() dialog (studio.html:1954):

  "Adding songs takes as long as typing them, and there's a starter pack of around sixty well-known covers you can add in a couple of taps and edit down."

Do NOT append the plan-cap sentence the accuser proposes. It restates about.html:610 inside an answer about how long setup takes, adds a limit to a paragraph whose job is to lower friction, and is the kind of padding Perry's landing-page discipline exists to prevent.

The real fix belongs in the server, and it is a one-line change that brings the third add path in line with the other two. In netlify/functions/admin.mjs, in the starterSetlist case (1974-1984), count the rows that arrived off and set the note importSongs already sets at :1910 — e.g. track an `off` counter alongside `live`, then after the loop: if (off) note = `Added — ${off} arrived switched off (your plan features ${featureCap} at a time)`. File that as a Studio nit, not a landing-page finding.

finding.claimText: Find live music near you
finding.evidence: There is no 'near you'. public/index.html has no geolocation of any kind — `navigator.geolocation` appears zero times. It is a manual country-then-city picker (index.html:264-265, :316-325) whose selection is remembered in localStorage (:329-335) and passed to /api/events as `?country=&city=` (:402). And there is almost nothing to find: the live city index is one country, one city, one artist — {"Thailand": {"Koh Phangan": ["perry-idyll"]}}. A reader anywhere else gets index.html:407, 'Nothing on in X this week'.
finding.proposedFix: "See what's on, city by city" — or, if the aspiration should stay in the H1 on the home page itself, make the footer link read "What's on".

check.correctedStatus: ACCURATE — no change needed on about.html
check.correctedEvidence: public/about.html:723 (footer nav link) vs public/index.html:24 (<title>MySet — live music near you</title>), :251 (H1 "Live music near you."), :21-22 (meta/og), and index.html:322-325, :329-335, :359, :307-309, :407; netlify/functions/events.mjs:27-31; netlify/functions/_events.mjs:165-200
check.betterFix: Leave public/about.html:723 as it is. The proposed "See what's on, city by city" is worse: it is clunkier, and it breaks the match between the link label and the name of the page it opens. If anyone ever wants the mechanism to catch up with the word, that is a feature request on index.html (offer a "use my location" prefill for the country/city combos), not a copy edit on the landing page — and it would have to be made alongside index.html:21, :22, :24, :251, artist.html:373, venue.html:310 and community.html:255, which all use the same phrase.
check.reasoning: Three independent reasons the finding fails. 1. It is not a marketing claim; it is a nav link labelled with its destination's own name. about.html:723 is inside the `foot2` block — `Find live music near you · Artist Studio · Venue Studio`. The other two labels are literally the names of their destinations. So is this one: the page at `/` is titled "MySet — live music near you" (index.html:24), its og:title is the same (index.html:22), its meta description opens with it (index.html:21) and its H1 is "Live music near you." (index.html:251). A footer link that names its target by the target's own title cannot be an overstatement by the target. 2. "Near you" never implied geolocation. The accuser applied a condition the page never set — reading a plain locality idiom ("gigs near you", as every listings site uses it) as a promise of `navigator.geolocation`. The page's claim is about the RESULT (music in your area), and the result is delivered: you say which city you are in, and the feed returns gigs in that city (events.mjs city-feed branch). I confirmed there is no geolocation anywhere in the repo — `grep -rn geolocation public/ netlify/` exits 1 — so the accuser's raw fact is right and their inference from it is wrong. Note also index.html:329-335: on a repeat visit the remembered country/city auto-fire `search()` on load, so the second visit genuinely does open on what is near you with no picker at all. 3. The "almost nothing to find" half is a content observation, not a copy defect, and its stated failure mode is not reachable. The accuser says a reader anywhere else "gets index.html:407, 'Nothing on in X this week'." They cannot. The city combobox is fed only from the live index (index.html:322-325 — `getItems` maps `PLACES.countries.find(...).cities`), and `#go` is enabled only when `CHOSEN.city` is set by picking one of those items (`(v)=>{ CHOSEN.city=v; $('#go').disabled=!v; }`, :325). Typing a city that is not in the index yields "Nothing matching “…”" (:359) and leaves Search disabled — no search runs, so :407 never renders. index.html:407 is reachable only for a city that IS listed but has no gigs in the next seven days. A reader in Paris sees a country list that does not contain France, with a live gig count beside every entry; if the index is empty entirely they get "No gigs listed yet / MySet is brand new" (index.html:307-309). events.mjs:27-29 says this is deliberate: keep a place listed "with the count, so the emptiness is visible before they commit." The {"Thailand": {"Koh Phangan": ["perry-idyll"]}} snapshot is live blob state, not code — _events.mjs:165-200 shows the index is built entirely from whatever artists and venues list, with nothing hardcoded. A marketplace having one city on day one is a growth fact the UI already discloses; it is not the landing page lying. Finally, the fix is mis-scoped even on its own terms. Changing only about.html:723 would leave the identical phrase in seven other places (index.html:21, :22, :24, :251; artist.html:373 "Find gigs near you"; venue.html:310; community.html:255) and would de-couple the footer link from the name of the page it opens — strictly worse than the current state.

check.reasoning:
I checked the three things the accusation stands on.

1. The literal claim holds. Grepping 671-702 for card/pay/checkout/Stripe/$/price/buy returns exactly one hit — "they cost votes rather than money" at :681 — which both sides agree is true. So the sentence under audit is accurate.

2. The accusation's decisive step is false. It says the setlist answer describes "a Plus feature on a plan with no checkout," and for that it cites about.html:658-660 — the marketing page's own honest note. That is the page being used as evidence about the app. In code, checkout exists and is wired end to end: admin.mjs:79-85 takes action planCheckout, _billing.mjs:121-160 opens a Stripe Checkout Session in subscription mode, and _billing.mjs:83-99 creates the product and price on first use, so no dashboard setup is required (MYSET.md:1040 says the same). The Studio offers it on a plain button — studio.html:2352 openPlans, 3564 "Upgrade to Plus", 3579-3583 startCheckout — with "Stripe handles the card." at 3576. The only failure mode is a missing STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, and that key is plainly set in production, because pay.mjs/confirm.mjs run real vote-pack and tip charges on it. _billing.mjs landed 2026-09-05 in commit 6fae274, titled "Plans you can pay for."

So "something that, today, only the founder can do" is wrong. isPlatformOwner (_plan.mjs:154) is a bypass for the founder, not the only door: any artist can buy Plus in the Studio and create setlists. Severity major cannot stand.

3. The proposed fix would ship a false sentence. Its last line — "Plus can't be bought yet" — contradicts admin.mjs:79-85. Putting that in the FAQ would take a page that is merely under-specific and make it untrue. That alone is reason to reject it.

What does survive is thin and different: the FAQ says "build a setlist instead" without noting it is paid, while creating one is gated at admin.mjs:735-736 (_plan.mjs:67, free: setlists:false). A free artist starts with zero lists (_lists.mjs:39 emptyLists), so on free the feature is effectively absent, not merely capped. But an FAQ answer is allowed to describe the product without repricing it, and this page carries a full pricing table two sections above.

The worse problem is one the accuser walked past. about.html:604 lists "Setlists, chord charts, keys and genres" as a FREE bullet, and the Plus card never lists setlists at all. That is not an omission, it is an affirmative promise the server refuses. The FAQ is downstream of it; fixing the FAQ while the free card still sells setlists fixes the smaller half.

Separately, and worth flagging on its own: about.html:658-660 ("Plus and Pro can't be bought yet. There's no checkout") now looks stale against _billing.mjs. about.html was last touched 2026-09-05 21:59, billing at 01:21 the same day, so the note survived the commit that made it false. If that is confirmed, the FAQ needs less disclosure than claimed, not more.

finding.claimText: The real interaction, not a video: tap a song, the count moves, the queue reorders with a spring.
finding.evidence: public/about.html:734-775 is a self-contained replica. SEED, rows, mine, left are local variables (:735-740); the click handler (:763-774) mutates them and calls draw(); there is no fetch, XMLHttpRequest or '/api' anywhere in :729-813 (grepped). I tried to break this finding and could not. Every code fact the accuser cited is real, and the underlying problem is bigger than they described.

WHAT I CONFIRMED MYSELF

1. "Request" is a defined product term on this page, and it is off by default.
netlify/functions/_lib.mjs:181-183 sets `requests: { on: false, cost: 3 }` with the comment "Off by default — an artist who can't play requests should never be asked for them." Charging happens in netlify/functions/_requests.mjs:90-99 (`me.spent = (me.spent||0) + cost`, 402 "no-credits" when short). The page teaches that same meaning in body copy at about.html:396-401 ("they only exist if you switch them on") and about.html:680-683 ("Requests are off until you turn them on").

2. Every other prose use of "request" on the page means that feature.
Only six non-code hits exist: about.html:390 and :404 (image alt text), :398, :592, :680, :681 — all the ask-for-a-song feature. Line 760 is the sole outlier.

3. There is no code path that makes line 760 true. This is the part the accuser understated.
The winning song plays next when the ARTIST taps play, in netlify/functions/admin.mjs:1771-1783 (`case 'play'`) and :1784-1806 (`case 'playTop'` — ranks the pool, sets `show.nowPlaying = pool[0].id`, `resetVotes = true`). Nothing in that path touches requests. And accepting a request does NOT start a song: askAccept only adds it to the setlist, which the Studio itself announces as "Added — the room can vote for it now" (public/studio.html:2646). So even with requests switched ON, "the next request is taken" is not the event that starts the top-voted song. The sentence names a mechanism that does not exist under either reading of the word.

4. The sentence is internally inconsistent with its own two siblings, eight lines apart.
about.html:758 "the next song refreshes everyone", about.html:761 "Starting a song gives everybody theirs back", and the static default at about.html:354-355 all use "song" / "starting a song". Only about.html:760 reaches for "request". That reads as a slip, not careful wording — there is no charitable reading in which the author meant the defined term.

Their harm story runs the wrong way round. The demo section is at about.html:336-357, which is BEFORE beat 3 (:396) and the FAQ (:680). So a linear reader does not "just read that" and then hit line 760 — line 760 fires first. Worse, it fires on the reader's very first tap (the `mine.size` branch shows as soon as one vote is cast with votes remaining), which makes it the first time the word "request" appears in visible body copy on the page, teaching the wrong meaning before the page defines the right one. Same collision, opposite direction, and if anything a stronger reason to fix it.

WHY IT IS STILL "MINOR"

The page never states that voting requires requests; the false idea is an inference a reader could draw, not a claim the copy makes. So AMBIGUOUS/minor is the right severity. But it should be recorded as confirmed, not left open.

I tried to refute this and could not. Taking the falsifier's points one at a time.

WHERE THE FALSIFIER IS RIGHT. Its poll arithmetic checks out exactly. _lib.mjs:852-858 returns 3000 ms for any room up to 200 phones. vote.html:1120 picks signature() (not stageSig) whenever FLOOR is 3000, and signature() at :1072-1075 appends d.totalVotes — so any vote by anyone changes the signature, QUIET resets to 0, and the phone sits on the 3 s rung with ±20% jitter (:1094). In the forty-person pub the copy describes, other people's votes land in about 2.4–3.6 s, not 25 s. 25 s is the sixth-consecutive-unchanged-poll rung, which a lively room never reaches. It is also right that the fan's own tap is instant: vote.html:517-522 moves the count and the credit before the POST at :528. One small correction to the falsifier's own wording — a vote does not drop a phone "straight back" to 3 s; a phone already on the 25 s rung only learns of it on its next poll, up to 25 s later. That only matters in a room that was already silent, which is not the room in the copy.

WHY THAT DOES NOT SAVE THE PAGE. The falsifier fixed the least important of the mismatches, and its proposed rewrite keeps the load-bearing words "This is the real thing, running on this page." Those words are false in three verified ways, and the third is not a matter of degree.

1. It is not the real thing. about.html:734 is a hardcoded SEED array and the file contains no fetch() at all. The handler at :763-774 mutates three local variables. Nothing here is the product.

2. One tap is not how a vote is cast. In the app the Vote button calls openVote() (vote.html:640, 726), which opens a bottom sheet with a quantity stepper, five rules and a Confirm button (:479). Nothing is cast until confirmVote() (:506-510). The demo teaches a one-tap product. The shipped product is two taps with a modal in between.

3. THE ONE NEITHER AGENT CAUGHT, and the reason I am upgrading this. The demo lets you take a vote back: about.html:768, `if (mine.has(id)) { mine.delete(id); row.n--; left++; }`, with the button rendering as a live "Voted" toggle at :751-752. Production does the opposite. _flags.mjs:28-35 sets `voteFinal` default: true, shipped as the code default on purpose so production behaviour is visible in the diff. With it on, vote.html:421-422 never reaches openUnvote — a second tap opens the sheet to add MORE votes (:632 "tap to add more"), and the sheet itself says "Once you confirm, that's final — votes can't be taken back" (:445). So the demo does not merely simplify the product; on the single most consequential rule in a voting app it demonstrates the opposite of what the product does, directly under a sentence promising this is the real thing. A fan who learns "I can undo" from the landing page and then cannot undo at the gig is the trust failure the codebase's own comments keep warning about.

Also missing, as the falsifier noted: the "Couldn't reach the room" failure state (vote.html:534) and the fact that other people's votes arrive on a poll.
