check.reasoning:
I tried to knock this down and could not. I verified it independently at the source rather than trusting the accuser.

WHAT I CONFIRMED MYSELF

1. The two real numbers are real. I read the live production blob read-only (`python3 tools/prod.py get hist_perry-idyll_2026-08-30-1210`). It returns venue "The Ugly Duckling Irish Pub", city "Koh Phangan, Thailand", startedAt 2026-08-30 12:10 UTC (19:10 Thai), endedAt 14:21 UTC, and stats `{songsPlayed: 10, totalVotes: 21, peakVoters: 8, topSong: Catch & Release}`. about.html:486-487 says 8 and 21. Exact match. Same numbers appear in MYSET.md:68 and HANDOFF-MySet.md:389.

2. I checked it is the right night, which the accuser did not. Production holds three perry-idyll shows on 2026-08-30: 1210 (the gig, 2h11m, 21 votes / 8 voters), 1855 (3 minutes, all zeros), 1928 (starts 02:28 Thai and runs until 2026-09-04 — Perry testing afterwards, 6 votes / 1 voter). The 1210 record is unambiguously the gig, so the page cites the correct record and does not silently merge the test sessions in.

3. "8 people voted" is conservative, and more so than the accuser realised. peakVoters is `Math.max(nowVoters, ...played.map(p => p.voters))` (_history.mjs:106), and `voters: votersNow` is the count of distinct fan records holding at least one vote at the instant a song starts (admin.mjs:1756). In THIS record `played` is empty, so peakVoters collapsed to nowVoters — distinct devices with unconsumed votes. It cannot overstate.

4. "…that you didn't type in yourself" (about.html:480-481) is structurally true, which is the accuser's strongest unused defence of the page. history.mjs accepts only `heal` and `reconcile` (lines 18-21); there is no artist-facing path anywhere in netlify/functions that writes a show's stats. The counts genuinely cannot be typed.

WHERE THE ACCUSER IS WRONG, BUT NOT FATALLY

- "animates from 0 to 0, which is invisible" is imprecise. count() (about.html:794-804) writes `Math.round(to * eased) + suffix` on every frame (line 800), so the 0 tile renders a visible "0" throughout — it simply does not move. And the final values are already in the HTML, so a no-JS or no-IntersectionObserver reader sees 8/21/0/100% regardless (line 781). The tile is inert, not blank.
- The quoted heading is two paragraphs above the tiles and is about the READER's future gigs ("Every gig you play is counted…", :480). The tiles' actual lead-in is "Here is MySet's own first night, and we're not going to dress it up" (:482), and the sentence under them says "That's a small number and a true one" — singular, pointing at 8/21. The page is more carefully worded than the accuser allows.

WHY IT STILL SURVIVES

`data-to` appears on exactly four elements in the whole file (486, 487, 488, 489). The count-up animation is a device reserved for this one row, so it does function as a visual signal of instrumentation, and two of the four things it decorates were never counted.

AND ONE THING THAT IS WORSE THAN STATED, which I confirmed in the code

Because line 800 writes `Math.round(to * eased) + '%'` on every frame, the 100% tile does not just look instrumented — it renders a sequence of false sentences. For roughly a second on scroll it literally reads "37% of it from the room, not from you", then "68%…", before landing on 100%. The 8 and 21 tiles counting through wrong intermediate values is harmless (a smaller count is just an animation). A provenance percentage counting through intermediate values states, on screen, that some of it did come from you. That is the real reason that tile must leave the counting row, and it is stronger than "it is a figure of speech".

Severity stays minor/cosmetic — nothing on the page is false at rest — and the accuser's status downgrade is correct.

finding.claimText: and always prefers the network for pages
finding.evidence: The strategy is right — public/sw.js:92-98 tries fetch(req) first and only reaches the cache on throw — but 'always' hides two things. There is no AbortController or timeout, so a network that hangs rather than fails leaves the navigation hanging rather than falling back. More seriously, the fallback chain at :99 is `caches.match(req) || caches.match('/')`, and I verified what that does: serving a local https copy of public/ with a self-signed cert, I loaded /about (worker registered, scope /), loaded / (so '/' entered the cache), then killed the server and navigated to /someartist/vote. The browser was handed the public what's-on home page — document.title 'MySet — live music near you', body text 'Live music near you. You pick what plays…' — while the address bar still read /someartist/vote. A fan whose signal drops at a gig gets the wrong page rather than the 'No connection' card that sw.js:100-105 was written to show.
finding.proposedFix: Drop the second link in the chain at sw.js:99 so an uncached route falls straight to the offline card: `return (await caches.match(req)) || new Response(...)`. Then the comment is true as written.

check.correctedStatus: ACCURATE (severity: none for the quoted statement). A separate, genuine code defect exists at public/sw.js:99, but it is a minor code bug, not a false statement, and it is not on the landing page.
check.correctedEvidence: public/sw.js:83-106 (navigation branch at :92-96 fetches unconditionally; fallback chain at :99); public/about.html:814-817 (the "claim" is a JS comment inside a <script> block, not rendered copy); identical comment in public/index.html:608, vote.html:1157, artist.html:541, venue.html:560, studio.html:4256, venue-studio.html:1841; netlify.toml (/:slug/vote → vote.html, status 200)
check.reasoning:
Three independent reasons this finding does not stand as written.

1. It is not a page statement at all. about.html:813 closes the previous script and :814 opens a new one; lines 815-817 are a `/* ... */` JavaScript comment inside that block. Nothing at myset.vip/about renders it. The same comment is pasted into seven files as a developer note next to the registration call. A landing-page audit finding of "major" severity against a source comment no visitor can read is misplaced by category. If the audit's scope is honestly "developer comments in the page source", it should say so.

2. The sentence is literally true, and I checked every path. The fetch handler returns early for non-GET (:85), cross-origin (:88) and /api (:89) — all of which go straight to the network, untouched. Every remaining navigation reaches :92 and runs `const fresh = await fetch(req)` (:94) unconditionally. There is no cache-first branch, no stale-while-revalidate branch, and no timeout that could pre-empt the network for a document. A navigation to a .html URL is caught by the navigate branch at :92 and returns at :96 before the STATIC branch at :112 is ever reached. There is no code path in which a page is served from cache while the network is answering. "Always prefers the network for pages" is exactly, unconditionally true.

3. The accuser's first sub-point argues the opposite of their own verdict. They say the absence of an AbortController/timeout is evidence against "always". It is evidence for it: a timeout is the mechanism by which a network-first worker stops preferring the network and falls to cache early. Its absence makes the preference stronger, not weaker. A hanging network is a real UX complaint about MySet's offline behaviour, but it cannot make "prefers the network" false — it is that preference taken to its limit.

The second sub-point is a real defect, and I believe their reproduction. The cache is populated only by successful navigations (:95) and static assets (:116), so once a fan has loaded myset.vip/ online, '/' sits in the cache; an offline navigation to a route never visited falls through `caches.match(req)` and is answered by `caches.match('/')` — index.html's document under someone else's URL, instead of the "No connection" card at :100-105. But that happens strictly *after* the network was preferred and threw. It is a defect in the offline fallback ordering, not in the network preference, and it cannot be used to grade this sentence as overstated.

Severity is also inflated. Reaching it needs a fan who cached '/' online, then went offline, then navigated to a route they had never loaded. A fan who scans a QR straight to /someartist/vote has no '/' in cache and correctly gets the offline card; a fan who has loaded that vote page gets the correct page back from `caches.match(req)`. Nothing is lost either way — no vote and no payment can be cached (:89, and the header rule 1), so the failure mode is one confusing screen while the phone has no signal, not lost votes or money. Minor, not major.
check.betterFix:
Leave about.html:816 alone — the sentence is correct and it is a source comment, not copy. File the sw.js:99 issue on its own as a minor bug.

Their fix (drop the `caches.match('/')` link) is directionally right but leaves value on the table. Better, at sw.js:99:

  return (await caches.match(req, { ignoreSearch: true })) || new Response(...)

Two gains over just deleting the second link. It removes the wrong-page hand-off, and `ignoreSearch: true` makes an offline fan with the page already cached still get it when the QR or share link carries a query string (?src=qr, a UTM tag, a Stripe return param) — today those miss the cache and fall through to the '/' bug, which is very likely how the real-world case arises. It is safe here because every one of these routes is a static document whose query string is only ever read client-side: netlify.toml rewrites /:slug/vote to the single vote.html for every artist, so the cached bytes do not vary by query.

While in that block, also give the offline Response `'cache-control': 'no-store'` so the 503 card can never itself be persisted by an intermediary.

finding.claimText: MySetPull();
finding.evidence: Verified by blocking /pull.js at the network layer in headless Chrome and loading /about: the page threw 'ReferenceError: MySetPull is not defined', and because that call sits at the top of the same <script> block, lines 822-824 never executed and no service worker was registered. The demo still worked (it lives in the separate earlier <script>), so the failure is silent — the page looks fine and the three claims at :815-817 are describing a worker that is not there. This is the same class of trap the comment at :29-34 was written to avoid; the ordering was fixed but the failure mode was not guarded, and all eight pages share the pattern.
finding.proposedFix: Wrap the call: `try { MySetPull(); } catch (err) {}` — or move the service-worker block above it, so one missing file cannot take out the other feature.

check.correctedStatus: TRUE — not a discrepancy. Downgrade from "FALSE / minor" to at most a trivial code-robustness nit (nit, not a landing-page truth finding), and correct two factual errors in the write-up.
check.correctedEvidence: public/about.html:35 (blocking `<script src="/pull.js">`, 785 lines above the call) · public/pull.js:113 (`window.MySetPull = function (fn)`) · public/about.html:820-824 · netlify.toml redirects block ("Real files always win over these") · live: `curl https://myset.vip/pull.js` → 200, `application/javascript; charset=UTF-8`, 5996 bytes — byte-identical to the repo file · public/sw.js:18 (rule 4, nothing precached), :91 (rule 2, navigations network-first), :111 (rule 3, static stale-while-revalidate serves /pull.js from cache offline) · INVARIANTS.md:0cf (1256-1264) · SW registration is in its OWN `<script>` on public/community.html:883-887, public/studio.html:4255-4261, public/vote.html:1155-1161, public/venue-studio.html:1839-1845
check.reasoning:
The line does exactly what it says, in production. /pull.js is a same-origin static file loaded BLOCKING at about.html:35, 785 lines before the call at :820; it defines window.MySetPull at pull.js:113. netlify.toml's slug rules are non-forced 200s, so real files win — and I confirmed against production rather than trusting that: https://myset.vip/pull.js returns 200, content-type application/javascript, 5996 bytes, byte-for-byte the repo file. So MySetPull is defined, the call succeeds, and the service worker at :822-824 registers. Nothing on the page is false.

The accuser did not find a defect in the page; they manufactured one. Blocking /pull.js at the network layer is a condition that does not occur — the file ships in the same deploy as the HTML, from the same origin, and for any returning visitor sw.js rule 3 (:111-120) serves it from cache when the network is failing, so the induced state is self-healing in the one real-world scenario (flaky bar wifi) that could produce it.

Two of the write-up's own supporting statements are wrong, and I checked each:
1. "all eight pages share the pattern" — false. Only four do (about:820/823, index:612/615, venue:564/567, artist:545/548). On the other four the service-worker registration sits in a SEPARATE `<script>` element (community:883, studio:4255, vote:1155, venue-studio:1839) and a separate script is a separate compilation unit, so a throw in the MySetPull block cannot touch it. Half the codebase already has the fix the accusation proposes.
2. "the three claims at :815-817 are describing a worker that is not there" — false on both halves. The worker is there and does what the comment says: registration is on the `load` event so it cannot delay first paint (:823), /api is returned untouched (sw.js:89), and navigations are network-first (sw.js:91-105). The comment is accurate; it is only "not there" inside the accuser's artificial block.

The residual risk, stated honestly, is close to zero. If /pull.js ever did fail mid-flight on one of the four coupled pages, the cost is that ONE page load skips registering a worker that precaches nothing (sw.js:18-21) and serves pages network-first anyway; the next load registers it. And the project has already reasoned about this exact failure and accepted it: INVARIANT 0cf keeps the browser's native pull-to-refresh precisely so a failed pull.js loses nothing that matters.

Where the accusation is right, narrowly: JS semantics do mean the coupling exists on those four pages, and the fix is nearly free. That is worth a one-line cleanup, not a "FALSE" verdict on a landing-page claim.
check.betterFix: Do not wrap it in try/catch — that swallows unrelated errors inside the block and hides a genuinely broken deploy. Instead make the four content pages match the four that are already correct: move the service-worker `if ('serviceWorker' in navigator ...)` block into its own `<script>` element, exactly as community.html:883, studio.html:4255, vote.html:1155 and venue-studio.html:1839 already do. One separate script tag decouples the two features with no error swallowing, costs nothing at runtime, and makes all eight pages consistent — which is the real value here, since the inconsistency is what let this look like a systemic bug. If a guard is still wanted for the pull call itself, `if (window.MySetPull) MySetPull();` states the dependency rather than hiding failures. Apply to public/about.html:820-824, public/index.html:612-616, public/venue.html:564-568, public/artist.html:545-549.

check.reasoning:
The accusation misreads a developer comment as marketing copy. Line 732 falls inside a block comment that opens at line 730 ("/* — the live demo") and closes at line 733 ("...above every screenshot on the page. */"), three lines after the <script> tag at 729. The page does not say this. No reader can see it. This is the exact failure mode the brief warns about, inverted: reading a comment as if it were the artifact.

Read as what it actually is, the sentence is also not the equivalence claim alleged. "Somebody who has done it once already understands the product" is a claim about a person grasping the idea (tap a song, the count moves, the queue reorders) after one tap. It is not an assertion that the widget and vote.html are mechanically identical, and it does not survive being tested against a six-point parity checklist it never invited.

I did verify the six code facts independently, and five and a half of them are real — but they attach to a different sentence, and they are weaker than presented. (1) Shape: confirmed, openVote -> drawVoteSheet -> confirmVote (vote.html:423, :436, :506-510) versus a single click handler on about.html. Two more things the accuser did not notice. The page never states the product's free-vote allowance anywhere: the visible "3 votes left" at :337 and left=3 at :740 are the widget's own state, and the demo footer at :354-355 says "a few free votes" — deliberately unnumbered. finding.claimText: Live music near you — and you pick what gets played.
finding.evidence: There is no geolocation of any kind: grep for navigator.geolocation in public/index.html returns nothing, and netlify/functions/events.mjs accepts only `country` and `city` strings (events.mjs:55-57) with no lat, lng, radius or distance anywhere in the file. finding.claimText: vote on what the band plays next
finding.evidence: Votes produce a ranked queue: show.mjs:78 rankSongs orders songs by votes then first-voted, and show.mjs returns that list. 2) THE PROPOSED FIX CHANGES NOTHING SEMANTICALLY. The claim is that "vote on what the band plays next" promises the band is bound, while "vote on the next song" does not. finding.claimText: 4KB, same origin, and the service worker serves it from cache, so blocking costs nothing measurable.
finding.evidence: Both halves are wrong. Size: `wc -c public/pull.js` = 5,996 bytes, and the live response confirms it (`content-length: 5996`) — 5.9KB, ~50% more than stated. finding.proposedFix: "6KB, same origin. The service worker caches it after the first visit — it precaches nothing (sw.js rule 4) — so only the first load pays for it, and that is the trade for the gesture arming reliably."

check.correctedStatus: MOSTLY TRUE — cosmetic doc-drift only. Not FALSE. The accusation's headline half (size) is wrong, and its own "live response confirms it" evidence is a measurement artifact.
check.correctedEvidence: public/index.html:30-36 (the comment + the blocking script tag; identical text also at public/about.html:30-35 and public/vote.html); public/sw.js:18 (rule 4, no precache), public/sw.js:111-120 (the stale-while-revalidate branch, the only cache-write path for a static asset); public/index.html:614-615 (SW registered on `load`); measured live: `curl -H 'Accept-Encoding: br' https://myset.vip/pull.js | wc -c` = 2571 bytes, response header `content-encoding: br`; `curl -sSI` with no Accept-Encoding = `content-length: 5996`; `wc -c public/pull.js` = 5996; `wc -c public/app.css` = 11117 raw / 3317 brotli over the wire.
check.reasoning:
I checked both halves myself.

SIZE — the accusation is wrong, and it is wrong in the opposite direction from what it claims. Netlify serves /pull.js brotli-compressed: the response carries `content-encoding: br` and the actual bytes on the wire to any real browser are 2,571 — 2.5KB. The "live response confirms it (content-length: 5996)" line is an artifact of curl sending no Accept-Encoding header by default; no browser ever makes that request. So the file that reaches a phone is *smaller* than the 4KB the comment claims, not "~50% more". The sentence's whole subject is transfer cost ("blocking costs nothing measurable"), and on transfer cost the comment is conservative — it overstates the price of its own decision.

The only true residue is that the on-disk source has drifted: it was 5,054 bytes when the comment was written (117661d, the commit that introduced both the file and the comment) and is 5,996 today after 931d18d. If you insist on reading "4KB" as a source-file figure it was already rounded down when written and is looser now. That is documentation drift inside an HTML comment, invisible to every user, in a note whose audience is the next developer. It is not a marketing claim on a landing page and does not deserve a FALSE.

CACHE — the accuser's facts are right and their conclusion overreaches. sw.js:18 does say nothing is precached, and sw.js:111-120 is indeed the only path that ever writes a static asset into the cache, so it runs after a first fetch. In fact it is stronger than they noticed: index.html:614-615 registers the worker on the `load` event, so on a genuine first visit no service worker is installed or controlling at all — precaching is beside the point. But that is true of every service worker ever written, and the sentence never claims first-visit coverage; it is justifying a build decision for the steady state. The practical claim — "blocking costs nothing measurable" — also survives the first visit on its own merits: 2.5KB brotli, same origin, multiplexed over the HTTP/2 connection the HTML just arrived on, sitting one line below a render-blocking `/app.css` that is 3,317 bytes over the same wire. The script the comment is defending is smaller than the stylesheet the page already blocks on beside it. "Nothing measurable" is a fair description of that.

The accuser's proposed fix would make the comment less accurate, not more: it swaps the honest-and-conservative 4KB for "6KB", which is the uncompressed disk size and roughly 2.4× what a browser actually downloads.

One thing worth passing on regardless of verdict: the comment is byte-identical in three files (public/index.html, public/about.html, public/vote.html), so any edit has to land in all three or they drift apart.

Blocking costs nothing measurable." Do NOT adopt the proposed "6KB": that is the uncompressed disk size, about 2.4× what any browser actually downloads, and it would replace a conservative true statement with a misleading one.

finding.claimText: Sits ON TOP of a page that has already rendered, so it can never delay anything.
finding.evidence: index.html:43 makes #intro position:fixed, so it is out of flow and delays no layout and no paint of the content behind it — the render claim is right. But it covers the whole viewport with an opaque var(--bg) for about 1.65 seconds (index.html:44: a 0.5s animation on a 1.15s delay), so the visitor waits even though the browser did not. And the real first-paint cost on this page is the render-blocking `<script src="/pull.js">` at index.html:36 — 5,996 bytes, uncached on a first visit — which the comment immediately above it (line 34) calls free. See home-08.
finding.proposedFix: "Sits ON TOP of a page that has already rendered, so it delays no layout and no paint. It does hold the view for about 1.6 seconds, which is the whole cost of it — keep it short."

check.reasoning:
I tried to refute this and could not. The mechanical half of the sentence is correct and I confirm it: index.html:43 sets #intro to position:fixed;inset:0, so it is out of flow, adds no layout work to the content, and does not block that content's paint. If the comment had stopped at "delays no layout and no paint" it would be accurate.

But the word "anything" is absolute, and two things are in fact delayed. First, the visual one the accuser named: index.html:44 is `animation:introOut .5s var(--ease) 1.15s both` against `@keyframes introOut{to{opacity:0;visibility:hidden}}` at :55, over an opaque `background:var(--bg)` covering the full viewport. app.css:36 shows --ease is a plain cubic-bezier, adding no time. So the content is hidden from the visitor for the full 1.15s and only clear at 1.65s. Confirmed.

Second, and the accuser understated this: #intro has NO `pointer-events:none`. It is not set at index.html:43, and app.css contains no `#intro` rule whatsoever (grep for "intro" in app.css returns nothing but unrelated .bg/.confetti lines). `visibility:hidden` only lands at the END of the introOut keyframe, so for the entire 1.65s the overlay is a live hit-target sitting at z-index:90 over the whole page. Every tap or click a visitor makes in the first 1.65 seconds is eaten by an invisible-purpose overlay and does nothing. That is not just "the visitor waits" — the page is genuinely unresponsive, which is the strongest possible counterexample to "can never delay anything."

I checked for exculpating paths and found none that rescue the sentence. index.html:293 does remove the intro when sessionStorage 'myset.seen' is set, and :56 disables it under prefers-reduced-motion — but those are the comment's OTHER two sentences ("shown once per session", "not at all if motion is unwelcome"), both of which are true, and neither helps the first-visit-in-a-session default case the sentence is about. The :296 setTimeout(…,2200) removal is a backstop that fires after the animation, so it does not shorten anything. There is no other #intro rule anywhere.

Nor is the accuser reading a doc as code or a comment as behaviour: they cited the CSS rule itself, and their line numbers (:43, :44, :36, :34) are all exactly right. Their cross-reference also checks out — sw.js:18 states "NOTHING is precached at install", so /pull.js (5,996 bytes, loaded render-blocking at index.html:36) really is uncached on a first visit, which makes the :34 comment's "4KB … blocking costs nothing measurable" a second, separate overclaim (home-08).

The one fair mitigation for the page: this is a CSS source comment written in engineering register, where "delay" most naturally means "delay the render pipeline" — and in that narrow sense it is true. That is why this is minor and not a lie. But the comment is doing the job of justifying a decision, and the justification it gives ("can never delay anything") is precisely the thing a future reader would rely on when deciding not to shorten the animation. An overclaim that discourages the right fix is worth correcting.

So: not refuted, and slightly worse than stated. I would raise the accuser's status from AMBIGUOUS to a confirmed overclaim, severity minor.
check.correctedStatus: CONFIRMED OVERCLAIM (minor) — not ambiguous. The render half is true and verified; the absolute "can never delay anything" is false in two ways, one of which the accuser missed: the overlay is opaque for 1.65s AND, lacking pointer-events:none, it swallows every tap for that same 1.65s.
check.correctedEvidence: public/index.html:41 (the claim); public/index.html:43 (position:fixed;inset:0;z-index:90;background:var(--bg) — and NO pointer-events:none); public/index.html:44 (animation:introOut .5s var(--ease) 1.15s both); public/index.html:55 (@keyframes introOut{to{opacity:0;visibility:hidden}} — visibility only drops at the end); public/index.html:56 (prefers-reduced-motion escape hatch, true); public/index.html:234 (the #intro markup, aria-hidden="true"); public/index.html:293 and :296 (sessionStorage 'myset.seen' removal + 2200ms backstop); public/app.css:36 (--ease is a plain cubic-bezier, adds no time); public/app.css — no #intro rule exists anywhere, so nothing overrides pointer-events; public/sw.js:18 ("NOTHING is precached at install", corroborating the home-08 cross-reference about /pull.js at public/index.html:36, 5,996 bytes on disk).
check.betterFix:
Replace the comment with one that separates the two costs, since the second is the one a future reader would otherwise not know about:

/* ── the opener ──
   position:fixed, so it is out of flow: no layout and no paint of the page
   behind it waits on this. What it does cost is 1.65s of the visitor —
   fully opaque until 1.15s, faded out by 1.65s — and with no pointer-events:none
   it is a live hit-target for that whole window, so a tap in the first 1.65s

Two notes on the fix itself. (1) Do NOT "solve" this by adding pointer-events:none to #intro at index.html:43 — that would let taps through to controls the visitor cannot see, which is worse than a dead tap. If the tap-blocking is judged unacceptable, the correct change is to cut the 1.15s delay at :44, not to make an opaque overlay transparent to input. (2) The accuser's proposed wording ("it does hold the view for about 1.6 seconds, which is the whole cost of it") is good but is itself now slightly untrue as an absolute — holding the view is NOT the whole cost, the input block is the other half. My wording fixes an overclaim without introducing a smaller one.

finding.claimText: Shown once per session, and not at all if motion is unwelcome.
finding.evidence: The once-per-session gate is index.html:292-295, inside a try/catch that swallows storage failures (:295). With storage blocked — Safari set to block all cookies, some managed devices — the getItem throws, the catch eats it, and the splash plays on every single load. The reduced-motion rule at index.html:56 is `display:none`, so nothing is seen; the element is still inserted and the 2200ms removal at :296 still runs, which is harmless since it carries aria-hidden="true" (:234). app.css:190-193 would also flatten the animation independently.
finding.proposedFix: "Shown once per session where the browser will remember that, and hidden entirely if motion is unwelcome. With storage blocked it plays every time — the trade for not setting a cookie for an animation."

check.reasoning:
Three independent reasons the finding does not stand as written.

1) IT IS NOT A PAGE CLAIM. The sentence lives inside a CSS comment: public/index.html:37 opens `<style>`, and lines 40-42 are `/* ── the opener ── ... Shown once per session, and not at all if motion is unwelcome. */`, closed before the `#intro` rule at :43. I stripped `<style>`/`<script>` from the body and searched the rendered text: neither "once per session" nor "motion is unwelcome" appears anywhere a visitor can read (nor anywhere in public/about.html, the actual landing page). No user is ever told this. A discrepancy audit of the marketing surface has nothing to bite on here; this is an engineering note to the next engineer.

2) THE SECOND CLAUSE IS UNCONDITIONALLY TRUE, AND THE ACCUSER CONCEDES IT. index.html:56 `@media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){#intro{display:none}}` fires regardless of storage, JS, or anything else. app.css:190-193 flattens it again independently.

3) THE PROPOSED FIX INTRODUCES A FALSE STATEMENT. It ends "the trade for not setting a cookie for an animation," which implies a cookie would have survived. It would not: the condition the accuser names (Safari "Block All Cookies", managed profiles) is the same setting that makes `sessionStorage` throw — `document.cookie` writes are dropped by it too. There is no storage mechanism that works in that state, so there was no "trade." Shipping that sentence would put a mechanism error into the file to replace a sentence that has none.

On the mechanism itself the accuser is technically correct but proves too much: :292-295 does wrap the gate in try/catch, and with storage denied the opener replays. But index.html:299-300 wraps `localStorage` in the exact same swallow for the country/city memory, and nobody asks that comment to caveat itself. check.reasoning:
I tried to break this finding and could not break its core, but two of its sub-claims are overstated and its proposed fix is wrong in one place.

WHAT I CONFIRMED MYSELF
1. The branch is exactly as quoted. public/index.html:303 swallows every fetch/parse failure into an empty catch, leaving PLACES null; :305 tests `!PLACES||!PLACES.ok||!PLACES.countries.length`; :306 disables the country field; :307 prints "No gigs listed yet" and, worse than the accuser noted, the paragraph under it asserts "MySet is brand new" — an unconditional claim about the business, printed on a network hiccup.
2. The places branch of the API genuinely cannot return ok:false. netlify/functions/events.mjs:19-37 has a single exit, `return json({ ok: true, src: MARK, countries })` at :36. `bad()` (netlify/functions/_lib.mjs:891) is the only producer of ok:false and the places branch never calls it. So `!PLACES.ok` at :305 is dead against a healthy function; only an unhandled throw (blob read failure, or a timeout inside countUpcoming's N-blob-reads loop, events.mjs:117-128) reaches the client, and it arrives as a non-JSON Netlify error page, which throws in `r.json()` and lands in the same empty catch. The accuser read this correctly.
3. There is no in-page retry. boot() is called exactly once (index.html:604) and nothing re-runs it — no online, pageshow, visibilitychange or interval listener exists in the file.
4. The page's own author already knows the right pattern and applied it 100 lines later: index.html:404 renders "Couldn't load that / Try again in a moment" for a failed city search, and there `!d.ok` is live because that path really can return bad(). So this is an inconsistency inside one file, not a missing idea.

WHERE THE ACCUSER OVERSTATES
a. "The only realistic way to reach this copy is the catch at :303." Not so. netlify/functions/_events.mjs:165-170 returns `{v:1,countries:{}}` when the index doc is missing, which yields ok:true with countries:[] — a real, designed, currently-unused path on which the sentence is perfectly true. And the failure side is WIDER than stated: a fan simply offline or on a dead bar wifi hits the same catch, which at a live gig is more likely than a cold function.
b. "No retry anywhere on screen" is too strong. public/pull.js is loaded blocking at index.html:36 and MySetPull() runs at :612, giving every page a pull-to-refresh that does a real reload — plus the browser's own reload, and boot() re-runs on load. The visitor is not stranded; there is just no visible affordance and no explanation.

So the correct charge is narrower and cleaner than "the page states something false": the sentence is true on the path it was written for, and the bug is that one branch conflates "we asked and there is nothing" with "we could not ask". That is a conflation defect, and I would land it moderate rather than major, because it self-heals on reload and the three CTAs beneath it still work.

WHY THE PROPOSED FIX IS PARTLY WRONG
It says to leave the country field enabled on failure. Do not. With PLACES null the combo has no options at all (:317-325 read PLACES.countries), so an enabled field would open an empty list and swallow typing — a worse lie than a disabled one. And "Pull down to try again" is desktop-blind and, per pull.js's own header comment, cannot help a page whose JS is broken.

ONE MORE TRAP THE FIX MUST NOT WALK INTO: a retry button that simply calls boot() again will re-run :326, binding a second click listener to #go, so a later Search fires search() twice. An in-place retry has to be idempotent or it has to reload.

finding.claimText: ${x.n} gig${x.n===1?'':'s'}

So the picker and the feed answer the same question two different ways. An act playing Bangkok and Chiang Mai is genuinely in both lists, and today contributes their Bangkok gigs to Chiang Mai's number and vice versa. No. The picker's numbers come only from `/events?places=1` (index.html:303); nothing else supplies x.n. - Comment-vs-behaviour? The comment at events.mjs:177 says "How many gigs these artists have in the window", which is an honest description of the code — it is the PAGE that adds the place claim, not the comment. - More carefully worded than noticed? finding.claimText: Couldn't load that / Try again in a moment.
finding.evidence: index.html:401-404 catches every failure into one message written as if the problem were transient — a function crash, a bad deploy and a dropped connection all read as "try again in a moment" — and offers no retry control, so the only way back is to re-pick the city. The specific catch-all worry does not apply here: netlify.toml:15-18 routes /api/* above the /:slug rule at :79-82, so an API path never falls through to an HTML page.
finding.proposedFix:
"Couldn't load that

Tap Search to try again.

" — and re-enable the Search button in that branch so the sentence is actionable.

check.reasoning: The load-bearing half of the accusation is factually wrong, and the copy half is weaker than stated. 1) "Offers no retry control, so the only way back is to re-pick the city" — FALSE. The Search button (public/index.html:270, id="go") sits in .finder directly ABOVE the #out box (:274) that renders the error, and it is ENABLED at that moment. Its only enable/disable rules are: it starts disabled (:270), it is disabled when a country is picked (:320), and it is set to `!v` when a city is picked (:325) — so it is enabled exactly when a city is chosen. search() itself (:396-404) never touches it, and search() early-returns unless a city is chosen (:398). Therefore any time the error at :404 can render, #go is enabled and its click handler (:326) calls search() again. Retry is one tap on a button already on screen. The restore-from-localStorage path (:335) explicitly sets `$('#go').disabled=false` before auto-searching, so that route too leaves the button live. 2) The second half of the proposed fix — "re-enable the Search button in that branch" — fixes a state that does not exist. Applying it would be a no-op edit to production code. 3) "Written as if the problem were transient" — the sentence is more careful than the accuser noticed, because EVERY path that reaches :404 is transient or user-indistinguishable from transient. For a country/city pair (and the combos only offer values the server itself returned), netlify/functions/events.mjs never returns ok:false on the city-feed path: an unknown or empty city returns ok:true with total 0 (:144-150), which lands in the "Nothing on in this week" branch (:406), not the error branch. The only `bad()` on that path is a missing country/city (events.mjs:57), which the client guards at index.html:398. So :404 is reached only by: fetch rejection (offline, dropped bar wifi, DNS), a non-JSON body (function 500, cold-start timeout, bad deploy), or a platform 5xx. For all of those, "try again in a moment" is the correct and only actionable instruction — there is nothing else the fan can do, and naming a server bug would be neither truer nor useful. 4) What IS genuinely worse, and sits at a different line: boot() at :303-313. If the `?places=1` fetch throws — the same dropped connection — PLACES is null and the page renders "No gigs listed yet ... MySet is brand new" and sets `cs.disabled=true` on the country input. THAT copy is a false statement (it asserts an empty database when the truth is a failed request), and unlike :404 it leaves NO control enabled at all — the country box is disabled, so a reload really is the only way back. If a finding belongs here, it is that one, at :305-313, not :404.
check.correctedStatus: REFUTED as written (the "no retry control" claim is false and the code half of the fix is a no-op). Downgrade from a discrepancy to an optional copy nicety at :404 — severity trivial/cosmetic, not a page-vs-code discrepancy. Separately, OPEN a new, stronger finding at public/index.html:305-313: a boot-time network failure states "No gigs listed yet / MySet is brand new" and disables the country picker, leaving no retry.

Do not touch the button — it is already enabled. If anything changes at :404, change copy only, to point at the control that exists: `Couldn't load that

Check your connection, then tap Search again.

`. That is honest about the likeliest cause (a phone on bar wifi), names the existing control, and adds no code. Optional and low value on its own. finding.claimText: Nothing on in ${city} this week
finding.evidence: Measured on the live feed: today 2026-09-06, horizon 2026-09-13. events.mjs:8 sets WINDOW_DAYS = 7 and the expansion is inclusive of the end date (_events.mjs:96 `if (d < fromDate || d > toDate) return;`), so the feed covers today through today+7 — eight calendar days. Both "this week" here and "the next seven days" at index.html:408 and :490 undersell it by a day, and the two phrases mean different spans on a Friday.
finding.proposedFix: Pick one span and make the code match it. Set WINDOW_DAYS = 6 in events.mjs:8 so the horizon really is seven days including today, then use "the next seven days" in all three places — index.html:407 becomes "Nothing on in ${city} in the next seven days".

check.correctedStatus: NOT A DISCREPANCY — cosmetic copy-consistency nit at most; the proposed fix is a product regression
check.correctedEvidence: netlify/functions/events.mjs:8, :76-77, :146, :171; netlify/functions/_events.mjs:96; public/index.html:406-408, :488-490
check.reasoning:
The accuser's span arithmetic is correct, and it is the only correct part. I confirmed it independently: events.mjs:8 sets WINDOW_DAYS = 7; events.mjs:77 expands `occurrencesFor(events, addDays(from,-1), addDays(from, WINDOW_DAYS))`; _events.mjs:96 `if (d < fromDate || d > toDate) return;` is inclusive at both ends; past rows are then dropped by `if (o.endsAt <= now) continue` (events.mjs:78). So the visible feed really does run from now through the end of today+7 — eight calendar days.

But the accusation does not follow from that, because it gets the direction of the error backwards. Every one of the three sentences is an UNDERSTATEMENT of a superset window, and an understatement of a superset cannot be false.

1. index.html:407 fires only inside `if(!d.total)` (index.html:406) — i.e. the eight-day window is completely empty. If nothing is on in eight days, then nothing is on this week. The sentence is true. So is the sub-line at :408, "nothing in the next seven days" — also true, for the same superset reason.

2. index.html:490, "That's everything in ${city} for the next seven days", is the only positive claim, and it is also true: the rendered list does contain everything in the next seven days. It never claims the list contains nothing beyond them. A list that also happens to carry an eighth day still satisfies "that's everything for the next seven days."

Three further points weaken the finding:

- The "two phrases mean different spans on a Friday" ambiguity is self-resolving on the page. :407 and :408 sit in the same rendered block, two lines apart, so the page defines its own "this week" as "the next seven days" to the reader's eye. That is more careful wording than the accuser credited.

- The `horizon` field the accuser measured against is dead. `grep -rn horizon public/*.html netlify/functions/*.mjs` returns exactly one hit — events.mjs:146, where it is emitted. No page reads it. The accuser measured a payload field no user ever sees and then judged user-facing copy by it.

- The target of this audit is public/about.html, the landing page. Neither :407 nor :490 is on it; both are JS template strings on the secondary what's-on home. about.html's only related phrase, :528 "MySet shows the week", is the same harmless understatement.

Finally, the proposed fix is worse than the alleged problem. Setting WINDOW_DAYS = 6 is a server behaviour change made to satisfy a wording preference: it silently deletes a whole day of real gigs from the city feed (events.mjs:77) AND from the country/city picker's advertised counts, because countUpcoming uses the same constant (events.mjs:171). An artist with a gig a week out stops appearing, and the picker undercounts the city. Never shrink what the product shows to make a sentence tidier when the sentence is free to change and is not even false.

One thing the accuser missed that is a real, separate observation: the window is computed per owner in each owner's own zone (`const from = localDate(now, tz)` at events.mjs:76-77, with tz from `guessTz`, which takes the first event carrying a tz — not necessarily the city's), and the response's `today` comes from `rows[0].tz` (events.mjs:88-89). So there is no single crisp calendar span to name in the first place, which is an argument for the soft wording the page already uses, not against it. That is a different finding and not this one.
check.betterFix:
Do not touch WINDOW_DAYS. If Perry wants the two phrases unified, it is a pure copy edit with no server change: make index.html:407 read "Nothing on in ${city} in the next seven days" and drop the now-duplicated tail of :408 — that removes the "this week" / "seven days" mismatch and stays true, since an empty eight-day window is an empty seven-day window.

If exactness is actually wanted, there is a strictly better move that also costs nothing server-side: the response already carries `horizon` (events.mjs:146) and index.html already has the `dayMonth()` helper at :498. Carry horizon into FEED at index.html:401 (`FEED={days:d.days,city,fmt,horizon:d.horizon}`) and make the endcard at :490 read "That's everything in ${city} up to ${dayMonth(FEED.horizon)}." That names the real end date instead of approximating a span, so the copy can never drift out of step with WINDOW_DAYS again — and no gig disappears from the feed to achieve it.

finding.claimText: ${d.artists} artist${…} play${…} here — nothing in the next seven days.
finding.evidence: events.mjs:148 sets `artists: ids.filter((x) => !isVenueOwner(x)).length` — the size of the city index's membership list, not a count of anyone who plays there now. reindexCities (_events.mjs:180-186) adds an artist for ANY repeating event with that city and never looks at repeat.until, so a residency that ended two years ago keeps them listed forever; a one-off keeps them for seven days after it finishes (:185); and the index is only rewritten when that artist next saves an event (admin.mjs:489, :496). So the number over-counts, and it is presented to a stranger as a fact about their town.
finding.proposedFix: Drop the number rather than publish one the code cannot stand behind: "Acts have played here before — nothing listed in the next seven days." If the number is wanted, honour repeat.until in _events.mjs:182 first.

check.correctedStatus: SURVIVES on mechanism, but the label is wrong: not FALSE/major — IMPRECISE / STALE-COUNT, severity minor-to-moderate. The sentence is true in the common case and wrong only in a stale-index tail case, and it sits in an empty-state on a secondary page, not in a headline claim.
check.correctedEvidence: public/index.html:408 (the sentence); netlify/functions/events.mjs:148 (`artists: ids.filter((x) => !isVenueOwner(x)).length`) and :147 (`total: rows.length`); netlify/functions/_events.mjs:182 (`if (e.repeat) { places.add(placeKey(e.country, e.city)); continue; }` — no `until` check) vs :185 (the 7-day tail for one-offs); netlify/functions/_events.mjs:94 and :113 (`stop`/`limit` — expand DOES honour repeat.until, which is what creates the mismatch); public/studio.html:1720 + :1743 ("Stop repeating on (optional)" → `repeat:{freq,until:v('gUntil')||null}`, so an expired residency is a state a real artist can create); netlify/functions/venue-studio... public/venue-studio.html:1665 (`repeat:{freq,until:null}` — venue events can never expire, same index, counted as `venues:` at events.mjs:149).
check.reasoning:
I tried to refute this and could not. The mechanism is real and I confirmed each link personally.

What holds: `expand()` honours `repeat.until` (_events.mjs:94, :113), so a residency with an end date in the past yields zero occurrences and `total` (events.mjs:147) is 0 — the empty branch fires. But `reindexCities` (_events.mjs:182) adds the city for ANY repeating event with no `until` check at all, so that artist stays in the city index and is still counted at events.mjs:148. And this is not hypothetical: studio.html:1720 is a real "Stop repeating on (optional)" date field, written straight into `repeat.until` at :1743. Traced the arithmetic both ways (weekly jump-ahead and the monthly `d > limit` break) — both produce zero pushes with a past `until`. So `artists >= 1` with `total === 0` and nobody actually playing there is reachable.

Where the accusation overreaches, and why I downgrade it:

1. Its own headline example is wrong. "A residency that ended two years ago keeps them listed forever" only produces THIS sentence if the artist set an end date. If they simply stopped showing up and never touched the record, `expand` keeps generating occurrences forever, `total > 0`, and the empty state never renders — the page instead advertises phantom gigs. That is a different and worse bug that this finding does not actually cover.

2. It describes the number as "the size of the city index's membership list, not a count of anyone who plays there now." That is unfair to the code. The index is rebuilt from live event records on every save; for the overwhelming majority it is exactly "artists with a current event naming this city." The dominant reason this branch renders at all is an artist with a monthly or biweekly residency whose date falls outside this particular week — and for them "3 artists play here" is straightforwardly true and is the most useful thing on the screen. Over-count is the tail, not the norm.

3. The 7-day one-off tail at :185, which the finding lists as a defect, is close to honest. Saying an act "plays here" when they played in that town four days ago is not a lie; it is a deliberate, commented grace window.

4. Severity "major" does not fit the surface. This is public/index.html — the brief's secondary page — inside an empty state a stranger only reaches after picking a country and city and finding nothing on. The load-bearing half of the sentence ("nothing in the next seven days") is always correct; the disputed half is a count offered as context. Compare it to a pricing or capability claim in the hero of about.html and it is plainly not the same weight.

One way it is WIDER than stated: the same stale ids also produce `venues:` at events.mjs:149 and the picker's per-city `artists`/`venues` at events.mjs:29-30, and venue-studio.html:1665 hard-codes `until:null`, so a venue owner cannot expire a recurring event even in principle. index.html only renders the picker's `gigs` today (:315, :324), so nothing else surfaces on-page right now — but the payload is wrong for anything that consumes it next. That is the argument for fixing _events.mjs:182 rather than deleting the sentence.

finding.claimText: No one has listed a gig here yet.
finding.evidence: index.html:408 branches on `d.artists ? … : 'No one has listed a gig here yet.'`, and events.mjs:148-149 sends `artists` and `venues` as two separate counts. A city whose index holds only venue owners therefore has artists = 0 and venues > 0 — and the page tells the visitor nobody has ever listed a gig there while a venue's quiz nights, DJs and full-moon parties are sitting in that very index (events.mjs:81 emits them as kind 'event').
finding.proposedFix: Branch on both, and say the smaller true thing: `${(d.artists||d.venues) ? 'Nothing listed here in the next seven days.' : 'Nobody has listed anything here yet.'}`

check.reasoning:
I tried to break this finding four ways and it survived all four.

1) Is the empty branch even reachable with venues in the index? Yes. `venueadmin.mjs:136,146,233` calls `reindexCities(evOwner(vid), events)` with a `v_<vid>` owner, and `_events.mjs:163` defines `isVenueOwner` on exactly that prefix. So a city key in `cityindex` can hold only `v_` ids. `events.mjs:148-149` then returns `artists: 0, venues: >0`, and `index.html:408` tests `d.artists` alone, so the visitor is shown "No one has listed a gig here yet." (`index.html:409`).

2) Is the statement rescued by the fact that the empty branch only fires when `!d.total`? No — this is where I expected to refute it and could not. `reindexCities` (`_events.mjs:178-186`) keeps an owner in a city if the event repeats, OR if the one-off is later than `Date.now() - 7 days`. The feed window (`events.mjs:8,77`) is only yesterday..+7 days and drops anything already ended (`events.mjs:79`). So two ordinary cases give venues>0 with total=0: a venue whose only listing is a one-off more than seven days out (the full-moon party three weeks away — indexed, invisible, and the page says nobody ever listed anything), and a venue whose one-off ran two nights ago (still indexed for seven days). The accuser's phrasing implies live quiz nights are being hidden — that specific case is wrong, because a recurring quiz night inside the window makes `total > 0` and this branch unreachable. The bug is real; the accuser's illustration of it is not.

3) Is "gig" a narrower word than the accuser noticed — i.e. does the page mean "artist gig", making the sentence technically true when only a venue has listed? No, and the page itself refutes that. The city picker at `index.html:358` renders `${x.n} gig${...}`, and that count comes from `countUpcoming` (`events.mjs:178-189`) which walks every id in the city including `v_` venue owners. The same page counts a venue's event as a "gig" one screen earlier, so it cannot fall back on "gig means artist" one screen later.

Three separate problems with the accusation, checked in the files myself.

1. It is not a page claim. Line 421 sits inside the <script> that opens at public/index.html:287 — it is a /* */ JavaScript comment. `grep` finds "filtering forty rows" exactly once in the file, in that comment. No visitor to myset.vip ever sees this string; it is not marketing copy on the landing page (/about) nor rendered text on the home page. Auditing it as "THE PAGE SAYS" is a scope error.

2. What the sentence actually asserts is true. The load-bearing claim is about WHO filters: "Keep the fetched week so the search box can re-render it without another request — filtering ... is the phone's job, not the server's." The code does exactly that: search() stores the fetched week in FEED (:422), renderFeed() filters that cached array client-side (:445-450), and the search input's oninput calls renderFeed directly (:452) with no fetch anywhere in the path. 3. The accuser's proposed rewrite is substantively wrong about the failure mode. It says "the per-keystroke innerHTML rebuild is the thing that gives first." It is not. Shipping the accuser's fix would publish a sentence that points the reader at the wrong bottleneck. If anything the comment's premise is stronger than the accuser allows: the phone's filtering really is the cheap side.

finding.claimText: That’s everything in ${city} for the next seven days.
finding.evidence: Three gaps behind "everything". (1) The span is eight days, not seven — live today 2026-09-06, horizon 2026-09-13, inclusive (events.mjs:8, _events.mjs:96). (2) Completeness depends entirely on the city index, and _events.mjs:180 silently drops any event with a blank country or city, so those gigs exist on the artist's page and never reach this feed. (3) City matching is exact string equality (events.mjs:78 `o.city !== city`), so "Koh Phangan" and "Ko Pha Ngan" are two separate cities that never see each other — the same literal-name fragility about.html:568-571 admits about venues. There is at least no cap: events.mjs:68-86 returns every row it finds.

check.reasoning:
I tried to kill this one and could not, but one of its three legs is wrong and the severity is inflated.

LEG 1 — WRONG, and it inverts the direction of the error. events.mjs:8 sets WINDOW_DAYS=7 and events.mjs:75 expands `occurrencesFor(events, addDays(from,-1), addDays(from,7))`, so the feed carries today-1 (still-running only, filtered by `o.endsAt <= now` at events.mjs:79) through today+7 — eight forward calendar dates. That means the feed shows MORE than seven days, not fewer. "That's everything for the next seven days" is a completeness claim about a window; a window that is one day WIDER than claimed cannot make the claim false. This is over-delivery, not overstatement. The accuser counted the span correctly and then drew the opposite conclusion from it. Drop this leg entirely.

LEG 2 — HOLDS, and I confirmed it end to end myself. _events.mjs:181 `if (!e.country || !e.city) continue;` skips the event when building the city index. And a blank-city gig is fully creatable: studio.html:1744-1745 validates only venue and date client-side, and admin.mjs:469-470 validates only date and venue server-side (`if (!ev.date) return bad('Pick a date'); if (!ev.venue) return bad('Where is it?')`) — nothing anywhere requires city or country. That gig still renders on the artist's own page, because the artist-diary branch (events.mjs:41-50, `?a=<slug>`) applies no city/country filter at all. So a real gig can exist on myset.vip/<slug> and be structurally invisible to the city feed that says it shows "everything".

LEG 3 — HOLDS. events.mjs:78 `if (o.city !== city || o.country !== country) continue;` is exact string equality, and the stored value is only trimmed and whitespace-collapsed, never case-folded or canonicalised (_events.mjs:56-57, `str(e.city,60)`); normPlace (_maps.mjs:64-73) touches address/mapUrl/lat/lng and never the city. studio.html:1696 is a free-text `<input id="gCity" maxlength="60">` with no autocomplete against existing cities. So "Koh Phangan", "koh phangan" and "Ko Pha Ngan" are three separate index keys and three separate feeds. Partial mitigation the accuser didn't credit: the picker (index.html:322-325) lists every index key with its gig count, so a fan can at least SEE the second spelling — but the endcard still says "everything in Koh Phangan" while the other spelling's gigs sit elsewhere.

THE LEG NOBODY ARGUED, and it's the big one. Both legs 2 and 3 are edge cases next to the plain fact that the index is built exclusively from MySet account holders' own entries — reindexCities is only ever called off an artist or venue write (admin.mjs:489/496/517, venueadmin.mjs:136/146/233, _account.mjs, _venueaccount.mjs). There is no ingestion of anyone else's listings. So on a night when four bars in town have music and one of them has a MySet artist, the page tells the fan "That's everything in Koh Phangan." That single fact justifies the fix on its own, and it is far more likely to bite a real user than a blank city field.

The page's own vocabulary already knows this. index.html:307 says "No gigs listed yet" and index.html:408 says "No one has listed a gig here yet." The one line that drops "listed" is the one under audit — which makes this a slip, not a position.

SEVERITY, though, is overcooked at major. Nothing turns on it: no money, no access, no claim about what the product can do. It is a soft superlative in an end-of-list flourish, on a page that already uses the honest word twice a few lines up. Minor.

Also confirming the accuser's one concession is right: the feed loop at events.mjs:68-86 iterates `for (const id of ids)` with no slice, so there is genuinely no cap. (The 40-id cap at events.mjs:166 `ids.slice(0, 40)` is in countUpcoming, which only feeds the picker's counts — worth a separate look, since a city with more than 40 listers shows an understated number in the dropdown, but it is not this line.)
