So the one step in the flow that tells someone where to look is wrong for a real slice of the audience the page is targeting.
finding.proposedFix: "Tap Share in Safari" / "the square with an arrow coming out of it — bottom of the screen on an iPhone, top on an iPad"

check.reasoning:
I read the actual code and the accusation does not hold up as stated. Three problems with it.

1. THE IPHONE HALF IS FACTUALLY WRONG. The accuser says "the same is true on an iPhone whose owner has moved the address bar to the top in Settings -> Safari." It is not. On iPhone, Settings -> Safari -> Tabs -> "Single Tab" moves the address bar to the top but restores the pre-iOS-15 layout, which still has the bottom toolbar carrying back / forward / SHARE / bookmarks / tabs. The Share button sits at the bottom of an iPhone in BOTH tab-bar layouts. So the "real slice of the audience" the accusation leans on to justify severity is, for iPhones, empty. Only the iPad half survives.

2. THE PAGE IS MORE CAREFULLY SCOPED THAN THE ACCUSER NOTICED. The sentence does not float free — it lives inside a device-tabbed sheet. index.html:589-591 renders a two-button group labelled `aria-label="Choose your phone"` with the tabs literally reading "iPhone" and "Android", and the selected tab is highlighted. index.html:596-597 closes the same panel with "It has to be **Safari** on an iPhone — Chrome on iOS can't add to the home screen." So an iPad user who opens this sheet is looking at a panel that says "iPhone" twice, on a tab they can see is selected. The step is TRUE for every device the panel names. This is a coverage gap (there is no iPad tab), not a false statement — which drops it below "minor" to cosmetic.

3. IT IS AIMED AT THE WRONG SURFACE. The brief names public/about.html as "the landing page under audit". I grepped all of public/ — the string "at the bottom of Safari" exists only at index.html:563. about.html contains no add-to-home-screen instructions at all (grep for Safari / home screen / install returns only marketing copy at about.html:293, 488, 710). So this is a finding against the secondary surface.

WHAT I DID CONFIRM, and where the accuser is actually UNDER-stating it:
IOSISH does include iPad (index.html:517-518), but IOSISH is not what selects the steps. index.html:560 is `let OS = ANDROIDISH && !IOSISH ? 'android' : 'ios';` — 'ios' is the DEFAULT for everything that is not an Android user agent. And nothing gates the sheet to mobile: drawFootInstall (index.html:527-532) sets `hidden = INSTALLED` only, so the footer "Add to home screen" button (index.html:279) is visible on desktop too. Result: desktop macOS Safari, desktop Firefox, iPad, iPod — every non-Android, non-Chromium visitor who opens this sheet gets the iPhone Safari steps. On macOS Safari the whole flow is wrong, not just the word "bottom" (Share is top-right, and the menu item is "Add to Dock", not "Add to Home Screen"). So the exposure is wider than the accusation describes, while the specific charge it makes is weaker.

Corroborating evidence for the fix wording: the repo already solved this elsewhere. studio.html:3231 says "Tap **Share** in Safari" with the sub-line "the square with an arrow pointing up" — no position claim at all. index.html:563 is the outlier, and the house style is already the position-free phrasing.
check.correctedStatus: NOT A DISCREPANCY as charged — downgrade to a cosmetic copy-consistency nit. The sentence at index.html:563 is accurate for the device its own panel names (index.html:590 tab "iPhone", index.html:597 "on an iPhone"), and it is accurate for iPhones in both address-bar layouts, so the accusation's iPhone claim is false. The residual iPad case is a missing-tab coverage gap, not a wrong statement. Severity: cosmetic, not minor.
check.correctedEvidence: /Users/perryidyll/Docs/MySet/public/index.html:563 (the step), :589-591 (the "iPhone"/"Android" tabs that scope it), :596-597 ("It has to be Safari on an iPhone"), :560 (OS defaults to 'ios' for every non-Android UA), :517-518 (IOSISH), :527-532 and :279 (the sheet is not gated to mobile); /Users/perryidyll/Docs/MySet/public/studio.html:3231 (the same instruction already written position-free); /Users/perryidyll/Docs/MySet/public/about.html — grep finds no add-to-home-screen copy, so the audited landing page is unaffected.
check.betterFix: Do not adopt the proposed fix — "bottom of the screen on an iPhone, top on an iPad" adds a second device to a panel whose tab still says "iPhone", which makes the labelling more confusing, not less, and it spends words on a distinction almost no reader needs. Adopt the wording the repo already uses on itself. Change index.html:563 to match studio.html:3231: ['Tap Share in Safari', 'the square with an arrow coming out of it'], That drops the only false-able clause, needs no new tab, brings the two surfaces into one voice, and is correct on iPhone, iPad and Mac simultaneously. If anyone wants to close the real gap rather than the cosmetic one, the fix is at index.html:560, not :563 — the default OS is 'ios' for every non-Android visitor, so desktop macOS Safari and Firefox users who click the footer button (index.html:279) are shown iPhone Safari steps for a menu item ("Add to Home Screen") that does not exist on their machine. Either hide the footer install button when the device is neither IOSISH nor ANDROIDISH and no beforeinstallprompt has fired, or add a Mac branch. That is a separate, larger finding and should be filed on its own.

finding.claimText: Scroll down and tap Add to Home Screen
finding.evidence: This is a claim about current iOS Safari, not about any code in this repo — nothing in public/ or netlify/functions/ can determine it, and I did not test it on a device this session. What is knowable: "Add to Home Screen" is a standard iOS share-sheet action, and its position varies with the user's customised action list, so "scroll down" is a reasonable default rather than a fact. index.html:598 already sets that precedent by hedging the Android wording.

check.correctedStatus: NOT A FINDING — out of audit scope (no product claim; nothing to reconcile against code). Optional copy polish at most.
check.correctedEvidence: public/index.html:561-573 (A2HS_STEPS.ios/android arrays), public/index.html:596-598 (the ternary whose iOS branch at 597 is unhedged and whose Android branch at 598 is the hedge cited as "precedent"), public/index.html:570 (Android step already carries the alternate label inline), public/studio.html:3231-3234 and 3243-3245 (same iOS instruction and the same iOS-hard / Android-hedged split, app-wide)
check.reasoning:
Three independent grounds, all checked in code I read myself.

1. SCOPE. The audit's unit is "the page asserts X about MySet, the code does Y." Line 564 is one entry in the A2HS_STEPS.ios array (index.html:561-567) — instructional help text about Apple's share sheet, rendered into a bottom sheet by drawA2HSSheet() (583-598). It makes no assertion about MySet. The accuser's own body concedes nothing in public/ or netlify/functions/ can determine it. A finding that states no code can bear on it, cites no defect, and proposes no fix is a note, not a discrepancy.

2. THE PRECEDENT IS MISREAD — this is the accusation's only positive argument and it is wrong. The accuser writes that "index.html:598 already sets that precedent by hedging the Android wording." Line 598 is the ELSE branch of the ternary opened at 596; it renders only when OS==='android'. The iOS branch, line 597, is flat and unhedged: "It has to be Safari on an iPhone — Chrome on iOS can't add to the home screen." So the file does not establish a convention of hedging platform instructions. It establishes the opposite: hedge Android, state iOS plainly. That split is deliberate and repeated in studio.html:3243-3245. The reason is substantive — Android OEM skins genuinely rename the control, which is why line 570 also carries the alternate label inline ("or Install app, if you see that instead") while the iOS steps need no such alternate. iOS Safari is one vendor, one browser, one label. The variance argument does not transfer across the platform boundary.

3. THE CRITERION DOESN'T GENERALISE. Lines 563, 565, 569, 570, 571 and studio.html:3231-3234 are the same class of statement — claims about Apple's and Google's UI, none verifiable from this repo. Under the accuser's rule there are ten findings here, not one. Singling out the line that happens to contain a hedgeable verb ("Scroll down") is pattern-matching on phrasing rather than applying a defect criterion.

Also, the sentence is more careful than the accuser noticed. It pairs a gesture with a target: the load-bearing half is the control label "Add to Home Screen", which is stable; "scroll down" is wayfinding that is a harmless no-op for a user whose customised action list already shows the item (a sheet at its scroll end simply doesn't move). It cannot route anyone to a wrong action, so there is no failure mode even if the hint is unnecessary for some users. And on a default iPhone the action list does extend past the visible sheet, so the hint is the common case.

Nothing here is worse or wider than stated — I checked for that. The one adjacent behaviour I verified as real but out of scope: OS defaults to 'ios' for every non-Android user including desktop (line 560), but the sheet exposes iPhone/Android tabs (590-591) and desktop users get the native install path via INSTALL_EVENT (585-586), so that is a deliberate default, not a bug.

Per the instruction to default to refuted absent personal confirmation: I could not confirm any problem, and I additionally showed the supporting argument offered is incorrect.
check.betterFix: No change is required. If Perry wants copy polish anyway, do NOT add a hedging clause — this is a four-step ritual where every word is load-bearing ("no pixel without a purpose"). The stronger edit keeps the target hard and softens only the wayfinding, at a cost of three words: public/index.html:564 ['Tap Add to Home Screen', 'scroll down if you don’t see it'], That uses the existing sub-line slot (the second array element, rendered as the grey sub-text at 594), so it adds no new UI. It preserves the imperative on the control that matters, removes "scroll" as an apparent precondition for users whose action list is customised, and stays consistent with how line 570 already handles Android's label variance in the sub-line rather than in a footnote. If this is applied, apply the same shape to public/studio.html:3232 so the two sheets stay in step.

finding.claimText: Then it opens like an app — full screen, one tap, and it remembers where you were.
finding.evidence: manifest.webmanifest:6 sets `"start_url": "/?src=pwa"` — the installed app always opens the fan home page, wherever the visitor was. The only memory in the product is the localStorage country/city recall at index.html:328-337, which refills the finder and re-runs a city search. It does not return anyone to a gig, an artist page, the Studio, or a scroll position.
finding.proposedFix: "Then it opens like an app — full screen, one tap, and it remembers the city you were looking at."

check.reasoning:
I read the code myself and the accusation does not hold at status FALSE.

1) WHERE THE SENTENCE LIVES. It is not body copy on a marketing page. It is the lede of the "Put MySet on your home screen" bottom sheet, built inside drawA2HSSheet() at public/index.html:585. That sheet is opened only from openA2HS(), and the only two callers are the install card (public/index.html:539) and the footer button (public/index.html:279) — both on index.html. I grepped every other page in public/ for a2hs/openA2HS: none has it (studio.html has its own separate sheet with different copy, public/studio.html:3238, which makes no memory claim). So the only person who ever reads this sentence is standing on the fan home page. The accuser's framing — "the installed app always opens the fan home page, wherever the visitor was" — applies a condition the sentence never sets up. Nobody is being told from a vote page that the app will reopen on that vote page.

2) WHAT THE CODE ACTUALLY DOES ON RELAUNCH. manifest.webmanifest:6 start_url "/?src=pwa" lands on index.html. boot() then hits the recall path at public/index.html:328-337, and the accuser understates it: line 335 does not merely refill the finder, it calls search(), which fetches the city feed and renders the gig list (public/index.html:395-424). So the fan reopens the installed app and is looking at the same city's what's-on list they were looking at last time — the same screen, repainted. On the surface where the sentence appears, "it remembers where you were" is a fair colloquial description of the actual behaviour, not a false one.

3) I CHECKED THE OBVIOUS FRAGILITY AND IT ISN'T THERE. The recall is gated on the country and city still existing in the picker feed (lines 330, 334). I read the server: netlify/functions/events.mjs:19-36 keeps a city in the index even when its gig count is zero ("keep it listed, with the count, so the emptiness is visible"). So the restore is not conditional on there being gigs — it holds for any city ever picked.

4) THE ACCUSER'S OWN FIX PROVES THE POINT. "It remembers the city you were looking at" describes the same code path. You do not replace a FALSE claim with a restatement of the same true mechanism; you replace an imprecise one. That makes this a wording nit, not a truth failure.

WHAT IS GENUINELY LOOSE (the honest residue, and it is small): a cold launch does not return an artist to the Studio or a fan to a specific gig's vote page — no route memory exists anywhere; public/sw.js is navigation-network-first with no state restore, and the only other fan storage is a fan id, a sort preference and a pending request in public/vote.html:287, 541, 982. And on a warm relaunch from the app switcher the OS restores the exact page anyway, which is platform behaviour I cannot cite as product code. So the sentence is true-but-loose at worst. FALSE is the wrong status and "minor" overstates the severity; nothing here misleads a buyer or a fan.
check.correctedStatus: TRUE (imprecise wording at most — downgrade from FALSE/minor to a cosmetic copy nit; no fix is required)
check.correctedEvidence: public/index.html:585 (sentence, inside drawA2HSSheet); public/index.html:279 and 539 (the only callers of openA2HS — sheet is index-only); public/index.html:328-337 (recall runs search(), not just a refill); public/index.html:395-424 (search renders the city gig list); netlify/functions/events.mjs:19-36 (zero-gig cities stay in the picker, so recall doesn't break); manifest.webmanifest:6 and 9 (start_url "/?src=pwa", display standalone); public/sw.js:87-110 (navigations network-first, no route restore); public/studio.html:3238 (studio's separate sheet makes no memory claim)
check.betterFix: Leave it. If Perry wants it tighter, name the payoff rather than the mechanism: "Then it opens like an app — full screen, one tap, and straight back to what's on in your city." That is more concrete than the accuser's "it remembers the city you were looking at" (which undersells it — the app doesn't just refill the box, it re-renders the gig list) and it stays true to index.html:328-337.

finding.claimText: It has to be Safari on an iPhone — Chrome on iOS can’t add to the home screen.
finding.evidence: Chrome for iOS has carried "Add to Home Screen" in its share menu since 2023 (Chrome 108 / iOS 16.4), and Edge and Firefox on iOS have their own equivalents. The line is stated as a hard requirement (index.html:597) rather than a recommendation, so a Chrome-on-iPhone visitor is told to go and install another browser to do something their browser already does. This is a claim about iOS rather than about this code, and it was not device-tested this session.
finding.proposedFix: "It's easiest in Safari. Chrome on iOS can do it too — look for Add to Home Screen in the same share menu."

check.reasoning:
I tried to break this finding and could not. Four angles, all failed to save the page: 1. IS THERE A CODE PATH THAT MAKES IT TRUE? No. I read the whole install feature. The only Safari-related logic is UA sniffing: `public/index.html:516` sets `IOSISH = /iPad|iPhone|iPod/.test(navigator.userAgent) || (navigator.platform==='MacIntel' && navigator.maxTouchPoints>1)`, and `public/index.html:560` sets `OS = ANDROIDISH && !IOSISH ? 'android' : 'ios'`. Chrome for iOS ships a UA containing "iPhone", so a Chrome-on-iPhone visitor lands on the iOS branch and is shown line 597 verbatim. There is no browser detection anywhere in the install code — nothing distinguishes Safari from Chrome, so nothing anywhere in the app depends on Safari being the browser that did the adding. The repo actually knows CriOS exists, but only server-side for device labelling (`netlify/functions/_session.mjs:121`). 2. IS THE ACCUSER READING A COMMENT OR A DOC AS BEHAVIOUR? No. This is literal rendered copy, injected into the install sheet's `

` by `drawA2HSSheet()` (`public/index.html:596-598`). Every iPhone visitor who opens the sheet reads it. 3. IS THE SENTENCE MORE CAREFULLY WORDED THAN NOTICED? No — it is the opposite. "It has to be Safari" is the hardest possible framing; there is no hedge, no "easiest", no "we've only tested". The accuser's characterisation of it as a stated hard requirement is exact. 4. IS THE WORLD-FACT WRONG? I could not device-test, so I weighed it carefully. Chrome for iOS has carried Add to Home Screen in its own share menu since iOS 16.4 (March 2023), when Apple opened Home Screen web app creation to third-party browsers; Edge and Firefox on iOS have the same. That is a three-year-old, well-established platform change, not a marginal or disputed one. The only population for whom line 597 is true is iPhones still on iOS 16.3 or older. And because the resulting web app is WebKit-backed either way, `INSTALLED` (`public/index.html:514-515`, via `display-mode: standalone` / `navigator.standalone`) resolves true for a Chrome-added install exactly as for a Safari-added one — so there is no functional harm hiding behind the wrong sentence, only misdirection. WHERE THE FINDING IS UNDERSTATED — the problem is WIDER than reported. The same false sentence exists a second time, in the Studio: `public/studio.html:3244` — "It has to be Safari — Chrome on iPhone can't add to the home screen." That one sits inside `openStudioInstall()`, the sheet an artist is sent to when push alerts are blocked (`public/studio.html:3196`, the `ios-not-installed` state). The gate itself is honest and correct — `pushState()` at `public/studio.html:3152` blocks on `PUSH_IOS && !PUSH_INSTALLED`, which is a real iOS rule — but the instructions under it tell a Chrome-using artist to go and install a different browser before they can receive song-request alerts. Fixing only index.html leaves the higher-stakes copy wrong. WHERE THE PROPOSED FIX IS TOO SMALL. Rewriting only the footnote leaves step 1 contradicting it: `public/index.html:563` still reads "Tap Share at the bottom of Safari", and `public/studio.html:3232` reads "Tap Share in Safari". A Chrome user told in the footnote that their browser works, then told in step 1 to use Safari's bottom bar, is worse off than before — Chrome on iOS puts share behind the address-bar/⋯ menu, not a Safari bottom bar. The step text has to move with the footnote, in both files. So: not refuted. Status FALSE stands, severity minor on the landing page, and I'd raise it to minor-to-moderate for the Studio copy since it stands between a paying artist and a working feature.
check.correctedStatus: FALSE — confirmed, and wider than reported. The sentence is rendered copy shown to every iPhone user agent (Chrome included, since detection is `/iPad|iPhone|iPod/` only), no code path makes it true, and the identical false claim appears a second time in the Artist Studio.
check.correctedEvidence: public/index.html:597 (the claim), public/index.html:563 (Safari-specific step 1 that must change with it), public/index.html:516 and 560 (UA detection routes Chrome-on-iPhone to the iOS branch), public/index.html:514-515 (INSTALLED detection is browser-agnostic, so nothing depends on Safari), public/studio.html:3244 (the duplicate claim), public/studio.html:3232 (its Safari-specific step), public/studio.html:3152 and 3196 (the real, correct iOS install gate the copy sits under), netlify/functions/_session.mjs:121 (the codebase already recognises CriOS server-side)

finding.claimText: favicon and apple-touch-icon as inline data-URI SVGs of three bars
finding.evidence: The assertion holds — the mark is inline, so it costs no network request, and the gradient stops (#FF375F → #FF6B45, index.html:25) match --grad in app.css:25. about.html:25 carries a byte-identical data URI. But the two drawings in THIS file have drifted. The data URI (index.html:25-26, viewBox 0 0 100 100) has bars at x 26/44/62, width 11, heights 32/48/22. The markup mark (index.html:243, viewBox 0 0 24 24) has x 4/10.3/16.6, width 3.4, heights 11/16/8 — which normalised to the same 100-unit box is x 16.7/42.9/69.2, width 14.2, heights 45.8/66.7/33.3. So the on-page mark is materially chunkier and wider-spread than the tab icon: bar-to-gap ratio 1.17 versus 1.57.
finding.proposedFix: Rebuild the markup mark from the data URI at 24/100 scale so the tab and the page show the same drawing — index.html:243: <rect x="6.24" y="10.08" width="2.64" height="7.68" rx="1.32"/><rect x="10.56" y="6.24" width="2.64" height="11.52" rx="1.32"/><rect x="14.88" y="12.48" width="2.64" height="5.28" rx="1.32"/>

check.reasoning:
The accusation fails on three independent grounds, and it missed the one part of the assertion that is genuinely false.

1) THE GEOMETRY IS MIS-MEASURED. The accuser normalised the markup mark's 24-unit viewBox onto a 100-unit box "to the same 100-unit box", assuming the SVG fills its tile. It does not. index.html:60-62 (identically about.html:51-53) reads `.mark i{width:26px;height:26px;border-radius:8px;background:var(--grad);...}` and `.mark i svg{width:14px;height:14px;fill:#fff;display:block}`. The 24-unit viewBox is rendered at 14px, centred inside a 26px tile — 53.8% of the tile, not 100%. Correct tile-relative figures: the favicon's bar group spans x 26→73 = 47% of the tile width and y 26→74 = 48% of its height; the on-page group spans 16 viewBox units = 9.33px in a 26px tile = 35.9% on both axes. The on-page mark is therefore SMALLER and more inset than the tab icon, not "materially chunkier and wider-spread." The accuser's own cited ratio contradicts their prose: bar:gap 1.17 (on-page) versus 1.57 (favicon) means the on-page bars are THINNER relative to their gaps, i.e. airier, which is the opposite of chunkier.

2) THE PROPOSED FIX WOULD MAKE IT WORSE. Rescaling the favicon rects by 0.24 into the 24-box, then rendering that box at 14px inside a 26px tile, puts the bar group at 47% x (14/26) = 25.3% of the tile — further from the favicon's 47% than today's 35.9%. It corrects the bar:gap ratio while breaking the overall scale.

3) IT IS OUT OF SCOPE. The assertion is "favicon and apple-touch-icon as inline data-URI SVGs of three bars." The brandbar `.mark` at index.html:243 / about.html:278 is a third drawing the sentence never mentions and never claims parity with. The drift is a house-style nitpick, not a discrepancy against the claim.

WHAT I POSITIVELY CONFIRMED FOR THE PAGE: I hashed the three data-URI lines — index.html:25 (rel=icon), index.html:26 (rel=apple-touch-icon) and about.html:25 (rel=icon) are byte-identical (sha1 b560ded33e11044370983c0bb50275b4c61014da). Gradient stops #FF375F -> #FF6B45 match --grad at app.css:25 exactly. So the inline, three-bar, brand-matched part of the assertion is true.

WHAT THE ACCUSER MISSED — THE ACTUAL FALSE HALF. The apple-touch-icon claim does not hold. I grepped every file in public/ for apple-touch-icon: about.html — the landing page under audit — has exactly ONE, at about.html:27, `<link rel="apple-touch-icon" href="/icons/icon-512.png">`. There is no inline apple-touch-icon on about.html at all; only the favicon is inline. On index.html the inline one at :26 is followed by a SECOND apple-touch-icon at index.html:28 pointing at the same PNG; with neither carrying a `sizes` attribute, the later declaration is the one Apple resolves to (medium confidence on that resolution rule specifically), and separately apple-touch-icon has never accepted SVG on iOS — it requires a raster PNG. Either way no Apple device renders the inline SVG as a home-screen icon. I opened public/icons/icon-512.png: it is the same three-bar mark on the same gradient, so nothing looks wrong to a user — but the "inline, costs no network request" rationale is false for the apple-touch-icon on BOTH pages. That makes the assertion partially false for a completely different reason than the one alleged, and the severity stays cosmetic because the delivered artwork is correct.
check.correctedStatus: PARTIALLY FALSE — but not for the alleged reason. The drift finding is REFUTED (mis-measured, direction reversed, out of scope, fix counterproductive). The favicon half of the assertion is fully TRUE and byte-identical across both pages. The apple-touch-icon half is FALSE: about.html has no inline apple-touch-icon at all, and index.html's inline one is superseded by a PNG declaration and unsupported by iOS. Severity remains cosmetic — the PNG carries the identical mark.
check.correctedEvidence: public/index.html:25-26 and public/about.html:25 (three byte-identical data URIs, sha1 b560ded33e11044370983c0bb50275b4c61014da); public/app.css:25 (--grad #FF375F -> #FF6B45, matches); public/about.html:27 (apple-touch-icon = /icons/icon-512.png, the ONLY one in the file); public/index.html:28 (second apple-touch-icon = /icons/icon-512.png, after the inline one); public/index.html:60-62 and public/about.html:51-53 (.mark i is 26px, .mark i svg is 14px — the scale factor the accuser omitted); public/index.html:243 and public/about.html:278 (the 24-box markup mark); public/icons/icon-512.png (same three-bar mark, same gradient)
check.betterFix:
Two separate fixes; do not apply the accuser's.

A) The assertion's actual defect — make the apple-touch-icon claim true, or reword it. Cheapest and most correct: reword the inventory line to "favicon as an inline data-URI SVG of three bars; apple-touch-icon as /icons/icon-512.png." If you instead want the claim to stand as written, you cannot — apple-touch-icon does not accept SVG on iOS. Separately, delete the dead inline apple-touch-icon at index.html:26, since index.html:28 already supersedes it; that removes ~700 bytes of head weight that never renders anywhere. about.html needs no change to its icons.

B) If parity between the tab icon and the brandbar mark is wanted anyway (cosmetic, optional), the accuser's rects are right but the tile scale is not. Let the SVG fill the tile so the 24-box maps to the tile the way the favicon's 100-box maps to its own:
  - index.html:62 and about.html:53 -> .mark i svg{width:26px;height:26px;fill:#fff;display:block}
  - index.html:243 and about.html:278 -> <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24"><rect x="6.24" y="10.08" width="2.64" height="7.68" rx="1.32"/><rect x="10.56" y="6.24" width="2.64" height="11.52" rx="1.32"/><rect x="14.88" y="12.48" width="2.64" height="5.28" rx="1.32"/></svg>
  That yields a bar group at 47% of the 26px tile and bar:gap 1.57 — both matching the favicon. Apply the rects WITHOUT the 26px svg change and the mark shrinks to 25.3% of the tile, worse than today.
  While there, the tile corner is also drifted and the accuser missed it: the favicon is rx 24 on 100 = 24%, but .mark i is border-radius 8px on 26px = 30.8%. Set border-radius:6.24px at index.html:60 / about.html:51 for true parity. Note both files carry their own copy of these rules — edit both or they diverge.

gaps.lens: A working gigging musician who read myset.vip/about, signed up, and then got the keys to the whole app — ranking every gap by whether knowing it would have changed the decision to sign up (or to pay).

gaps.feature: Card payments work for every artist now — the page says the opposite
gaps.whereInCode: netlify/functions/_connect.mjs:131-180 (ensureAccount / onboardingLink, Express, daily payouts); netlify/functions/admin.mjs:1105-1123 (payStart, any artist, owner role); public/studio.html:1552-1577 (the "Set up card payments" card, shown to every artist who is not the founder); netlify/functions/_pay.mjs:49-54 (canTakeMoney gates on Connect, not on plan)
gaps.state: BUILT AND LIVE for any artist on any plan, including Free. Stripe Connect Express onboarding, direct charges, daily payouts, MySet never sees bank details. gaps.structuralNotes:
The page's shape is still right. What has broken is that the app moved and the page's honesty block did not — and it moved in the direction that costs signups.

1. The "Three honest notes" block is now the single biggest liability on the page. Two of the three are false, and both falsely claim a thing does NOT exist when it does: card payments (live for every artist via Stripe Connect, _connect.mjs:131-180) and buying Plus or Pro (live via Stripe Checkout, _billing.mjs:120-161). Beat 4 defers to that block from the middle of the page — "the note under the plans says exactly where that stands" — so a stale note is poisoning the strongest section too. Rewrite it as two notes: (1) MySet is early, one real gig, still built in public — keep that one exactly as it is, it earns trust; (2) the four Pro extras marked Soon are not built. Then move a new, truer third piece of honesty into pricing: Stripe's own card fee comes off the artist's side. The block should shrink, not grow — but the sentence it loses must be replaced by a harder one, or the page loses the quality that makes it work.

2. One section is missing entirely, and it is the strongest argument the app has. Everything that runs without the artist — the calendar starting and ending the show, the setlist loading itself, votes coming back when a song is dropped, the night filing itself into history, the city feed rewriting itself — is invisible here. The section already titled "Five things happen. None of them need you." is the natural home: add a sixth beat about the calendar running the night and the title stops being a claim and becomes a demonstration. Before writing it, resolve the drift: the code puts no plan gate on auto-shows (_auto.mjs:133) but the Studio's plan cards list them under Plus and Pro only (studio.html:3531, 3545). Two surfaces already disagree; a third must not join in.

3. The pricing table has quietly become the least accurate section on the page, in four separate ways: setlists listed as free when creating one is Plus (admin.mjs:730-737); the Free room number reading as a locked door when it is not; "2% cut — stays yours" implying 98% when Stripe's fee sits on top; and the verified tick, which the Studio sells under Plus, missing altogether. Plus currently has no single reason to exist that a stranger can see from outside. The tick is that reason, and it is sitting unused.

4. Nothing on the page is for the artist after the gig. Beat 5 covers being findable and then the page moves on. The community page — stars, photos, thirty-second clips with sound, one reply of your own, hide-anything-free — is one bullet in a price list. Extend beat 5 rather than adding a section; it is already the after-the-gig beat and it is the thinnest of the five.

5. The venues section reads as a free product with no price. It is not: Venue Pro is $20 a month, buyable today, and the cut on venue merch is 10% or 2%. Either give the pricing grid a fourth card or give the venues section its own short price paragraph. Right now a publican finishes signup and then finds a tier.

6. Two things must be kept OFF the page despite being in the code: Spotify playlist import (needs SPOTIFY_CLIENT_ID / SPOTIFY_CLIENT_SECRET, unset in production, endpoint 503s) and push alerts to the artist's phone (needs VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY / VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY, unset). Both read like excellent copy and both would be untrue today.

7. One correction inside the page's own JavaScript, not just its prose: the live demo lets a reader take a vote back (about.html:768), which is the OFF behaviour of the voteFinal flag. The default has been ON since 2026-09-02. The demo is the most-used part of this page and it is currently teaching the wrong lesson about how the room behaves.

8. Length is not the problem people will think it is. Four of the must-adds are edits to sentences that already exist, and two of them delete text. The page can absorb the sixth beat and the community-page paragraph and still come out shorter than it is now if the honest block loses its two dead notes.

gaps.structuralNotes:
The shape is mostly right. Three things about it have gone wrong, in descending order of cost.

1. The demo is now the weakest thing on the page, and it is the load-bearing thing. Section 3 says "This is the real thing, running on this page" — and it isn't any more. It runs a one-tap toggle with take-backs, which is exactly the behaviour the app switched off on 2 September. It also shows 3 free votes where the app ships 5, and no replay row. Everything downstream of it inherits the wrong mental model, including the reader's. Rebuilding it with the stepper, finality and one already-played row fixes four gaps at once with almost no added words, which is the only kind of edit a page this long can afford. This is the single highest-value change on the list.

2. Beat 5 is doing two jobs and dropping one of them. "And afterwards, they can find you" currently carries the lyrics button, the profile page, the links, the gigs and the city feed — and the community page, the whole surface where the room writes back with photos and clips, appears nowhere in the narrative at all. It should split: Beat 5 keeps the profile (find you), a new Beat 6 takes the community page (say something). The page already has a "solo" full-width beat style for a beat with no screenshot, so it costs no new CSS. This is the only place I'd add a section rather than a paragraph.

3. The honest-notes box has inverted. It was the page's credibility device; two of its three notes are now stale in the artist's favour — card payments work per-artist once Stripe onboarding is done, and Plus/Pro checkout is built and live. Left as-is the page talks a musician out of the product on the one point that decides it. The box should stay, with its three-note shape, rewritten. The remaining true note is note 1 (MySet is early, one real gig), which is worth keeping exactly as it is.

Nothing needs killing. Section 6 (proof, the eight people and twenty-one votes) and Section 7 (venues) are unchanged by any of this and are the strongest writing on the page.

gaps.structuralNotes:
The shape no longer fits. The section is built as one idea — *it fills itself in* — expressed as six benefit rows, three feeling cards, and a closing beat that re-explains the name matching. That was the right shape when a venue page was a listing. The venue side is now six tabs, a paid tier, a fan-facing feed, a shop and a payout account, and none of the last four have a home in the current structure.

Three structural moves, in order of value:

1. **Split the six rows into two lists: what fills itself in, and what you fill in.** Right now rows 1-3 and 5 are automatic and rows 4 and 6 are not, and the mix is why "your menu and your offers" can appear twice without the reader ever learning they are things you type. Two short lists under one heading keep the length identical and make the product legible.

2. **The community page needs to be its own beat, not a bullet.** It is the only surface where fans touch a venue, it is the section's best proof of "one less weekly job" (photos from the night, posted by the people in them), and it carries the one thing a bar owner will worry about — moderation. A bullet cannot carry the reassurance that hiding is instant, undoable and free on every plan. Put it between the checklist and the Ease/Confidence/Pull cards.

3. **Venue pricing has to exist somewhere.** The pricing section (about.html:586-700) is three artist plans and nothing else, while the venue block ends on "Claim your venue — free" with no hint that $20/month exists. Either add a small two-line Free/Pro block inside the venue section, or give the venues a fourth card in the pricing grid. The former is better: it keeps the venue argument in one place and keeps the artist pricing grid at three columns.

Two things to fix in the app before the page can carry the new copy, both internal contradictions rather than landing-page problems:

- **Venue Pro says two different things.** venueadmin.mjs:414-419 opens a real Stripe Checkout and public/venue-studio.html:816-833 offers the button, but the verification checklist at public/venue-studio.html:1458 still reads "Not self-serve yet: message us and we'll switch it on for your page." Whichever is true has to be true in both places before the landing page names a route to Pro.

- **The venue public page tells artists the wrong thing about vouching.** public/venue.html:487 renders "${need} artists who play here does it — **no website needed**", and falls back to `need=10` when the payload is missing (public/venue.html:485). The real rule is three artists (_verify.mjs:30) *and* a website that passes two checks *and* a paid plan — all five, ANDed at _verify.mjs:204-206. So an artist is currently told they can hand a bar its green tick on their own, and they can't.

One thing the section gets right and should keep untouched: "Free. Your page works whether you verify it or not." Everything proposed above sits around that sentence rather than replacing it — it is the line that makes the five-step tick safe to describe.

gaps.structuralNotes:
The page's shape has drifted out from under it in one specific place, and is missing a section in another.

1 · The honest-notes block is now the weakest part of the page, not the strongest. It was written when nothing could be bought and nobody could be paid, and it is doing the opposite of its job — two of its three notes are advertising limitations that no longer exist (_billing.mjs, _connect.mjs). Do not just soften them: notes 2 and 3 need replacing with what is actually true, and the block should keep three notes so it still reads as candour rather than as a retreat. Suggested new set: (1) MySet is early, one real gig — unchanged and still the right thing to lead with; (2) getting paid takes one setup step, and here is the irreversible bit; (3) you can buy Plus and Pro today, and the four Pro extras marked Soon are still Soon.

2 · Beat 4 needs to split. "Money happens without you asking" is currently doing two jobs — the fan-facing magic (tip button, buy votes) and an apology for payments not working. With the apology gone there is room for the half the page has never had: how the money gets to you. Same beat, two paragraphs: what the room sees, then what you set up once and what lands in your bank. That is where daily payouts, "the money is yours not ours", and the permanent country choice go.

3 · The fee facts do not fit in checkmark bullets and should stop trying to. Three separate things are true — MySet's cut (10/2/0), Stripe's own fee on the artist's side, and what the cut covers (tips included) — and a bullet that says "2% cut instead of 10% — stays yours" cannot carry any of them honestly. Add one small block under the plan grid, before the honest notes, headed something like "About the fee". It replaces one misleading bullet with three true sentences and it is the single highest-value structural change on the page.

4 · The venues section has no money in it at all, which is a whole missing half rather than a missing line. It currently reads as a free product with no ceiling, when in fact the green tick — the thing venues care about most — is $20 a month, and there is a cut on anything a venue sells. It does not need a fourth plan card (that would unbalance the section and bury the free-first pitch); it needs one short paragraph at the end, after "Claim your venue — free".

5 · One thing to leave alone: the Pro card's four "Soon" bullets are correctly marked, correctly disclosed in the markup rather than in CSS content, and still accurate against NOT_BUILT (_plan.mjs:130). Resist adding the built-but-flag-gated featured spots into that list — a $10 one-off purchase and an unbuilt Pro feature must not look like the same thing.

6 · A drift risk worth naming to Perry rather than fixing in copy: every number on this page — 4 shows, 200/1000/2000, 2000 songs, 50 live, 10/2/0% — is typed by hand here, and typed by hand again in studio.html's TIER_COPY (3509-3552), and defined for real in _plan.mjs:17-111. Three copies, one source of truth. The page is already showing what happens when one of them stops being updated.

gaps.lens: Information architecture — does the PAGE'S SHAPE still fit the product
gaps.structuralNotes:
THE SHAPE NO LONGER FITS, IN ONE SENTENCE: the page tells a one-act story ("the room votes") and MySet is now a three-act product — the room votes, the night runs itself, and the money is legally yours and lands in your own bank. Act one is told beautifully. Act two is completely absent. Act three is on the page as an apology for something that already shipped.

1) THE PROMISE IS MADE AND NEVER PAID. Section 4 is headed "Five things happen. None of them need you." That is precisely the promise of `_auto.mjs` — a gig on your calendar starts its own show and ends it three hours after the scheduled finish, never mid-song, never overruling you. That machinery is nowhere in the five beats. The page's own headline is describing a feature it does not mention. This is the single biggest structural hole: a NEW beat is needed, and it should be beat 2 (before "You stop guessing"), because it is the thing that happens before you even pick up the guitar.

2) BEAT 4 IS UPSIDE DOWN. "Money happens without you asking" is written as a promise with a caveat stapled to the end ("card payments are the part still being built"). In the code, payouts are the most finished thing in the app: Stripe Connect Express onboarding is live for any artist (`netlify/functions/_connect.mjs:131-180`, `admin.mjs:1105-1123`), charges are DIRECT so the artist is the merchant of record and the money lands in their own balance on daily payouts (`_connect.mjs:12-40`, `:151`), MySet's share is an explicit application fee, and there is a twelve-month earnings statement with a CSV (`_ledger.mjs:186-236`, `:418-438`). A caveat has to become a section — and it has to carry the one fact the page has never said, which is that Stripe's own ~2.9% + 30c comes off the ARTIST's side, so "2% cut" is not "you keep 98%" (`_connect.mjs:30-35`, `:314-319`). Concealing that until a musician's first payout is the exact thing this page's voice exists to avoid.

3) THE PRICING SECTION'S CLOSING BLOCK IS TWO-THIRDS OBSOLETE, AND ITS OBSOLESCENCE IS LOAD-BEARING. Honest note 2 ("Card payments aren't on yet") and note 3 ("Plus and Pro can't be bought yet") are both false now — `_billing.mjs:120-161` is a working Stripe Checkout in subscription mode for artists AND venues, with proration on upgrade, cancel-at-period-end on downgrade, the Customer Portal, invoices, and three days of grace on a failed card. Structurally this is not a copy edit: three notes shrink to ONE (note 1, "MySet is early — one real gig", which stays and stays first), and the space they vacate is where a short "how paying works" line belongs. Right now the page's most credible-sounding block is the block most likely to be caught out.

4) THE VENUE BLOCK IS IN THE WRONG PLACE AND MISSING ITS ONE DECIDING FACT. Section 7 runs ~80 lines and sits BETWEEN the artist's proof section and the artist's pricing — so an artist reader is handed to a different audience and handed back, with the pricing they came for pushed most of a screen further down. And the block never says what a venue pays. Venues now have a real two-tier ladder with self-serve checkout (`_venues.mjs:130-133`, `venueadmin.mjs:414-425`): Free, and Pro at $20/month for the green tick, twelve photos, merch and a 2% fee instead of 10%. A venue can read the whole section and not learn there is a paid tier. Two fixes, in order of preference: (a) move the venue block AFTER artist pricing and add a two-line price row inside it; or (b) cut it to a four-line teaser plus a link and give venues their own page. Either way it stops interrupting the artist's decision.

5) POST-GIG HAS NO REPRESENTATION AT ALL. The community page (`/:slug/community`) takes star ratings, up to three photos and a 30-second video clip with its sound (`_video.mjs:73`, `clipup.mjs`), the artist replies once, pins, and hides anything instantly and free. It appears on this page exactly once — as a bullet inside the Free plan card. It is the only part of the product with a public URL that the marketing page never shows. Its natural home is beat 5, which is already titled "And afterwards, they can find you" and currently talks only about links and gigs.

6) THE FAQ IS ANSWERING 2026-08's OBJECTIONS. Four of the seven still earn their place. The three highest-friction questions a working musician now asks are missing: "do I have to type my whole setlist in?" (import from CSV, a paste, or a Spotify playlist — `admin.mjs:1888-1913`, `:1606-1632`), "how do I actually get paid?" (Connect), and "what happens if I lose my phone at 1am?" (passkey, eight recovery codes, a device list you can sign out one at a time — `_passkey.mjs`, `_session.mjs:190-234`). "I play originals" is the weakest of the seven and is the one to drop if length is a problem.

7) ONE ROW OF THE PRICING TABLE READS AS A TURNSTILE AND ISN'T ONE. The Plus card carefully explains that going over 1,000 doesn't break the night. The Free card says "up to 200 people in the room at each" with no such note — so the plan most people will read is the one that looks like it locks the door at 200. It doesn't: `vote.mjs:81-92` is an explicit, commented NON-check. The reassurance is on the wrong card.

WHAT TO CUT TO PAY FOR THIS. The page is long and I am proposing additions. Three places to take the length back: the venue block (points 4), two of the three honest notes (point 3), and the "I play originals" FAQ (point 6). Net, the page should get slightly shorter and gain a whole act.

newFindings.claim: Studio plan sheet (public/studio.html:3531 and :3545): 'Shows that start and end themselves — from your calendar', listed under Plus and Pro only.
newFindings.problem: It is free. netlify/functions/_auto.mjs contains no reference to plan, limits or PLANS — grep returns zero. Its only plan interaction is that startShow counts the night against the same 4-shows-a-month free cap a manual tap does. So every free artist already has auto-start and auto-end, and the Studio's plan sheet tells them to pay $10/month for it. It is absent from TIER_COPY.free (studio.html:3510-3519), which lists ten items and not this one. Worse, it escapes every guard the project built for exactly this: it is a bare string with no plan flag behind it, so has()/isSoon() (studio.html:1274-1295) cannot reach it and test/limits.mjs cannot assert it. And about.html never mentions the feature at all, so the marketing page omits a free capability while the back office mis-sells it. This is the inverse of Perry's standing rule — not a locked feature hidden, but an unlocked feature shown as locked.
newFindings.evidence: grep -c 'plan\|PLANS\|limits' netlify/functions/_auto.mjs = 0. _auto.mjs:5 imports only { startShow, endShow }. _auto.mjs:133 is the sole opt-out (`show.autoStart === false`), default ON, and admin.mjs:1814 is a free action. studio.html:3531/:3545 carry the line; studio.html:3510-3519 (TIER_COPY.free) does not. test/autoshow.mjs:62 sets plan='plus' with the comment 'no cap for the first half' — the only plan interaction anywhere in the auto-show tests is the gig cap.

newFindings.claim: about.html:683 (FAQ, 'What if they request something I can't play?'): 'declining refunds them automatically, so you're never the villain and nobody's out of pocket.'
newFindings.problem: 'Out of pocket' is an explicit money claim, and it is false for any fan who bought a vote pack. A request is charged to me.spent (_requests.mjs:96). creditsUsed = sum(costOf(votes)) + spent (_lib.mjs:719). paidUsed = max(0, creditsUsed - freeCredits) (_lib.mjs:499-501). Every play/playTop is in RESETTERS (admin.mjs:1730) and fires clearAllFanVotes (admin.mjs:2001), which settles the paid portion — bag[id].extra -= paid — and then zeroes spent (_lib.mjs:517-521). The refund is me.spent = max(0, spent - cost) (_requests.mjs:141-143). So once a song has started, the request has already been paid for out of purchased credits and the later decline subtracts from a zeroed field and returns nothing. Worked example on shipped defaults: fan buys the 5-vote/$5 pack (extra=5); votes on three unplayed songs (creditsUsed 3); makes a 3-vote request (spent 3, creditsUsed 6). Artist starts the next song: paidUsed = 6-5 = 1, so extra drops 5 to 4 and spent goes to 0. Artist then declines. Nothing comes back and one vote the fan paid real money for is gone for good. The audit examined the softer line at :400 ('their votes come straight back') and its skeptic even identified this mechanism — then filed it as 'a code bug, not a wording problem on the landing page'. The wording problem exists; it is 283 lines further down, on a sentence nobody read.
newFindings.evidence: netlify/functions/_requests.mjs:96 (me.spent += cost), :141-143 (refund clamps at zero), :155-178 (resolveRequest); netlify/functions/_lib.mjs:499-501 (paidUsed), :517-521 (settle then zero spent), :719 (creditsUsed); netlify/functions/admin.mjs:1730 (RESETTERS includes play and playTop), :2001 (clearAllFanVotes).

newFindings.problem: A retired page name is not protected, and the code comment that says it is, is wrong. auth.mjs:451 deletes the old name from a.bySlug and :452-453 writes it into a.oldSlug. The comment immediately above (:449-451) claims 'It is not claimable by anyone else while it is here — pickSlug and setSlug both refuse a name already in bySlug.' Neither does: setSlug's only clash test is `const owner = a.bySlug[want]` (auth.mjs:441), and pickSlug's free() is `!RESERVED.has(v) && !reg.bySlug[v] && !reg.byId[v]` (_auth.mjs:96) — neither consults oldSlug, and the name was removed from bySlug two lines earlier. So the first new signup or rename that lands on that name takes it, and artistBySlug (_auth.mjs:82) resolves bySlug FIRST — meaning every printed table tent and poster then opens a STRANGER's live voting page, not a 404. The audit's skeptic bumped into this while refuting a different finding and explicitly declined to file it, reasoning that 'a stranger's page still answers the code, so print it once holds for the overwhelming case'. Sending a room to another artist's setlist is the worst outcome available, not an acceptable one.
newFindings.evidence: netlify/functions/auth.mjs:441 (bySlug-only clash check), :451 (delete a.bySlug[old]), :449-453 (the comment asserting a guard, and the oldSlug write); netlify/functions/_auth.mjs:96 (pickSlug free() ignores oldSlug), :82 (artistBySlug resolves bySlug first).

newFindings.claim: about.html:543 (venue tick-list, 'One code on the tables'): 'Tonight's music, your menu and your offers. Print it once.'
newFindings.problem: For venues there is no oldSlug mechanism at all — not a broken guard, an absent one. venueauth.mjs:148 is `if (old && old !== want) delete r.bySlug[old];` with no oldSlug write. venueBySlug (_venues.mjs:45-52) has no fallback. pickVenueSlug (_venues.mjs:58-68) has none. `grep -rn oldSlug netlify/functions/` returns five hits, every one artist-side. So the day a venue renames its page, every code printed on every table stops resolving, and the retired name is immediately claimable by another venue. The artist side at least attempts the promise; the venue side never has. The audit refused this finding on the grounds that it is 'an unimplemented invariant, not a landing-page discrepancy' — which is the wrong test for an audit of what the page promises. Separately, in the same function: venue setSlug never checks VRESERVED, while the artist path checks RESERVED at auth.mjs:439, so a venue can rename itself to api, community, merch or orders.
newFindings.evidence: netlify/functions/venueauth.mjs:138-152 (no oldSlug, no VRESERVED); netlify/functions/_venues.mjs:45-52 (venueBySlug), :58-68 (pickVenueSlug), :41-43 (VRESERVED, unused by setSlug); grep -rn oldSlug netlify/functions/ = 5 hits, all artist-side.

newFindings.claim: about.html:672 (FAQ, the page's self-declared most important design decision): 'Do my fans have to download anything? No — and they never will.' Reinforced at :293, 'Nothing for your fans to download.'
newFindings.problem: The fan-facing page that about.html's own footer sends readers to contradicts it in its second visible element. public/index.html:536-546 renders a card headed 'Saved MySet to your home screen yet? / Takes about six seconds' with an Install or How button; :279 keeps a permanent footer button 'Add to home screen'; :585 opens a sheet titled 'Put MySet on your home screen — Then it opens like an app'. One page tells the artist their fans will never install anything; the page it links them to asks the fans to install it. A careful reader can reconcile 'download' with 'home screen', but 'and they never will' is an unhedged forward promise about a fan surface that already nudges toward install — and this is the one claim the page italicises as load-bearing.
newFindings.evidence: public/about.html:672-674, :293, :723 (the footer link to /); public/index.html:536-546 (drawA2HS card), :279 (footer install button), :583-598 (drawA2HSSheet, 'Put MySet on your home screen').

newFindings.claim: about.html:628 (Plus card): 'Merch on your page — sell your tees, prints and stickers from your community page, paid straight to you'
newFindings.problem: There is no merch on the artist page. `grep -ci merch public/artist.html` returns 0. profile.mjs:40 ships a merch COUNT that public/artist.html never reads. Merch renders only on the community page (community.html:222-231, fed by community.mjs:72-73). The Studio's own card gets it right — studio.html:3530 reads 'Merch on your community page, paid straight to you'. The bolded lead-in on about.html is the inaccurate half and its own sub-clause corrects it, which is the tell that the phrase was written before the surface was decided.
newFindings.evidence: grep -ci merch public/artist.html = 0; netlify/functions/profile.mjs:40 (count shipped, unread); public/community.html:222-231; public/studio.html:3530.

critic.verdict: The audit was thorough on the hero, the demo widget and the pricing block, but it left four whole classes untouched. (1) It never opened ask.png, the beat-3 screenshot — which shows a retired 3-vote credit pill, the retired $3 pack price, and is missing the ↗ link and the per-row + buttons that shipped after it was captured. (2) It never read the FAQ's money sentence at :683, 'nobody's out of pocket', which is falsifiable in code: a fan who bought a vote pack and whose request is declined after the next song starts permanently loses a purchased vote. (3) It cleared 'Print it once. It's good forever.' twice — once for artists, once for venues — when the artist guarantee is asserted only in a comment the code does not implement (a retired name is claimable and resolves to a stranger's page, not a 404) and the venue guarantee has no implementation at all. (4) It never diffed about.html against the Studio's own plan sheet, which is where the sharpest contradiction sits: studio.html sells 'Shows that start and end themselves' as a Plus/Pro feature while _auto.mjs contains no plan gate whatsoever, so every free artist already has it. On structural drift the answer is stark — no test in the repo reads public/about.html, while test/limits.mjs is a 200-line purpose-built guard pointed at studio.html, venue-studio.html, lock.css, app.css and admin.mjs, and test/copy.mjs already loops over every public/*.html for one word. The harness exists; the marketing page is simply not in it, which is precisely how :606 came to sell Plus-only setlists as free. Two smaller gaps worth logging: public/mp4trim.js (516 lines, the no-re-encode clip trimmer that keeps a fan's audio) is in no surface of the app index, and test/structure.mjs guards six Studio tabs when there are seven — the unguarded one being Merch, which about.html sells.
